Born about 1530, he served as a parish priest at Kazan, and in 1579 stood at the event that marked his life, the finding of the Kazan Icon of the Mother of God, carrying the newly revealed image in procession with his own hands and later composing both the narrative of its appearance and the service in its honor, the priest becoming the icon's first historian;.
Hieromartyr Hermogenes, Patriarch of Mos.patron: Invoked for patriarchs; defenders of the nation's soul.
Hieromartyr Hermogenes, Patriarch of Mos.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Irenarchus, Abbot of Solovki.life: Saint Irenarchus received the monastic tonsure at the Solovki monastery in the far north of Russia, where he zealously imitated the founders of that holy place, Saints Zosimus and Sabbatius, in their ascetic labors. In the year 1614, upon the death of the abbot Anthony, he was chosen to succeed him as igumen, and he governed the community faithfully in a difficult age, when the Solovki monastery stood as a bulwark for the defense of the northern lands against the Swedes and the Danes.
Venerable Irenarchus, Abbot of Solovki.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saints Xanthippi and Polyxeni of Spain.life: Saints Xanthippe and Polyxene were sisters of Spain, disciples of the apostles, who reposed in peace in the year 109. Xanthippe, the wife of Probus, a man of high standing, received the faith of Christ through the preaching of the Holy Apostle Paul when the Gospel first reached the far west, and with her husband served the Lord in holiness.
Saints Xanthippi and Polyxeni of Spain.patron: Invoked for women disciples; chastity preserved.
Saints Xanthippi and Polyxeni of Spain.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Apostle Ananias of the Seventy.life: The Holy Apostle Ananias of the Seventy was a disciple of the Lord dwelling at Damascus, to whom the Lord appeared in a vision, bidding him go to the street called Straight and lay hands upon Saul of Tarsus, the persecutor of the Church, who was praying there blind.
Apostle Ananias of the Seventy.patron: Invoked for the healing of blindness; obedience to God's call.
Apostle Ananias of the Seventy.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Meletius, Archbishop of Khar'kov a.life: Saint Meletius, Archbishop of Kharkov and Akhtyrsk, born Leontovich in the Poltava lands, was one of the hidden ascetics whom the synodal Church of the nineteenth century raised, almost despite itself, to her thrones. Brilliant in the schools, he taught and governed in the theological academies, rector and formator of a generation of clergy, and passed through the episcopate of several sees before coming in 1835 to Kharkov;.
Saint Meletius, Archbishop of Khar'kov a.patron: Invoked for hierarchs of the night vigil; ascetics in office.
Saint Meletius, Archbishop of Khar'kov a.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Autonomus, Bishop in Italy.life: The Hieromartyr Autonomus was a bishop in Italy in the days of Diocletian's persecution, and withdrawing before the storm, he came to Soreoi in Bithynia, where he was received by a pious man named Cornelius and, far from resting in safety, gave himself to tireless preaching, converting so great a multitude of pagans that he ordained Cornelius deacon and later bishop for the flock he had gathered.
Hieromartyr Autonomus, Bishop in Italy.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Dositheus, Abbot of Verkneostr.life: Saint Dositheus of Verkneostrov was a disciple of the great elder Euphrosynus of Pskov, under whose guidance he was formed in the strict traditions of the Pskov wilderness, in obedience, fasting, and unceasing prayer. Seeking a place of stillness, he settled on the Upper Island, Verkhny Ostrov, among the islands of Lake Pskov, where the waters shielded his solitude;.
Venerable Dositheus, Abbot of Verkneostr.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Anastasius the Fuller at Salona i.life: The Holy Martyr Anastasius the Fuller was born at Aquileia in Italy and practiced the fuller's trade at Salona in Dalmatia, in the days of Diocletian's persecution. Refusing to hide the faith for which others were dying, he painted the Cross of Christ openly upon the door of his workshop, that all who passed might know whose servant labored within;.
Martyr Anastasius the Fuller at Salona i.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Sebastian, Abbot of Pshekhonye.life: Saint Sebastian of Poshekhonye labored in the northern forests of Russia at the turn of the sixteenth century, and founded on the river Sokhot, in the Poshekhonye country toward Vologda, a hermitage of the Transfiguration of the Lord, gathering about himself a brotherhood formed on the strict common life: nothing owned, everything shared, and every mouth fed by the labor of its own hands.
Venerable Sebastian, Abbot of Pshekhonye.patron: Invoked for weavers; monastics who labor with their hands.
Venerable Sebastian, Abbot of Pshekhonye.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Silvanus of Gaza.life: The Holy Hieromartyr Silvanus of Gaza was a native of that city, first a soldier and afterward a priest, and in his old age he was raised to the episcopate, shepherding the Church of Gaza in the years of the great persecution. Falsely accused and condemned, he was sentenced to penal labor in the copper mines of Phaeno, where, aged and worn, he bore the crushing toil with unbroken faith, strengthening the many confessors condemned with him and never ceasing to instruct and console them as a true father.
Hieromartyr Silvanus of Gaza.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Arethas and 4,299 Martyrs with hi.life: The Holy Martyr Arethas and with him four thousand two hundred and ninety-nine martyrs suffered in the year 523 in the city of Najran in Arabia, where the Christian faith had taken deep root. Dunaan, ruler of the Himyarites, a persecutor of the Church, besieged the Christian city, and unable to take it by force, swore falsely that he would harm no one, and being admitted, gave the faithful the choice of denying Christ or death.
Martyr Arethas and 4,299 Martyrs with hi.patron: Invoked for Christians under persecution; whole cities faithful unto death.
Martyr Arethas and 4,299 Martyrs with hi.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Theodora the Empress.life: Saint Theodora the Empress, the wife of Saint Justinian, is honored by the Church as a penitent whom grace raised from the depths to the throne. In her youth an actress of the theaters and a woman of notorious life, and for a time inclined toward the error of the Monophysites, she repented with her whole heart;.
Saint Theodora the Empress.patron: Invoked for repentance; the protection of fallen women.
Saint Theodora the Empress.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Glorification of Saint Innocent, Metropo.life: On this day the Church commemorates the glorification of Saint Innocent, Metropolitan of Moscow, Enlightener of the Aleuts and Apostle to the Americas, numbered among the saints by the Russian Orthodox Church on the sixth of October 1977, at the petition of the Orthodox Church in America. Born John Popov-Veniaminov in 1797 in a Siberian village on the.
Glorification of Saint Innocent, Metropo.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Akepsimas and Aithalas of Egypt.life: The Holy Martyrs Acepsius and Aithalas suffered at Arbela in the land of Persia, in the persecutions that the Persian kings raised against the Church, when the magi pressed the Christians of the empire to worship the sun and the fire and sealed their refusals with blood. The tradition of that suffering Church relates that Aithalas had himself been a priest of the idols at Arbela before the grace of Christ found him, so that the persecutors lost to the Gospel one of their own altar-servers, a wound they never forgave;.
Martyrs Akepsimas and Aithalas of Egypt.patron: Invoked for the Church under Persia; priests of the idols converted.
Martyrs Akepsimas and Aithalas of Egypt.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Finding of the relics of Monastic Martyr.life: On this day the Church commemorates the uncovering of the relics of the Monastic Martyr Adrian of Poshekhonsk, which took place on the nineteenth of November 1625. Saint Adrian, a monk and gifted iconographer formed in the tradition of the great northern monasteries, had founded with a fellow ascetic a monastery of the Dormition of the Most Holy Theotokos in the forests of Poshekhonye in the Yaroslavl lands, laboring there in fasting, prayer, and the painting of holy icons, and gathering a brotherhood around the wilderness church.
Finding of the relics of Monastic Martyr.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Gurias, Archbishop of Kazan.life: Saint Gurias, first Archbishop of Kazan, in the world Gregory Rugotin, was born at Radonezh to a poor family of courtiers, and served in his youth as steward of the estates of Prince Ivan Penkov; and there the envy of men forged his sanctity, for he was slandered as an adulterer with the prince's wife, and the prince, believing the lie, cast him into an underground cell, where for two years the innocent man sat in darkness on straw, with oats and water flung down to him.
Saint Gurias, Archbishop of Kazan.patron: Invoked for prisoners; teachers of children.
Saint Gurias, Archbishop of Kazan.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

First Translation of the relics of Saint.life: Saint Herman, Archbishop of Kazan, was born at Staritsa of the noble Sadyrev-Polev family, and receiving the tonsure at the Volokolamsk monastery, he was formed in the school of Saint Joseph, becoming known for his learning, his ascetic life, and his labor of copying books. When the newly conquered lands of Kazan were opened to the Gospel, he was sent with Saint Gurias for their enlightenment, and founded at Sviyazhsk the monastery of the Dormition of the Mother of God, which became the center of the mission to the peoples of the Volga;.
First Translation of the relics of Saint.patron: Invoked for missionaries; the enlightenment of the Kazan lands.
First Translation of the relics of Saint.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Longinus the Gatekeeper of the.life: Saint Longinus the Gatekeeper of the Kyiv Caves fulfilled his monastic obedience at the gates of the great Lavra, and his fervent prayer and humble love of labor were rewarded by the Lord with the gift of discernment, so that the doorkeeper of the monastery became a doorkeeper of souls.
Venerable Longinus the Gatekeeper of the.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyrs John the Bishop and Jacob (.life: The Hieromartyrs John the Bishop and James the Presbyter, called the Zealot, suffered in Persia in the reign of King Shapur the Second, the great persecutor of the Church beyond the eastern border of the empire. Preaching the true faith with boldness, they drew many devout souls to Christ, and the growth of the Church through their labors brought them before the king;.
Hieromartyrs John the Bishop and Jacob (.patron: Invoked for the Church under Persian persecution.
Hieromartyrs John the Bishop and Jacob (.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Leavetaking of the Nativity of the Mothe.life: This is the Leavetaking of the Feast of the Nativity of the Most Holy Theotokos, the final day of the festal period in which the Church celebrates the birth of the Mother of God. On this day the hymns and readings of the feast are sung once more in their fullness, and the faithful take their leave of the festival, having been filled with its joy;.
Leavetaking of the Nativity of the Mothe.patron: Commemorated in the holy calendar of the Church.
Leavetaking of the Nativity of the Mothe.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Uncovering of the relics of Saint Vsévol.life: On this day the Church commemorates the uncovering of the relics of the Holy Prince Vsevolod of Pskov, named Gabriel in holy baptism, which took place in the year 1192. Grandson of Vladimir Monomakh and son of Saint Mstislav the Great, Vsevolod ruled Novgorod from his youth with justice and open hands, building churches, feeding the poor in famine at his own cost, and leading the city's hosts;.
Uncovering of the relics of Saint Vsévol.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Arethus the Recluse of the Kyi.life: Saint Arethas the Recluse of the Kyiv Caves had been rich in the world, and even in the monastery the passion of avarice held him, for he kept a hidden treasure in his cell, giving nothing to the poor and grudging even himself. When thieves stole his hoard, Arethas fell into such grief that he murmured against God and accused the innocent, and coming near to death in his affliction, he lay as one already judged.
Venerable Arethus the Recluse of the Kyi.patron: Invoked for deliverance from the love of money; thanksgiving in loss.
Venerable Arethus the Recluse of the Kyi.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Aidan, Bishop of Lindesfarne.life: Saint Aidan, enlightener of Northumbria, was born in Ireland and became a monk on the island of Iona, in the monastery founded by Saint Columba, where he was known for his strict asceticism and gentleness. When Oswald, the Christian king of Northumbria, asked for a bishop to bring the Gospel to his still-pagan people, Aidan was sent, and he established his episcopal see upon the island of Lindisfarne, near the royal stronghold, choosing a place of quiet apart from the world.
Saint Aidan, Bishop of Lindesfarne.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Synaxis of the Hierarchs of Kazan.life: On this day the Church keeps the Synaxis of the Hierarchs of Kazan, honoring together the holy bishops who planted and watered the Church in the lands of the Volga after the fall of the khanate: Saint Gurias, the first Archbishop of Kazan, apostle of the newly won region;.
Synaxis of the Hierarchs of Kazan.patron: Invoked for the enlightenment of the Kazan lands.
Synaxis of the Hierarchs of Kazan.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Sophia and her three daughters at.life: The Holy Martyr Sophia and her three young daughters, Faith, Hope, and Love, suffered at Rome about the year 137, in the reign of the emperor Hadrian. Sophia, whose name means Wisdom, was a Christian widow who had named her daughters for the three great virtues and raised them in fervent love for Christ;.
Martyr Sophia and her three daughters at.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Virgin Martyr Julia of Carthage.life: Saint Julia was a noble and devout maiden of Carthage in North Africa who, when the city fell to its enemies, was carried off and sold into slavery. Serving her master faithfully and humbly, she gave all her free hours to prayer and fasting, and she would not be parted from her faith in Christ.
Virgin Martyr Julia of Carthage.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint John [Maximovitch], Archbishop of.life: Saint John, Archbishop of Shanghai and San Francisco, one of the great wonderworkers of the twentieth century, was born Michael Maximovitch in 1896 in the Kharkiv region to a pious noble family. Fleeing the Bolshevik revolution, he studied theology at Belgrade and was tonsured a monk in 1926, taking the name John, and in 1934 he was consecrated bishop and sent to Shanghai.
Saint John [Maximovitch], Archbishop of.patron: Invoked for refugees and émigrés; the sick.
Saint John [Maximovitch], Archbishop of.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Frumentius, Archbishop of Abyssini.life: Saint Frumentius, Archbishop of Abyssinia and Enlightener of Ethiopia, was born at Tyre; and as a boy, sailing the Red Sea with his kinsman Aedesius in the company of a scholar, he was cast by God's providence into the strangest of missions, for when the ship touched the African coast, the crew was slain, and only the two boys were spared and carried to the royal court of Aksum.
Saint Frumentius, Archbishop of Abyssini.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Passion-Bearer Gleb (in Baptism David).life: The Holy Passion-Bearer Gleb, named David in holy baptism, was among the first saints glorified in the land of Rus, suffering in the year 1015 together with his brother Boris at the hands of their brother Svyatopolk the Accursed. When their father, Great Prince Vladimir, had died, Svyatopolk, having already murdered Boris, sent word to the young Gleb that his father was ill and summoned him to Kyiv, using deceit to draw another rightful heir to his death.
Passion-Bearer Gleb (in Baptism David).patron: Invoked for innocent sufferers; peace among kindred.
Passion-Bearer Gleb (in Baptism David).src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Holy and Righteous Ancestors of God, Joa.life: On the day after the Nativity of the Theotokos the Church keeps the Synaxis of the Holy and Righteous Ancestors of God, Joachim and Anna, gathering to honor those through whom the Mother of God was given to the world. Joachim was of the royal line of David and Anna of the priestly lineage of Aaron, and they lived in righteousness, giving a third of their income to God and a third to the poor;.
Holy and Righteous Ancestors of God, Joa.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous James the Brother of the Lord.life: The Holy Righteous James, the Brother of the Lord, is commemorated in the days after the Nativity together with Joseph the Betrothed his father and David the King, in the synaxis of the Lord's kinsmen according to the flesh; his full commemoration as apostle, first bishop of Jerusalem, and martyr the Church keeps in October, and here she remembers him precisely as family.
Righteous James the Brother of the Lord.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Nicholas Sviatosha Prince of C.life: Saint Nicholas Sviatosha, Prince of Chernihiv and wonderworker of the Kyiv Caves, was a great-grandson of Yaroslav the Wise and son of Prince David of Chernihiv, and ruled as prince of Lutsk, having a wife and children. On the seventeenth of February 1106, leaving family and principality, he was tonsured at the Kyiv Caves monastery, the first of the princes of Rus to exchange the crown for the cowl;.
Venerable Nicholas Sviatosha Prince of C.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Eustratius, Auxentius, Eugene, M.life: The Holy Martyrs Eustratius, Auxentius, Eugene, Mardarius, and Orestes, the Five Companions, shone like five stars over Armenia in the persecution of Diocletian and Maximian, about the year 296, and their contest is a chain of free confessions, each man stepping forward unforced. Auxentius, a priest of Arauraka, was seized first by the governors Lysias and Agricolaus;.
Martyrs Eustratius, Auxentius, Eugene, M.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Job of Ushchelsk.life: Saint Job, called the Gorge-dweller, was a monk of the Solovki Monastery who in the year 1608 was ordained hieromonk by Metropolitan Isidore of Novgorod. In 1614 he was sent to the far northern region of the Mezen, and there, at a place called Ushchelye where the river Ezega meets the Mezen, he founded a hermitage and raised a church, gathering about him a small brotherhood in that remote wilderness.
Venerable Job of Ushchelsk.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Forefeast of the Nativity of our Lord.life: The Forefeast of the Nativity of our Lord embraces the days from the twentieth of December to the vigil of the feast, and in them the Church, like Bethlehem in the hymns, makes ready. The services turn wholly toward the cave: at each day's stichera the summons rings out, Bethlehem, prepare;.
Forefeast of the Nativity of our Lord.patron: Commemorated in the holy calendar of the Church.
Forefeast of the Nativity of our Lord.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Pamphilius the Presbyter, Valens.life: The Holy Martyrs Pamphilius the Presbyter, Valens the Deacon, Paul, Porphyrius, Seleucus, Theodulus, Julian, and the five Egyptian youths Elias, Jeremiah, Isaiah, Samuel, and Daniel suffered at Caesarea in Palestine about the year 309, in the seventh year of the great persecution, and their contest was recorded by an eyewitness who loved them, Eusebius the historian, who called their company a perfect image of a whole congregation of the Church.
Martyrs Pamphilius the Presbyter, Valens.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Repose of Venerable Cornelius of Pereyas.life: Saint Cornelius of Pereyaslavl, named Konon in the world, was the son of a merchant of Ryazan. In his youth he left his parental home and served for five years as a novice under the elder Paul in the Lukianov wilderness, afterward transferring to the Pereyaslavl monastery of Saints Boris and Gleb on the Sands.
Repose of Venerable Cornelius of Pereyas.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Paul and Juliana of Syria.life: The Holy Martyrs Paul and his sister Juliana suffered for Christ in the reign of the emperor Aurelian, in the Phoenician city of Ptolemais. When the emperor came to that city, Paul, meeting him among the crowd, made the Sign of the Cross, and for this he was seized and cast into prison, and on the next day, brought to trial, he confessed his faith in Christ openly and without fear, for which he was cruelly tortured.
Martyrs Paul and Juliana of Syria.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Timothy, Agapius, and Thekla, of.life: The Holy Martyrs Timothy, Agapius, and Thecla suffered for Christ in the year 304, in the persecution under Diocletian. Saint Timothy was a native of Caesarea in Palestine, who had studied the holy Scriptures and, being gifted with eloquence, became a teacher of the Christian faith. Arrested and commanded to deny Christ and sacrifice to the idols, he refused with firmness, and after enduring cruel torments he was burned alive, giving up his soul to God.
Martyrs Timothy, Agapius, and Thekla, of.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Sabbatius, Wonderworker of Sol.life: Saint Sabbatius, wonderworker of Solovki, was a monk of Valaam on Lake Ladoga, where his humility and severity of life drew such veneration from the brethren that the saint, fleeing the praise of men, sought a wilderness where no one might know him. Hearing of the uninhabited island of Solovki in the White Sea, two days' sail from.
Venerable Sabbatius, Wonderworker of Sol.patron: Invoked for monastics; the uttermost solitude.
Venerable Sabbatius, Wonderworker of Sol.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Theodota, mother of the Unmercenar.life: Saint Theodota, the mother of the Holy Unmercenaries Cosmas and Damian of Asia, was a Christian woman of Asia Minor whose pagan husband died while her children were still small, leaving her to raise them alone. She brought up her sons in Christian piety, teaching them by her own example and by reading to them from the holy.
Saint Theodota, mother of the Unmercenar.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Euthymius the New of Thessalon.life: Saint Euthymius the New of Thessalonica was born in 824 in the village of Opso in Galatia and named Nicetas; married in his youth in obedience to his mother and given a daughter, he departed after her birth, having provided for his household, and received the monastic tonsure with the name Euthymius on the mount of Olympus in Bithynia, where he was formed for many years in obedience and stillness.
Venerable Euthymius the New of Thessalon.patron: Invoked for monastics; the pioneering of Athos.
Venerable Euthymius the New of Thessalon.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Right-believing Princess Juliana of Vyaz.life: The Right-believing Princess Juliana of Vyazma, chaste passion-bearer, was the wife of Prince Simeon Mstislavich of Vyazma, and shared his exile when Smolensk and Vyazma fell to Lithuania and the dispossessed princes took refuge at Torzhok in the service of Prince Yuri of Smolensk. There her beauty became her cross: Yuri, inflamed with passion for the wife of his own faithful companion, and finding her virtue immovable, resolved on force, and at a feast in the winter of 1406 he cut down Prince Simeon at the table, thinking to seize the widow with the husband;.
Right-believing Princess Juliana of Vyaz.patron: Invoked for wives; women in danger.
Right-believing Princess Juliana of Vyaz.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Phocas, Bishop of Sinope.life: The Hieromartyr Phocas, Bishop of Sinope on the Black Sea, led a virtuous life from his youth and as bishop of his native city converted many pagans to faith in Christ. In the persecution under the emperor Trajan the governor demanded that he renounce the Lord, and when the saint refused, he was subjected to fierce tortures and at last shut into a heated bath, where he received the crown of martyrdom in the year 117.
Hieromartyr Phocas, Bishop of Sinope.patron: Invoked for sailors; protection from fire.
Hieromartyr Phocas, Bishop of Sinope.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

The Entry of the Most Holy Mother of God.life: The Entry into the Temple celebrates the presentation of the child Mary in the Temple at Jerusalem by her parents Joachim and Anna when she was three years old, in fulfillment of the vow they had made to dedicate her to God. According to the tradition of the Church, she was received by the priest Zacharias and, by.
The Entry of the Most Holy Mother of God.patron: Commemorated in the holy calendar of the Church.
The Entry of the Most Holy Mother of God.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Philemon, Apollonios, Arrian, an.life: The Holy Martyrs Philemon, Apollonius, Arrianus, and Theonas suffered in Egypt about the year 286, and their story is a relay of grace in which each runner hands the crown to the next. Apollonius, a reader of the church of Antinoe, fearing the tortures, hired the pagan Philemon, a flute player famous through all Egypt, to veil himself in his clothes and offer the sacrifice in his name;.
Martyrs Philemon, Apollonios, Arrian, an.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Kazan Icons of the Mother of God in Kaza.life: This feast commemorates the appearance of the Kazan Icon of the Mother of God, which was miraculously revealed in the city of Kazan in the year 1579, when the Theotokos directed a young girl in a vision to the place where the icon lay hidden in the ashes of a burned house.
Kazan Icons of the Mother of God in Kaza.patron: Invoked for protection of Russia; marriage and families.
Kazan Icons of the Mother of God in Kaza.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Paul the New, Patriarch of Constan.life: Saint Paul, called the New, was a Cypriot by birth who became Patriarch of Constantinople during the reign of the iconoclast emperors, a virtuous and pious man but timid of heart. Seeing the sufferings that the Orthodox endured for the sake of the holy icons, he at first hid his own belief and went along with the iconoclasts, but his conscience gave him no peace;.
Saint Paul the New, Patriarch of Constan.patron: Invoked for repentance; the veneration of icons.
Saint Paul the New, Patriarch of Constan.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Finding of the relics of Righteous Saint.life: Saint Nicodemus was a Pharisee and a ruler of the Jews who came to the Lord Jesus by night, as the Gospel of John relates, and heard from Him of the new birth by water and the Spirit. Though at first he came in secret for fear of the Jews, he defended the Savior before the council, and after the crucifixion he came openly with Joseph of Arimathea, bringing a mixture of myrrh and aloes, and helped to anoint and bury the body of the Lord.
Finding of the relics of Righteous Saint.patron: Invoked for secret disciples; seekers of truth.
Finding of the relics of Righteous Saint.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Romanus the Melodist, “Sweet-S.life: Saint Romanus the Melodist, the sweet-singer of the Church, was born at Emesa in Syria and served as deacon first at Beirut and then at Constantinople in the days of the emperor Anastasius, attending the church of the Theotokos at Kyros and keeping vigil by night at Blachernae.
Venerable Romanus the Melodist, “Sweet-S.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

20,000 Martyrs of Nicomedia.life: The Holy 20,000 Martyrs of Nicomedia suffered in the year 302, when the emperor Maximian, learning how mightily the faith had grown in his own capital, resolved to destroy the Christians of the city in a single night, and chose for it the night on which they would all be gathered: the feast of the Nativity of Christ.
20,000 Martyrs of Nicomedia.patron: Invoked for congregations under threat; catechumens.
20,000 Martyrs of Nicomedia.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Holy Martyr and Confessor Michael and hi.life: The Holy Martyr and Confessor Michael, Prince of Chernihiv, and his faithful counselor the boyar Theodore suffered at the Golden Horde in the year 1246. Prince Michael, noted from childhood for piety and gentleness, had ruled in Novgorod and Kyiv in the years of the Mongol storm; and when he was summoned to the Horde to receive from Batu the right to his principality, the pagans demanded that he first pass between the fires and bow to their idols, as their custom was.
Holy Martyr and Confessor Michael and hi.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Anthousa the Confessor.life: Saint Anthousa the Confessor lived in the eighth century at Mantinea in Paphlagonia, in the age of the iconoclast emperor Constantine Copronymos, and she was raised in piety by her devout parents, Strategios and Febronia. Embracing the monastic life, she became abbess of a community of nuns, and when the emperor waged war against the holy icons, she stood firm as a confessor of the faith, refusing to forsake their veneration and enduring suffering for the sake of the sacred images.
Venerable Anthousa the Confessor.patron: Invoked for nuns; the veneration of icons.
Venerable Anthousa the Confessor.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Eudocimus of Cappadocia.life: Saint Eudocimus, a native of Cappadocia, lived in the ninth century in the reign of the emperor Theophilus, and was the son of pious and illustrious parents, Basil and Eudokia, who raised him in the discipline and admonition of the Lord. True to his name, which signifies one of good repute, he was successful in every virtue, devoting his life to pleasing God and serving his neighbor.
Righteous Eudocimus of Cappadocia.patron: Invoked for the family hearth; orphans and widows.
Righteous Eudocimus of Cappadocia.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Lucian the Presbyter of Antioch.life: The Holy Martyr Lucian, presbyter of Antioch, was born at Samosata and, orphaned young, gave his inheritance to the poor and himself to sacred learning, becoming presbyter at Antioch and the master of its famous school of the Scriptures, where he labored at the correction of the Greek text of the Old Testament against the corruptions that had crept in, and formed many disciples in the exact study of the word of God.
Martyr Lucian the Presbyter of Antioch.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Dositheus of Palestine, discip.life: Venerable Dositheus of Palestine is the Church's proof that obedience alone can sanctify, preserved by his elder Dorotheos of Gaza as the first and dearest exhibit of his teaching. A page in the household of a general, young, pampered, and so ignorant of God that he had never heard the faith preached, Dositheus visited Jerusalem with the household and stood before an icon of the dread Judgment in Gethsemane;.
Venerable Dositheus of Palestine, discip.patron: Invoked for novices; the sick who cannot fast.
Venerable Dositheus of Palestine, discip.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Paisios the Athonite (1994).life: Saint Paisios of the Holy Mountain, one of the most beloved elders of the twentieth century, was born Arsenios Eznepidis in 1924 at Pharasa in Cappadocia, and was baptized by Saint Arsenios of Cappadocia, who foretold that the child would become a monk. Brought to Greece as an infant in the exchange of populations, he grew up in Konitsa, worked as a carpenter, and served as a radio operator in the army during the civil war, showing courage and self-sacrifice.
Venerable Paisios the Athonite (1994).patron: Invoked for monastics; those in distress.
Venerable Paisios the Athonite (1994).src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Polycarp of Briansk.life: Venerable Polycarp of Briansk labored at the turn of the seventeenth century, in the years when the Time of Troubles was breaking over the Russian land, and his sanctity took the form the age most needed, the rebuilding of a house of God amid the general ruin. The tradition of Briansk holds that he was a man of.
Venerable Polycarp of Briansk.patron: Invoked for penitents of rank; restorers of monasteries.
Venerable Polycarp of Briansk.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Christodoulos.life: The Holy Martyr Christodoulos is commemorated on this day among the witnesses of the early Church, and his name is his biography: Christodoulos, the slave of Christ, the title that the martyrs of the first centuries claimed before tribunals as their entire legal identity, sweeping away family, city, and station in the one allegiance that the empire could neither tax nor command.
Martyr Christodoulos.patron: Invoked for all who bear Christ's name; the name confessed to the end.
Martyr Christodoulos.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

The Nativity of our Lord God and Savior.life: The Nativity celebrates the birth of the Son of God in the flesh, born of the Virgin Mary in a cave near Bethlehem and laid in a manger because there was no room in the inn. The Church proclaims this as the mystery of the Incarnation: the eternal Word, through whom all things were made, enters His own.
The Nativity of our Lord God and Savior.patron: Commemorated in the holy calendar of the Church.
The Nativity of our Lord God and Savior.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Kuksha and Venerable Pimen o.life: The Hieromartyr Kuksha was a monk of the Caves of Kyiv who went out to preach the Gospel to the Vyatichi, a fierce pagan people dwelling in the forests along the river Oka, who lived, as the chronicler said, only for the present day and knew nothing of the law of God.
Hieromartyr Kuksha and Venerable Pimen o.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Troadius of Neocaesarea.life: The Holy Martyr Troadius of Neocaesarea suffered in the persecution of Decius, about the year 250, a young man of that Pontic city whose contest is famous less for its own record than for its audience, since the Church knows of Troadius chiefly through the eyes of a saint who watched him from miles away.
Martyr Troadius of Neocaesarea.patron: Invoked for the young in trial; those upheld by unseen prayer.
Martyr Troadius of Neocaesarea.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Maximus, Theodotus, Hesychius, a.life: The Holy Martyrs Maximus, Theodotus, Hesychius, and Asclepiodota suffered in Thrace in the persecution of Maximian, about the year 305, three men of Adrianopolis and with them Asclepiodota, a woman of noble family whose courage set the tone of the company's whole contest. Denounced as Christians in the years when the imperial edicts were emptying the churches of.
Martyrs Maximus, Theodotus, Hesychius, a.patron: Invoked for companions in trial; noblewomen of courage.
Martyrs Maximus, Theodotus, Hesychius, a.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Titus the Soldier, of the Kyiv.life: Venerable Titus the Soldier of the Kyiv Caves came to God the way many warriors have, through a wound: a fighting man of the fourteenth century, he took in battle a blow to the head so grievous that it ended his soldiering, and the injury that closed his career opened his eternity, for Titus, carried to the threshold.
Venerable Titus the Soldier, of the Kyiv.patron: Invoked for soldiers turned monks; veterans.
Venerable Titus the Soldier, of the Kyiv.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Savva the Sanctified.life: Saint Savva the Sanctified, the lawgiver of Palestinian monasticism, was born in 439 at Mutalaska in Cappadocia, and entering a monastery at eight years of age, he showed as a child the will of an elder: having once plucked and eaten an apple against the rule, he vowed never to taste apples again, and kept the vow to his death, and once walked unharmed into a burning oven to retrieve garments, God bearing witness to the boy.
Venerable Savva the Sanctified.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

12 Greeks who built the Dormition Cathed.life: The Twelve Greeks who built the great Dormition cathedral of the Kyiv Caves are commemorated on this day, master builders of Constantinople whom the Mother of God herself hired for the greatest construction project of old Rus. The Paterikon of the Caves preserves their own sworn account: the Queen of Heaven appeared to them at the church of Blachernae in Constantinople, in the form of an empress attended by warriors, and commanded them to go to Rus, to Kyiv, and build there a church in her honor at the place that would be shown them;.
12 Greeks who built the Dormition Cathed.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Simeon Stylites, the Elder.life: Saint Simeon the Stylite, the first and most famous of those who struggled upon a pillar, was born of Christian parents in a village on the borders of Cilicia and Cappadocia, and as a boy he tended his father's sheep. Struck to the heart one day by the words of the Beatitudes, he sought out an elder to.
Saint Simeon Stylites, the Elder.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Apostle Philip of the Seventy, One of th.life: The Holy Apostle Philip of the Seventy, one of the Seven Deacons, was chosen with Stephen and the others by the apostles to serve the tables of the widows in the first Church of Jerusalem, being a man full of faith and of the Holy Spirit. When persecution scattered the Church, Philip went down to Samaria and preached Christ there with signs and wonders, so that the city received the word with great joy, and even Simon the sorcerer believed and was baptized;.
Apostle Philip of the Seventy, One of th.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

7 Holy Maccabee Martyrs.life: The seven holy Maccabee brothers, Abim, Antonius, Gurias, Eleazar, Eusebonus, Alimus, and Marcellus, suffered in the year 166 before Christ under the impious king Antiochus Epiphanes, who despised the faith of the Jews and strove to turn the people from the Law of Moses, desecrating the Temple and setting up in it an idol of Zeus for all to worship.
7 Holy Maccabee Martyrs.patron: Invoked for faithfulness to God's law; courage under torture.
7 Holy Maccabee Martyrs.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Great Martyr Euphemia the All-praised.life: The Holy Great Martyr Euphemia the All-Praised was the daughter of pious Christians of Chalcedon, and suffered in that city in the year 303, in the persecution under Diocletian. When the proconsul Priscus commanded all the inhabitants to take part in the festival of the idol Ares, Euphemia, with other Christians who had hidden themselves to worship the true God, was discovered and brought to trial;.
Great Martyr Euphemia the All-praised.patron: Invoked for purity; the vindication of Orthodoxy.
Great Martyr Euphemia the All-praised.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Translation of the relics of the Hieroma.life: This feast commemorates the translation of the relics of the Hieromartyr Phocas, Bishop of Sinope, from his own city to Constantinople in the year 403 or 404. Born at Sinope on the Black Sea, Phocas led a virtuous Christian life from his youth and in due time became bishop of that city, where by his preaching he converted many pagans to Christ.
Translation of the relics of the Hieroma.patron: Invoked for sailors; protection from fire.
Translation of the relics of the Hieroma.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable John of Damascus.life: Saint John of Damascus, the last of the great fathers of the ancient Church and the first singer of her completed theology, was born about 675 at Damascus, the son of a high Christian official at the court of the caliph; educated together with his adopted brother Cosmas by a learned monk ransomed from captivity, he mastered all the wisdom of the Greeks, and succeeded his father in office under the Saracen rule.
Venerable John of Damascus.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Palladius of Thessalonica.life: Venerable Palladius of Thessalonica labored in asceticism in that great and holy city of Macedonia, in the sixth or seventh century, in the age when Thessalonica, guarded by the Great Martyr Demetrius, was a fortress of Orthodoxy and a mother of monks. Renouncing the world, Palladius took up the whole warfare of the venerable ones: fasting that lightened the body, vigil that armed the mind, unceasing prayer that kept the heart, and the deep humility that crowns and guards them all;.
Venerable Palladius of Thessalonica.patron: Invoked for monastics; the hidden life.
Venerable Palladius of Thessalonica.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Stephen (in monasticism Simeon.life: Saint Simeon the Myrrh-gusher was born Stephen Nemanja, Great Zhupan of Serbia, the founder at once of a state, a dynasty, and a river of holiness. Ruling in the twelfth century, he toiled greatly for his fatherland, uniting the greater part of the Serbian lands and winning for his country its independence;.
Venerable Stephen (in monasticism Simeon.patron: Invoked for rulers who renounce; fathers of saints.
Venerable Stephen (in monasticism Simeon.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Serapion.life: The Holy Martyr Serapion suffered for Christ in the persecution under the emperor Severus. Brought before the governor Achilles and commanded to renounce his faith, he firmly proclaimed himself a Christian and confessed the true God before the pagans, and for this he was subjected to inhuman tortures and cast into prison.
Martyr Serapion.patron: Commemorated in the holy calendar of the Church.
Martyr Serapion.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Arkadios the Wonderworker, Bishop.life: Saint Arkadios the Wonderworker was born at Arsinoe on the island of Cyprus, the son of pious and wealthy parents named Michael and Anna, and lived from the end of the third century into the beginning of the fourth. Sent to be educated in Constantinople, he returned to his native Arsinoe, where he became renowned for his ascetic labors and the greatness of his virtues, so that when the bishop Nikon reposed, Arkadios was chosen to succeed him upon the episcopal throne.
Saint Arkadios the Wonderworker, Bishop.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Euphrosynē of Suzdal.life: Saint Euphrosyne of Suzdal was born the eldest daughter of the holy Prince Michael of Chernihiv, who later shed his blood for Christ at the Horde, and in baptism she was named Theodulia. Raised in piety and learning beyond her years, she was betrothed to a prince; but when her bridegroom died on the very eve of the marriage, she beheld the providence of God in her sorrow and remained in the convent of the Deposition of the Robe at Suzdal, where she received the tonsure with the name Euphrosyne.
Venerable Euphrosynē of Suzdal.patron: Invoked for nuns; teachers of women.
Venerable Euphrosynē of Suzdal.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Repose of Saint Arsenius, Archbishop of.life: Saint Arsenius, Archbishop of Serbia, was born in Srem and became a monk at the Zhicha monastery under the guidance of Saint Sava, the first archbishop of the Serbs, who for the strictness of his life made him igumen of that royal monastery. When Hungarian armies threatened the land, Sava sent Arsenius south to find a safer seat for the Church;.
Repose of Saint Arsenius, Archbishop of.patron: Invoked for hierarchs; the Serbian Church.
Repose of Saint Arsenius, Archbishop of.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

“Kozel'shchansk” Icon of the Mother of G.type: Icon of the Mother of God · 19th c.
“Kozel'shchansk” Icon of the Mother of G.life: The Kozelshchansk Icon of the Mother of God, one of the last of the great wonderworking icons to be revealed before the Russian catastrophe, was the family icon of the Counts Kapnist at their estate of Kozelshchyna in the Poltava country, an image of Italian style long in the household, showing the Mother of God with the Child, and beside them a cup with a spoon, whence the sick have always read in it a promise of medicine from heaven;.
“Kozel'shchansk” Icon of the Mother of G.patron: Invoked for the paralyzed; girls and young women.
“Kozel'shchansk” Icon of the Mother of G.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Agapitos the Confessor and Wonderw.life: Saint Agapitos the Confessor and Wonderworker, Bishop of Synnada, was a Cappadocian who entered the monastic life in his youth, laboring in a Phrygian brotherhood where his fasting, obedience, and prayer were crowned early with the gift of wonders, the young monk healing the sick who were brought to the gates;.
Saint Agapitos the Confessor and Wonderw.patron: Invoked for conscripts; soldiers of faith.
Saint Agapitos the Confessor and Wonderw.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Finding of the relics of Saint Abibas.life: Saint Abibas was the son of the righteous Gamaliel, the teacher of Saint Paul, and together with his father he received holy baptism at the hands of the apostles, embracing the faith of Christ. Living in purity, he reposed while still young and was buried by his father in the cave at Caphargamala, where the Protomartyr Stephen and Saint Nicodemus already lay.
Finding of the relics of Saint Abibas.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Hilarion of Tvali.life: Saint Hilarion of Tvali, called Tulashvili, served as abbot of the Khakhuli Monastery in southwestern Georgia at the beginning of the eleventh century. He was renowned for his virtue, his ascetic labors, and his preaching, and he was an eminent theologian, writer, and translator in an age when Georgian monasticism flourished.
Saint Hilarion of Tvali.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Charitina, Princess of Lithuania.life: Saint Charitina, Princess of Lithuania, left her native land in the troubled times of the thirteenth century and found refuge at Novgorod, where, resolving to give her life wholly to the Lord, she received the monastic tonsure in the women's monastery of the holy apostles Peter and Paul on Sinich hill.
Saint Charitina, Princess of Lithuania.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Carpus, Papylus, Agathadorus, an.life: The Holy Martyrs Carpus, Papylus, Agathadorus, and Agathonica suffered at Pergamum in the persecution under Decius, in the year 251. Carpus was bishop of Thyateira and Papylus his deacon, a man who had given his wealth to the poor; and when the governor of the region learned that they did not keep the pagan festivals, he had them brought to trial, and finding them unshakable in the confession of Christ, subjected them to torments: they were dragged behind horses, torn, and given to the beasts, which would not harm them.
Martyrs Carpus, Papylus, Agathadorus, an.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Agathonicus of Nicomedia, and tho.life: The Holy Martyr Agathonicus, together with Zoticus, Theoprepius, Acindynus, Severian, Zeno, and others, suffered for Christ in the persecution under Maximian. Agathonicus was of a noble family and dwelt at Nicomedia, and being well versed in the holy Scriptures he turned many from idolatry to Christ, among them the leading member of the Senate.
Martyr Agathonicus of Nicomedia, and tho.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Uncovering of the relics Saint Acacius,.life: Saint Acacius the Confessor was Bishop of Melitene in Armenia in the days of the persecution under Decius. Arrested as a Christian and brought before the governor Marcianus, he boldly confessed Christ and refuted the folly of idolatry, for which he was subjected to torture; yet he was not put to death, but after a time was set at liberty, bearing upon his body the wounds of Christ, and he governed his flock thereafter as a living martyr, reposing at last in peace.
Uncovering of the relics Saint Acacius,.patron: Invoked for confessors; endurance under torture.
Uncovering of the relics Saint Acacius,.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Sergius and Bacchus in Syria.life: The Holy Martyrs Sergius and Bacchus were noble Romans, officers of high rank in the household troops of the emperor Maximian, who held them in honor not knowing that they were Christians. When it was reported that they did not enter the temples with the court, the emperor commanded them to sacrifice;.
Martyrs Sergius and Bacchus in Syria.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Cyril, Bishop of Gortyna in.life: The Hieromartyr Cyril was bishop of Gortyna on the island of Crete, which he shepherded faithfully for fifty years, and he was an old man of great age when the persecution of the Christians reached his city. Seized and commanded to sacrifice to the idols, he refused, and was condemned to be burned alive;.
Hieromartyr Cyril, Bishop of Gortyna in.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Rusticus the Presbyter and Eleut.life: The Holy Martyrs Rusticus the Presbyter and Eleutherius the Deacon were the faithful companions of the Hieromartyr Dionysius the Areopagite in his apostolic labors in the West. Journeying with him from land to land, they shared his preaching, his dangers, and his bonds, converting many to Christ at Rome and beyond;.
Martyrs Rusticus the Presbyter and Eleut.patron: Invoked for faithful companionship in the Gospel.
Martyrs Rusticus the Presbyter and Eleut.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint John, Bishop of Polybotum.life: Saint John, Bishop of Polybotum in Phrygia, shepherded his flock in the eighth century, in the days when the emperor Leo the Isaurian raised his hand against the holy icons and demanded that the Church cast out the images of Christ, His Mother, and the saints. The bishop of the small Phrygian city answered the master of the.
Saint John, Bishop of Polybotum.patron: Invoked for the veneration of the holy icons; healing and deliverance.
Saint John, Bishop of Polybotum.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Gennadius, Patriarch of Constantin.life: Saint Gennadius ascended the patriarchal throne of Constantinople in the year 458, in the reign of the emperor Leo the Great, and governed the Church of the imperial city for thirteen years. He was distinguished for his mildness, his purity, and his abstinence, and was so careful of the dignity of the clergy that he would not ordain any who did not know the Psalter by heart;.
Saint Gennadius, Patriarch of Constantin.patron: Invoked for against simony; the peace of the Church.
Saint Gennadius, Patriarch of Constantin.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Theophanes the Faster of the K.life: Venerable Theophanes the Faster labored in the Near Caves of the Kyiv Lavra in the twelfth century, in the first great age of the monastery of Saints Anthony and Theodosius, and his title is his biography: he was a faster, one of those athletes of abstinence in whom the Caves tradition saw the surest road to purity of heart.
Venerable Theophanes the Faster of the K.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Prophet Daniel.life: The Holy Prophet Daniel, of the royal line of Judah, was carried to Babylon as a youth in the first deportation, about six hundred years before Christ, and there, in the furnace of exile, God forged the statesman-prophet of the captivity. Refusing with his three companions the defilement of the king's table, he was given wisdom beyond all.
Prophet Daniel.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Lupus, slave of Saint Demetrius o.life: The Holy Martyr Lupus lived at the turn of the fourth century and was the faithful servant of the Holy Great Martyr Demetrius of Thessalonica. Being present at the death of his master, he dipped his own garment in the martyr's blood and took the ring from his hand;.
Martyr Lupus, slave of Saint Demetrius o.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Nikon the Dry, of the Kyiv Nea.life: Venerable Nikon the Dry, of the Near Caves, was the son of a wealthy and honored family of Kyiv who had renounced it all for the Caves of Saint Anthony; and in the Polovtsian raids that ravaged the Lavra he was carried off captive into the steppe. His captor set a great ransom, knowing his family's wealth;.
Venerable Nikon the Dry, of the Kyiv Nea.patron: Invoked for captives; prisoners of war.
Venerable Nikon the Dry, of the Kyiv Nea.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Barlaam, Abbot of Khutyn, Novg.life: Saint Barlaam of Khutyn, one of the greatest of the saints of Novgorod, was born in that city to wealthy and pious parents and named Alexis; and when they reposed, he gave away his inheritance, received the monastic tonsure with the name Barlaam, and sought out for his dwelling the hill of Khutyn on the Volkhov, a place the people shunned as evil and haunted, which the ascetic chose precisely that the power of Christ might be shown where the enemy had reigned.
Venerable Barlaam, Abbot of Khutyn, Novg.patron: Invoked for monastics; the sanctification of evil places.
Venerable Barlaam, Abbot of Khutyn, Novg.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Eustathius, Archbishop of Antioch.life: Saint Eustathius, Archbishop of Antioch, was among the chief fathers of the First Ecumenical Council and the first of them to fall to the Arian counterattack, the protomartyr, in reputation if not in blood, of Nicaea's long defense. Born at Side in Pamphylia, bishop first of Beroea, he was raised to the great throne of Antioch on the.
Saint Eustathius, Archbishop of Antioch.patron: Invoked for the slandered; deposed hierarchs.
Saint Eustathius, Archbishop of Antioch.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Presbyters and Confessors Eugene and Mac.life: The Holy Presbyters and Confessors Eugene and Macarius suffered at Antioch under Julian the Apostate, the emperor who tried to rebuild paganism upon the ruins his uncle's house had made of it; and the two priests earned their title in the most direct way the Church records, by telling Julian the truth about himself to his face.
Presbyters and Confessors Eugene and Mac.patron: Invoked for priests in exile; those who rebuke power.
Presbyters and Confessors Eugene and Mac.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Tikhon, Bishop of Voronezh, Wonder.life: Saint Tikhon of Zadonsk, born Timothy in the year 1724 in the Novgorod region, was the son of a poor village cantor, and after his father's death the family knew such want that his mother almost gave him away to be raised by a coachman. Through the care of his brother he was able to study, and he rose to teach in the Novgorod seminary before being tonsured and, in time, consecrated bishop.
Saint Tikhon, Bishop of Voronezh, Wonder.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Euphrosyne of Alexandria.life: Saint Euphrosyne of Alexandria lived in the fifth century, the only and much-loved daughter of a wealthy and pious man named Paphnutius. Vowed in her heart to virginity, and unable to escape the marriage her father had arranged, she secretly received the monastic tonsure, and knowing that her father would seek her in every convent of women, she clothed herself as a man and entered a monastery of monks under the name of the eunuch Smaragdus.
Venerable Euphrosyne of Alexandria.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Emilian and with him Martyrs.life: The Hieromartyr Emilian, Bishop of Trebia, together with Hilarion, Dionysius, and Hermippus, was born in Armenia; and after the death of their parents the brothers Emilian, Dionysius, and Hermippus, with their teacher Hilarion, left their homeland and came to Italy, to the city of Spoleto. There Emilian preached the Gospel to the pagans, and being esteemed for his strict and virtuous life he was chosen Bishop of Trebia and consecrated by Marcellinus of Rome.
Hieromartyr Emilian and with him Martyrs.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Clement the Stylite who lived as a.life: Venerable Clement the Stylite lived as an ascetic on Mount Sagmata in Boeotia and reposed in the year 1111, one of the late and lonely heirs of the pillar saints, carrying into the twelfth century the most vertical of all the Church's vocations. Withdrawing from the world to the summit of Sagmata, the mountain that stands over the Boeotian plain within sight of ancient Thebes, Clement mounted a narrow pillar and made its capital his cell, his church, and his tomb-in-waiting, exposed alone to the sun, the wind, and the winters of the height;.
Saint Clement the Stylite who lived as a.patron: Invoked for stylites; solitaries of the mountains.
Saint Clement the Stylite who lived as a.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Apostle Silas of the Seventy.life: The Holy Apostle Silas, one of the Seventy, was a respected member of the first Church in Jerusalem and reckoned among the chief men of the brethren. When the Apostolic Council met at Jerusalem to decide that Gentile converts need not keep the Mosaic Law, Silas was chosen, being full of the grace of the Holy Spirit, to carry and explain its decree to the faithful at Antioch.
Apostle Silas of the Seventy.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint James the Wonderworker, Bishop of.life: Saint James, Bishop of Rostov, shepherded that ancient see in the fourteenth century, a defender of the faith who refuted the heretic Markian, troubler of the Rostov church, and a father to his flock; and his sanctity was revealed through an act of mercy that cost him everything.
Saint James the Wonderworker, Bishop of.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

10 Holy Martyrs of Crete.life: The Ten Holy Martyrs of Crete, Theodulus, Saturninus, Euporus, Gelasius, Eunician, Zoticus, Pompius, Agathopus, Basilides, and Evaristus, suffered in the year 250 under the emperor Decius, whose governor on the island, a Decius likewise in name and in cruelty, set himself to root the faith out of Crete.
10 Holy Martyrs of Crete.patron: Invoked for joy in the face of death; the crown contested in love.
10 Holy Martyrs of Crete.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Boniface at Tarsus in Cilicia, an.life: The Holy Martyr Boniface was the steward of Aglaida, a wealthy young Roman woman, and the two lived in sin together, though Boniface was merciful to the poor and hospitable to strangers, a kind heart drowning in drink and dissipation. Wishing to have holy relics as a guard for her soul, Aglaida sent her steward to the East, where the persecution raged, to buy the bodies of martyrs;.
Martyr Boniface at Tarsus in Cilicia, an.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable John, Ascetic of the Syrian De.life: Venerable John, ascetic of the Syrian deserts, is commemorated on this day with the company of the open-air hermits of Syria whose exploits Theodoret of Cyrrhus, their neighbor and bishop, set down for the Church; and among that regiment of the exposed, John held his station on a bare height for some twenty-five years, a quarter of a century without roof, cell, or shelter, the hermit standing in the weather of Syria as in a liturgy that admitted no dismissal.
Venerable John, Ascetic of the Syrian De.patron: Invoked for solitaries; those who endure without witnesses.
Venerable John, Ascetic of the Syrian De.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Sophia of Suzdal, the Wonderwo.life: Saint Sophia of Suzdal, in the world the Great Princess Solomonia Saburova, was born about 1490, daughter of the noble Yuri Saburov, and in 1505 was chosen from among five hundred maidens of all Russia as bride of the heir Basil, their marriage blessed by Metropolitan Simon in the Dormition cathedral of the Kremlin.
Venerable Sophia of Suzdal, the Wonderwo.patron: Invoked for women wronged in marriage; the childless.
Venerable Sophia of Suzdal, the Wonderwo.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Macarius the Roman of Mesopotamia.life: Saint Macarius the Roman is known to the Church through the ancient narrative of three monks of Mesopotamia, Theophilus, Sergius, and Hyginus, who journeyed toward the east seeking the ends of the earth, and after long wanderings through strange lands found, in a wilderness beyond all habitation, a cave and an elder of awesome appearance, clothed only in the white hair of his great age, with two lions dwelling tame beside him.
Saint Macarius the Roman of Mesopotamia.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Forefeast of the Elevation of the Cross.life: This is the Forefeast of the Universal Exaltation of the Precious and Life-Giving Cross, on which the Church begins to celebrate the great feast of the morrow. In the services the hymns of the Cross begin to sound, calling the faithful to purify their souls that they may behold the holy Wood lifted up in the midst of the earth;.
Forefeast of the Elevation of the Cross.patron: Commemorated in the holy calendar of the Church.
Forefeast of the Elevation of the Cross.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Dometius of Persia and his two di.life: Saint Dometius lived in Persia in the fourth century and was converted to Christ in his youth by a believer named Uaros. Leaving his homeland, he came to the frontier city of Nisibis, where he was baptized and tonsured a monk, and afterward he moved to the monastery of Saints Sergius and Bacchus under the strict archimandrite Urbelos.
Martyr Dometius of Persia and his two di.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Barulas the Youth of Caesarea.life: The Holy Martyr Barulas the Youth was a small child of Antioch whom God made a witness of the truth before the powers of the age. When the deacon Romanus stood on trial before the prefect Asclepiades and was mocked for his faith, the confessor pointed to a young boy in the crowd and said that even a child knows the one true God whom the wise men of the pagans deny;.
Martyr Barulas the Youth of Caesarea.patron: Invoked for children; the witness of children.
Martyr Barulas the Youth of Caesarea.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Mamas of Caesarea in Cappadocia.life: The Holy Great Martyr Mamas was born in Paphlagonia in the third century, the son of the noble Christians Theodotus and Rufina, who were cast into prison in Caesarea of Cappadocia for confessing Christ; there his father died before he could be tortured, and his mother, giving birth to him in the prison, entrusted him to God and departed this life, so that the newborn was left between the bodies of his parents.
Martyr Mamas of Caesarea in Cappadocia.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Holy Apostles of the Seventy and Deacons.life: Saints Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, and Parmenas were among the seven men, full of the Holy Spirit and wisdom, whom the twelve apostles chose and ordained as the first deacons of the Church, as related in the Acts of the Apostles, and they are numbered also among the Seventy.
Holy Apostles of the Seventy and Deacons.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Church New Year.life: On the first day of September the Church keeps the beginning of the Indiction, that is, the Ecclesiastical New Year. The Fathers of the First Ecumenical Council at Nicaea appointed that the year of the Church should begin on this day, following the ancient reckoning by which September, the month of the ingathering of the harvest, was the start of the year among the Hebrews, who at this season offered their thanks to God for His bounty;.
Church New Year.patron: Invoked for the new year; thanksgiving.
Church New Year.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Translation of the relics of the Protoma.life: After the holy Protomartyr and Archdeacon Stephen was stoned to death, his body was left unburied outside the city, but by night the renowned teacher of the Law Gamaliel, a secret disciple of Christ, took it up and laid it in a cave on his own land at Caphargamala, some twenty miles from Jerusalem.
Translation of the relics of the Protoma.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Holy, Righteous Anna the Prophetess.life: Saint Anna the Prophetess stands beside Simeon at the Meeting of the Lord, the second aged witness God stationed in the Temple for the fortieth day; and the Evangelist Luke, who alone records her, gives her a full and careful introduction, as though entering a deposition: Anna, a prophetess, the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Asher.
Holy, Righteous Anna the Prophetess.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Translation of the relics of Venerable T.life: Saint Theodosius of the Caves was the father of cenobitic monasticism in the land of Rus. Born at Vasilevo near Kiev, he was drawn from his childhood to the ascetic life, disdaining the games of children, clothing himself in poor garments, and laboring in the fields, until he left his home to seek God in the monastic life.
Translation of the relics of Venerable T.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Protomartyr and Equal of the Apostles Th.life: The Holy Protomartyr and Equal of the Apostles Thekla was born at Iconium of noble family, and at eighteen years of age, betrothed to a young man of the city, she heard from her window the preaching of the Apostle Paul concerning virginity and the kingdom of God, and her heart was so kindled that for three days she neither ate nor drank, but hung upon his words.
Protomartyr and Equal of the Apostles Th.patron: Invoked for virgins; those who leave all for Christ.
Protomartyr and Equal of the Apostles Th.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Ignatius, Patriarch of Constantino.life: Saint Ignatius, Patriarch of Constantinople, was born Nicetas, son of the emperor Michael Rangabe; and when his father was overthrown, the boy of fourteen was made a eunuch and shut in a monastery, where, accepting the ruin of his worldly hopes as the call of God, he became a true monk, and in time abbot, renowned for austerity and mercy.
Saint Ignatius, Patriarch of Constantino.patron: Invoked for hierarchs; firmness in righteousness.
Saint Ignatius, Patriarch of Constantino.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Protomartyr and Archdeacon Stephen.life: The Holy Protomartyr and Archdeacon Stephen was the first of the seven deacons chosen by the apostles, a man full of faith and of the Holy Spirit, and full of grace and power, who did great wonders among the people.
Protomartyr and Archdeacon Stephen.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Lazarus the Iconographer, of C.life: Saint Lazarus the Iconographer, a monk of Constantinople, was famed for his holiness of life and for his art, painting the holy icons in the years when the emperor Theophilus, the last of the iconoclasts, persecuted both the images and the hands that made them. Commanded to cease from his work, Lazarus answered by painting;.
Venerable Lazarus the Iconographer, of C.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Joasaph, Bishop of Belgorod.life: Saint Joasaph, Bishop of Belgorod, was born on the eighth of September 1705, the feast of the Nativity of the Theotokos, at Pryluky in the Poltava region, of the old Ukrainian noble line of the Gorlenkos, and named Joachim in baptism; and while he was still a boy, his father beheld in a vision the Mother of God with an angel casting a hierarch's mantle over the child, the sign of the burden to come.
Saint Joasaph, Bishop of Belgorod.patron: Invoked for bishops; clergy under discipline.
Saint Joasaph, Bishop of Belgorod.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Andrew Stratelates, and 2,593 sol.life: The Holy Martyr Andrew was a commander in the Roman army under the emperor Maximian, beloved by all for his courage and his justice, and when a great Persian host invaded the Syrian lands he was given the chief command with the title of Stratelates. Choosing a small band of brave soldiers, as Gideon of old chose his three hundred, he marched against the enemy;.
Martyr Andrew Stratelates, and 2,593 sol.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

The Annunciation of our Most Holy Lady,.life: The Annunciation celebrates the day the Archangel Gabriel was sent to Nazareth to the Virgin Mary with the greeting, Rejoice, thou who art full of grace, the Lord is with thee, announcing that she would conceive and bear the Son of God. When Mary asked how this could be, the angel answered that the Holy Spirit would come upon her and the power of the Most High would overshadow her.
The Annunciation of our Most Holy Lady,.patron: Commemorated in the holy calendar of the Church.
The Annunciation of our Most Holy Lady,.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Repose of Saint Raphael, Bishop of Brook.life: Saint Raphael, Bishop of Brooklyn, whose repose this day commemorates, was the good shepherd of the lost sheep of America, and the first Orthodox bishop consecrated in the New World. Born at Beirut in 1860 to a poor Damascene family in flight from the massacres of that year, he was educated by the Church that discerned him, at the patriarchal school, at Halki, and at the Theological Academy of Kyiv, mastering Arabic, Greek, Turkish, Russian, and in time English, a one-man synod of languages;.
Repose of Saint Raphael, Bishop of Brook.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Icon of the Mother of God of Pochaiv.life: The Pochaev Icon of the Mother of God is one of the greatest treasures of the Orthodox world, enshrined for more than four centuries in the Lavra of Pochaev in Volhynia. The icon was brought from Constantinople in the year 1559 by the Metropolitan Neophytos, who, being received in the home of the pious noblewoman Anna Goyska, blessed her with the icon in gratitude;.
Icon of the Mother of God of Pochaiv.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Entrance of the Apostle Andrew into Geor.life: On this day the Church of Georgia commemorates the entrance of the Holy Apostle Andrew the First-Called into the Georgian lands, the apostolic foundation upon which that ancient Church stands. The tradition of Georgia relates that when the apostles cast lots for the nations, Iberia fell to the Most Holy Theotokos herself;.
Entrance of the Apostle Andrew into Geor.patron: Invoked for the apostolic foundation of the Georgian Church; the Theotokos as protectress of Georgia.
Entrance of the Apostle Andrew into Geor.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Trophimus and 14 Others in Lycia.life: The Holy Martyrs Trophimus, Theophilus, and thirteen others with them suffered for Christ in Lycia during the persecution under the emperor Diocletian. Brought to trial, they boldly confessed themselves Christians and refused to offer sacrifice to the idols, and after being subjected to fierce tortures their legs were broken and they were cast into a fire.
Martyr Trophimus and 14 Others in Lycia.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Flavian the Confessor, Patriarch o.life: Saint Flavian the Confessor, Patriarch of Constantinople, paid with his life for the two natures of Christ, and his coffin presided over the council that vindicated him. Raised to the throne in 446, a man of ascetic life and unambitious honesty, he made an enemy at once by having nothing to give, for when the all-powerful eunuch Chrysaphius hinted that the new patriarch owed the emperor a gift of gold, Flavian sent the sacred vessels' worth in blessed bread, the only treasure he recognized, and the court never forgave the lesson.
Saint Flavian the Confessor, Patriarch o.patron: Invoked for hierarchs under violence; the vindicated dead.
Saint Flavian the Confessor, Patriarch o.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Agathocleia.life: The Holy Martyr Agathocleia was the servant of a certain Nicholas and his wife Paulina; and though the master was a Christian, the mistress was an idolater who raged against the faith of her slave. For long years Agathocleia endured from her cruel and hard labors, beatings, and every kind of torment devised to force her to deny Christ and to sacrifice to the idols, bearing all with the patience of the martyrs while remaining unmoved in her confession.
Martyr Agathocleia.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Anastasius the Fuller of Salona i.life: The Holy Martyr Anastasius the Fuller lived at Salona in Dalmatia at the close of the third century, a tradesman who made his fuller's shop a pulpit. He preached Christ openly in the city by word and by sign, painting the cross in plain view upon his door, so that his trade and his faith stood advertised together;.
Martyr Anastasius the Fuller of Salona i.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Alexander, Bishop of Comana.life: Saint Alexander lived in the third century near Neocaesarea, a man learned in the Scriptures and in many sciences, who yet took upon himself the hidden exploit of folly for Christ, living in poverty and selling charcoal in the city square. His face was always blackened with coal dust, and many looked upon him with contempt, not knowing his wisdom or his holiness.
Hieromartyr Alexander, Bishop of Comana.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Julian of Dalmatia.life: The Holy Martyr Julian suffered for Christ in the reign of the emperor Antoninus Pius, in the Italian province of Campania. When the governor Flavian was seeking out Christians to bring them to trial, the young Julian, who had come to Campania from Dalmatia, was found to be a follower of Christ.
Martyr Julian of Dalmatia.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Fathers of the First Six Councils.life: This day commemorates the holy Fathers of the first six Ecumenical Councils, the God-bearing hierarchs and teachers gathered from every part of the Christian world to defend the apostolic faith against the heresies that assailed it. At Nicaea and at the First Council of Constantinople they proclaimed the divinity of the Son and of the Holy Spirit and gave the Church the Symbol of Faith we confess to this day;.
Fathers of the First Six Councils.patron: Invoked for Orthodox doctrine; the true faith.
Fathers of the First Six Councils.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Translation of the relics of Venerable L.life: This feast commemorates the translation of the relics of Saint Lazarus the Wonderworker of Mount Galesion. Born at Magnesia in Lydia, Lazarus was a learned young man who loved God from his youth, and he traveled to the Holy Land, where he was tonsured at the Lavra of Saint Sabbas and labored for ten years, winning the love of the brethren by his ascetic struggles, until he was ordained a priest by the Patriarch of Jerusalem.
Translation of the relics of Venerable L.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Athanasius “the Resurrected On.life: Venerable Athanasius the Resurrected, recluse of the Near Caves, labored in the Kyiv Caves Lavra in the twelfth century, a contemporary of the archimandrite Polycarp, and God made of him a witness sent back from the doors of death. After long and grievous illness he died; the brethren prepared his body for burial, and on the third day the igumen came with the fathers to bury him, and all beheld the dead man alive, sitting up and weeping.
Venerable Athanasius “the Resurrected On.patron: Invoked for remembrance of death; repentance each hour.
Venerable Athanasius “the Resurrected On.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Translation of the relics of Righteous S.life: Righteous Simeon of Verkhoturye was a nobleman of European Russia who, concealing his birth, came in the troubled times of the early seventeenth century to the newly settled lands beyond the Urals and lived as a poor wanderer in the village of Merkushino near Verkhoturye. He earned his bread by sewing fur coats for the peasants, and it was his custom, in order to avoid payment, to leave some small part of the work unfinished and quietly depart, bearing the reproaches of his employers for the sake of holy poverty;.
Translation of the relics of Righteous S.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Nestor, Bishop of Magydos in.life: The Hieromartyr Nestor, Bishop of Magydos in Pamphylia, suffered in the year 250, in the persecution of Decius, and his contest displays the shepherd's arithmetic in its purest form: everyone out, himself last, himself alone. When the imperial edict reached Pamphylia and the hunt began, Nestor did not summon his flock to a glorious common stand;.
Hieromartyr Nestor, Bishop of Magydos in.patron: Invoked for bishops who stay; shepherds of hunted flocks.
Hieromartyr Nestor, Bishop of Magydos in.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Makarios, Abbot of Zheltovod a.life: Saint Makarios was born in the year 1349 at Nizhni-Novgorod of pious parents, and at the age of twelve he left his home and was tonsured a monk at the Ascension Caves Monastery under the holy abbot Dionysius, devoting himself with the fervor of youth to the work of salvation.
Venerable Makarios, Abbot of Zheltovod a.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Eulogius, Archbishop of Alexandria.life: Saint Eulogius, Patriarch of Alexandria, was one of the enlightened hierarchs of his age, a Syrian by formation who governed the see of Mark for twenty-seven years at the turn of the seventh century.
