He was first igumen of the monastery of the Mother of God at Antioch, where his learning and his firmness in the faith of Chalcedon made his name;.
Saint Eulogius, Archbishop of Alexandria.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Flavian, Archbishop of Antioch.life: Saint Flavian, Archbishop of Antioch, succeeded the confessor Meletius in 381, having stood beside him through the exiles and factions of the Arian troubles as priest and fellow ascetic; and his long episcopate healed by patience the wounds that polemic had kept open, the ancient schism of Antioch closing at last under his mild persistence, so that the great see ended the century united which had begun it divided four ways.
Saint Flavian, Archbishop of Antioch.patron: Invoked for peacemakers; intercessors for cities.
Saint Flavian, Archbishop of Antioch.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Uncovering of the relics of Venerable Ma.life: On this day the Church commemorates the uncovering of the relics of Saint Martinian, Abbot of Belozersk, which took place in the year 1514. Born Michael in 1370 in a village near the White Lake, he came at thirteen years of age in secret to Saint Cyril of White Lake, under whom he was formed in perfect obedience, learning his letters and laboring with the blessing of his elder at the copying of books, and being ordained in time deacon and hieromonk.
Uncovering of the relics of Venerable Ma.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Dalmatus the Ascetic of the Da.life: Saint Dalmatus served as a soldier in the army of the emperor Theodosius the Great and won the emperor's favor, but he was seized with a longing to serve the King of Heaven rather than an earthly ruler. Between the years 381 and 383 he left the army and came with his son Faustus to the monastery of Saint Isaac near Constantinople, where both father and son were tonsured and took up a strict ascetic life.
Venerable Dalmatus the Ascetic of the Da.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Pitirim, Bishop of Tambov.life: Saint Pitirim, Bishop of Tambov, was born Procopius at Vyazma in the year 1645, and from childhood the Lord prepared him for spiritual service, for he loved the church, learned reading and writing early, and delighted in the divine services. Having embraced the monastic life and risen to be an abbot, he was consecrated Bishop of Tambov by the Patriarch Joachim in 1685.
Saint Pitirim, Bishop of Tambov.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Athanasios, Venerable Anthou.life: Saint Athanasius, Bishop of Tarsus in Cilicia, and those with him suffered for Christ in the third century. Saint Anthousa, a maiden of Seleucia in Syria and the daughter of wealthy pagans, had heard of the Christian faith and longed to be instructed by the bishop Athanasius, and so, taking with her two servants, Charisimus and Neophytus, she came to Tarsus under the pretext of another journey.
Hieromartyr Athanasios, Venerable Anthou.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Repose of Saint Alexander Nevsky.life: On this day the Church commemorates the repose of the Holy Prince Alexander Nevsky, the defender of Rus in her darkest century. Born in 1220 at Pereslavl-Zalessky, the son of Prince Yaroslav, he was still a youth of twenty when the Swedes came up the Neva against Novgorod;.
Repose of Saint Alexander Nevsky.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Hermes, Serapion, and Polyaenus.life: The Holy Martyrs Hermes, Serapion, and Polyaenus were citizens of Rome in the second century, zealous in spreading the faith of Christ and in confuting the arguments of the pagans. Arrested and brought before the authorities, they stood firm in the confession of their faith and would not offer sacrifice to the idols, and for this they were cruelly beaten and cast into a dark and foul prison, where they endured hunger and every hardship without wavering.
Martyrs Hermes, Serapion, and Polyaenus.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Deborah.life: The Righteous Deborah, prophetess and judge of Israel, sat beneath her palm tree between Ramah and Bethel in the hill country of Ephraim, and the children of Israel came up to her for judgment, in the dark generation when Jabin of Canaan and Sisera his commander, with nine hundred chariots of iron, crushed the tribes for twenty years.
Righteous Deborah.patron: Invoked for judges; women who lead.
Righteous Deborah.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Uncovering of the relics of Venerable Ma.life: Blessed Maximus of Moscow chose one of the hardest paths to salvation, taking upon himself the folly of Christ. Nothing is known of his parents or his birth, only that summer and winter alike he went about scarcely clothed, enduring cold and heat, hunger and the scorn of men, that he might crucify his flesh and hide his holiness from the eyes of the world.
Uncovering of the relics of Venerable Ma.patron: Invoked for patience in hardship; repentance.
Uncovering of the relics of Venerable Ma.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyrs Nicander, Bishop of Myra, a.life: The Hieromartyrs Nicander, Bishop of Myra, and Hermas the Presbyter were disciples of the Apostle Titus, the companion of Paul, and were ordained by him to the sacred ministry in Lycia. Joining unceasing pastoral labor to the ascetic life, they converted many pagans to Christ, for which they were denounced and brought before the prefect Libanius;.
Hieromartyrs Nicander, Bishop of Myra, a.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Blessed Yaropolk (in Baptism Peter), Pri.life: The Holy Prince Yaropolk of Volodymyr-Volhynia, named Peter in holy baptism, was the son of Grand Prince Izyaslav of Kyiv and grandson of Yaroslav the Wise; and his short life was a school of dispossession, for he shared his father's repeated exiles among the Poles and the Germans when the strife of the princes drove them from Rus, learning early that thrones are lent and not given.
Blessed Yaropolk (in Baptism Peter), Pri.patron: Invoked for rulers; princes who suffer wrong without vengeance.
Blessed Yaropolk (in Baptism Peter), Pri.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Pancratius, Bishop of Taormi.life: The Hieromartyr Pancratius, Bishop of Taormina, was born in the days when our Lord walked upon the earth, to parents of Antioch. His father, hearing of the great Teacher, took the young Pancratius with him to Jerusalem, and beholding the miracles and hearing the divine teaching, he believed in Christ and drew close to the apostles, especially to Peter.
Hieromartyr Pancratius, Bishop of Taormi.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Eudokia (in monasticism Euphro.life: Saint Euphrosyne, known in the world as Eudokia, was the daughter of the prince of Suzdal, and from the year 1367 the wife of the Grand Prince Demetrius of the Don, whose union was a pledge of peace between Moscow and Suzdal. Guided in the spiritual life by Saint Alexis of Moscow and by Saint Sergius of Radonezh, who baptized one of her sons, she bore the cares of a ruling princess while cultivating a hidden life of prayer and severe asceticism, wearing heavy chains beneath her royal garments.
Venerable Eudokia (in monasticism Euphro.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Anthony of the Kyiv Far Caves.life: Saint Anthony, the founder of monasticism in the land of Rus, was born in the year 983 at Liubech near Chernigov and named Antipas in baptism. Drawn from his youth to the monastic life, he journeyed to Mount Athos, where he was tonsured and trained in the ascetic struggle, until the abbot, moved by God, sent him back to his homeland to plant there the monastic way.
Venerable Anthony of the Kyiv Far Caves.patron: Invoked for monastics; monastic life in Rus.
Venerable Anthony of the Kyiv Far Caves.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint George, Bishop of Amastris on the.life: Saint George, Bishop of Amastris on the Black Sea, was born at Kromna near that city in answer to his aged parents' prayers, and fled as a young man to the mountains of Paphlagonia, laboring as a hermit and then in a monastic brotherhood, hidden, he intended, for life;.
Saint George, Bishop of Amastris on the.patron: Invoked for defenders of cities; bishops of the coasts.
Saint George, Bishop of Amastris on the.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Gorazd of Prague, Bohemia and Mor.life: The Hieromartyr Gorazd, Bishop of Prague and of Bohemia and Moravia-Silesia, was born in Moravia in 1879 and named Matthias in baptism. Ordained first in the Roman church, he came to Orthodoxy after the First World War and led tens of thousands of his countrymen into the Orthodox Church, being consecrated bishop for the Czech lands under the Serbian Patriarchate, taking the name of Gorazd after the disciple of Saint Methodius.
Martyr Gorazd of Prague, Bohemia and Mor.patron: Invoked for those who shelter the persecuted; the Czech and Slovak faithful.
Martyr Gorazd of Prague, Bohemia and Mor.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Hyacinth of Caesarea, in Cappadoc.life: The Holy Martyr Hyacinth was a native of Caesarea in Cappadocia, raised in a Christian family, who served as chamberlain to the emperor Trajan while keeping his faith in Christ hidden. One day, when the emperor and his court were offering sacrifice to the idols, the young Hyacinth withdrew to a private room and prayed fervently to Christ;.
Martyr Hyacinth of Caesarea, in Cappadoc.patron: Invoked for constancy in the faith.
Martyr Hyacinth of Caesarea, in Cappadoc.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Afterfeast of the Entry of the Most Holy.life: In the days of the afterfeast of the Entry of the Most Holy Theotokos into the Temple, the Church remains within the light of the feast, continuing to sing its hymns and to contemplate its mystery: the three-year-old child, brought by Joachim and Anna in fulfillment of their vow, ascending the great steps of the Temple unaided, received by the high priest Zachariah, and led, beyond all custom, into the Holy of Holies itself, where the ark and the mercy seat once stood;.
Afterfeast of the Entry of the Most Holy.patron: Invoked for abiding in the grace of the feast.
Afterfeast of the Entry of the Most Holy.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Sebastian at Rome, and his compan.life: The Holy Martyr Sebastian and his companions suffered at Rome in the year 288, under Diocletian. Sebastian, captain in the praetorian guard, honored by the emperors and secretly a Christian, used his rank as a shield for the Church.
Martyr Sebastian at Rome, and his compan.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Theodore, Prince of Smolensk and Y.life: The Holy Prince Theodore of Smolensk and Yaroslavl, called the Black, was born in the terrible days of the Mongol invasion of Rus and named for the Great Martyr Theodore Stratelates. Receiving at first only the small town of Mozhaisk as his portion, he governed it so well that it grew and prospered, and by marriage he became prince of Yaroslavl;.
Saint Theodore, Prince of Smolensk and Y.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Monastic Martyr Macarius of Saint Anne S.life: Saint Macarius the New Martyr was born at Kios in Bithynia, and in his youth, in the days of the Ottoman yoke, he was drawn by force and deceit toward the religion of the conquerors, a wound that burned in his conscience thereafter. Fleeing to the Holy Mountain of Athos, he came to the skete of Saint Anne, where he was received, tonsured, and formed in repentance, prayer, and tears under the elders of that holy place;.
Monastic Martyr Macarius of Saint Anne S.patron: Invoked for repentance sealed in blood; steadfast confession.
Monastic Martyr Macarius of Saint Anne S.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Christina of Tyre.life: Saint Christina lived in the third century, the daughter of a wealthy man named Urban who was governor of Tyre. Intending that she should serve as a pagan priestess, her father shut her away with many idols of gold and silver and commanded her to burn incense before them.
Martyr Christina of Tyre.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Commemoration of the Holy Fathers of the.life: On this day the Church commemorates the Holy Fathers of the Seventh Ecumenical Council, which gathered at Nicaea in the year 787, in the days of the empress Irene and her son Constantine, under the presidency of Saint Tarasius, Patriarch of Constantinople. Some three hundred and fifty fathers assembled against the heresy of the iconoclasts, which for decades had ravaged the Church, destroying the holy images and persecuting those who venerated them;.
Commemoration of the Holy Fathers of the.patron: Invoked for the veneration of the holy icons; the fullness of Orthodox teaching.
Commemoration of the Holy Fathers of the.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Right-Believing Prince Roman of Uglich.life: Right-believing Prince Roman of Uglich ruled his Volga appanage in the thirteenth century, in the bitter first generations of the Mongol yoke, and left behind him the rarest of medieval reputations, a reign remembered for nothing but goodness. Son of the pious prince Vladimir of Uglich, Roman was raised in the fear of God, and receiving the principality.
Right-Believing Prince Roman of Uglich.patron: Invoked for rulers; builders of churches and hospitals.
Right-Believing Prince Roman of Uglich.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Alexei (Kabalyuk).life: Saint Alexei of Carpatho-Russia, in the world Alexander Kabalyuk, the Apostle of Carpatho-Russia, was born on the first of September 1877 into a lumberjack's family in Transcarpathia and named for the holy Prince Alexander Nevsky. A novice first in a Uniate monastery, he journeyed to the Holy Mountain of Athos, and there, at the Russian monastery of the Great Martyr Panteleimon, he was received into the Orthodox Church whose faith his people had kept in their bones through centuries of enforced union;.
Venerable Alexei (Kabalyuk).src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Apostles of the Seventy: Erastus, Olympa.life: The Holy Apostles Erastus, Olympas, Herodion, Sosipater, Quartus, and Tertius of the Seventy were disciples and fellow laborers of the Holy Apostle Paul, who greets them in his Epistle to the Romans. Erastus, whom Paul calls the treasurer of the city, served as steward of the Church of Jerusalem and afterward as bishop of Paneas in Palestine.
Apostles of the Seventy: Erastus, Olympa.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Synaxis of the Saints of North America.life: On the second Sunday after Pentecost the Orthodox Church in America commemorates all the saints who have shone forth on this continent, both those glorified and those known only to God. Their history begins in 1794, when a small band of monastic missionaries from Valaam, among them Saint Herman of Alaska, came to the native peoples of Alaska bearing the light of the Gospel.
Synaxis of the Saints of North America.patron: Invoked for the Church in North America.
Synaxis of the Saints of North America.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Anatolius the Recluse of the K.life: Saint Anatolius the Recluse pursued the monastic life in the Far Caves of the Kyiv Caves in the thirteenth century, living enclosed in stillness and unceasing prayer. Though little of his history survives, he is honored among the venerable recluses and fathers of the Caves whose relics repose incorrupt in the Lavra, and he is commemorated with the whole assembly of the Kyiv Caves saints.
Venerable Anatolius the Recluse of the K.patron: Commemorated in the holy calendar of the Church.
Venerable Anatolius the Recluse of the K.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Gregory, Bishop of Greater A.life: The Hieromartyr Gregory, Bishop of Greater Armenia, Equal of the Apostles and Enlightener of Armenia, was the son of the Parthian noble Anak, who had slain the Armenian king; and the infant Gregory, saved from the vengeance that destroyed his house, was carried to Caesarea in Cappadocia and raised there in the Christian faith.
Hieromartyr Gregory, Bishop of Greater A.patron: Invoked for missionaries; the enlightenment of nations.
Hieromartyr Gregory, Bishop of Greater A.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Theodoulus, Eparch of Constantinop.life: Saint Theodoulus, Eparch of Constantinople, held under the emperor Theodosius the Great the highest office of the imperial city, and beheld from that height the vanity of its glory. Grieved by the injustice that no office could cure, and pierced by the death of his pious wife, he distributed his great wealth to the poor, laid down the.
Saint Theodoulus, Eparch of Constantinop.patron: Invoked for officials who renounce power; hidden virtue revealed.
Saint Theodoulus, Eparch of Constantinop.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Felicitas of Rome, and her seven.life: The Holy Martyr Felicitas of Rome, a wealthy and noble widow, suffered with her seven sons under the emperor Marcus Aurelius, about the year 164, and the Church has always set her beside the mother of the Maccabees, the two mothers of seven who watched their whole posterity precede them into glory.
Martyr Felicitas of Rome, and her seven.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

New Martyr John Kalphes, the Apprentice.life: The Holy New Martyr John Kalphes suffered at Constantinople in the year 1575, in the second generation after the City's fall, and his title is his trade: kalphes, the journeyman master builder, for John was a skilled young craftsman of the imperial workshops, a Christian whose excellence had carried him into the service of the Ottoman court itself, where he built and finished for the conquerors with a workman's honesty, esteemed by the great for his craft and by the Christians for his piety and his generous alms.
New Martyr John Kalphes, the Apprentice.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Valerian.life: The Holy Martyr Valerian is commemorated on this day together with the Martyr Philoumenus of Ancyra, among those who suffered in Galatia in the persecution under the emperor Aurelian, about the year 274. The Greek synaxaria record that he was perfected in martyrdom by the sword: confessing Christ before the persecutors and refusing every demand to sacrifice, he was beheaded, and his soul ascended to the Lord for whom he had counted his life as nothing.
Martyr Valerian.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Beheading of Venerable Cornelius, Abbot.life: The Hieromartyr Cornelius, Abbot of the Pskov Caves, was born at Pskov in 1501 to the noble Stephen and Maria, and was formed at the Mirozh monastery in the whole culture of northern monasticism, making candles, chopping wood, transcribing and adorning books, and painting icons; and when the clerk Misiur Munekhin took the youth to the poor little Caves monastery in the woods, the beauty of the place and the solemnity of the cave church decided his life, for Cornelius took the tonsure there and never left.
Beheading of Venerable Cornelius, Abbot.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Cyril, Abbot of Chelma Hill.life: Saint Cyril of Chelma Hill, Enlightener of the Chud people, was born at White Lake and tonsured at the monastery of Saint Anthony the Roman in Novgorod, where for six years he passed through the obediences of the common life; then, after three years of wandering through the northern wilderness, he settled upon Chelma Hill near Kargopol, and there he remained.
Venerable Cyril, Abbot of Chelma Hill.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Theodosius (Prince Theodore of Ost.life: Saint Theodore, Prince of Ostrog in Volhynia, was descended from the holy Prince Vladimir, and he won renown both for building churches and for defending the Orthodox faith in his land against the pressures of the Latins. A valiant ruler, he took part in the great victory over the Teutonic Knights at Grunwald, and out of sympathy for the persecuted Orthodox he lent his aid to the faithful in neighboring lands;.
Saint Theodosius (Prince Theodore of Ost.patron: Invoked for the defense of Orthodoxy.
Saint Theodosius (Prince Theodore of Ost.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Translation of the Relics of Venerable S.life: Saints Sergius and Herman were the founders of the great monastery of the Transfiguration on the island of Valaam in Lake Ladoga, the northern Athos of the Russian land. Ancient tradition holds that they were Greek hieromonks who came to the lands of Novgorod and settled on the rocky island, gathering a brotherhood and planting the light of Orthodoxy among the pagan tribes of Karelia;.
Translation of the Relics of Venerable S.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Recovery of the relics of Saint Job of P.life: Saint Job, abbot and wonderworker of Pochaev, was one of the great defenders of Orthodoxy in the western Russian lands during the age of the Union of Brest, when the faithful of Volhynia were sorely pressed to submit to Rome. Tonsured in his youth and later called to govern the monastery on the mountain of Pochaev, he strengthened.
Recovery of the relics of Saint Job of P.patron: Invoked for monastics; defense of Orthodoxy.
Recovery of the relics of Saint Job of P.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Antiochus.life: Saint Antiochus the Monk, of the Great Lavra of Saint Sabbas, lived through the darkest hour of Palestinian monasticism and turned its ruin into a book. A Galatian by origin and a Sabbaite by formation, he was a monk of the Lavra when the Persian invasion of 614 broke over the Holy Land, and he became the eyewitness chronicler of its martyrs, recording the slaughter of the forty-four fathers of Saint Sabbas who would not flee their cells, a memorial the Church keeps to this day on his testimony.
Saint Antiochus.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Romanus the Deacon of Caesarea.life: The Holy Martyr Romanus, deacon of the church of Caesarea in Palestine, was at Antioch when the persecution of Diocletian broke upon that city; and seeing the Christians streaming in fear toward the pagan festival to save their lives by sacrifice, he stood at the gates and cried out to them to remember Christ, turning many back from apostasy at the very threshold of the temple.
Martyr Romanus the Deacon of Caesarea.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Heliodorus and Dosa of Persia.life: The Holy Martyrs Heliodorus and Dosa suffered for Christ in Persia in the year 380, during the long persecution of the Christians under the emperor Sapor. Though little of their contest has been preserved, it is known that they confessed the faith and endured death rather than deny their Lord or worship the fire and the sun as the Persians did.
Martyrs Heliodorus and Dosa of Persia.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Menas of Egypt.life: The Holy Great Martyr Menas was an Egyptian and a soldier, serving in Phrygia at Cotyaeum; and when the decrees of Diocletian commanded all to sacrifice to the idols, he laid aside his military belt rather than deny Christ, and withdrew into the mountains, where in fasting and prayer he prepared for a greater warfare.
Martyr Menas of Egypt.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Daniel the Stylite of Constant.life: Saint Daniel the Stylite was born in 409 at Maratha near Samosata, the child of his mother Martha's vowed and answered prayers, and entered the monastic life at twelve years of age; and journeying twice to the pillar of Saint Simeon the Stylite, he received the great archetype's blessing, and after Simeon's repose his leather tunic, the mantle of that strange and mighty calling passing to him.
Venerable Daniel the Stylite of Constant.patron: Invoked for counselors of rulers; perseverance in one calling.
Venerable Daniel the Stylite of Constant.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Monastic Martyr Damascene of the Lavra.life: The Holy Monastic Martyr Damascene of the Lavra was born in the Galata district of Constantinople to pious parents named Kyriakos and Kyriake, who called their son Diamantes. Orphaned young and left without guidance, the boy fell into a disordered life, and being caught one day in an unlawful act, he saved himself from punishment by consenting to accept Islam;.
Monastic Martyr Damascene of the Lavra.patron: Invoked for repentance after denial; the washing away of apostasy in blood.
Monastic Martyr Damascene of the Lavra.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Demetrius, his wife Euanthia, an.life: The Holy Martyrs Demetrius, his wife Euanthia, and their son Demetrian suffered for Christ in the first century in the city of Skepsis on the Hellespont. Demetrius was ruler of that city, and according to the tradition of the Church he was brought to faith by the preaching and wonders of the Hieromartyr Cornelius the Centurion, the same whom the Apostle Peter had baptized, when Cornelius came to Skepsis proclaiming Christ;.
Martyrs Demetrius, his wife Euanthia, an.patron: Invoked for Christian families; steadfast confession.
Martyrs Demetrius, his wife Euanthia, an.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Vincent of Spain.life: The Holy Martyr Vincent of Spain was archdeacon of the church of Saragossa under the aged bishop Valerius, whose impediment of speech the eloquent deacon supplied, preaching the word of God in his bishop's name; and when the persecution of Diocletian reached Spain, the governor Dacian had both arrested and brought in chains to Valencia.
Martyr Vincent of Spain.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Sergius, Abbot of Nurma, disci.life: Saint Sergius of Nurma, the wonderworker of Vologda, was a Greek by birth who labored on the Holy Mountain of Athos, and though already an experienced elder, he traveled to the land of Rus to consult Saint Sergius of Radonezh and to place himself under his guidance, spending some years as the great abba's disciple.
Venerable Sergius, Abbot of Nurma, disci.patron: Invoked for monastics; the wilderness life.
Venerable Sergius, Abbot of Nurma, disci.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Forefeast of the Entry into the Temple o.life: On this day the Church keeps the forefeast of the Entry of the Most Holy Theotokos into the Temple, standing at the threshold of the feast as the child Mary stood at the threshold of the sanctuary. The hymns of the forefeast summon the faithful to prepare: Let us the faithful make glad today, singing psalms to the Lord, and let us honor His sanctified tabernacle, the living ark that contained the Word who cannot be contained;.
Forefeast of the Entry into the Temple o.patron: Invoked for preparation for the feasts of the Mother of God.
Forefeast of the Entry into the Temple o.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

“O All-Hymned Mother” Icon of the Mother.life: The Icon of the Mother of God called O All-Hymned Mother takes its name from the opening words of the thirteenth kontakion of the Akathist hymn, O All-hymned Mother, worthy of all praise, who gave birth to the Word, the Holiest of all the holy; and it is celebrated on this day.
“O All-Hymned Mother” Icon of the Mother.patron: Invoked for the praise of the Mother of God; help in every need.
“O All-Hymned Mother” Icon of the Mother.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Ambrose, Bishop of Milan.life: Saint Ambrose, Bishop of Milan, one of the great fathers of the West, was born about 340 at Trier, the son of the praetorian prefect of Gaul; and the tradition tells that a swarm of bees settled upon the infant's lips and departed without harm, the omen of the honeyed speech to come.
Saint Ambrose, Bishop of Milan.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

The Three Holy Youths: Ananias, Azarias.life: The Three Holy Youths, Ananias, Azarias, and Misael, called in Babylon Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, were companions of the Prophet Daniel in the captivity, youths of Judah who kept the whole law of their God at the heart of the empire that had burned His Temple. When Nebuchadnezzar raised his image of gold on the plain of Dura and commanded all peoples to fall down at the sound of the music, the three stood;.
The Three Holy Youths: Ananias, Azarias.patron: Invoked for all who face the furnace of trial; confessors before rulers.
The Three Holy Youths: Ananias, Azarias.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Porphyrius, Bishop of Gaza.life: Saint Porphyrius, Bishop of Gaza, whose life his faithful companion Mark the Deacon wrote from the inside, was born at Thessalonica in 347 to a wealthy family, and left it all at twenty-five for the desert of Scetis, laboring five years among the Egyptian fathers and then five more in a cave by the Jordan, where the damp and the severity broke his health and gave him the affliction that God would use as the hinge of his story, a disease of the leg that left him barely able to walk.
Saint Porphyrius, Bishop of Gaza.patron: Invoked for bishops of hostile cities; guardians of the Cross.
Saint Porphyrius, Bishop of Gaza.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Translation of the relics of Venerable Z.life: Saints Sabbatius and Zosimas were the founders of the great monastery of Solovki on its island in the cold White Sea of the Russian North. Saint Sabbatius, seeking utter solitude, was the first to settle upon the uninhabited island, where he labored and reposed in the year 1435;.
Translation of the relics of Venerable Z.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Anatolius of the Kyiv Near Cav.life: Saint Anatolius was a monk of the Kyiv Caves who labored in the Near Caves in the twelfth century. Little is recorded of the particulars of his life, but he is numbered among the venerable fathers of the Caves who gave themselves to prayer, fasting, and obedience, and whose relics rest incorrupt in the caves of the Lavra as an enduring witness to their holiness.
Venerable Anatolius of the Kyiv Near Cav.patron: Commemorated in the holy calendar of the Church.
Venerable Anatolius of the Kyiv Near Cav.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Afterfeast of the Elevation of the Cross.life: These are the days of the Afterfeast of the Universal Exaltation of the Precious and Life-Giving Cross, during which the Church continues to celebrate the great feast of the Cross of the Lord. The hymns of the Exaltation are joined to the daily services, and the faithful continue to venerate the holy Wood lifted up in the midst of the earth, contemplating the mystery by which the instrument of death became the tree of life.
Afterfeast of the Elevation of the Cross.patron: Commemorated in the holy calendar of the Church.
Afterfeast of the Elevation of the Cross.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Varnava (Nastic).life: Saint Varnava the New Confessor, Bishop of Hvosno, was born Vojislav Nastic on the thirty-first of January 1914 in Gary, Indiana, to Serbian immigrant parents, and was the first child baptized in the church of Saint Sava there, where he served at the altar as a boy; so that the Serbian Church numbers among her confessors a son of America.
Saint Varnava (Nastic).patron: Invoked for catechists; the Church under communism.
Saint Varnava (Nastic).src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Marcian of Cyrrhus.life: Saint Marcian of Cyrrhus was born of a noble family of that Syrian city, and forsaking rank and wealth, he withdrew into the desert of Chalcis, where he enclosed himself in a cell so small that he could neither stand upright nor lie at full length, dwelling there in fasting, unceasing prayer, and the singing of psalms.
Saint Marcian of Cyrrhus.patron: Invoked for hermits; moderation with strictness.
Saint Marcian of Cyrrhus.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Eutropius, Cleonicus, and Basili.life: The Holy Martyrs Eutropius, Cleonicus, and Basiliscus suffered at Amasea in Pontus about the year 308, and their contest is the continuation of a famous one, for the three were companions of the Great Martyr Theodore the Recruit, Basiliscus his kinsman by blood and all three his kinsmen in arms, seized in the same persecution that had crowned Theodore two years before and held in the same prison, where the memory of the recruit's victory was the air the three men breathed.
Martyrs Eutropius, Cleonicus, and Basili.patron: Invoked for kinsmen and companions in trial; soldiers of Christ.
Martyrs Eutropius, Cleonicus, and Basili.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Antonina of Nicea, in Bithynia.life: The Holy Martyr Antonina of Nicaea in Bithynia suffered in the persecution raised under Maximian at the turn of the fourth century, when the imperial edicts were once more filling the tribunals of Asia Minor with Christians who would not trade one grain of incense for their lives.
Martyr Antonina of Nicea, in Bithynia.patron: Invoked for women before tribunals; the confession kept through the waters.
Martyr Antonina of Nicea, in Bithynia.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Averkios the Wonderworker, Bishop.life: Saint Abercius the Wonderworker, Bishop of Hierapolis in Phrygia, Equal of the Apostles, shepherded his small flock in a city given over to idols in the days of Marcus Aurelius. Commanded in a vision to destroy the deceits of the demons, he entered the temple by night and overthrew the idols;.
Saint Averkios the Wonderworker, Bishop.patron: Invoked for healing; the conversion of cities.
Saint Averkios the Wonderworker, Bishop.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Irenarchus and Seven Women Martyr.life: The Holy Martyr Irenarchus of Sebaste in Armenia served, in the reign of Diocletian, as an executioner, one of those who tortured the confessors of Christ; and God, who called Paul on the road and the thief on the cross, called Irenarchus at the instruments of his trade.
Martyr Irenarchus and Seven Women Martyr.patron: Invoked for executioners converted; those who repent of cruelty.
Martyr Irenarchus and Seven Women Martyr.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

The Placing of the Honorable Robe of the.life: This feast commemorates the enshrining of the honorable Robe of the Most Holy Theotokos in the church at Blachernae in Constantinople during the reign of the emperor Leo the Great. According to tradition, before her Dormition the Virgin bequeathed one of her garments to a pious maiden, and it was preserved from generation to generation in a devout family in Palestine, working many healings.
The Placing of the Honorable Robe of the.patron: Invoked for protection of cities and the faithful.
The Placing of the Honorable Robe of the.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Greatmartyr James the Persian.life: The Holy Great Martyr James the Persian, called Intercisus, the Cut-in-Pieces, was a Christian noble of Persia, rich, honored, and beloved of King Yezdegerd; and his soul, entangled by the king's friendship, fell into the great sin of his life, for when the king turned against the Christians, James, unwilling to lose favor, denied Christ with the court.
Greatmartyr James the Persian.patron: Invoked for courtiers; repentance after denial.
Greatmartyr James the Persian.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

“Chukhloma” Icon of the Mother of God fr.life: The Chukhloma Icon of the Mother of God, also called the Galich Icon and belonging to the Tenderness type, appeared in the year 1350 to Saint Abramius of Galich, who had come to the northern wilderness for ascetic labors with the blessing of Saint Sergius of Radonezh. On the wild shores of the Galich lake, near a great mountain hidden in dense forest, Saint Abramius prayed to the Mother of God for her blessing upon his endeavors, and he beheld upon the mountain her holy icon shining with an indescribable light.
“Chukhloma” Icon of the Mother of God fr.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Joseph, Abbot of Volokolamsk,.life: Saint Joseph of Volotsk, in the world John Sanin, was born in 1440 in a village near Volokolamsk, and being given as a boy to the elder Arsenius for schooling, he mastered the Psalter in a single year and all the Scriptures in the next, astonishing all by his memory.
Venerable Joseph, Abbot of Volokolamsk,.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs and Unmercenaries Cosmas and Dam.life: The Holy Martyrs and Unmercenaries Cosmas and Damian of Arabia, whom the Church distinguishes from the two other pairs of holy unmercenary brothers of the same names, were physicians who traveled through the cities and villages healing the sick without payment, asking of those they cured only faith in Christ, and by their art and their charity they drew a multitude to the knowledge of God.
Martyrs and Unmercenaries Cosmas and Dam.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Theophilus of the Kyiv Caves, Bish.life: Saint Theophilus, Archbishop of Novgorod, was chosen by lot to that great see in 1470, in the last troubled years of Novgorod's independence, and was consecrated at Moscow the following year. He shepherded his flock amid the storm of the city's fall, interceding for the conquered and burying the slain;.
Saint Theophilus of the Kyiv Caves, Bish.patron: Invoked for hierarchs; patience in disgrace.
Saint Theophilus of the Kyiv Caves, Bish.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Antiochus the Physician of Sebast.life: The Holy Martyr Antiochus was a native of Sebaste in Cappadocia and a physician by profession, and he was the brother of the holy Martyr Platon. When it became known to the pagans that he was a Christian, he was arrested and brought to trial, and though he was subjected to fierce tortures he remained steadfast in his confession of Christ.
Martyr Antiochus the Physician of Sebast.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Markella of Chios.life: Saint Markella lived in the village of Volissos on the island of Chios. Her parents were devout and among the wealthiest of the village, and after her mother died young, her father, the local headman, saw to her upbringing; she grew up modest and pure, shunning company that might do her spiritual harm.
Martyr Markella of Chios.patron: Invoked for purity; protection of chastity.
Martyr Markella of Chios.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Prophet Joel.life: The Holy Prophet Joel, son of Pethuel, prophesied in the kingdom of Judah about eight hundred years before Christ, and his short book stands among the twelve minor prophets. Taking occasion from a devastating plague of locusts and drought that stripped the land, he called priests and people to fasting and repentance, crying, Rend your heart and not your garments, and turn unto the Lord your God, for He is gracious and merciful;.
Prophet Joel.patron: Invoked for repentance; the outpouring of the Holy Spirit.
Prophet Joel.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Synaxis of the Most Holy Mother of God.life: On the day after the Nativity the Church celebrates the Synaxis of the Most Holy Theotokos, the assembly of the faithful gathered to glorify her through whom the Incarnation was accomplished; and this is by all evidence the most ancient feast of the Mother of God in the Christian tradition, the very beginning of her liturgical veneration, preached upon already by the fathers of the fourth century, Saint Epiphanius of Cyprus among them, and called in the oldest service books the Nativity Gifts, in memory of the offerings of the Magi.
Synaxis of the Most Holy Mother of God.patron: Commemorated in the holy calendar of the Church.
Synaxis of the Most Holy Mother of God.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Apostle Epenetus of the Seventy.life: The Holy Apostle Epenetus, one of the Seventy, was a disciple of the Savior whom the Apostle Paul greets warmly in his Epistle to the Romans as his beloved Epenetus, the firstfruits of Achaia unto Christ. He was appointed Bishop of Carthage, and there, enduring many afflictions at the hands of the idolaters, he labored to bring the pagans to the knowledge of the true God, winning many to the faith.
Apostle Epenetus of the Seventy.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Matrona, Abbess of Constantino.life: Saint Matrona of Constantinople was born at Perge in Pamphylia and given in marriage to a nobleman named Dometian, to whom she bore a daughter; and coming to Constantinople, she was so kindled with love for God in the churches and vigils of the capital that, entrusting her child to a pious woman, she resolved to give herself wholly to the Lord.
Venerable Matrona, Abbess of Constantino.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Virgin Martyr Eupraxia of Tabenna.life: Saint Eupraxia was the daughter of Antigonos, a noble dignitary of Constantinople and a kinsman of the emperor Theodosius the Great, and of his devout wife, also named Eupraxia, who were generous in their almsgiving. After her father's death, her mother took the young girl to Egypt, and there the child, though only seven years old, was so drawn to the life of a women's monastery near Tabennisi that she begged to remain among the nuns, and she was received.
Virgin Martyr Eupraxia of Tabenna.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Apostle Aquila of the Seventy.life: The Holy Apostle Aquila, one of the Seventy, was a Jew and a native of Pontus who lived at Rome with his wife Priscilla until, in the reign of the emperor Claudius, the Jews were expelled from the city and the couple settled in Corinth. There they met the Apostle Paul, who, being of the same trade, lodged with them and worked with them at making tents, and having received baptism from him they became his devoted disciples.
Apostle Aquila of the Seventy.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Synaxis of the Venerable Fathers of the.life: On this day the Church celebrates the Synaxis of the Venerable Fathers of the Kyiv Near Caves, the great assembly of saints whose incorrupt relics rest in the caves of Saint Anthony at the Kyiv Caves Lavra. In this holy company are numbered the first fathers of Russian monasticism and their innumerable children in the spirit: Anthony the founder, who planted the monastic life in the land of Rus;.
Synaxis of the Venerable Fathers of the.patron: Invoked for monastics; the land of Rus.
Synaxis of the Venerable Fathers of the.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Icon of the Mother of God “of the Sign”,.life: The Kursk-Root Icon of the Mother of God of the Sign is one of the most venerated wonderworking icons of the Russian land. It was found on the eighth of September in the year 1295, when a hunter in the forest by the river Tuskar, near the city of Kursk which the Tatars had laid waste, saw an icon lying face down at the root of a tree;.
Icon of the Mother of God “of the Sign”,.patron: Invoked for protection; the Russian diaspora.
Icon of the Mother of God “of the Sign”,.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Anthony, Abbot of Leokhnov, No.life: Saint Anthony of Leokhnov was born of a noble family and forsook the world in his youth, withdrawing into the wilderness of the Novgorod lands, where he lived at first as a hermit in a solitary place called Rublevo; and being directed by a voice from God, he settled at Leokhnovo, where he received the monastic tonsure and founded a monastery in honor of the Transfiguration of the Lord.
Venerable Anthony, Abbot of Leokhnov, No.patron: Invoked for monastics; the wilderness life.
Venerable Anthony, Abbot of Leokhnov, No.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Apostle Tertius of the Seventy.life: The Holy Apostle Tertius of the Seventy has left his own greeting within the Holy Scriptures, for it was his hand that wrote the Epistle of the Apostle Paul to the Romans at the Apostle's dictation, and there he set down, I Tertius, who wrote this epistle, salute you in the Lord, the scribe of the great letter of the Gospel of grace becoming himself a small living word within it.
Apostle Tertius of the Seventy.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Victorinus, Victor, Nikēphóros,.life: The Holy Martyrs Victorinus, Victor, Nikephoros, Claudius, Diodorus, Serapion, and Papias suffered at Corinth in the year 251, in the persecution under the emperor Decius, seven Christians of that city seized in the empire-wide harvest that Decius decreed when he commanded every subject to sacrifice or die. Brought before the tribunal, the seven confessed with one voice;.
Martyrs Victorinus, Victor, Nikēphóros,.patron: Invoked for companies of friends; those facing varied trials.
Martyrs Victorinus, Victor, Nikēphóros,.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Leavetaking of the Dormition of the Moth.life: This is the Leavetaking of the Feast of the Dormition of the Most Holy Theotokos, the final day on which the Church celebrates her blessed falling asleep and her translation in glory to heaven before bringing the feast to its close. On this day the festal service is sung once more, that the faithful may take their leave of the feast having been filled anew with its joy and consolation.
Leavetaking of the Dormition of the Moth.patron: Commemorated in the holy calendar of the Church.
Leavetaking of the Dormition of the Moth.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Matrona of Chios.life: Saint Matrona of Chios was born at the village of Volissos on that island, of wealthy and devout parents named Leon and Anna, and was called Mary in the world. Inclined from her youth to the monastic life, she fled the marriage her family intended and withdrew to a solitary place of the island, giving herself to fasting and prayer;.
Venerable Matrona of Chios.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Benjamin.life: The Righteous Benjamin, youngest of the twelve sons of the Patriarch Jacob, was the second child of the beloved Rachel, who died in bearing him on the road to Ephrath and named him with her last breath Ben-oni, son of my sorrow; but his father called him Benjamin, son of the right hand, and the child of grief became the darling of the patriarch's old age.
Righteous Benjamin.patron: Invoked for the youngest and best-loved; sorrow turned to strength.
Righteous Benjamin.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Sophrony (Sakharov) of Essex (.life: Saint Sophrony of Essex, one of the great elders of the twentieth century, was born Sergei Sakharov in Moscow in 1896 and in his youth pursued the life of a painter. Amid the upheavals of his age he left Russia, and after a period of searching he came to Mount Athos, where he became a monk at the Monastery of Saint Panteleimon and the close disciple of Saint Silouan the Athonite, from whom he received the teaching on prayer and humility that would shape his whole life.
Venerable Sophrony (Sakharov) of Essex (.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Greatmartyr Procopius of Caesarea, in Pa.life: The Holy Greatmartyr Procopius, called Neanius before his baptism, was a native of Jerusalem who lived under the emperor Diocletian. Raised by his pagan mother Theodosia after the death of his Christian father, he received an excellent education, rose swiftly in the imperial service, and was sent as proconsul to Alexandria to persecute the Christians.
Greatmartyr Procopius of Caesarea, in Pa.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Akepsimas the Hermit of Cyrrhu.life: Saint Akepsimas the Hermit lived in the fourth century near Cyrrhus in Syria, and his contest is recorded by Theodoret among the glories of the Syrian desert. Enclosing himself in a small cell, he passed sixty years without being seen and without speaking, receiving his scant food through a window dug obliquely through the wall, so that no eye could meet his;.
Venerable Akepsimas the Hermit of Cyrrhu.patron: Invoked for recluses; total enclosure for God.
Venerable Akepsimas the Hermit of Cyrrhu.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Prophet Haggai.life: The Holy Prophet Haggai, tenth of the twelve minor prophets, was born in Babylon during the captivity and came up to Jerusalem with the returning exiles; and in the second year of Darius the king, about five hundred and twenty years before Christ, when the rebuilding of the Temple had lain abandoned for a generation while the people built their own paneled houses, the word of the Lord came through him like a trumpet: Consider your ways.
Prophet Haggai.patron: Invoked for builders; those who rebuild what was lost.
Prophet Haggai.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Afterfeast of the Transfiguration of our.life: This is the first day of the Afterfeast of the Transfiguration of the Lord, on which the Church continues to celebrate the glory revealed upon the holy mountain. The hymns of the feast recall the amazement of the apostles Peter, James, and John when they beheld their Master transfigured before them, His face and garments shining brighter than the sun, and they proclaim His equality with the Father, for He who covers Himself with light as with a garment showed forth His divine radiance to His disciples.
Afterfeast of the Transfiguration of our.patron: Commemorated in the holy calendar of the Church.
Afterfeast of the Transfiguration of our.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Synaxis of the Saints of Volhynia.life: On this day the Church keeps the Synaxis of the Saints of Volhynia, gathering in one feast the holy men and women of that western borderland of Rus which through centuries of trial kept the Orthodox faith. In this choir are honored the holy bishops Stephen and Amphilochius of Vladimir in Volhynia, who planted the Church there in the generations after the Baptism of Rus;.
Synaxis of the Saints of Volhynia.patron: Invoked for the Volhynian land; fidelity to Orthodoxy in the western lands.
Synaxis of the Saints of Volhynia.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Varus, and seven Monastic Martyrs.life: The Holy Martyr Varus was a military commander in Egypt in the days of the persecution under Maximian, and a Christian in secret, who by night visited the imprisoned confessors, bringing them food, binding their wounds, and strengthening their souls. Once he passed the whole night in the prison with seven ascetic teachers of the Christians who awaited execution, marveling at their courage and lamenting that fear had until then kept him from open confession;.
Martyr Varus, and seven Monastic Martyrs.patron: Invoked for soldiers; the departed who died outside the faith.
Martyr Varus, and seven Monastic Martyrs.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Virgin Martyr Euthalia of Sicily.life: The Holy Virgin Martyr Euthalia of Sicily lived with her mother and brother at Leontini, and her short life turned entire on one night's dream in another woman's sleep. Her mother, a pagan, had suffered long years with an issue of blood that no physician could stanch, the affliction of the woman in the Gospel visited on a woman who had never heard the Gospel;.
Virgin Martyr Euthalia of Sicily.patron: Invoked for daughters of divided houses; the newly baptized.
Virgin Martyr Euthalia of Sicily.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Cherimon (Chaeremon) of Egypt.life: Saint Cherimon was an ascetic of the Egyptian desert who lived in the wilderness of Sketis at the end of the fourth century and the beginning of the fifth. He dwelt in a cave far from the church and from the nearest spring of water, so that even to draw water or to attend the services required great labor, and by such hardship he wearied his body for the sake of his soul.
Venerable Cherimon (Chaeremon) of Egypt.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Paphnutius and Euphrosynē of A.life: Venerable Paphnutius of Alexandria is commemorated on this day with his daughter Euphrosynē, whose principal feast the Church keeps in September; the February commemoration belongs especially to the father, and to the strangest consolation in the lives of the saints. Paphnutius was a rich and devout citizen of Alexandria whose long-childless marriage was answered with a single daughter, Euphrosynē, raised in piety and betrothed by her father to a noble youth;.
Venerable Paphnutius and Euphrosynē of A.patron: Invoked for fathers of consecrated children; parents of the vanished.
Venerable Paphnutius and Euphrosynē of A.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Neilos the Ascetic of Sinai.life: Saint Nilus the Ascetic of Sinai was a man of high rank at Constantinople, prefect of the capital, married and the father of two children, and a disciple of Saint John Chrysostom, whose teaching kindled in him the desire for the angelic life. With the consent of his wife, the family divided for the sake of God: she.
Venerable Neilos the Ascetic of Sinai.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Eleazar the Teacher of the Holy S.life: Saint Eleazar lived in the second century before Christ and was a scribe and teacher, a man of great dignity and advanced age. When Antiochus Epiphanes sought to compel the Jews to abandon the Law of Moses and to eat swine's flesh in violation of the covenant, Eleazar, though ninety years old, refused to save his life by so small a compromise or even to feign obedience, judging it unworthy of his years and a scandal to the young.
Martyr Eleazar the Teacher of the Holy S.patron: Invoked for teachers; integrity in old age.
Martyr Eleazar the Teacher of the Holy S.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Zeno the Faster, of the Kyiv C.life: Venerable Zeno the Faster and Lover of Labor of the Kyiv Far Caves lived in the fourteenth century, and the two titles the Lavra gave him are his whole biography, exact and sufficient: the Faster, and the Lover of Labor. In the caves of Saint Theodosius, in the hard generations after the Mongol ruin, Zeno waged the double.
Venerable Zeno the Faster, of the Kyiv C.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Afterfeast of the Nativity of our Lord a.life: The Afterfeast of the Nativity of our Lord carries the celebration through the days that follow the feast, for the Church does not close the cave of Bethlehem after one day but dwells within it, repeating at every service the troparion and kontakion of the feast, singing Christ is born, glorify Him over each day's saints and each day's labors, so that martyrs, hierarchs, and ascetics commemorated in these days are all beheld in the light of the manger.
Afterfeast of the Nativity of our Lord a.patron: Commemorated in the holy calendar of the Church.
Afterfeast of the Nativity of our Lord a.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Chariton of Syanzhemsk, Vologd.life: Saint Chariton of Syanzhemsk was the disciple and spiritual son of Saint Euthymius of Syanzhemsk, one of the desert-dwellers of the Vologda north, and labored under his guidance at the monastery of the Ascension of the Lord which Euthymius had established on the river Syanzhema. Formed in perfect obedience and in the strict traditions of the northern wilderness.
Venerable Chariton of Syanzhemsk, Vologd.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Theoctistus.life: Saint Theoctistus was a great ascetic of the Judean wilderness and the close companion of Saint Euthymius the Great, with whom he was joined in such love and oneness of mind that the two seemed to be one soul in two bodies. Each year after the feast of Theophany they would withdraw together into the desert to pray in solitude, returning only at Palm Sunday;.
Venerable Theoctistus.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Theodota at Nicea.life: The Holy Martyr Theodota suffered for Christ at Nicaea in Bithynia about the year 230, in the reign of the emperor Alexander Severus. Denounced as a Christian, she was cast into prison and held for a long time, and being brought forth to trial she confessed her Lord without wavering;.
Martyr Theodota at Nicea.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Repose of Saint Cyril, Equal of the Apos.life: On this day the Church keeps the repose of Saint Cyril, Equal of the Apostles and Teacher of the Slavs, who died at Rome on the fourteenth of February 869; his joint feast with his brother Methodius is celebrated in May, but this day belongs to the man himself.
Repose of Saint Cyril, Equal of the Apos.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Apostle Timon the Deacon of the Seventy.life: The Holy Apostle Timon was one of the seven deacons appointed by the apostles, as the Acts of the Apostles records, when the Twelve chose men full of the Holy Spirit and of wisdom to minister to the destitute widows of the Jerusalem church, Stephen and Philip at their head and Timon among their number, the first ordained servants of the Church's mercy.
Apostle Timon the Deacon of the Seventy.patron: Invoked for deacons; bishops of frontier sees.
Apostle Timon the Deacon of the Seventy.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

First and second finding of the Honorabl.life: On this day the Church celebrates the First and Second Findings of the Precious Head of Saint John the Forerunner, the two earliest chapters in the strange itinerary of the most venerated relic in Christendom after the instruments of the Passion. When Herodias had obtained the Baptist's head on the platter of her revenge, she would not suffer it to be buried with his body, fearing, the tradition says, the resurrection of the man she had silenced, and hid it in an unclean place in Herod's palace;.
First and second finding of the Honorabl.patron: Invoked for all who seek what is hidden; guardians of relics.
First and second finding of the Honorabl.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Finding of the relics of Venerable Maxim.life: This feast commemorates the finding of the relics of Saint Maximus the Greek, the learned monk and confessor. Born Michael Trivolis at Arta in Greece around 1470, he studied in Italy, then became a monk on Mount Athos, and in 1518 was sent to Russia to translate and correct the sacred books.
Finding of the relics of Venerable Maxim.patron: Invoked for translators and scholars; the unjustly imprisoned.
Finding of the relics of Venerable Maxim.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Athanasius, founder of the Gre.life: Saint Athanasius the Athonite, founder of the Great Lavra and of communal monasticism on the Holy Mountain, was born at Trebizond and named Abraham in baptism. Orphaned young and raised by a pious nun whose way of life he made his own, he was educated at Constantinople, and, drawn to the ascetic life, withdrew to Mount Athos seeking silence and solitude.
Venerable Athanasius, founder of the Gre.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Piamoun.life: Saint Piamoun the Virgin, whose memory the Church received from Palladius' history of the holy ascetics, proved that the desert is a condition and not an address, for she lived her whole consecrated life in her mother's cottage in a village of the Egyptian Nile. There, unnoticed by the world she had renounced without leaving, Piamoun kept the.
Saint Piamoun.patron: Invoked for home ascetics; spinners and weavers.
Saint Piamoun.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Mίlos (or Milēs) the Wonderw.life: The Hieromartyr Milos, Bishop of Persia, had been in his youth a soldier and commander, and leaving the service of earthly kings, he became a monk and was in time consecrated bishop of the ancient city of Susa, where the Prophet Daniel had beheld his visions. For his ascetic life God adorned him with the gifts of healing and prophecy;.
Hieromartyr Mίlos (or Milēs) the Wonderw.patron: Invoked for prophetic boldness; the Persian Church.
Hieromartyr Mίlos (or Milēs) the Wonderw.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Eumenius, Bishop of Gortyna.life: Saint Eumenius, Bishop of Gortyna in Crete, shone forth in the seventh century as an ascetic and wonderworker. From his youth he renounced the world and its goods, giving his substance to the poor and making himself poor for Christ, and by his humility he ascended to the heights of virtue, so that he was found worthy of the episcopal throne of Gortyna.
Saint Eumenius, Bishop of Gortyna.patron: Invoked for humility; rain in drought.
Saint Eumenius, Bishop of Gortyna.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Holy Wonderworkers and Unmercenaries Cos.life: The Holy Wonderworkers and Unmercenaries Cosmas and Damian of Asia, the first of the three pairs of holy unmercenary brothers of these names, were born in Asia Minor of a pagan father who died while they were small, and of the holy Theodota, who raised them in piety and in the reading of the divine books.
Holy Wonderworkers and Unmercenaries Cos.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Domnina of Anazarbus.life: The Holy Martyr Domnina of Anazarbus in Cilicia suffered for Christ under the emperor Diocletian, being brought to trial before Lysias, the governor of the region. Confessing herself a Christian and refusing to offer sacrifice to the idols, she was beaten mercilessly with rods and subjected to other torments, and was then cast into prison, where, worn out by her wounds and her bonds, she gave up her soul to God about the year 286.
Martyr Domnina of Anazarbus.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Dedication of the Church of the Greatmar.life: On this day the Church commemorates the consecration of the church of the Holy Great Martyr George at Kyiv. It was the pious custom of the princes of Rus, beginning with Saint Vladimir, to raise churches in honor of their patron saints: Vladimir, named Basil in baptism, built temples of Saint Basil at Kyiv and Vyshgorod, and his sons followed him in this;.
Dedication of the Church of the Greatmar.patron: Invoked for the veneration of the Great Martyr George in Rus; churches built in thanksgiving.
Dedication of the Church of the Greatmar.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Philogonius, Bishop of Antioch.life: Saint Philogonius, Bishop of Antioch, was raised to that great see straight from the law courts, and the leap tells his character: as an advocate he had been famed through the city as the defender of the wronged, the poor man's lawyer whose eloquence was a shelter, and whose private life, a husband and father of blameless virtue, matched his public justice;.
Saint Philogonius, Bishop of Antioch.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Abramius, Archimandrite of Ros.life: Saint Abramius, Archimandrite of Rostov, labored in the early generations after the Baptism of Rus, when in the Rostov land many still clung to the old gods, and at the Chudskoy end of the city there stood a stone idol of Veles to which the people offered worship.
Venerable Abramius, Archimandrite of Ros.patron: Invoked for missionaries; the overthrow of idols.
Venerable Abramius, Archimandrite of Ros.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Probus, Tarachus, and Andronicus.life: The Holy Martyrs Probus, Tarachus, and Andronicus suffered in Cilicia in the year 304, in the persecution under Diocletian. Tarachus was an aged Roman soldier of sixty-five years, who had left the army rather than deny Christ; Probus was a man of Side, who forsook wealth for the faith;.
Martyrs Probus, Tarachus, and Andronicus.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Cyprian, Bishop of Carthage.life: The Hieromartyr Cyprian, Bishop of Carthage, one of the greatest Fathers of the early Church, was born about the year 200 in that city, the son of a wealthy pagan senator, and became a celebrated teacher of rhetoric and philosophy and an advocate in the courts. For long, as he later confessed, he remained in a deep darkness, far from the light of truth, and his riches and pleasures could not quench his thirst for something higher;.
Hieromartyr Cyprian, Bishop of Carthage.patron: Invoked for theologians; the unity of the Church.
Hieromartyr Cyprian, Bishop of Carthage.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Damian the Healer, Jeremiah, a.life: Saints Damian the Presbyter and Healer, Jeremiah and Matthew the Clairvoyants, ascetics of the Near Caves of Kyiv, were described by Saint Nestor the Chronicler among the first generation of the disciples of Saints Anthony and Theodosius. Damian, a zealous imitator of Theodosius, was gentle, industrious, and obedient, passing whole nights in prayer and the reading of the Scriptures and eating nothing but bread and water;.
Venerable Damian the Healer, Jeremiah, a.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Abramius the Wonderworker, Arc.life: Saint Abramius of Smolensk was a preacher of repentance and of the dread Last Judgment, born in the middle of the twelfth century to wealthy parents who, having twelve daughters, had long begged God for a son. From childhood he loved the church and the reading of books, and after his parents' death he gave away all his wealth to monasteries, churches, and the poor, and went about the city in rags, entreating God to show him the way of salvation.
Venerable Abramius the Wonderworker, Arc.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Holy Righteous Joseph the Betrothed.life: The Holy Righteous Joseph the Betrothed, of the royal line of David, was a carpenter of Nazareth, an aged widower with sons and daughters, among them James, Joses, Simon, and Jude, whom the Gospels call the brothers of the Lord; and to him, as to a proven guardian, the priests of the Temple betrothed the Virgin Mary when her years of dwelling in the sanctuary were fulfilled, a betrothal that was a guardianship, the just man receiving the treasure of Israel to protect her vow.
Holy Righteous Joseph the Betrothed.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Prophet Jonah.life: The Holy Prophet Jonah, son of Amathi, was of Gath-hepher in Galilee and prophesied in the eighth century before Christ, and his book is read in the Church above all at the Paschal vigil, for in him the Lord Himself gave the sign of His own death and Resurrection.
Prophet Jonah.patron: Invoked for repentance; those in the deep.
Prophet Jonah.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Simeon, Wonderworker of Verkho.life: On this day the Church keeps the glorification of Righteous Simeon of Verkhoturye, wonderworker of the Urals and all Siberia, whose relics were solemnly translated and glorified on the eighteenth of December 1694. Born of noble family in European Russia, Simeon buried his rank in the deepest hiding place available to a Russian nobleman, the life of a.
Righteous Simeon, Wonderworker of Verkho.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Philip, Abbot of Irap Near Novgoro.life: Saint Philip of Irap, in the world Theophilus, never knew his parents: an orphan begging his bread, the twelve-year-old boy wandered until he settled near the Komel monastery, living on the charity of the brethren; and Saint Cornelius of Komel, who had built an orphanage in his monastery courtyard and loved the poor as Christ's own, received the child, discerned the grace upon him, and in time tonsured him with the name Philip.
Saint Philip, Abbot of Irap Near Novgoro.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saints Eutychius and Florentius of Nursi.life: Saints Eutychius and Florentius were monks who lived an ascetic life in a monastery near Nursia in Italy during the sixth century, and their memory is preserved in the Dialogues of Saint Gregory. Saint Eutychius drew many to God by his teaching, and when the abbot of a neighboring monastery died he was asked to guide that community as its superior.
Saints Eutychius and Florentius of Nursi.patron: Invoked for monastics; rain in drought.
Saints Eutychius and Florentius of Nursi.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Tryphaίnē at Cyzicus.life: The Holy Martyr Tryphaena of Cyzicus, the city on the Hellespont, was the daughter of the senator Anastasios and his devout wife Sokratia, and was raised in a piety that her contest made public; for when persecution fell on the city and she saw the weak among the Christians trembling toward denial, Tryphaena did not wait to be found but confessed her faith boldly and openly, proclaiming Christ and the final triumph of His truth precisely in order to strengthen the wavering, the strong soul volunteering as the example the frightened needed.
Martyr Tryphaίnē at Cyzicus.patron: Invoked for nursing mothers; women who strengthen the weak.
Martyr Tryphaίnē at Cyzicus.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Dionysius the Areopagite, Bi.life: The Hieromartyr Dionysius the Areopagite was a noble Athenian, learned in all the wisdom of the Greeks, who as a young man studying at Heliopolis in Egypt beheld the darkness that covered the earth at the hour of the Crucifixion and said, Either God is suffering, or the world is coming to its end.
Hieromartyr Dionysius the Areopagite, Bi.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Philip, Bishop of Heraclea a.life: Saint Philip, Bishop of Heraclea, suffered for Christ in the city of Philippopolis in Thrace, together with a great company of the faithful, in the persecution under Diocletian. Among them was Saint Severus, who had brought the centurion Memnon to faith in Christ; and when this was made known to the governor, he gave the soldier over to torture, and Severus also was cruelly tormented, raked with iron hooks, burned with red-hot rings and an iron belt, and at the last deprived of his sight.
Hieromartyr Philip, Bishop of Heraclea a.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Gerasimus the New Ascetic of C.life: Saint Gerasimus the New Ascetic of Cephalonia, the great wonderworker of that island, was born in 1506 at Trikala in the Peloponnese of the noble house of Notaras. Becoming a monk on the island of Zakynthos, he was perfected on the Holy Mountain of Athos, where he received the great schema;.
Venerable Gerasimus the New Ascetic of C.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Babylas, Bishop of Antioch,.life: The Hieromartyr Babylas, Bishop of Antioch, suffered under the emperor Decius together with the three young brothers Urban, Prilidian, and Epolonius and their mother Christodula. When the emperor, during a pagan festival in the city, sought out of curiosity to enter the church where the holy bishop was serving the Divine Liturgy, Babylas went out and barred his way, refusing to allow the impious ruler into the temple of God;.
Hieromartyr Babylas, Bishop of Antioch,.patron: Invoked for boldness before rulers; steadfast confession.
Hieromartyr Babylas, Bishop of Antioch,.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Alexander, Bishop of Jerusal.life: The Hieromartyr Alexander, Bishop of Jerusalem, was formed at the catechetical school of Alexandria under Clement, a fellow student and lifelong friend of Origen, and became bishop of a city in Cappadocia, where the persecution of Septimius Severus put him in chains for years, a confessor before he was a hierarch.
Hieromartyr Alexander, Bishop of Jerusal.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Icon of the Mother of God of Rzhevsk.life: The Rzhev Icon of the Mother of God, also called the Okovetskaya, appeared in the year 1539 in a forest near the town of Rzhev, where a wonderworking cross and an icon of the Mother of God with Saint Nicholas were discovered upon a tree. Many healings were granted to those who came in faith, and word of the wonders spread, so that the holy images were brought for a time to Moscow and venerated with honor before being returned to the place of their appearance.
Icon of the Mother of God of Rzhevsk.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Sebastian Dabovich.life: Saint Sebastian of Jackson and San Francisco, the Apostle of the Americas, was born Jovan Dabovich on the twenty-first of June 1863 in San Francisco, to Serbian immigrant parents, and was the first person born in the United States to be ordained to the Orthodox priesthood, so that in him American Orthodoxy beholds its own first fruits.
Venerable Sebastian Dabovich.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Nektarios, Metropolitan of Pentapo.life: Saint Nektarios of Aegina, one of the most beloved wonderworkers of modern times, was born Anastasios Kephalas in 1846 at Selymbria in Thrace to a poor and pious family. After laboring to educate himself in Constantinople and teaching on Chios, he became a monk there in 1876 and was later ordained, and under the patronage of the Patriarch of Alexandria he studied theology at Athens and served with distinction in Egypt, where in 1889 he was consecrated Metropolitan of Pentapolis.
Saint Nektarios, Metropolitan of Pentapo.patron: Invoked for those seeking work; cancer and grave illness.
Saint Nektarios, Metropolitan of Pentapo.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Bassian of Tiksnensk, Vologda.life: Saint Bassian of Tiksnensk was a peasant of the Vologda lands who worked as a tailor near Totma before forsaking the world; received into the Totma monastery of the Savior, he was tonsured and after some years, seeking greater stillness, settled by the river Tiksna near a church of Saint Nicholas, where he built a cell and lived in complete solitude.
Venerable Bassian of Tiksnensk, Vologda.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Arcadius of Novotorsk.life: Saint Arcadius of Novotorsk was born at the beginning of the eleventh century in the city of Vyazma, of a pious merchant family, and in his youth he took up the hard exploit of folly for Christ. Before every procession of the Cross he would take a broom and sweep the streets for two days beforehand, from the cathedral to the church, teaching by this that the soul must be made clean and the commandments kept before the coming of a feast.
Venerable Arcadius of Novotorsk.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Ananias of Persia.life: The Holy Martyr Ananias of Persia confessed Christ in the land of the fire-worshippers and sealed his confession with his blood. Seized and commanded to deny the Lord, he refused, and was given over to torments; and in the midst of his sufferings God opened his eyes, so that the martyr cried out before all, I see a ladder leading to heaven, and radiant men calling me to a marvelous city of light.
Martyr Ananias of Persia.patron: Invoked for visions granted to the suffering.
Martyr Ananias of Persia.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Gregory the Decapolite.life: Saint Gregory the Decapolite was born at Irenopolis, in the Decapolis of Isauria, and fleeing in his youth from the marriage his parents had arranged, he gave himself to God in the monastic life, formed under a discerning elder and tried by years of seclusion in a cave, where he endured the open assaults of the demons and was granted visions of grace.
Venerable Gregory the Decapolite.patron: Invoked for travelers for the truth; the defense of the holy icons.
Venerable Gregory the Decapolite.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Cyril the Wonderworker, Abbot.life: Venerable Cyril the Wonderworker of Novoezersk was marked by God before he drew breath: as his mother stood praying in church at the Divine Liturgy, the infant in her womb cried out, Holy, Holy, Holy, Lord of Sabaoth, the unborn child joining the angelic hymn, and the parents understood that the boy was not theirs to keep.
Venerable Cyril the Wonderworker, Abbot.patron: Invoked for founders; children marked for God.
Venerable Cyril the Wonderworker, Abbot.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Hilarion, Metropolitan of Suzdal a.life: Saint Hilarion, Metropolitan of Suzdal and Yuriev, was born in 1631 in the Nizhny Novgorod lands, the son of a priest, and took the monastic path in his youth; and his first great work was the Florishchev hermitage of the Dormition near Gorokhovets, which he built up from a poor forest settlement into a flourishing monastery, laboring with.
Saint Hilarion, Metropolitan of Suzdal a.patron: Invoked for builders of churches; prisoners.
Saint Hilarion, Metropolitan of Suzdal a.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Procession of the Honorable Wood of the.life: On the first of August the Church celebrates the Procession of the Precious and Life-giving Cross of the Lord, the first of the three Feasts of the Savior kept in this month and the day on which the Dormition Fast begins. The feast has its origin in the imperial city of Constantinople, where, because of the sicknesses that came with the heat of August, it was the custom to carry the venerable Wood of the Cross in procession through the streets for the sanctification of the city and the deliverance of the people from disease.
Procession of the Honorable Wood of the.patron: Invoked for deliverance from sickness; sanctification of the waters.
Procession of the Honorable Wood of the.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Paul the Confessor, Archbishop of.life: Saint Paul the Confessor, Archbishop of Constantinople, a native of Thessalonica, served as secretary to Alexander, the aged archbishop of the capital, who on his deathbed named him worthiest of the throne; and Paul was elected in 337, in the years when the Arian heresy, favored by the emperor Constantius, held power in the palaces though not in the truth.
Saint Paul the Confessor, Archbishop of.patron: Invoked for hierarchs; the Nicene faith.
Saint Paul the Confessor, Archbishop of.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Alexander, Bishop of Adriano.life: The Holy Martyrs Alexander the Bishop, Heraclius the soldier, and the women Anna, Elizabeth, Theodota, and Glyceria suffered at Adrianopolis in Thrace in the age of the persecutions.
