Alexander, bishop of that city, proclaimed the Gospel with boldness and refused to offer sacrifice to the idols, for which he was subjected to prolonged and savage tortures;.
Hieromartyr Alexander, Bishop of Adriano.patron: Invoked for conversion through the witness of martyrs.
Hieromartyr Alexander, Bishop of Adriano.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Fulvian (in Baptism Matthew), Prin.life: Saint Fulvian, Prince of Ethiopia, named Matthew in holy baptism, was the very ruler who put the Apostle Matthew to death, and by the mercy of God became the heir of his victim's apostleship. Though the apostle had healed his wife and son of unclean spirits, Fulvian, fearing for the gods of his fathers, accused him of sorcery and condemned him to the fire;.
Saint Fulvian (in Baptism Matthew), Prin.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Manetha of Cæsarea in Palestine.life: The Holy Martyr Manetha suffered at Caesarea in Palestine about the year 308, in the persecution under Maximinus, being seized together with the holy martyrs Antoninus, Nikephoros, and Germanus, who are commemorated with her on this day. A virgin consecrated to Christ, she was subjected to many tortures to break her constancy;.
Martyr Manetha of Cæsarea in Palestine.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Eutyches, disciple of Saint.life: The Hieromartyr Eutyches was a disciple of the holy Apostles John the Theologian and Paul, and though he was not among the Seventy, he is honored with the name of Apostle for his labors alongside them, by whom he was made a bishop. Born in the city of Sebastea in Samaria, he first followed the Apostle John, and afterward, meeting the Apostle Paul, he preached the Gospel together with him in his journeys, and he traveled through many lands proclaiming Christ and casting down the temples of the idols.
Hieromartyr Eutyches, disciple of Saint.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Alypius the Stylite of Adriano.life: Saint Alypius the Stylite was born at Adrianopolis in Paphlagonia; his mother, widowed early, gave her son to be raised by the bishop Theodore, distributed her substance to the poor, and served the church as a deaconess, teaching her child renunciation by living it. Longing from youth for the solitary life, Alypius was shown his path by the holy Martyr Euphemia, who appeared to him in a vision as he journeyed toward Constantinople, bidding him return and build her a church in his own city;.
Venerable Alypius the Stylite of Adriano.patron: Invoked for stylites; endurance unto extreme old age.
Venerable Alypius the Stylite of Adriano.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr and Archdeacon Laurence, and thos.life: The Holy Archdeacon Laurence and those with him suffered at Rome in the year 258, in the persecution under the emperor Valerian. Saint Sixtus, an Athenian who had been a philosopher before becoming a Christian, was then Bishop of Rome, and when he was seized with his deacons Felicissimus and Agapitus, Laurence followed him weeping and begging to.
Martyr and Archdeacon Laurence, and thos.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Antiochus and Antoninus, ascet.life: Venerable Antiochus and Antoninus, ascetics of the Syrian deserts, are commemorated on this day among the company of open-air hermits whose lives the blessed Theodoret of Cyrrhus gathered into his history of the monks of Syria, the generation of athletes who filled the hills of that country in the fifth century with a warfare the cities below could scarcely imagine.
Venerable Antiochus and Antoninus, ascet.patron: Invoked for companions in asceticism; the open sky endured together.
Venerable Antiochus and Antoninus, ascet.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Apostle Onesimus of the Seventy.type: Apostle of the Seventy, Martyr · 2nd c.
Apostle Onesimus of the Seventy.life: The Holy Apostle Onesimus of the Seventy is the one man in the New Testament who is also its subject, for the shortest of Paul's epistles was written entirely about him. A slave of Philemon, the Christian of Colossae, Onesimus wronged his master and fled, and the runaway's road ended, by the providence that governs such roads, in Rome, at the feet of the imprisoned Paul;.
Apostle Onesimus of the Seventy.patron: Invoked for servants; the formerly enslaved.
Apostle Onesimus of the Seventy.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

New Martyr Anastasius of Epirus.life: The Holy New Martyr Anastasius of Paramythia in Epirus suffered under the Ottoman yoke in the year 1750. A young Greek Christian of that town, he was seized by the men of the local ruler and, being falsely accused, was given the choice that broke or crowned so many of his generation: to embrace Islam and live in honor, or to remain a Christian and die.
New Martyr Anastasius of Epirus.patron: Invoked for the enslaved Church; witness that converts the persecutor's house.
New Martyr Anastasius of Epirus.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Arsenius of Novgorod the Fool-.life: Saint Arsenius, Fool-for-Christ of Novgorod, embraced for the love of God the hard and humbling path of folly, hiding his holiness beneath the appearance of madness and enduring cold, hunger, and the scorn of men. Living at Great Novgorod in the sixteenth century, in the fearful days of Tsar Ivan the Terrible, he was granted the gifts of prophecy and boldness, and it is recounted that he did not shrink from speaking hard truths even to the powerful of the earth.
Venerable Arsenius of Novgorod the Fool-.patron: Commemorated in the holy calendar of the Church.
Venerable Arsenius of Novgorod the Fool-.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Theocteristus, Abbot of Symbol.life: Venerable Theocteristus was abbot of the monastery of Symbola on the Bithynian Olympus, that holy mountain which in the eighth and ninth centuries was the greatest nursery of monasticism in the Christian East, its slopes filled with lavras and cells, its monasteries the strongholds of the faith through the iconoclast storms.
Venerable Theocteristus, Abbot of Symbol.patron: Invoked for abbots; fidelity under iconoclasm.
Venerable Theocteristus, Abbot of Symbol.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Zoticus the Keeper of Orphans.life: The Hieromartyr Zoticus, Keeper of Orphans, was an illustrious and wealthy Roman in the service of Saint Constantine the Great, and came with the emperor to the new capital on the Bosphorus, where he was ordained priest and where his riches found their vocation. When an edict, dreading contagion, condemned the lepers of the city to be drowned, Zoticus went to the emperor and asked for gold to purchase precious stones and pearls for the imperial glory;.
Martyr Zoticus the Keeper of Orphans.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Athanasius, Abbot of Bretsk.life: The Hieromartyr Athanasius, Abbot of Brest, was born about 1597 of a pious Belarusian family named Philippovich and received a thorough education, serving in his youth as a teacher before receiving the tonsure at the Vilna monastery of the Holy Spirit. Ordained hieromonk and later made head of the monastery of Saint Simeon at Brest, he became one of the boldest defenders of Orthodoxy in the lands seized by the Polish crown, where the Union of Brest was being imposed upon the faithful by force.
Martyr Athanasius, Abbot of Bretsk.patron: Invoked for defense of Orthodoxy; boldness before rulers.
Martyr Athanasius, Abbot of Bretsk.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

The Placing of the Cincture (Sash) of th.life: On this day the Church commemorates the Placing of the venerable Cincture, or sash, of the Most Holy Theotokos in the Church of the Mother of God at Chalkoprateia in Constantinople. According to tradition the Theotokos, at her Dormition, gave her cincture to the Apostle Thomas, and it was afterward brought to the imperial city and kept in a sealed reliquary, having been carried there from Zela in Cappadocia in the days of the emperors of the house of Theodosius.
The Placing of the Cincture (Sash) of th.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Monastic Martyr Anastasia of Rome.life: The Holy Monastic Martyr Anastasia the Roman was orphaned at three years of age and raised in a community of virgins near Rome by the holy eldress Sophia, who formed her in prayer, fasting, and the love of Christ, so that as she grew the beauty of her soul outshone the great beauty of her face.
Monastic Martyr Anastasia of Rome.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Menas, Patriarch of Constantinople.life: Saint Menas, Patriarch of Constantinople, was at first a presbyter of that city and the warden of the hospice of Saint Sampson, where in the days of the emperor Justinian he cared for the poor and the sick with great compassion. When the patriarch Anthimus was deposed for secretly holding the Monophysite error, Menas, a man of proven holiness, was chosen in his place and consecrated by Pope Agapetus of Rome, who was then in the imperial city;.
Saint Menas, Patriarch of Constantinople.patron: Invoked for the poor and sick; charity.
Saint Menas, Patriarch of Constantinople.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Greatmartyr Niketas the Goth.life: The Holy Great Martyr Niketas was a Goth, born and dwelling on the banks of the Danube, and he was baptized by Theophilus, Bishop of the Goths, who had taken part in the First Ecumenical Council. When war divided his people and the pagan chieftain Athanaric raised a fierce persecution against the Christians among the Goths, Niketas, who by his preaching and holy life had brought many of his kinsmen to Christ, became a pillar of the persecuted Church, strengthening the faithful for martyrdom and boldly denouncing the persecutor for his cruelty and impiety.
Greatmartyr Niketas the Goth.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Isaac the Recluse of the Kyiv.life: Venerable Isaac the Recluse of the Kyiv Near Caves was the first of the Caves' deceived solitaries, and the Paterikon tells his fall and his victory with equal honesty, because the Church needs both halves. A wealthy merchant of Toropets, he gave away everything, came to Saint Anthony, and outran everyone in severity: walled into a cell four cubits wide, wearing a raw goatskin that dried onto his body, eating one prosphora every second day, he prayed without lying down for seven years;.
Venerable Isaac the Recluse of the Kyiv.patron: Invoked for the deceived and restored; kitchen workers.
Venerable Isaac the Recluse of the Kyiv.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Limnaeus, Hermit of Syria.life: Venerable Limnaeus, Hermit of Syria, began his ascetic course under Saint Thalassius on the hill by Targala, dwelling with him long enough, as the historian Theodoret records, to acquire the virtues of his teacher, simplicity of manner, gentleness, and humility, the disciple copying not the elder's austerities first but his character, which is the right order;.
Venerable Limnaeus, Hermit of Syria.patron: Invoked for the blind; open-air ascetics.
Venerable Limnaeus, Hermit of Syria.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Cassian of Uglich.life: Saint Cassian of Uglich, called the Greek, was in the world Constantine, a descendant of the Greek princes of Mangup in the Crimea, and came to Russia in the suite that accompanied the princess Sophia Palaiologina to her marriage with the Great Prince of Moscow. Honored at court and offered high station, he chose instead the company of holy men, withdrawing with Archbishop Joasaph to the Ferapontov monastery on the White Lake;.
Venerable Cassian of Uglich.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Julian the Hermit of Mesopotam.life: Saint Julian the Hermit of Mesopotamia, whom the people called Sabas, the Elder, set up his cell in the desert of Osrhoene by the Euphrates, finding a cave not made by hands in the depth of the wilderness, which he prized above palaces of gold; and there for half a century he labored in fasting and unceasing prayer, his food bread of millet with salt, his drink water, taken once in the week.
Venerable Julian the Hermit of Mesopotam.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Child Artemius of Verkola.life: The Holy Righteous Child Artemius of Verkola was born about 1532 in a village on the Pinega river in the far north, the son of pious peasants, and from his earliest years he was meek, obedient, prayerful, and diligent in every good work, a child unlike other children.
Righteous Child Artemius of Verkola.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Uncovering of the relics of the Holy Mar.life: On this day the Church commemorates the uncovering of the relics of the Holy Martyrs at the Gate of Eugenius in Constantinople, one of the quiet feasts by which the Church confesses that the ground of the Christian city is an unread reliquary. In the days of the emperor Arcadius, at the beginning of the fifth century, healings began to occur by the gate and tower of Eugenius at the edge of the capital, grace breaking out of unmarked earth;.
Uncovering of the relics of the Holy Mar.patron: Invoked for the forgotten faithful; archaeologists of holiness.
Uncovering of the relics of the Holy Mar.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Gregory, Abbot of Pelsheme and.life: Saint Gregory of Pelsheme, wonderworker of Vologda, was born of the boyar family of the Lopotovs in the principality of Galich, and refusing in his youth both marriage and inheritance, he received the monastic tonsure and so shone in virtue that he was made abbot and offered still higher honor, from which he fled into the northern forests.
Venerable Gregory, Abbot of Pelsheme and.patron: Invoked for monastics; boldness before princes.
Venerable Gregory, Abbot of Pelsheme and.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Repose of Saint John Chrysostom, Archbis.life: Saint John Chrysostom, called the Golden-mouthed for his unrivaled eloquence and honored as one of the Three Holy Hierarchs, was born at Antioch about the year 347 and raised in piety by his widowed mother Anthusa. Trained in rhetoric under the famed Libanius, he forsook a brilliant worldly career, was baptized by Saint Meletius, and gave himself to the ascetic life in the hermitages near Antioch, until his health failed and he returned to the city, where he was ordained deacon and then priest.
Repose of Saint John Chrysostom, Archbis.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable John the Long-Suffering of the.life: Saint John the Much-Suffering struggled at the Kyiv Caves Lavra, and he bears his name from the fierce and lifelong warfare he waged for the sake of purity. From his youth he was tormented by the passion of the flesh, and neither hunger nor thirst nor the wearing of heavy chains could deliver him from it.
Venerable John the Long-Suffering of the.patron: Invoked for chastity; those tempted by lust.
Venerable John the Long-Suffering of the.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Anna.life: The Holy Martyr Anna was a noblewoman of Constantinople who, kindled with love for Christ, sold all her possessions, gave the money to the poor, and received the monastic tonsure from Saint Stephen the New while he labored on Mount Auxentius, who sent her to the women's monastery called Trichinarion, where she shone in fasting and obedience.
Martyr Anna.patron: Invoked for nuns; the refusal of false witness.
Martyr Anna.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Polycarp, Bishop of Smyrna.life: The Hieromartyr Polycarp, Bishop of Smyrna, is the great hinge between the apostles and the Church of the ages: a disciple of John the Theologian himself, appointed to the see of Smyrna in the succession of Bucolus, the friend to whom the condemned Ignatius wrote from the road, Stand firm as an anvil under the hammer, and the.
Hieromartyr Polycarp, Bishop of Smyrna.patron: Invoked for bishops; the aged faithful.
Hieromartyr Polycarp, Bishop of Smyrna.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Forefeast of the Nativity of the Mother.life: This is the Forefeast of the Nativity of the Most Holy Theotokos, on which the Church begins to celebrate the first of the great feasts of the new ecclesiastical year, the birth of the Mother of God from the righteous Joachim and Anna. On this day the hymns of the coming feast begin to sound in the services, calling the faithful to prepare their hearts to greet the Virgin whose birth announced to the world the approach of its salvation.
Forefeast of the Nativity of the Mother.patron: Commemorated in the holy calendar of the Church.
Forefeast of the Nativity of the Mother.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Repose of the Holy Right-believing Princ.life: The Holy Princess Anna of Kashin was the daughter of Prince Demetrius of Rostov, and in 1294 became the wife of the holy Great Prince Michael of Tver. God appointed her a life of almost unbroken sorrow: she buried her infant daughter and her father, saw Tver burn and pestilence sweep the land, and in 1318 her husband was tortured and murdered at the Horde for refusing to save himself at his people's cost;.
Repose of the Holy Right-believing Princ.patron: Invoked for widows; those bereaved by violence.
Repose of the Holy Right-believing Princ.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Apostle Titus of the Seventy and Bishop.life: The Holy Apostle Titus, one of the Seventy, was a native of Crete and the son of a distinguished pagan family, and in his youth he studied the philosophy and poetry of the Greeks while keeping himself from their vices. Drawn to the truth, he became a disciple and beloved co-worker of the Apostle Paul, who called him his true son in the common faith and made him the first Bishop of Crete;.
Apostle Titus of the Seventy and Bishop.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Maruthas, Bishop of Martyropolis i.life: Saint Maruthas, Bishop of Martyropolis, was the physician-diplomat whom God stationed at the hinge of two empires, shepherd of Mayperqat on the Roman-Persian frontier at the turn of the fifth century, learned in medicine, in Syriac letters, and in the ways of courts. Twice the emperors of Constantinople sent him as ambassador to the Persian king Yazdegerd, and.
Saint Maruthas, Bishop of Martyropolis i.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Translation of the relics of Venerable T.life: On this day the Church commemorates the translation of the relics of Venerable Theodore, abbot of the Studios, whose principal feast is kept in November; the January commemoration remembers the day the great confessor came home. Theodore had spent his life defending the holy icons and the freedom of the Church against emperors, enduring scourgings, prisons, and repeated exiles, and had reposed in 826 in banishment, far from his monastery, in the years when iconoclasm still held the palace;.
Translation of the relics of Venerable T.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Therapon, Abbot of Monza.life: Saint Therapon of Monza labored in the second half of the sixteenth century, formed in the monastic life in the region of Moscow, where he cherished the memory and the example of Blessed Basil, the great fool for Christ; and seeking stillness, he withdrew to the northern forests of the Kostroma country, settling at the monastery on the river Monza near Galich, which afterward bore his name.
Venerable Therapon, Abbot of Monza.patron: Invoked for farmers in famine; warning before calamity.
Venerable Therapon, Abbot of Monza.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Stephen, Abbot of Makhrishche,.life: Saint Stephen of Makhrishche was a native of Kyiv who received the monastic tonsure at the Monastery of the Caves, where he passed several years in obedience and prayer. When the oppression of the Latins made life difficult, he journeyed north to Moscow, where the Grand Prince Ivan received him kindly and allowed him to settle in the wilderness of Makhra, not far from the monastery of Saint Sergius of Radonezh, with whom he became a friend and fellow laborer in the monastic life.
Venerable Stephen, Abbot of Makhrishche,.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Holy Wonderworking Unmercenary Physician.life: The Holy Martyrs and Unmercenary Physicians Cosmas and Damian of Rome were brothers, born at Rome and trained as physicians, who received from God the gift of healing. Taking no payment for their care of the sick, for which they are called unmercenary, they treated all who came in the name of Christ and drew many to the faith.
Holy Wonderworking Unmercenary Physician.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Hosius the Confessor, Bishop of Có.life: Saint Hosius the Confessor was bishop of Cordoba in Spain for more than sixty years during the fourth century, and he was so esteemed for his wisdom and holiness that the emperor Saint Constantine the Great made him one of his closest counselors. It was Hosius who advised the emperor to summon the First Ecumenical Council at Nicaea against the heresy of Arius, and at that great council, where the Son was confessed to be of one essence with the Father, he was among the foremost of the fathers.
Saint Hosius the Confessor, Bishop of Có.patron: Invoked for Orthodoxy against heresy; the Council of Nicaea.
Saint Hosius the Confessor, Bishop of Có.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Anthony of the Kyiv Far Caves,.life: Saint Anthony, the founder of monasticism in the land of Rus, was born in the year 983 at Liubech near Chernigov and named Antipas in baptism. Drawn from his youth to the monastic life, he journeyed to Mount Athos, where he was tonsured and trained in the ascetic struggle, until the abbot, moved by God, sent him back to his homeland to plant there the monastic way.
Venerable Anthony of the Kyiv Far Caves,.patron: Invoked for monastics; monastic life in Rus.
Venerable Anthony of the Kyiv Far Caves,.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Theodotus, Bishop of Cyrenia.life: The Hieromartyr Theodotus, Bishop of Cyrenia in Cyprus, was a native of Galatia in Asia Minor who came to shepherd that Cypriot see in the last and worst season of the persecutions, when Licinius, breaking with his colleague Constantine, renewed in the East the terror the edict of Milan was supposed to have ended;.
Hieromartyr Theodotus, Bishop of Cyrenia.patron: Invoked for bishops under torture; those who outlive their persecutors.
Hieromartyr Theodotus, Bishop of Cyrenia.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Cyriacus of Tazlau, Romania.life: Venerable Cyriacus of Tazlău was born at the turn of the seventeenth century in the village of Mesteacăn in Moldavia, and being carried as a child by his parents to the services of the Tazlău monastery, the foundation of Stephen the Great, he felt his soul, as his life records, given wings by divine longing;.
Venerable Cyriacus of Tazlau, Romania.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Mother Olga of Kwethluk, Tanqi.life: The Holy Righteous Mother Olga of Kwethluk, Tanqilria Arrsamquq, Matushka of All Alaska, was born on the third of February 1916 in the Yup'ik village of Kwethluk on the Kuskokwim river, and her native name, Arrsamquq, means the lowly and hidden one, a prophecy of her whole life.
Righteous Mother Olga of Kwethluk, Tanqi.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Commemoration of the Holy Righteous Davi.life: In the days after the Nativity the Church commemorates together the Holy Righteous Joseph the Betrothed, David the King, and James the Brother of the Lord, the synaxis of the Lord's kin according to the flesh, appointed of old for the Sunday after the feast and kept also on this day.
Commemoration of the Holy Righteous Davi.patron: Invoked for families of the Lord's servants; kinship with Christ by obedience.
Commemoration of the Holy Righteous Davi.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Aithalas of Persia.life: The Holy Martyr Aithalas, a deacon of the Church in Persia, suffered for Christ in the year 380 during the persecution of the Christians under the emperor Sapor. Firmly confessing the faith and refusing to worship the fire and the sun as the Persians did, he was condemned by the king's order and put to death by stoning, and so received the crown of martyrdom.
Martyr Aithalas of Persia.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Anthony, Abbot of Siya, Novgor.life: Saint Anthony of Siya was born in 1477 in the village of Kekhta near the Northern Dvina, and named Andrew; gifted from youth, he learned the painting of icons as well as his letters, and after the early death of his young wife he turned wholly to God, receiving the tonsure with the name Anthony at the monastery of Saint Pachomius on the Kena.
Venerable Anthony, Abbot of Siya, Novgor.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Repose of Saint Cyprian, Metropolitan of.life: Saint Cyprian, Metropolitan of Kyiv and Moscow and of all Russia, was a Bulgarian by birth, of the city of Tarnovo, and was formed in the hesychast tradition, laboring as a monk on the Holy Mountain of Athos before being sent north by the Patriarch of Constantinople. Consecrated metropolitan in a time of division and turmoil, he endured.
Repose of Saint Cyprian, Metropolitan of.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Commemoration of the Vladimir Icon of th.life: The Vladimir Icon of the Most Holy Theotokos, according to tradition painted by the Evangelist Luke and brought from Constantinople to Rus, was set by Saint Andrew Bogolyubsky in the cathedral of Vladimir, from which it took its name, and it became the most beloved and protecting icon of the Russian land.
Commemoration of the Vladimir Icon of th.patron: Invoked for protection of Russia; deliverance from invasion.
Commemoration of the Vladimir Icon of th.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Repose of the Holy Apostle and Evangelis.life: The Holy Apostle and Evangelist John the Theologian, the beloved disciple, was the son of Zebedee and Salome and the brother of James, called from his nets on the sea of Galilee to follow Christ, and of all the disciples he lay closest to the breast of the Lord.
Repose of the Holy Apostle and Evangelis.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Finding of the relics of Saint Gamaliel.life: Saint Gamaliel was a Pharisee and a renowned doctor of the Law, honored among the Jews, who counseled moderation toward the apostles when they were brought before the council, as related in the Acts of the Apostles, and who had been the teacher of Saint Paul. In secret he became a disciple of Christ, and when the Protomartyr Stephen was stoned and left unburied, it was Gamaliel who reverently took up his body and laid it in a cave on his own land at Caphargamala.
Finding of the relics of Saint Gamaliel.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

“Virgin of Tenderness” Icon of the Mothe.life: The Tenderness Icon of the Most Holy Mother of God, of the Umilenie type in which the Christ Child presses His cheek to that of His Mother, belongs to the monastery of the Caves at Pskov, where it was brought in the early sixteenth century by pious Christians and became the protectress of the city.
“Virgin of Tenderness” Icon of the Mothe.patron: Invoked for protection of Pskov; deliverance from invasion.
“Virgin of Tenderness” Icon of the Mothe.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Leo of Cappadocia.life: Saint Leo of Cappadocia is remembered in the calendar for a single transaction, and it is the one the Lord Himself named as the ceiling of love. A monk of the Cappadocian country in the age of the Saracen raids, when the borderlands of Asia Minor lived under the perpetual scourge of slave-taking incursions, Leo saw the raiders carry off three of his brother monks, men sick and infirm, useless as laborers and therefore likely to be discarded in the desert the moment their weakness slowed the column;.
Saint Leo of Cappadocia.patron: Invoked for captives; those who ransom others.
Saint Leo of Cappadocia.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Thyrsos, Leukios, and Kallinikos.life: The Holy Martyrs Thyrsus, Leucius, and Callinicus suffered at Apollonia in Bithynia about the year 250, in the persecution of Decius. Leucius opened the contest: beholding the cruelties inflicted on the Christians, he rebuked the governor Cumbricius to his face for warring against God, and after tortures was beheaded, his boldness kindling the city.
Martyrs Thyrsos, Leukios, and Kallinikos.patron: Invoked for sawyers; priests converted from idols.
Martyrs Thyrsos, Leukios, and Kallinikos.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Nestor the Chronicler of the K.life: Saint Nestor the Chronicler, the father of Russian history, was born at Kyiv about the year 1050 and came at seventeen years of age to Saint Theodosius at the Caves monastery, receiving the tonsure under his successor Stephen, who also ordained him hierodeacon. Adorned with deep humility, which breathes through every page he wrote, he counted himself the.
Venerable Nestor the Chronicler of the K.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Benjamin of the Kyiv Caves.life: Saint Benjamin of the Kyiv Caves lived in the fourteenth century, and before receiving the monastic habit he was a great merchant, prospering in the affairs of this world. Once, standing at the divine services, he heard as if for the first time the words of the Savior, that a rich man shall hardly enter into the kingdom of heaven, and the word pierced his heart like a sword;.
Venerable Benjamin of the Kyiv Caves.patron: Invoked for merchants; renunciation of wealth.
Venerable Benjamin of the Kyiv Caves.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Blessed John “the Hairy” and Fool-For-Ch.life: Blessed John, called the Merciful and also the Hairy, took upon himself at Rostov the hard and hidden podvig of folly for Christ's sake, enduring cold, hunger, and reproach for the love of God. He had no home of his own, but found shelter now in the house of his spiritual father, a priest of the church of All Saints, now with one or another of the poor widows of the city;.
Blessed John “the Hairy” and Fool-For-Ch.patron: Invoked for humility; those without a home.
Blessed John “the Hairy” and Fool-For-Ch.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Menas, Hermogenes, and Eugraphus.life: The Holy Martyrs Menas, Hermogenes, and Eugraphus suffered at Alexandria about the year 313, under the emperor Maximian, and their contest is a chain of conversions forged under torture. Menas, an Athenian famed for eloquence, whom the Greeks call Kallikelados, the sweetly-speaking, was sent by the emperor to Alexandria to quiet the strife between pagans and Christians;.
Martyrs Menas, Hermogenes, and Eugraphus.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Nun-Martyr Eugenia of Rome.life: The Holy Nun-Martyr Eugenia was the daughter of Philip, governor of Egypt under the Romans, raised at Alexandria in all the learning of the age; and reading in secret the epistles of the Apostle Paul, the pagan governor's daughter conceived a love for Christ that overturned her life.
Nun-Martyr Eugenia of Rome.patron: Invoked for abbesses; women in disguise for God's sake.
Nun-Martyr Eugenia of Rome.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Commemoration of the Shepherds in Bethle.life: On the first day of the Nativity the Church commemorates the Shepherds of Bethlehem, who were keeping watch over their flocks by night in the fields when the glory of the Lord shone round about them, and they became the first of the human race to hear the Gospel preached.
Commemoration of the Shepherds in Bethle.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Tarasius, Archbishop of Constantin.life: Saint Tarasius, Archbishop of Constantinople, was the layman the Church drafted to end an heresy: first secretary of the empire, the most respected official of his generation, he was chosen for the widowed patriarchal throne in 784 by the empress Irene and the acclamation of the people while still unbaptized into any clerical order, and he accepted on a single, history-making condition, that an ecumenical council be convened to heal the schism of the icons and reunite the Church;.
Saint Tarasius, Archbishop of Constantin.patron: Invoked for patriarchs; statesmen called to the altar.
Saint Tarasius, Archbishop of Constantin.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Nestor of Thessalonica.life: The Holy Martyr Nestor of Thessalonica was a young Christian, fair in appearance and known to the Great Martyr Demetrios, who had instructed him in the faith. When the emperor Maximian held games in the city, his champion, a gigantic Vandal named Lyaeus, cast down challenger after challenger from a high platform onto upturned spears, to the emperor's delight and the destruction of many, among them Christians forced into the arena;.
Martyr Nestor of Thessalonica.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Holy Apostles Stakhys, Apelles, Amplias,.life: The Holy Apostles Stachys, Apelles, Amplias, Urban, and Narcissus of the Seventy are greeted by name in the Epistle of the Apostle Paul to the Romans, and the Church commemorates them together on this day with the Apostle Aristobulus. Stachys, whom Paul calls his beloved, was made by the Apostle Andrew the First-Called the first bishop of Byzantium, the small city that would one day be Constantinople, so that the throne of the ecumenical patriarchs traces its succession to him;.
Holy Apostles Stakhys, Apelles, Amplias,.patron: Invoked for bishops; the planting of local churches.
Holy Apostles Stakhys, Apelles, Amplias,.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Ananias the Presbyter, Peter, an.life: The Holy Martyrs Ananias the Presbyter, Peter the prison guard, and seven soldiers suffered in Phoenicia in the year 295, during the persecution under Diocletian. Ananias, a priest of that country, was arrested for confessing Christ and refusing the idols, and brought before Maximus, the governor of Phoenicia, who set upon him the full grammar of the tribunals: the presbyter was beaten with hammers, burned with fire, and had salt rubbed into his scorched flesh, and endured it all with the composure of a man whose treasure was elsewhere;.
Martyrs Ananias the Presbyter, Peter, an.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Holy, All-Praised Apostle Philip.life: The Holy and All-Praised Apostle Philip, one of the Twelve, was of Bethsaida in Galilee, the city of Andrew and Peter, and was versed from youth in the Scriptures; and when the Lord found him and said, Follow Me, Philip straightway found Nathanael and answered his doubts with the words that remain the whole method of the Gospel: Come and see.
Holy, All-Praised Apostle Philip.patron: Invoked for missionaries; the finding of Christ.
Holy, All-Praised Apostle Philip.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Prince Andrew, in Monasticism.life: Saint Joasaph of Kubensk, wonderworker of Vologda, was in the world the Prince Andrew, son of the pious Prince Demetrius of Lesser Zaozersk, a descendant of the holy Prince Theodore of Smolensk and Yaroslavl. Raised in deep piety, at twenty years of age he forsook his princely inheritance and received the tonsure with the name Joasaph at the Spaso-Kamenny monastery on the island in Lake Kubensk, being named for Joasaph, the prince of India who left his kingdom for Christ.
Venerable Prince Andrew, in Monasticism.patron: Invoked for monastics; youth given to God.
Venerable Prince Andrew, in Monasticism.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Monastic Martyr Andrew of Crete.life: The Holy Monastic Martyr Andrew of Crete, whom the Church distinguishes from the great hymnographer of the same name and island, was an ascetic of Crete in the days when the emperor Constantine Copronymus raged against the holy icons, torturing and killing the monks who defended them. Hearing of the sufferings of the confessors, Andrew left his stillness.
Monastic Martyr Andrew of Crete.patron: Invoked for the veneration of the holy icons; boldness before emperors.
Monastic Martyr Andrew of Crete.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Dormition of the Righteous Anna, the Mot.life: This feast commemorates the peaceful repose of the Righteous Anna, the mother of the Most Holy Theotokos and grandmother of our Lord according to the flesh. Anna was the daughter of the priest Matthan, of the tribe of Levi and the lineage of Aaron, and together with her husband, the Righteous Joachim, she bore for long years the reproach of childlessness, until in their old age God heard their prayers and granted them a daughter, the pure Virgin Mary, who was to become the Mother of God.
Dormition of the Righteous Anna, the Mot.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

“Enlightener of Minds” Icon of the Mothe.life: The icon of the Mother of God called the Enlightener of Minds depicts the Most Holy Theotokos together with her Divine Son, who is the fountain of all wisdom and understanding. Before this image the faithful pray for the enlightenment of the mind and heart by the truth of God, and parents whose children are slow to learn, whether in the things of the faith or in worldly knowledge, entreat the Mother of God that the minds of their children may be strengthened and that they may retain what they are taught.
“Enlightener of Minds” Icon of the Mothe.patron: Invoked for students; children slow to learn.
“Enlightener of Minds” Icon of the Mothe.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Translation of the Image “Not-Made-By-Ha.life: On this day the Church commemorates the translation of the Icon of our Lord Jesus Christ Not-Made-by-Hands from Edessa to Constantinople in the year 944, the third of the Feasts of the Savior kept in August. When the Lord was preaching in Galilee, Abgar, the ruler of Edessa, lay sick with leprosy, and having heard of the many miracles of Christ he sent a messenger to beg Him to come and heal him.
Translation of the Image “Not-Made-By-Ha.patron: Invoked for healing; the veneration of the holy icons.
Translation of the Image “Not-Made-By-Ha.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Theophanes the Merciful of Gaz.life: Saint Theophanes the Merciful was a citizen of Gaza, wealthy in goods and wealthier still in compassion. His house was open to every stranger and vagrant, he clothed the naked, fed the hungry, and tended the sick, and he poured out his whole substance in almsgiving until he himself was left in want;.
Venerable Theophanes the Merciful of Gaz.patron: Invoked for almsgivers; mercy to the poor.
Venerable Theophanes the Merciful of Gaz.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Barlaam of Caesarea, in Cappadoci.life: The Holy Martyr Barlaam was an aged Christian who suffered in the persecution under Diocletian, about the year 304; the ancient accounts place his contest at Caesarea in Cappadocia, or, as others relate, at Antioch. Arrested and brought to trial, the old man confessed himself a Christian in few and simple words, for he was unlearned;.
Martyr Barlaam of Caesarea, in Cappadoci.patron: Invoked for the aged; endurance in weakness.
Martyr Barlaam of Caesarea, in Cappadoci.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

45 Holy Martyrs at Nicopolis in Armenia.life: The Forty-five Holy Martyrs of Nicopolis in Armenia suffered under the emperor Licinius, who ruled the East and fiercely persecuted the Church, decreeing death for any Christian who would not return to the idols. When the persecution reached Nicopolis, more than forty faithful, led by Leontius, Mauricius, Daniel, Anthony, and Alexander, resolved not to hide but to present themselves openly before the persecutors and confess Christ.
45 Holy Martyrs at Nicopolis in Armenia.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Virgin Martyr Irais (Rhais) of Alexandri.life: The Holy Virgin Martyr Irais, also called Rhais, was a maiden of Alexandria in Egypt. Going out one day to draw water at the well, she saw at the shore a ship filled with confessors of Christ, priests, deacons, monks, and virgins, held in chains by the persecutors;.
Virgin Martyr Irais (Rhais) of Alexandri.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

First finding of the relics of Saint Met.life: Saint Metrophanes was the first Bishop of Voronezh, consecrated in 1682, and he was renowned for his deep piety, his care for the poor, and his zeal for the Church; a counselor and supporter of the emperor Peter the Great in the building of the Russian fleet at Voronezh, he did not fear to rebuke the sovereign when pagan statues were set up, and he was heard.
First finding of the relics of Saint Met.patron: Commemorated in the holy calendar of the Church.
First finding of the relics of Saint Met.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Gregory, Wonderworker of Neocaesar.life: Saint Gregory the Wonderworker, Bishop of Neocaesarea, was born of noble pagan parents in that city of Pontus, and seeking wisdom through the schools, he found it at last at Caesarea in Palestine at the feet of Origen, under whom he studied for years and through whom he came to Christ.
Saint Gregory, Wonderworker of Neocaesar.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Lupus.life: The Holy Martyr Lupus was the faithful servant of the Great Martyr Demetrios of Thessalonica, and stood by his master at his martyrdom. Dipping the hem of his garment and a ring in the blood of the great martyr, he kept these as a treasure; and through them the Lord wrought many miracles in Thessalonica, healings flowing from the blood of Demetrios by the hands of his servant, so that the whole city was stirred.
Martyr Lupus.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Apostles Patrobus, Hermes, Linus, Gaius,.life: The Holy Apostles Patrobus, Hermes, Linus, Gaius, and Philologus of the Seventy are greeted in the epistles of the Apostle Paul, and each served the Gospel as a bishop, enduring the labors and dangers of the Church's first age. Linus, whom Paul names in his last epistle, became after the martyrdom of the chief apostles the first bishop of Rome, governing the church of the imperial city in the years of Nero's persecution.
Apostles Patrobus, Hermes, Linus, Gaius,.patron: Invoked for bishops; the planting of the churches.
Apostles Patrobus, Hermes, Linus, Gaius,.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Xenophon of Robeika.life: Saint Xenophon of Robeika was a disciple of the great Varlaam of Khutyn, formed in the strictest school of the Novgorod land by the founder himself, and proved so worthy of his formation that the brotherhood raised him to be head of the Khutyn monastery after the igumen Isidore, the disciple governing the house of his master;.
Saint Xenophon of Robeika.patron: Invoked for abbots who begin again; founders.
Saint Xenophon of Robeika.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Holy Woman Olympias (Olympiada) the Deac.life: Saint Olympias was born at Constantinople of an illustrious senatorial family and was left in her youth a wealthy heiress. Betrothed to a noble prefect who died before their marriage was consummated, she counted herself a widow and, though the emperor and her kinsmen pressed her to marry again, she refused, choosing instead to dedicate herself wholly to God.
Holy Woman Olympias (Olympiada) the Deac.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

The Righteous Gideon.life: The Righteous Gideon, judge of Israel, was threshing wheat in the winepress to hide it from the Midianite raiders when the Angel of the Lord appeared to him and said, The Lord is with thee, thou mighty man of valor, commanding him to deliver Israel from the hand of Midian;.
The Righteous Gideon.patron: Invoked for soldiers; the fearful called to courage.
The Righteous Gideon.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Holy Empress Markianḗ.life: Saint Markiane the Empress was the wife of the emperor Justin the First, who reigned at Constantinople from 518 to 527, the soldier-emperor of peasant origins whose house God raised from the Balkan countryside to the purple; and Markiane, sharing that astonishing ascent, kept through it the virtues that thrones more often dissolve.
Holy Empress Markianḗ.patron: Invoked for women of rank; benefactresses.
Holy Empress Markianḗ.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Leavetaking of the Entry of the Most Hol.life: On this day the Church keeps the leavetaking, the apodosis, of the feast of the Entry of the Most Holy Theotokos into the Temple, gathering into a final celebration the grace of the festal days. Once more the services return to the hymns of the feast, and the Church beholds the three-year-old child led up the steps of the sanctuary, received by Zachariah, and brought into the Holy of Holies, the pure temple of the Savior entering the temple of the shadow, that the shadow might give way to the truth;.
Leavetaking of the Entry of the Most Hol.patron: Invoked for the sealing of the feast in the heart.
Leavetaking of the Entry of the Most Hol.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Persian Martyrs in Martyropolis in Mesop.life: The Holy Persian Martyrs in Martyropolis, commemorated together with Saint Maruthas who gathered them, are the host of those who suffered in the great persecution of the Persian empire, the longest the Church has ever endured, when for some forty years under Shapur the Second and his successors the Zoroastrian state set itself to destroy the Christians of Mesopotamia and Persia.
Persian Martyrs in Martyropolis in Mesop.patron: Invoked for the persecuted of the East; refugees of the faith.
Persian Martyrs in Martyropolis in Mesop.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Martha, mother of Saint Simeon.life: Saint Martha, the mother of Saint Simeon the Stylite, lived in Cilicia in the fourth and fifth centuries and came of a poor family, and with her husband Sisotion she raised the son who would become the wonder of his age. When Simeon was tonsured a monk without his parents' knowledge and mounted his pillar, Martha in later years came desiring to see him;.
Venerable Martha, mother of Saint Simeon.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Leavetaking of the Elevation of the Cros.life: This is the Leavetaking of the Feast of the Universal Exaltation of the Precious and Life-Giving Cross, the final day of the festal period of the Cross. The hymns of the Exaltation are sung once more in their fullness, and the faithful, having kept the feast through its afterfeast days, take their leave of the festival, venerating the holy Wood a last time before it is returned to the sanctuary.
Leavetaking of the Elevation of the Cros.patron: Commemorated in the holy calendar of the Church.
Leavetaking of the Elevation of the Cros.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Translation of the relics of Venerable J.life: On this day the Church commemorates the translation of the relics of Saint John of Rila, the heavenly protector of the Bulgarian people. Born about the year 876 in the village of Skrino, he kept his family's flocks as a poor orphan before forsaking all to become a monk;.
Translation of the relics of Venerable J.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Hezron.life: The Righteous Hezron, son of Perez and grandson of the Patriarch Judah, is one of the quiet bearers of the promise, a name that most readers pass over and heaven never did. He was among the souls of the house of Jacob who went down into Egypt in the days of Joseph, carried as a child into the land where the family of the promise would grow into a people;.
Righteous Hezron.patron: Invoked for the hidden links of God's promise.
Righteous Hezron.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Second Day of the Nativity of our Lord.life: The Second Day of the Nativity of our Lord continues the feast at full strength, for the Church does not celebrate the Incarnation in a day but dwells in it, repeating through all the days of the afterfeast the hymns of Bethlehem; and this second day carries its own commemorations.
Second Day of the Nativity of our Lord.patron: Commemorated in the holy calendar of the Church.
Second Day of the Nativity of our Lord.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Right-believing Prince Roman of Ryazan.life: The Holy Prince Roman Olegovich of Ryazan ruled his principality during the bitter years of the Tatar yoke, when the Russian lands lay under the domination of the Golden Horde. A pious and just ruler who defended his people and his faith, he was slandered before the Khan by envious men who accused him of reviling the Tatar religion.
Right-believing Prince Roman of Ryazan.patron: Invoked for confession of faith under persecution.
Right-believing Prince Roman of Ryazan.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Juvenal, Patriarch of Jerusalem.life: Saint Juvenal was Patriarch of Jerusalem through the middle years of the fifth century, occupying the throne of the Holy City for thirty-eight years, in an age adorned by such luminaries as Euthymios the Great, with whom he was a close friend. His episcopate fell in a time of great doctrinal struggle, and he took a leading part.
Saint Juvenal, Patriarch of Jerusalem.patron: Invoked for the defense of Orthodox doctrine.
Saint Juvenal, Patriarch of Jerusalem.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Theodore, Bishop of Edessa.life: Saint Theodore, Bishop of Edessa, was born in that Syrian city, and when at a young age he was left an orphan, he gave his inheritance to the poor and journeyed to Jerusalem, where he received the monastic tonsure at the Lavra of Saint Sabbas the Sanctified. For many years he labored there in stillness and asceticism, becoming a vessel of grace, until, against his own desire, he was chosen bishop of his native Edessa.
Saint Theodore, Bishop of Edessa.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Photius, Metropolitan of Kyiv.life: Saint Photius, Metropolitan of Kyiv and All Russia, was a Greek of Monembasia in the Peloponnese, who entered monastic life in his youth under a great ascetic elder. Renowned for his learning and holiness, he was chosen by the Patriarch of Constantinople to shepherd the Russian Church, and was consecrated Metropolitan in 1408, arriving in the land the following year.
Saint Photius, Metropolitan of Kyiv.patron: Invoked for the unity of the Church.
Saint Photius, Metropolitan of Kyiv.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Adrian, Abbot of Ondrusov, Val.life: Saint Adrian of Ondrusov, in the world the nobleman Andrei Zavalishin, owned a rich estate near the wilderness where Saint Alexander of Svir labored in solitude, and while hunting a stag in the forest he came upon the hidden ascetic; from that day he went often to Saint Alexander for counsel and brought bread to sustain him and the other hermits.
Venerable Adrian, Abbot of Ondrusov, Val.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Philaret the Merciful of Amnia.life: Righteous Philaret the Merciful, son of George and Anna, lived in the eighth century in the village of Amnia in Paphlagonia, a rich and honored man with a noble wife, Theoseba, and three children, John, Hypatia, and Evanthia; and holding fast the Savior's word about the least of His brethren, the Apostle's reminder that we carry nothing out of this world, and David's assurance that the righteous is not forsaken, he made his wealth a river for the poor until raids and losses left him nearly destitute, and then kept giving from the remnant.
Righteous Philaret the Merciful of Amnia.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Hippolytus, and those with h.life: The Hieromartyr Hippolytus of Rome suffered with the martyrs Censorinus, Sabinus, the virgin Chryse, and twenty others in the third century, about the year 269, under the emperor Claudius; and the company's contest began with a magistrate. Censorinus, a high-ranking official, was denounced as a Christian and imprisoned, and in the prison the grace of Christ worked through.
Hieromartyr Hippolytus, and those with h.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Mirax of Egypt.life: The Holy Martyr Mirax of Egypt is the martyr of the second chance, and his crown is the crown of repentance. Born at Tennis in Egypt of devout Christian parents in the years after the Saracen conquest, he fell in his youth: before the emir he renounced Christ, embraced the religion of the conquerors, and lived for years in his denial, while his father and mother, refusing both to disown him and to despair of him, besieged heaven with prayers and tears for their son.
Martyr Mirax of Egypt.patron: Invoked for repentance after apostasy; the return of those who denied.
Martyr Mirax of Egypt.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Julian, Bishop of Cenomanis (Le Ma.life: Saint Julian, first Bishop of Cenomanis in Gaul, the city now called Le Mans, was consecrated to the episcopate by the Apostle Peter and sent by him to preach the Gospel to the pagans of the West; and some hold that he is the same as Simon the Leper of the Gospel, who took the name Julian at his baptism.
Saint Julian, Bishop of Cenomanis (Le Ma.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Thomas of Mount Maleos.life: Saint Thomas of Mount Maleon was in his former life a soldier and a commander, distinguished and wealthy, who at the height of his worldly success turned his heart wholly to God. Renouncing his rank and distributing his goods to the poor, he embraced the monastic life, and, guided as tradition recounts by the Prophet Elijah, he withdrew to the solitude of Mount Maleon to give himself to prayer and ascetic struggle.
Venerable Thomas of Mount Maleos.patron: Commemorated in the holy calendar of the Church.
Venerable Thomas of Mount Maleos.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Paphnutius the Recluse of the.life: Venerable Paphnutius the Recluse of the Kyiv Caves labored in the thirteenth century in the Far Caves of Saint Theodosius, and the tradition of the Lavra remembers him by a single exploit carried to its perfection: Paphnutius wept. Enclosing himself in reclusion, he took as his one meditation the remembrance of death, the mnimi thanatou that the fathers.
Venerable Paphnutius the Recluse of the.patron: Invoked for mourners; those who keep the memory of death.
Venerable Paphnutius the Recluse of the.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Tabitha the Widow, raised from the.life: Saint Tabitha the Widow, whose name in Greek is Dorcas, that is, Gazelle, was a disciple of the Lord dwelling at Joppa in the days of the apostles, and the Scripture bears her this witness, that she was full of good works and almsdeeds which she did. With her own hands she sewed coats and garments for the widows and the poor, serving Christ in the needle and the loom;.
Saint Tabitha the Widow, raised from the.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Paraskevi (Petka) of Serbia.life: Saint Paraskevi the New, whom the Serbian people call with love Sveta Petka, was born in the eleventh century at Epivato in Thrace and gave her youth to Christ, distributing her garments and her inheritance to the poor, laboring in a convent at Heraclea, and living as an ascetic in the desert of the Jordan, before an angel bade her return to her homeland, where she reposed in obscurity and was glorified by God with incorrupt and wonderworking relics.
Venerable Paraskevi (Petka) of Serbia.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Ignatius, Archimandrite of the.life: Venerable Ignatius, Archimandrite of the Kyiv Caves, governed the great Lavra in the fifteenth century, about the year 1435, and his brief biography has been handed down in the inscription copied in later ages from his tombstone: that for his holy life the monk Ignatius gained from God the gift of miracles, and healed many of the sick by his prayers, and that healing was given through the taste of the prosphora he had offered, the faithful receiving cures by eating the holy bread from the Liturgies he served.
Venerable Ignatius, Archimandrite of the.patron: Invoked for priests who serve the Liturgy; the sick.
Venerable Ignatius, Archimandrite of the.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Apostle James, son of Alphaeus.life: The Holy Apostle James, son of Alphaeus, was one of the Twelve, called by the Lord together with the fishermen of Galilee, and by the tradition of the Church he was the brother of the Apostle and Evangelist Matthew the former publican. Of his words the Gospels record nothing, but his deeds fill the silence: after Pentecost he.
Apostle James, son of Alphaeus.patron: Invoked for the sowing of the word; apostolic labor.
Apostle James, son of Alphaeus.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Theodore, Archbishop of Constantin.life: Saint Theodore, Archbishop of Constantinople, served the Great Church of Hagia Sophia as presbyter and synkellos, the patriarch's trusted counselor, and was famed through the capital for the purity of his life before he was raised, in the days of the emperor Constantine Pogonatus, to the patriarchal throne itself.
Saint Theodore, Archbishop of Constantin.patron: Invoked for clergy of great churches; holiness kept amid the intrigues of capitals.
Saint Theodore, Archbishop of Constantin.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Ignatius of Loma and Yaroslav.life: Saint Ignatius of Loma and Yaroslavl hid his beginnings so well that the circumstances of his life in the world are unknown, which is itself the first fact of his biography, a man who entered the record only when he entered God's service. He began his ascetic path at the Priluki monastery of the Savior near Vologda, and received the monastic tonsure at the great monastery of Saint Cyril at White Lake, the two mother-houses of the northern Thebaid forming him in obedience and prayer;.
Venerable Ignatius of Loma and Yaroslav.patron: Invoked for hermits; founders who withdraw.
Venerable Ignatius of Loma and Yaroslav.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Gregory, Bishop of Agrigentum.life: Saint Gregory, Bishop of Agrigentum in Sicily, was born in the village of Pretorium near that city, of the pious Chariton and Theodota, and was baptized by the bishop of Agrigentum himself, who foresaw grace upon the child; a boy of extraordinary gifts, he mastered his letters and the Scriptures early, and as a young man set out for the East, becoming a monk at Jerusalem, and deepening his learning at Antioch and Constantinople, where his wisdom made him famous among the fathers of his day.
Saint Gregory, Bishop of Agrigentum.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Irenaeus, Bishop of Lyons.life: The Hieromartyr Irenaeus, Bishop of Lyons, one of the great teachers of the early Church, was born about the year 130 at Smyrna and received an excellent education in the learning of his day. His guide in the faith was Saint Polycarp of Smyrna, himself a disciple of the Apostle John the Theologian, and in his old age Irenaeus recalled how as a boy he had listened to Polycarp speak of his conversations with those who had seen the Lord, writing these things, as he said, not on paper but upon his heart.
Hieromartyr Irenaeus, Bishop of Lyons.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Thalassius, Hermit of Syria.life: Venerable Thalassius, Hermit of Syria, lived in the fifth century, and at a young age withdrew to a hill near the village of Targala, where he passed thirty-eight years in monastic struggle without a roof over his head, without a cell, and without any shelter at all, the sky of Syria his only architecture through nearly four decades of summers and winters, an endurance that placed him among the sternest of the open-air ascetics whom Theodoret of Cyrrhus recorded for the Church;.
Venerable Thalassius, Hermit of Syria.patron: Invoked for teachers of hermits; the gentle.
Venerable Thalassius, Hermit of Syria.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Phaedrus.life: The Holy Martyr Phaedrus is commemorated on this day together with the Martyr Philoumenus of Ancyra, in the company of those who suffered in Galatia in the persecution under the emperor Aurelian, about the year 274. The Greek synaxaria record the manner of his contest: refusing to deny Christ, he was put to death by having boiling pitch poured over his body, and so, scalded in the flesh but unscorched in soul, he gave up his spirit to God.
Martyr Phaedrus.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Publius the Ascetic of Syria.life: Saint Publius the Ascetic of Syria labored in the fourth century near Zeugma on the Euphrates, and his memory is preserved in the history of the Syrian monks written by Theodoret of Cyrrhus, who gathered the traditions of that country's fathers within living memory. Son of a leading citizen, Publius sold his patrimony at his conversion, distributed the price to the poor, and settled on a height near the river, where his solitude ran the usual course of the great ascetics and became a community;.
Saint Publius the Ascetic of Syria.patron: Invoked for communities of many tongues; abbots.
Saint Publius the Ascetic of Syria.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Icon of the Mother of God of Volokolamsk.type: Icon of the Mother of God · 16th c.
Icon of the Mother of God of Volokolamsk.life: The Volokolamsk Icon of the Mother of God is a wonderworking copy of the great Vladimir image, the most beloved icon of the Russian land, and its feast commemorates the day in 1572 when it was solemnly brought to the Joseph-Volokolamsk monastery, the famous house of Saint Joseph of Volotsk, and received with all honor at its gates, met by the brotherhood in procession and enshrined in the Dormition cathedral of the monastery.
Icon of the Mother of God of Volokolamsk.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Prophet Samuel.life: The Prophet Samuel was the fifteenth and last of the Judges of Israel and the first of the great prophets after Moses, living more than eleven hundred years before the coming of Christ. He was born through the fervent prayers of his mother Hannah, who had long been barren, and because she had besought him of the Lord she named him Samuel;.
Prophet Samuel.patron: Invoked for prophets; those seeking children.
Prophet Samuel.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Priest Aaron.life: The Righteous Aaron, first High Priest of the old covenant, elder brother of Moses and Miriam, of the tribe of Levi, was given by God to be his brother's mouth, going with him before Pharaoh and stretching out the rod of the signs; and at Sinai he was consecrated with his sons to the priesthood, clothed in the holy vestments, anointed with the oil of consecration, and set to offer for the people the sacrifices that taught Israel, century by century, the grammar of atonement in which the Gospel would one day be spoken.
Righteous Priest Aaron.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Silouan the Athonite (1938).life: Saint Silouan the Athonite was born in 1866 in the village of Shovskoe in the Tambov province of Russia, the son of devout peasants, and was named Simeon. Possessed in youth of great bodily strength and of a heart already wounded by the remembrance of God, he came in 1892 to the Russian monastery of Saint Panteleimon on Mount Athos, where he took up the unseen warfare with utter seriousness, praying with weeping for the world;.
Venerable Silouan the Athonite (1938).patron: Invoked for monastics; all who pray.
Venerable Silouan the Athonite (1938).src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Icon of Sophia, the Wisdom of God (Novgo.life: The icon of Sophia, the Wisdom of God, of the Novgorod type first appeared in that city in the fifteenth century, though the first church in Russia dedicated to the Holy Wisdom had been raised at Novgorod in the tenth century. At the center of the image the Wisdom of God is shown as a winged and fiery Angel, seated upon a golden throne borne up by seven pillars, according to the words of the Proverbs that Wisdom has built her house and hewn out her seven pillars;.
Icon of Sophia, the Wisdom of God (Novgo.patron: Invoked for divine wisdom; the sick.
Icon of Sophia, the Wisdom of God (Novgo.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

“Our Lady of Sitka” Icon of the Mother o.life: The Sitka Icon of the Mother of God is among the most revered icons of North America, enshrined at the Cathedral of Saint Michael the Archangel in Sitka, Alaska. It is attributed to the renowned Russian iconographer Vladimir Borovikovsky and came to Alaska in the early days of the Orthodox mission, where it has been honored as a wonderworking image and a protectress of the faithful in America.
“Our Lady of Sitka” Icon of the Mother o.patron: Invoked for protection of North America.
“Our Lady of Sitka” Icon of the Mother o.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Myron the Presbyter of Cyzicus.life: The Holy Martyr Myron was a priest in Achaia, a man of wealthy and noble birth who was yet gentle and kind to all, a lover of God and of his neighbor, and courageous in the defense of his flock. He suffered in the year 250, in the persecution under Decius, when on the feast of the Nativity of Christ the governor Antipater burst into the church during the service to seize the Christians, and Saint Myron boldly rebuked him for profaning the worship of God.
Martyr Myron the Presbyter of Cyzicus.patron: Invoked for defense of the flock.
Martyr Myron the Presbyter of Cyzicus.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Kindeos the Presbyter of Pam.life: The Hieromartyr Kindeos was a priest in Pamphylia in Asia Minor during the persecution of the emperor Diocletian. Undeterred by the danger, he labored zealously to preach the Gospel and to strengthen the faithful, and when he was denounced to the authorities for this, he was seized and put to death for the name of Christ.
Hieromartyr Kindeos the Presbyter of Pam.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Uncovering of the relics of Venerable Se.life: This feast commemorates the uncovering of the precious relics of Saint Sergius of Radonezh, the great abbot and wonderworker of the Russian land, on the fifth of July in the year 1422, thirty years after his repose. In 1408 the Tatar horde of Edigei had invaded and burned the Holy Trinity monastery, and the brethren fled with their abbot Saint Nikon;.
Uncovering of the relics of Venerable Se.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Andrew Rublev the Iconographer.life: Saint Andrew Rublev, the greatest of Russian iconographers, was born near Moscow around the year 1360 and in his youth entered the Holy Trinity Monastery, where he was deeply impressed by Saint Sergius of Radonezh. After Saint Sergius reposed he became a novice under Saint Nikon, and later moved to the Spaso-Andronikov Monastery in Moscow, where he received the monastic tonsure and learned the sacred art of iconography from Theophanes the Greek and from his friend and fellow-ascetic, the monk Daniel.
Venerable Andrew Rublev the Iconographer.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Michael, first Metropolitan of Kyi.life: Saint Michael, first Metropolitan of Kyiv, was by the tradition of the Church a Syrian by birth, and was sent from Constantinople to the land of Rus when Great Prince Vladimir received holy baptism and turned his people to Christ. Coming to Kyiv with clergy in the year of the Baptism of Rus, he stood at the prince's.
Saint Michael, first Metropolitan of Kyi.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Icon of the Mother of God “the Joy of Al.life: This wonderworking icon of the Mother of God, called the Joy of All Who Sorrow with coins, was glorified in Saint Petersburg in the year 1888. During a fierce thunderstorm, lightning struck a chapel by the Neva, and though the fire scorched and blackened all within, the icon of the Queen of Heaven was left unharmed and even appeared renewed and brightened;.
Icon of the Mother of God “the Joy of Al.patron: Invoked for comfort in sorrow; healing.
Icon of the Mother of God “the Joy of Al.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Apostle Quadratus of the Seventy.life: The Holy Apostle Quadratus of the Seventy preached the word of God at Athens and at Magnesia, and was Bishop of Athens, being called by his biographer a morning star shining amid the clouds of paganism. By his preaching he turned many pagans to the true faith, for which he endured persecution, stoning, and imprisonment at the hands of the enemies of Christ.
Apostle Quadratus of the Seventy.patron: Invoked for apologists; the defense of the faith.
Apostle Quadratus of the Seventy.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Forefeast of the Transfiguration of our.life: This day is the forefeast of the Transfiguration of our Lord, God, and Savior Jesus Christ, which the Church celebrates on the sixth of August. Desiring to give His disciples a foretaste of the glory of the Kingdom before His Passion, the Lord took with Him Peter, James, and John and led them up a high mountain, and there He was transfigured before them, so that His face shone like the sun and His garments became white as the light.
Forefeast of the Transfiguration of our.patron: Commemorated in the holy calendar of the Church.
Forefeast of the Transfiguration of our.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Anastasius of the Strumitza Eparch.life: The New Martyr Anastasius was born in the year 1774 in the village of Radoviste, in the diocese of Strumica, and as a young man went to Thessalonica to learn a trade. There, when he was about twenty years old, he fell under the anger of the Turks, who seized upon a pretext and sought to force him to deny Christ and embrace Islam.
Saint Anastasius of the Strumitza Eparch.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Chronides of Alexandria and those.life: The Holy Martyr Chronides suffered for Christ in the third century together with Leontius and Serapion, all three being Egyptians, in the persecutions of that age. After enduring fierce torments for their confession of the faith, the three martyrs were bound hand and foot and cast into the sea, where they gave up their souls to God;.
Martyr Chronides of Alexandria and those.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Acindynus, Pegasius, Aphthonius,.life: The Holy Martyrs Acindynus, Pegasius, Aphthonius, Elpidephorus, and Anempodistus, with seven thousand martyrs, suffered in Persia about the year 341, under King Shapur the Second. Acindynus, Pegasius, and Anempodistus were courtiers of the king and secret Christians; and when Shapur raised his persecution against the Church, they were denounced and brought to trial, where they confessed Christ openly and were given over to torments so cruel that wonder after wonder attended them, the sufferers being preserved whole while their tormentors fell blinded and were healed again at the martyrs' prayer.
Martyrs Acindynus, Pegasius, Aphthonius,.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Acacius of Sinai, who is menti.life: Saint Acacius lived in the sixth century as a young monk under an elder at a monastery in Asia, and he is remembered above all for his extraordinary obedience. His elder was a harsh and difficult man who worked him beyond measure, starved him, and beat him without cause, yet Acacius bore all of it meekly and gave thanks to God for everything.
Venerable Acacius of Sinai, who is menti.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Repose of Saint Jacob Netsvetov, Enlight.life: Saint Jacob Netsvetov, Enlightener of the peoples of Alaska, was born in the year 1802 on Atka Island in the Aleutians, the son of a Russian father from Tobolsk and an Aleut mother, and so he was joined by blood to the very people he would serve. Educated and in time ordained a priest, he returned to Atka.
Repose of Saint Jacob Netsvetov, Enlight.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Angelina of Serbia.life: Saint Angelina, honored as a mother of saints, was the daughter of Prince George of Albania. She was given in marriage to Saint Stephen Brankovic, the exiled and unjustly blinded ruler of Serbia, who had found refuge at her father's court, and she shared his sufferings with faith and courage.
Saint Angelina of Serbia.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Porphyrios of Kavsokalyvia (19.life: Saint Porphyrios of Kavsokalyvia, one of the great elders of the twentieth century, was born Evangelos Bairaktaris in 1906 to a poor family on the island of Evia; and reading as a boy the life of Saint John the Hut-dweller, he burned with such love for Christ that at about twelve years of age he fled to the Holy Mountain, to the skete of Kavsokalyvia, where he gave himself in absolute obedience to two austere elders, the brothers Panteleimon and Ioannikios.
Venerable Porphyrios of Kavsokalyvia (19.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Holy Apostles of the Seventy: Sosthenes,.life: The Holy Apostles of the Seventy Sosthenes, Apollos, Cephas, Tychicus, Epaphroditus, Caesar, and Onesiphorus were of that second choir whom the Lord Himself sent out two by two before His face, and their labors are woven through the epistles of Paul. Sosthenes had been ruler of the synagogue at Corinth, and was beaten before the judgment seat in the riot against Paul;.
Holy Apostles of the Seventy: Sosthenes,.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Leavetaking of the Transfiguration of ou.life: This is the Leavetaking of the Feast of the Transfiguration of the Lord, the final day on which the Church celebrates the glory revealed upon the holy mountain before bringing the feast to its close. On this day nearly the whole of the festal service is sung once more, that the faithful may take their leave of the great feast having been filled anew with the light of Tabor.
Leavetaking of the Transfiguration of ou.patron: Commemorated in the holy calendar of the Church.
Leavetaking of the Transfiguration of ou.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Longinus the Centurion, who stood.life: The Holy Martyr Longinus the Centurion was a Roman officer of Cappadocia serving in Judea under Pontius Pilate, and it was his detachment that kept watch at the Crucifixion of the Savior on Golgotha. Beholding the earthquake, the darkened sun, and the wonders that attended the death of the Lord, the centurion believed and confessed before all, Truly this was the Son of God;.
Martyr Longinus the Centurion, who stood.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Paul and two sisters, Chionia (T.life: The Holy Martyrs Paul and the two sisters Chionia and Alevtina were natives of Egypt who suffered for Christ in the persecution under the emperor Maximian. Seized for their faith, they were taken to Caesarea in Palestine, where without the least fear they confessed themselves followers of Christ before their judges and refused to sacrifice to the idols.
Martyrs Paul and two sisters, Chionia (T.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Pimen the Much-Ailing of the K.life: Saint Pimen, called the Much-Ailing, attained the Kingdom of Heaven through the patient endurance of grievous illness. Born and raised in sickness, he was preserved by his very infirmity from the sicknesses of the soul, and from his youth he begged his parents to bring him to the monastery of the Kiev Caves.
Venerable Pimen the Much-Ailing of the K.patron: Invoked for the chronically ill; patience in suffering.
Venerable Pimen the Much-Ailing of the K.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Julitta at Caesarea.life: The Holy Martyr Julitta lived at Caesarea in Cappadocia during the persecution under the emperor Diocletian. When a certain pagan seized all her property and she appealed to the courts for justice, her adversary denounced her before the judge as a Christian, which put her outside the protection of the law.
Martyr Julitta at Caesarea.patron: Invoked for integrity; preferring Christ to possessions.
Martyr Julitta at Caesarea.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Jonah the Presbyter, father of Sai.life: Saint Jonah the Presbyter lived in Palestine in the ninth century and is glorified as the father of two great confessors of Orthodoxy: Saint Theophanes the Hymnographer and Saint Theodore called the Branded, who for their defense of the holy icons had verses of mockery seared upon their faces by the iconoclast emperor.
Saint Jonah the Presbyter, father of Sai.patron: Invoked for fathers of clergy; raising children for God.
Saint Jonah the Presbyter, father of Sai.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Isidore of Pelusium.life: Venerable Isidore of Pelusium was born at Alexandria to pious Christians, a kinsman of the archbishops Theophilus and Cyril, and received the finest education of the greatest learned city of the age; and while still a youth he quit the world, withdrawing to a monastery on the mountain near Pelusium at the eastern mouth of the Nile, where he was in time ordained priest and became the father of the community, an ascetic of the strictest school who clothed himself, as his admirers wrote, in the whole armor of the monastic warfare.
Venerable Isidore of Pelusium.patron: Invoked for letter writers; spiritual directors.
Venerable Isidore of Pelusium.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Stephen of Saint Savva Monaste.life: Saint Stephen of the Monastery of Saint Sabbas was a nephew of Saint John of Damascus and was born in the year 725. When he was but ten years old he entered the Great Lavra of Saint Sabbas the Sanctified in the Judean desert and received the monastic tonsure, and there he passed the whole of his life, often withdrawing into the desert to give himself to solitude and spiritual struggle.
