Venerable Stephen of Saint Savva Monaste.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Vitalius, Bishop of Ravenna.life: The Hieromartyr Vitalius is honored among the early bishops and martyrs of the city of Ravenna, and he is commemorated on this day together with the Hieromartyr Apollinaris, the first bishop of that see. Little detailed account of his life has been preserved, but the Church remembers him as a shepherd who confessed Christ and sealed his witness with martyrdom in the early centuries, and who is numbered among the holy hierarchs who planted and watered the faith in that ancient city.
Hieromartyr Vitalius, Bishop of Ravenna.patron: Commemorated in the holy calendar of the Church.
Hieromartyr Vitalius, Bishop of Ravenna.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Zosimas the Hermit of Cilicia.life: The Holy Martyr Zosimas the Hermit lived in the fourth century as a desert-dweller in Cilicia, having withdrawn from the world to serve God in stillness; and such grace dwelt in him that the wild beasts of the wilderness gathered tamely about him as about Adam in paradise.
Martyr Zosimas the Hermit of Cilicia.patron: Invoked for harmony with creation; endurance under torture.
Martyr Zosimas the Hermit of Cilicia.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Prophet Zephaniah.life: The Holy Prophet Zephaniah, ninth of the twelve minor prophets, was of royal blood, tracing his line in the opening of his book through four generations to King Hezekiah; and he prophesied at Jerusalem in the days of the young King Josiah, in the seventh century before Christ, a contemporary of Jeremiah and a voice preparing the great reformation of that reign.
Prophet Zephaniah.patron: Invoked for the seeking of meekness; joy promised after judgment.
Prophet Zephaniah.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Apostle Epίmakhos of Alexandria.life: The Holy Martyr Epimachus of Alexandria was an Egyptian who from his youth loved the Lord and withdrew to the region of Pelusium, living as an ascetic in the wilderness in fasting and prayer. When the persecution of Decius fell upon Alexandria, the hermit, aflame with zeal, came down into the city to strengthen the confessors;.
Apostle Epίmakhos of Alexandria.patron: Invoked for healing of the eyes; zeal for God.
Apostle Epίmakhos of Alexandria.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Erasmus of the Kyiv Near Caves.life: Venerable Erasmus of the Kyiv Near Caves possessed great wealth, and gave the whole of it to God in one particular and beautiful form: he spent everything he had on the adornment of the Caves church, covering its icons with silver, gilding its holy images, and beautifying the house of the Theotokos until his fortune was entirely translated into splendor around the altar;.
Venerable Erasmus of the Kyiv Near Caves.patron: Invoked for benefactors of churches; the despondent.
Venerable Erasmus of the Kyiv Near Caves.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

The Protection of our Most Holy Lady the.life: The Protection of our Most Holy Lady the Mother of God and Ever-Virgin Mary is one of the most beloved feasts of the Church, kept above all in the lands of Rus. At the beginning of the tenth century, when the imperial city was in danger from its enemies, an all-night vigil was held in the church of Blachernae at Constantinople, where the robe of the Theotokos was kept;.
The Protection of our Most Holy Lady the.patron: Invoked for protection; intercession of the Theotokos.
The Protection of our Most Holy Lady the.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Appearance of Christ to Saint Martin of.life: On this day the Church commemorates the appearance of Christ to Saint Martin of Tours, the vision that stands at the head of one of the West's most beloved lives and preaches, in a single night scene, the whole twenty-fifth chapter of Matthew. Martin was then a young soldier of the Roman cavalry in Gaul, and still a catechumen, not yet baptized;.
Appearance of Christ to Saint Martin of.patron: Invoked for soldiers; givers of alms.
Appearance of Christ to Saint Martin of.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Icon of the Mother of God of Armatia.life: The Armatia Icon of the Mother of God was venerated in Constantinople at the Armatian monastery, which took its name from the place called Armation, associated with the magister Armatios in the days of the emperor Zeno. The celebration of this wonderworking icon was established in thanksgiving for the deliverance of the Church from the heresy of iconoclasm, which had warred against the holy images until the Church, guided by the Seventh Ecumenical Council, restored their veneration according to Scripture and Tradition.
Icon of the Mother of God of Armatia.patron: Invoked for the veneration of the holy icons.
Icon of the Mother of God of Armatia.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Eve of the Nativity of our Lord.life: The Eve of the Nativity of our Lord, called the Paramony, is the threshold of the feast, and the Church keeps it as she keeps the eve of Theophany alone, with a day of strict fasting and the most solemn preparation of her year. In the morning are sung the Royal Hours, so named because emperors once stood for them: at each hour the psalms of the Incarnation, the prophecies, the Apostle, and the Gospel of the birth are read, the whole of Scripture gathered around the cave;.
Eve of the Nativity of our Lord.patron: Commemorated in the holy calendar of the Church.
Eve of the Nativity of our Lord.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Cosmas of Yakhrom.life: Venerable Cosmas of Yakhrom was a servant, and his sanctity began in the perfect discharge of a servant's duty. Attached from youth to a boyar whom long illness had broken, Cosmas accompanied his master on the weary journeys from physician to physician and shrine to shrine, reading to him, nursing him, and carrying the sick man's hope when the sick man could not;.
Venerable Cosmas of Yakhrom.patron: Invoked for servants; caregivers of the sick.
Venerable Cosmas of Yakhrom.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Gervasius, Nazarius, Protasius,.life: The Holy Martyrs Nazarius, Gervasius, Protasius, and Celsus of Milan suffered in the reign of the emperor Nero. Nazarius, born at Rome of the Christian Perpetua and baptized, as tradition relates, by Linus the successor of Peter, gave his youth to preaching Christ and to the care of persecuted Christians, and coming to Milan he found there in prison the twin brothers Gervasius and Protasius, sons of the martyred Vitalius and of Valeria, who had given their inheritance to the poor and their lives to fasting and prayer.
Martyrs Gervasius, Nazarius, Protasius,.patron: Invoked for care for imprisoned Christians; the raising of children for God.
Martyrs Gervasius, Nazarius, Protasius,.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Priestmartyr John Kochurov.life: The Holy Hieromartyr John Kochurov, the first priest-martyr of the Russian revolution, was born in 1871 in the Ryazan province, the son of a village priest, and after the Theological Academy of Saint Petersburg he volunteered for the American mission, serving from 1895 as rector of Saint Vladimir's parish in Chicago.
Priestmartyr John Kochurov.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Stephen the Hymnographer of Sa.life: Saint Stephen the Hymnographer of Saint Savva Monastery lived the ascetic life in the great Lavra of Saint Sabbas in the Judean wilderness, the school of hymnographers which gave the Church Saint John of Damascus and Saint Cosmas of Maiuma; and there, formed in fasting, vigil, and the unceasing round of psalmody, he received the gift of sacred song.
Venerable Stephen the Hymnographer of Sa.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Dionysius of Aegina.life: Venerable Dionysius of Aegina is the same saint whom the Church glorifies this day as Dionysios of Zakynthos, remembered here under the title of the see he served: born on Zakynthos in 1547 of the noble Sigouros family, formed as a monk at the Strophades, he was consecrated Bishop of Aegina despite his protests of unworthiness, and shepherded that island with such teaching and wisdom that many were drawn to him from afar.
Venerable Dionysius of Aegina.patron: Invoked for bishops who resign for humility's sake; the flight from vainglory.
Venerable Dionysius of Aegina.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Anna the Prophetess and Daught.life: The Righteous Anna the Prophetess was of the tribe of Asher and the daughter of Phanuel, and having lived with her husband only seven years before his death, she gave the rest of her long life wholly to God. As the Gospel of Luke records, she did not depart from the Temple, but served God there night and day with fasting and prayer, and had reached the great age of fourscore and four years.
Righteous Anna the Prophetess and Daught.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Blessed Andrew of Totma the Fool-For-Chr.life: Blessed Andrew of Totma, the Fool-for-Christ, was born in 1638 in the village of Ust-Totma in the Vologda lands, and while still a child he resolved to leave the world. With the blessing of Stephen, abbot of the Resurrection monastery at Galich, he took upon himself the hard calling of folly for Christ's sake, and settled at the church of the Resurrection in the town of Totma on the river Sukhona.
Blessed Andrew of Totma the Fool-For-Chr.patron: Invoked for voluntary poverty; hidden almsgiving.
Blessed Andrew of Totma the Fool-For-Chr.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Andrew, Archbishop of Crete.life: Saint Andrew, Archbishop of Crete, one of the greatest hymnographers of the Church, was born at Damascus into a devout Christian family, and it is recounted that he was mute until the age of seven, receiving the gift of speech after he first partook of the Holy Mysteries.
Saint Andrew, Archbishop of Crete.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Makarios the Roman.life: Saint Makarios the Roman was born at the end of the fifteenth century into a wealthy family of Rome and was given an excellent education, but he set no store by earthly honors, seeking only the salvation of his soul. Grieved by the sins and divisions that shook the Western Church in his day, he prayed with tears that God would show him the way of truth, and coming to understand that the fullness of salvation was in the Orthodox Church, he journeyed to Russia.
Saint Makarios the Roman.patron: Invoked for monastics; conversion to Orthodoxy.
Saint Makarios the Roman.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Right-believing George the Great Prince.life: Right-believing George, Great Prince of Vladimir, was born in 1189, son of the Great Prince Vsevolod called Big Nest, and received the throne of Vladimir in 1212; distinguished from youth for military valor and for piety, he governed the strongest principality of the Russian north through a quarter century of building, founding in 1221, at the meeting of the Volga and the Oka, the fortress town of Nizhny Novgorod, whose walls guard his memory to this day.
Right-believing George the Great Prince.patron: Invoked for rulers in catastrophe; defenders of the homeland.
Right-believing George the Great Prince.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Repose of Saint Theoktistos, Archbishop.life: Saint Theoktistos, Archbishop of Novgorod, was igumen of the Annunciation monastery near that city when, on the repose of Archbishop Clement in 1300, the people of Novgorod chose him for their shepherd in the ancient manner of their republic; and he was consecrated on the twenty-ninth of June 1300 by Metropolitan Maximus of Kyiv and All Rus with the bishops of Rostov and Tver.
Repose of Saint Theoktistos, Archbishop.patron: Invoked for hierarchs who retire humbly; builders of churches.
Repose of Saint Theoktistos, Archbishop.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Apollinaris, Bishop of Raven.life: The Hieromartyr Apollinaris was a disciple of the Apostle Peter, whom he followed from Antioch to Rome, and Peter consecrated him the first Bishop of Ravenna and sent him there to preach the Gospel. Arriving as a stranger, he was given shelter by the soldier Irenaeus, whose blind son he healed, and so Irenaeus and his household became the first Christians of Ravenna;.
Hieromartyr Apollinaris, Bishop of Raven.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Procopius the Fool-For-Christ.life: Saint Procopius, the Fool-for-Christ of Ustiug, was by origin a wealthy merchant from the West who, coming to Novgorod on business, was so moved by the beauty of Orthodox worship that he embraced the faith, distributed all his goods to the poor, and took upon himself the hard and humbling path of folly for Christ.
Righteous Procopius the Fool-For-Christ.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Ariádnē of Phrygia.life: The Holy Martyr Ariadne was a slave in the household of Tertullus, a prominent citizen of Prymnessus in Phrygia, in the days of the emperor Hadrian; and though a servant in station, she was free in Christ and wiser than many of the noble women of her city.
Martyr Ariádnē of Phrygia.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Peter of Constantinople.life: Saint Peter was born into a patrician family at Constantinople toward the end of the eighth century. Commissioned as an officer under the emperor Nikephoros, he took part in the campaigns against Bulgaria, and in the battle in which the emperor was slain he was among the many taken captive.
Venerable Peter of Constantinople.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Return of the Relics of the Apostle Bart.life: The Holy Apostle Bartholomew, one of the Twelve, suffered for Christ in Armenia, where he was flayed and beheaded about the year 71, and his relics remained in that land working many miracles. In the reign of the emperor Anastasius they were carried to the new city of Anastasiopolis, but when hostile hands later threatened them, the faithful placed the relics in a chest of lead and gave them to the sea, entrusting the apostle to the providence of God;.
Return of the Relics of the Apostle Bart.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Botolph of Iken.life: Saint Botolph of Iken, one of the most beloved fathers of Orthodox England, labored in the seventh century in East Anglia. Formed in the monastic life and filled with its grace, he sought out for his foundation not rich land but wild, and in the year 654 began to build his monastery of Ikanhoe at Iken, on a lonely rise amid the tidal marshes of the river Alde, wrestling the ground, as the old accounts tell, from the desolation and the dark spirits that haunted it;.
Venerable Botolph of Iken.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Patapius of Thebes.life: Saint Patapius was born at Thebes in Egypt of pious Christian parents, and fleeing the honor his virtues drew, he withdrew young into the Egyptian desert, where he labored long in fasting, vigil, and prayer; and when fame found him even there, the hermit did what only the wisest dare, hiding himself not deeper in the desert but in the largest crowd on earth, coming to Constantinople and enclosing himself in a cell by the city wall at Blachernae, a desert of one in the midst of the multitude.
Venerable Patapius of Thebes.patron: Invoked for healers; healing of the blind and the sick.
Venerable Patapius of Thebes.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Longinus of Asistavi.life: Under the name of Longinus the Asistavi the Georgian calendar commemorates on this day the same holy Martyr Longinus the Centurion who stood at the Cross of the Lord; for asistavi, the head of a hundred, is the Georgian word for centurion, and is not a place but the martyr's title in the tongue of that ancient Christian nation.
Martyr Longinus of Asistavi.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Abramius the Recluse, and his.life: Saint Abramius the Recluse of Mesopotamia fled from his wedding feast in his youth, and walling himself into a cell near Edessa with only a small window, he lived there fifty years in fasting, tears, and prayer, his fame spreading through all the region. When the bishop could find no one to shepherd a pagan village that had beaten away every priest, he ordained the recluse against his will and sent him;.
Venerable Abramius the Recluse, and his.patron: Invoked for priests in hard places; the rescue of the fallen.
Venerable Abramius the Recluse, and his.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Royal Passionbearers Tsar Nicholas (Niko.life: On this day the Church commemorates the holy Royal Passion-bearers: Tsar Nicholas the Second, his wife the Tsaritsa Alexandra, their son the Tsarevich Alexei, and their daughters the Grand Duchesses Olga, Tatiana, Maria, and Anastasia, together with the faithful servants who chose to remain with them to the end.
Royal Passionbearers Tsar Nicholas (Niko.patron: Invoked for forgiveness of enemies; the family.
Royal Passionbearers Tsar Nicholas (Niko.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Peter the Hermit of Galatia Ne.life: Venerable Peter the Hermit of Galatia began his renunciation at an age when other children begin their schooling: at nine years old, yearning for the life of the spirit, he left his parents' house in Galatia and set out into the world of God, going first on pilgrimage to Jerusalem to venerate the holy places, and then to Antioch, where he settled for the rest of a very long life.
Venerable Peter the Hermit of Galatia Ne.patron: Invoked for healers; children called early to God.
Venerable Peter the Hermit of Galatia Ne.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Theodore the Silent of the Kyi.life: Venerable Theodore the Silent of the Kyiv Caves labored in the thirteenth century in the Far Caves of Saint Theodosius, and bears in the books of the Lavra the title that is his entire recorded biography: the Silent. Taking upon himself the exploit the fathers call hesychia of the tongue, Theodore renounced speech, keeping his voice for prayer and psalmody alone, and guarding the door of his lips through the years with the vigilance other ascetics spend on fasting or vigil;.
Venerable Theodore the Silent of the Kyi.patron: Invoked for the silent; guardians of the tongue.
Venerable Theodore the Silent of the Kyi.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Holy Martyr Euthymius.life: The Holy Martyr Euthymius suffered for Christ at Nicomedia in the great persecution under Diocletian and Maximian, in which the Christians of that city perished in vast numbers. When the bodies of the holy martyrs lay unburied, Euthymius, together with the virgin Domna who had turned from her former paganism to Christ, took pity upon the dead and gave themselves to the pious task of burying the fallen faithful with honor.
Holy Martyr Euthymius.patron: Invoked for care for the dead; steadfast confession.
Holy Martyr Euthymius.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Uncovering of the relics of Saint Demetr.life: Saint Demetrius, Metropolitan of Rostov, in the world Daniel Tuptalo, was born in 1651 near Kyiv and educated at the Kyiv academy, receiving the monastic tonsure in his youth.
Uncovering of the relics of Saint Demetr.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint John the Merciful, Patriarch of Al.life: Saint John the Merciful, Patriarch of Alexandria, was born at Amathus in Cyprus, the son of the governor of the island, and in obedience to his parents he married and had children; but when God took his wife and children to Himself, he gave the rest of his life wholly to Christ in the poor.
Saint John the Merciful, Patriarch of Al.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Priestmonk Jonah the Martyr of Pechenga.life: The Holy Priestmonk Martyr Jonah of Pechenga was born in the village of Varzuga in the Pomorie of the far Russian north, and served first as a parish priest; then, drawn to the northernmost monastery of the world, he entered the Pechenga monastery of the Holy Trinity on the Kola peninsula, founded by Saint Tryphon among the Lapps beyond the Arctic circle, and became one of the closest disciples of that great enlightener.
Priestmonk Jonah the Martyr of Pechenga.patron: Invoked for priests at the altar; monks of the far north.
Priestmonk Jonah the Martyr of Pechenga.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Julian the Presbyter and Caesari.life: The Holy Martyrs Julian the Presbyter and Caesarius the Deacon suffered for Christ at Terracina in Italy in the first age of the Church. Caesarius, a deacon come from Africa, beheld in that city the cruel pagan custom by which a young man, pampered for months at the city's expense, cast himself from a height as a sacrifice to the idols;.
Martyrs Julian the Presbyter and Caesari.patron: Invoked for protest against cruelty; steadfast confession.
Martyrs Julian the Presbyter and Caesari.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Xenophon, his wife, Mary, and.life: Venerable Xenophon, his wife Mary, and their sons Arcadius and John were noted citizens of Constantinople in the fifth and sixth centuries, rich in estate and rank and, the account insists, richer in simplicity of soul and goodness of heart, a great house that God intended to translate whole into the calendar.
Venerable Xenophon, his wife, Mary, and.patron: Invoked for families; parents of the lost.
Venerable Xenophon, his wife, Mary, and.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

New Martyr Habakkuk.life: The New Martyr Habakkuk bore witness to Christ in the great city of Thessalonica in the year 1628, during the long night of the Turkish yoke. Almost nothing of his life has been preserved, for no full account of his martyrdom survived; his memory is known only from a brief remembrance recorded in a manuscript of the Great Lavra on Mount Athos, which declares that in the month of August the venerable Habakkuk gave his witness to Christ, to the glory and pride of the Orthodox Christians.
New Martyr Habakkuk.patron: Invoked for steadfast confession under persecution.
New Martyr Habakkuk.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Maurice and his son, Photinus, a.life: The Holy Martyr Maurice, military commander of Apamea in Syria, suffered in the year 305 under Maximian Galerius, together with his son Photinus and the seventy soldiers of his command, of whom only two names, Theodore and Philip, have come down to us, the rest written, as the fathers say of such companies, in the Book of Life alone.
Martyrs Maurice and his son, Photinus, a.patron: Invoked for commanders; fathers and sons in arms.
Martyrs Maurice and his son, Photinus, a.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

The Placing of the Honorable Robe of the.life: This feast commemorates the placing of a portion of the precious Robe of our Lord Jesus Christ in the Dormition Cathedral of the Moscow Kremlin in the year 1625. The Robe, which by ancient tradition had been kept in the East since the time of the Crucifixion, was sent as a gift to the Tsar Michael Feodorovich and the Patriarch Filaret, and after its authenticity had been tested and confirmed by signs and healings, it was received in Moscow with great solemnity and enshrined in the cathedral.
The Placing of the Honorable Robe of the.patron: Invoked for veneration of the Lord's Passion.
The Placing of the Honorable Robe of the.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

5th Sunday of Great Lent: St Mary of Egy.life: Saint Mary of Egypt, whose life is read in church during Great Lent as an image of repentance, spent her youth in Alexandria in great licentiousness. Traveling to Jerusalem, she found herself held back by an unseen power from entering the church at the Exaltation of the Cross, and struck to the heart, she wept before an icon of the Mother of God and vowed to amend her life.
5th Sunday of Great Lent: St Mary of Egy.patron: Invoked for penitents at the Fast's summit; all who despair of change.
5th Sunday of Great Lent: St Mary of Egy.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Leo, Bishop of Catania in Sicily.life: Saint Leo, Bishop of Catania in Sicily, shepherded that city beneath Etna in the eighth century, a hierarch famed for compassion to the poor and the sick, for healings granted through his prayer, and for a gentleness that made his final severity the more terrible; and his name is fixed in the Church's memory by his duel with the sorcerer Heliodorus.
Saint Leo, Bishop of Catania in Sicily.patron: Invoked for bishops against sorcery; protectors of the flock's simple.
Saint Leo, Bishop of Catania in Sicily.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Polycarp, Archimandrite of the.life: Saint Polycarp entered the Kyiv Caves Monastery, where he was tonsured and struggled for the salvation of his soul, and true to his name, which means much fruit, he brought forth abundant fruits of repentance and virtue. His kinsman Saint Simon, who became Bishop of Vladimir and Suzdal, guided him in the spiritual life, and the two grew ever more united in spirit as they were joined in blood.
Venerable Polycarp, Archimandrite of the.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Uncovering of the relics of Venerable At.life: This day commemorates the uncovering of the relics of Saint Athanasius, abbot of Brest, a fearless champion of Orthodoxy in the age when the Unia was imposed upon the Orthodox of the Polish-Lithuanian lands. As igumen of the Monastery of Saint Simeon in Brest, he boldly opposed the Union by word and deed, defending his oppressed brethren and repeatedly declaring his prophecy, The Unia will die out, but Orthodoxy will flourish.
Uncovering of the relics of Venerable At.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Galaction and his wife, Epistemi.life: The Holy Martyrs Galaction and his wife Epistemis suffered at Emesa in Syria in the year 253, under the persecution of Decius. Galaction was born of the noblewoman Leucippe, long barren, who had been brought to Christ and baptized by a monk named Onuphrius, and who raised her son secretly in the faith;.
Martyrs Galaction and his wife, Epistemi.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Commemoration of the Founding of the Chu.life: On this day the Church commemorates the founding, that is the solemn consecration, of the Church of the Resurrection of Christ at Jerusalem, raised by Saint Constantine the Great and his mother the holy Empress Helen over the Tomb of the Lord and the hill of Golgotha. When Helen had come to Jerusalem, destroyed the pagan shrines that defiled the holy places, and found the Life-giving Cross beneath the temple of Venus, Constantine commanded that a great and splendid church be built enclosing both the place of the Crucifixion and the Sepulchre of the Resurrection;.
Commemoration of the Founding of the Chu.patron: Invoked for the consecration of churches.
Commemoration of the Founding of the Chu.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Virgin Martyr Eulalia of Barcelona and t.life: The Holy Virgin Martyr Eulalia lived near the city of Barcelona in Spain and was raised by her parents in piety and the Christian faith, so that even as a young maiden she gave herself to prayer, the reading of the Scriptures, and quiet labor at home. When in the persecution under Diocletian the governor Dacian came to Barcelona to destroy the Christians, Eulalia, though but a girl, secretly left her home by night, and in the morning stood before the ruler to confess Christ and to rebuke him for worshipping idols.
Virgin Martyr Eulalia of Barcelona and t.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Thais of Egypt.life: Saint Thais of Egypt was left by her mother to a life of sin, and her beauty made her famous and wealthy in shame, drawing many souls to ruin. The great elder Paphnutius, grieving for her and for those she destroyed, put on worldly clothes and came to her with a gold coin as though a client;.
Venerable Thais of Egypt.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Blessed Cleopatra with her son John, in.life: Blessed Cleopatra was a devout widow of Palestine, living in Egypt in the days of the persecution, and beholding the contest of the holy Martyr Varus, she obtained his body in secret and carried it to her native village of Edra near Mount Tabor, where she buried it with honor and built over it a church in the martyr's name, her whole household venerating him as their protector.
Blessed Cleopatra with her son John, in.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Proclus and Hilary of Ancyra.life: The Holy Martyrs Proclus and Hilary were kinsmen from a village near Ancyra who suffered in the persecution under the emperor Trajan. Proclus was arrested first, and when he boldly confessed Christ before the governor Maximus and foretold that the governor himself would one day be compelled to acknowledge the true God, he was cruelly tortured and made to run behind the governor's chariot.
Martyrs Proclus and Hilary of Ancyra.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Claudius, Asterius, Neon, and The.life: The Holy Martyrs Claudius, Asterius, and Neon, with the Martyr Theonilla, suffered at Aegae in Cilicia in the year 285, under the governor Lysias. The three were brothers, and when their father died, their stepmother, coveting the inheritance, denounced her husband's children to the authorities as Christians, delivering them up to torture for the sake of their goods.
Martyr Claudius, Asterius, Neon, and The.patron: Invoked for the defrauded and betrayed; orphans wronged by kin.
Martyr Claudius, Asterius, Neon, and The.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Sisoes the Schemamonk of the K.life: Saint Sisoes was a schemamonk of the Kyiv Caves who labored in the Far Caves in the thirteenth century. He is remembered for having subdued the passions of the flesh through strict fasting, and the Church honors him together with Saint Gregory the Faster as one given grace to help others in their own struggles against temptation.
Venerable Sisoes the Schemamonk of the K.patron: Invoked for mastery of the passions.
Venerable Sisoes the Schemamonk of the K.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Theodore Graptus, “the branded.life: Saint Theodore Graptus, the Branded, confessor for the holy icons, was born at Jerusalem and formed with his brother Theophanes as a monk of the Lavra of Saint Sabbas, the two brothers so learned and so holy that the Patriarch of Jerusalem sent them to Constantinople as his champions against the reborn iconoclasm;.
Venerable Theodore Graptus, “the branded.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Moses, Wonderworker of the Kyi.life: Saint Moses lived in the Kyiv Caves Monastery in the thirteenth and fourteenth centuries and gave himself wholly to God. He wore heavy chains and bore upon himself a great copper cross, and his constant and beloved labor was the chanting of the Psalms and the making of countless prostrations, by which he wearied his body for the sake of his soul.
Venerable Moses, Wonderworker of the Kyi.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Theophanes the Confessor and Hymno.life: Saint Theophanes the Confessor and Hymnographer, Bishop of Nicaea, called the Branded, was the younger brother of Saint Theodore, sons of the pious presbyter Jonah of Palestine; excellently educated and formed in philosophy, the brothers were tonsured in the Lavra of Saint Sabbas, where Theophanes became a hieromonk.
Saint Theophanes the Confessor and Hymno.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Eulampius and Eulampia, at Nicom.life: The Holy Martyrs Eulampius and Eulampia, brother and sister, lived at Nicomedia at the beginning of the fourth century. When the decree of the emperor Maximian condemning all Christians to death was posted in the city, the young Eulampius read it and grieved aloud that the emperor took up arms against his own innocent subjects rather than the enemies of the empire;.
Martyrs Eulampius and Eulampia, at Nicom.patron: Invoked for brother and sister in Christ; boldness before idols.
Martyrs Eulampius and Eulampia, at Nicom.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Daniel, Abbot of Shuzhgorsk, N.life: Saint Daniel of Shuzhgorsk was born in the lands of Moscow in the sixteenth century, and forsaking the world he received the monastic tonsure at the Komel monastery founded by Saint Cornelius, where he was formed in the traditions of the great northern ascetics. Desiring the solitary life, he departed into the wild country of the Russian north, and settled upon the wooded hill called Shuzhgora, in the region between Belozersk and Novgorod, where he labored alone in prayer, fasting, and the struggles of the wilderness.
Venerable Daniel, Abbot of Shuzhgorsk, N.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable John the Silent of Saint Sabba.life: Saint John the Silent, called also the Hesychast, was born in 454 at Nicopolis in Armenia, of a noble family of generals and governors; and having built a church of the Theotokos and gathered a small brotherhood in his youth, he was constrained at twenty-eight to accept the bishopric of Colonia.
Venerable John the Silent of Saint Sabba.patron: Invoked for hesychasts; bishops who lay down office.
Venerable John the Silent of Saint Sabba.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Proterius, Patriarch of Alex.life: The Hieromartyr Proterius, Patriarch of Alexandria, was the man set to hold the most dangerous see in Christendom for the faith of Chalcedon, and he held it to the last drop. A priest of Alexandria under the patriarch Dioscorus, he had the fearlessness to denounce his own hierarch's Monophysite error and confess the Orthodox faith of the two natures while Dioscorus stood at the height of his power;.
Hieromartyr Proterius, Patriarch of Alex.patron: Invoked for hierarchs amid mobs; defenders of Chalcedon.
Hieromartyr Proterius, Patriarch of Alex.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

The Dormition of our Most Holy Lady the.life:
The Dormition celebrates the falling asleep of the Most Holy Theotokos and her translation, body and soul, into heaven. According to the tradition of the Church, when the time of her repose drew near, the Apostles were miraculously gathered from the ends of the earth to Jerusalem, and the Lord Himself descended to receive her soul.

Her body was laid in a tomb in Gethsemane, and when the Apostle Thomas, who arrived after three days, wished to venerate her, the tomb was found empty, for she had been taken up to be with her Son.
The Dormition of our Most Holy Lady the.patron: Commemorated in the holy calendar of the Church.
The Dormition of our Most Holy Lady the.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Nicholas the Monk of Bulgaria.life: Venerable Nicholas the Soldier, called also the Commander, served in the imperial army in the campaign that the emperor Nicephorus led into Bulgaria in the year 811, and his sanctity was decided in a single night on the march. Lodged at an inn, he was assaulted not by an enemy but by a temptation, the innkeeper's daughter coming to him in the darkness;.
Venerable Nicholas the Monk of Bulgaria.patron: Invoked for soldiers; all who resist temptation on the eve of battle.
Venerable Nicholas the Monk of Bulgaria.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Andrew, John, and John’s childre.life: The Holy Martyrs Andrew, John, and John's children Peter and Antoninus were natives of Syracuse in Sicily, carried away captive to Africa in the ninth century, when the Saracens ravaged the island. The two boys, taken young, were raised at the court of the emir and instructed in the learning and religion of their captors, being outwardly counted among the Muslims;.
Martyrs Andrew, John, and John’s childre.patron: Invoked for captives; faith preserved in a foreign land.
Martyrs Andrew, John, and John’s childre.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Jonah, Abbot of Yashezersk.life: Saint Jonah of Yashezersk was a native of the Karelian lands and continued in the north the tradition of the great desert-dwellers of the school of Saint Alexander of Svir. Settling in the wilderness by Lake Yashezero, he lived at first in complete solitude, in fasting, vigil, and unceasing prayer;.
Venerable Jonah, Abbot of Yashezersk.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Prophetess Hannah the mother of the Prop.life: The Holy Prophetess Hannah, mother of the Prophet Samuel, was the wife of Elkanah of Ramathaim, barren for long years and wounded daily by the provocations of her rival; and going up to the sanctuary at Shiloh, she poured out her soul before the Lord, weeping and vowing that if He gave her a son, she would give the child back to Him all the days of his life.
Prophetess Hannah the mother of the Prop.patron: Invoked for mothers; the barren who pray.
Prophetess Hannah the mother of the Prop.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Synaxis of the Archangel Michael and the.life: The Synaxis of the Archangel Michael and the Other Bodiless Powers is the chief feast of the holy angels, established in the earliest centuries of the Church, which appointed it to the eighth day of November: the ninth month from March, the ancient beginning of the year, for the nine ranks of the angels, and the eighth day, as an image of the great Day of the Lord, the day of the eighth age, when the Son of Man shall come in His glory and all the holy angels with Him.
Synaxis of the Archangel Michael and the.patron: Invoked for protection; the guarding of every soul.
Synaxis of the Archangel Michael and the.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Blessed Nicholas Kochanov the Fool-For-C.life: Blessed Nicholas Kochanov, fool-for-Christ of Novgorod, was born of a wealthy and noble family and from his youth loved the church, fasting, and prayer. When the people began to praise him for his virtue, he fled their esteem by taking up the difficult path of folly for Christ, hiding his holiness beneath the guise of madness.
Blessed Nicholas Kochanov the Fool-For-C.patron: Invoked for reconciliation; peace amid strife.
Blessed Nicholas Kochanov the Fool-For-C.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Commemoration of the Great Earthquake at.life: On this day the Church commemorates the great earthquake that struck Constantinople in the year 740, in the reign of Leo the Isaurian, when the anger of God shook the imperial city, casting down churches, dwellings, and long stretches of the city walls with their towers, and destroying many people, the tremors continuing for months so that the inhabitants dwelt in fear under the open sky.
Commemoration of the Great Earthquake at.patron: Invoked for deliverance from earthquakes; repentance before the judgments of God.
Commemoration of the Great Earthquake at.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Virgin Martyr Juliana of Nicomedia, and.life: The Holy Virgin Martyr Juliana of Nicomedia suffered in the year 304, in the persecution of Diocletian and Maximian, and with her a harvest her own courage had sown. Daughter of the pagan Africanus and betrothed against her will to the senator Eleusius, the secret Christian delayed the marriage with conditions, and when at last she set the true one, that she would wed no man who would not worship her God, the rejected suitor, now raised to eparch of the city, became her judge;.
Virgin Martyr Juliana of Nicomedia, and.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Anthony of Alexandria.life: The Holy Martyr Anthony was a Christian of the city of Alexandria who was arrested for his confession of Christ. Tied to a tree, his body was torn with iron hooks, and he was then condemned to be burned alive; but standing in the midst of the fire, he was untroubled, and calmly urged those looking on to labor not for the body, which passes away, but for the soul in its ascent toward God.
Martyr Anthony of Alexandria.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Elpidius, Marcellus, and Eustoch.life: The Holy Martyrs Elpidius, Marcellus, and Eustochius suffered under Julian the Apostate, in the years 361 to 363, when the empire, having tasted the peace of the Church, was dragged back by its ruler toward the worship of the idols. Elpidius was a senator, a man of high dignity, and he was brought with his companions before the imperial judge on the charge of being a Christian;.
Martyrs Elpidius, Marcellus, and Eustoch.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Diodoros, Igoumen of George Hi.life: Saint Diodoros of George Hill was born in the village of Turchasovo on the river Onega, midway between Kargopol and the White Sea, to pious parents named Hierotheos and Maria, who called their son Diomedes. At fifteen years of age he went on pilgrimage to the great Solovki monastery in the northern sea, and remained there, receiving in time the monastic tonsure with the name Diodoros;.
Venerable Diodoros, Igoumen of George Hi.patron: Invoked for monastics; the hermit life of the far north.
Venerable Diodoros, Igoumen of George Hi.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Sisoes the Recluse of the Kyiv.life: Venerable Sisoes, Schemamonk of the Kyiv Caves, labored in the Near Caves of Saint Anthony in the thirteenth century, and was clothed in the great schema, the highest degree of monastic renunciation, whose bearer dies to the world twice over. Taking up the strictest form of the Caves warfare, he enclosed himself in the reclusion of the caves, where the schemamonk's whole rule is prayer without ceasing, prostration, fasting, and the guarding of the mind against the assaults that the enemy multiplies upon those who have left him nothing else to attack;.
Venerable Sisoes the Recluse of the Kyiv.patron: Invoked for the hidden warfare of reclusion.
Venerable Sisoes the Recluse of the Kyiv.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Cyriacus of Bisericani, Romani.life: Venerable Cyriacus of Bisericani, one of the greatest hesychasts of the Romanian land, labored at the beginning of the seventeenth century in the monastery of Bisericani in the Neamț country, whose brotherhood then numbered more than a hundred monks; and burning for the harder way, he took his confessor's blessing and withdrew to a stone cave on the mountain above the river Bistrița, and there accomplished a podvig that the Church of Moldavia has never ceased to marvel at.
Venerable Cyriacus of Bisericani, Romani.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Virgin Martyr Lucy of Syracuse.life: The Holy Virgin Martyr Lucy of Syracuse, whose name means light, suffered in Sicily in the year 304, in the great persecution of Diocletian, and her feast has carried light into the darkest days of winter ever since. Going with her mother Eutychia, who suffered an issue of blood, to pray at the tomb of Saint Agatha in Catania, Lucy beheld the martyr in a vision, and her mother was healed at the shrine;.
Virgin Martyr Lucy of Syracuse.patron: Invoked for the blind; those who work by lamplight.
Virgin Martyr Lucy of Syracuse.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Holy Martyrs and Confessors Gurias, Samo.life: The Holy Martyrs and Confessors Gurias, Samonas, and Habibus are the great protectors of the city of Edessa and of honorable marriage. Gurias and Samonas, preachers of the word of God, were arrested in the persecution under Diocletian; refusing to sacrifice, they were beaten, hung up by their hands with heavy weights bound to their feet, and cast into a stifling prison, and after long torments were beheaded, about the year 306, Samonas praying with words that a witness wrote down for the Church.
Holy Martyrs and Confessors Gurias, Samo.patron: Invoked for honorable marriage; deliverance from family turmoil.
Holy Martyrs and Confessors Gurias, Samo.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Tation (Tatio) of Claudiopolis.life: The Holy Martyr Tation lived in Bithynia and suffered for Christ in the persecution under Diocletian. When it became known that he was a Christian, he was seized and brought to the city of Claudiopolis before the governor Urban, who many times urged him to deny Christ and, when he would not, cast him into prison and subjected him to various torments, beating him with staves.
Martyr Tation (Tatio) of Claudiopolis.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable John the Faster of the Kyiv Ne.life: Venerable John the Faster labored in the Near Caves of the Kyiv Lavra in the twelfth century, in the first flowering of the monastery of Saints Anthony and Theodosius, and bore the same warfare and the same title as the great patriarch of Constantinople whose name he shared: he was a faster, an athlete of abstinence in the school where fasting was accounted the foundation of every other victory.
Venerable John the Faster of the Kyiv Ne.patron: Invoked for mastery of the appetite; hidden struggle.
Venerable John the Faster of the Kyiv Ne.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Paraskevi of Rome.life: Saint Paraskevi was the only daughter of devout Christian parents in Rome, and from her early years she gave herself to prayer and the study of the holy Scriptures. When her parents died she distributed her inheritance to the poor and consecrated her virginity to Christ, and in imitation of the apostles she went about preaching the Gospel and turning many of the pagans from their idols.
Martyr Paraskevi of Rome.patron: Invoked for eye ailments; the sick.
Martyr Paraskevi of Rome.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Prophet Habakkuk.life: The Holy Prophet Habakkuk, eighth of the twelve minor prophets, was of the tribe of Simeon and prophesied about the year 650 before Christ, foreseeing the destruction of the Temple, the Babylonian captivity, and the return of the exiles. His book preserves the great dialogue of the watchman with God: standing upon his tower to see what the Lord would answer concerning the prosperity of the wicked, he received the word that has fed the faith of both Testaments, The vision is yet for an appointed time;.
Prophet Habakkuk.patron: Invoked for watchmen; faith that waits upon the vision.
Prophet Habakkuk.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Repose of Venerable Abramius of Galich o.life: Saint Abramius of Galich was a disciple of Saint Sergius of Radonezh who labored at the Holy Trinity monastery through the fourteenth century, serving many years as a novice before being ordained priest. Longing for deeper stillness, he received his elder's blessing and in 1350 withdrew into the wilderness of the Galich country in the north of Russia, then still inhabited by unbaptized tribes.
Repose of Venerable Abramius of Galich o.patron: Commemorated in the holy calendar of the Church.
Repose of Venerable Abramius of Galich o.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Michael Maleinos.life: Saint Michael Maleinos was born in Cappadocia of noble and devout parents and was named Manuel, and being kin to the great families of the empire he was destined for a brilliant career at the imperial court. Yet while still a young man he forsook the world and its honors, and, withdrawing to Mount Kyminas in Bithynia, he was tonsured a monk and gave himself to a life of strict asceticism under an experienced elder.
Venerable Michael Maleinos.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Cosmas the Hymnographer, Bishop of.life: Saint Cosmas the Hymnographer, Bishop of Maiuma, was left an orphan and was adopted by the pious Sergius of Damascus, the father of Saint John of Damascus, so that the two boys were raised as brothers; and they were educated together by a learned elder, also named Cosmas, a monk from Italy whom Sergius had ransomed from captivity.
Saint Cosmas the Hymnographer, Bishop of.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Niphon, Bishop of Constantia, Cypr.life: Saint Niphon, Bishop of Constantia on Cyprus, was born in Paphlagonia in the fourth century and educated at Constantinople, a gentle child who loved the services of the Church; and then his youth fell into the pit, years of wild and dissolute living in which the boy who had loved the altar became a stranger to himself, until grace, using the grieved face of a friend as its mirror, showed Niphon his own darkened countenance, and the great repentance began.
Saint Niphon, Bishop of Constantia, Cypr.patron: Invoked for penitents; those tormented by evil spirits.
Saint Niphon, Bishop of Constantia, Cypr.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Apostles of the Seventy Philemon and Arc.life: The Holy Apostles Philemon and Archippus, the Martyr Apphia, wife of Philemon, and Saint Onesimus, disciple of the Apostle Paul, are bound together forever by the shortest of Paul's epistles, written to Philemon our dearly beloved and fellow laborer, to the beloved Apphia, to Archippus our fellow soldier, and to the church in thy house.
Apostles of the Seventy Philemon and Arc.patron: Invoked for households of faith; masters and servants.
Apostles of the Seventy Philemon and Arc.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Amphilokhios, Bishop of Iconium.life: Saint Amphilochius, Bishop of Iconium, was born about the year 340 at Caesarea in Cappadocia, that nursery of the great fathers, and was kinsman of Gregory the Theologian and beloved friend of Basil the Great. A lawyer of brilliance at Constantinople, he left the courts for Christ, withdrawing to a life of asceticism and the care of his aged father;.
Saint Amphilokhios, Bishop of Iconium.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

33 Holy Martyrs of Melitene.life: The Holy Thirty-Three Martyrs of Melitene suffered about the year 290, in the reign of Diocletian and Maximian, when a detachment under the commander Lysias was sent into Cappadocia to root out the Christians and to conscript strong men for the army. At their head stands Hieron, a farmer of Tyana, raised in piety by his mother, a man of extraordinary bodily strength;.
33 Holy Martyrs of Melitene.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Dadas, Gabdelas, and Kazdoa of P.life: The Holy Martyrs Dadas, Gabdelas, and Kazdoa suffered for Christ in Persia under the king Sapor. Dadas, a kinsman of the king and chief steward of his court, was discovered to be a Christian and stripped of his honors, and given over to torture; but when the fire prepared for him was turned aside by his prayer and wonders were wrought before all, the king's own son Gabdelas and his daughter Kazdoa, beholding the power of Christ, believed in the God of the man they had been sent to condemn.
Martyrs Dadas, Gabdelas, and Kazdoa of P.patron: Invoked for converts from the household of persecutors.
Martyrs Dadas, Gabdelas, and Kazdoa of P.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Juvenal of Alaska.life: The Holy Martyr Juvenal, Protomartyr of America, was born in 1761 at Nerchinsk in Siberia, and in the world was John Feodorovich Hovorukhin, trained as a mining engineer. After the death of his wife he entered the monastic life, and as a hieromonk of Valaam he was chosen for the first Orthodox mission to America, arriving at Kodiak in 1794 with Saint Herman and their companions.
Martyr Juvenal of Alaska.patron: Invoked for missionaries; the enlightenment of America.
Martyr Juvenal of Alaska.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Elias of Murom, Wonderworker o.life: Venerable Elias of Murom, wonderworker of the Near Caves, came from the city of Murom on the Oka, and finished his course as a monk of the Kyiv Caves Lavra about the year 1188. The brethren called him Chobotok, the Boot, for the tradition that, surprised once by enemies, the warrior beat them off with the only weapon in reach, his own boot;.
Venerable Elias of Murom, Wonderworker o.patron: Invoked for soldiers; warriors who become monks.
Venerable Elias of Murom, Wonderworker o.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Forefather Abraham.life: The Holy Righteous Forefather Abraham, the father of all who believe, was called by God out of Ur of the Chaldees, leaving his country and his kindred at the word of the Lord, who promised that in his seed all the families of the earth would be blessed;.
Righteous Forefather Abraham.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Uncovering of the relics of Venerable Se.life: This feast commemorates the uncovering of the relics and the solemn glorification of Saint Seraphim of Sarov, one of the most beloved saints of the Russian Church, which took place in the year 1903, seventy years after his repose. At the urging of the faithful and with the strong support of Tsar Nicholas the Second, who came to.
Uncovering of the relics of Venerable Se.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Charitina of Amisos.life: The Holy Martyr Charitina of Amisos in Pontus was orphaned in childhood and raised as a daughter by a pious Christian named Claudius, in whose house she grew in beauty, sense, and kindness, studying the law of God day and night and vowing her virginity to Christ, while by her words she brought many to the way of salvation.
Martyr Charitina of Amisos.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Greatmartyr Euphemia the All-praised.life: This day commemorates the great miracle wrought through Saint Euphemia the All-praised in defense of the Orthodox faith. Having suffered martyrdom at Chalcedon under Diocletian, she was glorified anew a century and a half later, in the year 451, when the Fourth Ecumenical Council assembled in the very church where her relics lay, to condemn the heresy of the Monophysites and to confess the two natures of Christ, divine and human.
Greatmartyr Euphemia the All-praised.patron: Invoked for the defense of Orthodox doctrine.
Greatmartyr Euphemia the All-praised.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Afterfeast of the Dormition of the Mothe.life: During the days of the Afterfeast of the Dormition, the Church continues to celebrate the blessed falling asleep of our Most Holy Lady the Theotokos and her translation in glory to the heavenly kingdom. The hymns of these days proclaim that she who bore the Author of Life did not abandon the world in her repose, but was taken up by her Son to reign with Him and to intercede without ceasing for all who honor her.
Afterfeast of the Dormition of the Mothe.patron: Commemorated in the holy calendar of the Church.
Afterfeast of the Dormition of the Mothe.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Anthimus, Bishop of Nicomedi.life: The Hieromartyr Anthimus, Bishop of Nicomedia, was born in that city and raised from childhood in the Christian faith, and being humble, peaceable, and filled with zeal for the glory of God, he was in time made bishop of Nicomedia. He shepherded the Church there during the fierce persecution under Diocletian and Maximian, when the blood of Christians.
Hieromartyr Anthimus, Bishop of Nicomedi.patron: Invoked for steadfast confession; faithful shepherding under persecution.
Hieromartyr Anthimus, Bishop of Nicomedi.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Arrival of the Ivḗron Icon of the Mother.life: On this day the Georgian Church commemorates the arrival of the Iveron Icon of the Most Holy Theotokos in Georgia. On the twenty-sixth of September in the year 1989, an exact copy of the renowned wonderworking Portaitissa, the Gate-Keeper of the Iveron monastery on Mount Athos, arrived in Tbilisi from the Holy Mountain, painted by the Athonite monks with the blessing of Catholicos-Patriarch Ilia the Second as a token of love and gratitude toward the Georgian people, whose fathers had founded the Iveron monastery of old.
Arrival of the Ivḗron Icon of the Mother.patron: Invoked for protection of Georgia; consolation in hard times.
Arrival of the Ivḗron Icon of the Mother.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr and Archdeacon Euplus of Catania.life: The Holy Archdeacon Euplus suffered in the year 304 in the Sicilian city of Catania, during the persecution under Diocletian and Maximian. He carried the Gospel with him everywhere and preached Christ boldly to the pagans, and once, while he was reading and explaining the sacred book to the people, he was seized and brought to trial.
Martyr and Archdeacon Euplus of Catania.patron: Invoked for deacons; preaching the Gospel.
Martyr and Archdeacon Euplus of Catania.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Forefeast of the Dormition of the Mother.life: This day is the forefeast of the Dormition of our Most Holy Lady the Theotokos, on which the Church begins to celebrate her blessed falling asleep, kept on the fifteenth of August at the close of the fast dedicated to her. The hymns of the forefeast call the faithful to gather in gladness, for the Mother of God is about to depart from the earth to the heavenly kingdom, to be taken up in glory by her Son.
Forefeast of the Dormition of the Mother.patron: Commemorated in the holy calendar of the Church.
Forefeast of the Dormition of the Mother.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Timothy of Symbola in Bithynia.life: Venerable Timothy of Symbola labored on the Bithynian Olympus, the holy mountain of Asia Minor whose gorges in the eighth century held a commonwealth of monasteries second only to the deserts of old, and among its communities the one called Symbola received him young and kept him to the end.
Venerable Timothy of Symbola in Bithynia.patron: Invoked for monks of purity; exorcists.
Venerable Timothy of Symbola in Bithynia.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Theophilus the Recluse of the.life: Venerable Theophilus the Silent labored in the Near Caves of the Kyiv Lavra in the twelfth and thirteenth centuries, and took upon himself the podvig that his title preserves: the ascetic discipline of silence, by which the monk offers to God the member that is hardest of all to tame.
Venerable Theophilus the Recluse of the.patron: Invoked for silence; prayer in hiddenness.
Venerable Theophilus the Recluse of the.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Dius, Abbot of Antioch.life: Saint Dius was born at Antioch in Syria toward the end of the fourth century into a devout Christian family, and from his youth he was distinguished for his temperance, eating little and not every day, and humbling his flesh with vigil and unceasing prayer. For these labors the Lord granted him dispassion and the gift of wonderworking.
Venerable Dius, Abbot of Antioch.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Confessors Barses and Eulogius, Bishops.life: Saints Barses and Eulogius, Bishops of Edessa, and Protogenes, Bishop of Carrhae, were confessors who suffered from the Arians in the latter half of the fourth century, when the emperor Valens sought to spread that heresy and cruelly harassed the Orthodox. Saint Barses, a steadfast champion of the true faith, was driven from his throne at Edessa and sent into exile, first to one place and then to another, ever farther from his city;.
Confessors Barses and Eulogius, Bishops.patron: Invoked for Orthodoxy against heresy; endurance in exile.
Confessors Barses and Eulogius, Bishops.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Prokopios the Confessor of Dec.life: Venerable Prokopios the Confessor of Decapolis was a monk of that region of Asia Minor in the days when the emperor Leo the Isaurian raised the first great persecution against the holy icons, and he earned his title in the fullest coin the age offered short of death.
Venerable Prokopios the Confessor of Dec.patron: Invoked for confessors; monks under persecution.
Venerable Prokopios the Confessor of Dec.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Moses, Archbishop of Novgorod.life: Saint Moses, Archbishop of Novgorod, was born in that city to wealthy and pious parents and named Mitrofan in baptism; and fleeing marriage and inheritance alike, he was tonsured with the name Moses, labored in the monasteries of the Novgorod land, and rose by pure reputation to be archimandrite of the great Yuriev monastery, from which, in 1325, the city summoned him to its archiepiscopal throne.
Saint Moses, Archbishop of Novgorod.patron: Invoked for scribes; builders of churches.
Saint Moses, Archbishop of Novgorod.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Paramon and 370 Martyrs in Bithyn.life: The Holy Martyr Paramon and the three hundred and seventy martyrs with him suffered in Bithynia in the year 250, in the persecution under Decius. The ruler Aquilinus, coming to the warm springs of those parts, held with him in bonds a multitude of Christians, three hundred and seventy in number;.
Martyr Paramon and 370 Martyrs in Bithyn.patron: Invoked for speech that will not be silent before injustice.
Martyr Paramon and 370 Martyrs in Bithyn.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Anthony the Roman and Abbot of.life: Saint Anthony was born at Rome in the year 1067 to wealthy parents who held to the Orthodox faith, and after their death, when he was seventeen, he gave himself to the study of the Fathers in the Greek tongue. Distributing part of his inheritance to the poor, he sealed the rest in a wooden cask and cast it into the sea, and was tonsured a monk in a wilderness monastery, where he lived for twenty years until a persecution of the Latins against the Orthodox scattered the brethren.
Venerable Anthony the Roman and Abbot of.patron: Commemorated in the holy calendar of the Church.
Venerable Anthony the Roman and Abbot of.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Translation of the relics of Saint Maxim.life: Saint Maximus the Confessor, one of the greatest theologians of the Church, was born at Constantinople about the year 580 and served as first secretary to the emperor Heraclius before forsaking the court for the monastic life at the monastery of Chrysopolis, where in time he became abbot.
Translation of the relics of Saint Maxim.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Barlaam, Abbot of the Kyiv Nea.life: Saint Barlaam of the Kyiv Caves, the first abbot of that great Lavra, was the son of an eminent boyar of Kyiv; and coming often to the cave of Saint Anthony, the young nobleman was so pierced by the elder's word that he rode out one day in his finest garments, dismounted, laid his rich clothing at the elder's feet, and begged the tonsure.
Venerable Barlaam, Abbot of the Kyiv Nea.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Platon of Ancyra.life: The Holy Martyr Platon suffered at Ancyra in Galatia at the beginning of the fourth century, a young man of a Christian house and brother of the martyr Antiochus. Going boldly about the city, he taught his fellow citizens to despise the idols and know the true God, for which he was seized and brought before the governor Agrippinus;.
Martyr Platon of Ancyra.patron: Invoked for the young; refusal of every bargain against Christ.
Martyr Platon of Ancyra.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Anna at Rome.life: The Holy Martyr Anna suffered for Christ at Rome in the age of the persecutions. Little concerning her has been preserved, but the hymns of the Church honor her as a bright star who confessed Christ boldly, turning the faithful away from the allure of idols and receiving from the Lord an incorruptible crown for her sufferings.
Martyr Anna at Rome.patron: Commemorated in the holy calendar of the Church.
Martyr Anna at Rome.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Commemoration of the Miracle of the Arch.life: On this day the Church commemorates the glorious miracle wrought by the Archangel Michael at Chonae, near Colossae in Phrygia. In that place there was a wonderworking spring, foretold by the Apostle John the Theologian when he preached at Hierapolis; and a man of Laodicea, whose mute daughter received speech by its waters after the Archangel appeared to him in a dream, was baptized with all his house and built over the spring a church in honor of the Chief Commander Michael.
Commemoration of the Miracle of the Arch.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

The Universal Exaltation of the Precious.life: The Universal Exaltation of the Precious and Life-Giving Cross is one of the twelve Great Feasts of the Church, and a day of strict fasting, in reverence for the sufferings of the Lord upon the Tree. When the holy Empress Helen came to Jerusalem to seek the Cross of Christ, it was found hidden in the earth beneath a pagan temple, together with the crosses of the two thieves;.
The Universal Exaltation of the Precious.patron: Invoked for the whole world; victory over evil.
The Universal Exaltation of the Precious.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint John the Chozebite, Bishop of Caes.life: Saint John the Chozebite was an Egyptian of Thebes who from his youth gave himself to the ascetic life, and coming to the Holy Land, he settled in the wild gorge of Choziba in the Judean wilderness, on the road from Jerusalem to Jericho, where his holiness and his wonders became known throughout Palestine.
Saint John the Chozebite, Bishop of Caes.patron: Invoked for monastics; the love of stillness.
Saint John the Chozebite, Bishop of Caes.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Apostle Matthias of the Seventy.life: The Holy Apostle Matthias was born at Bethlehem of the tribe of Judah, and from his childhood he was taught the Law of God by Saint Simeon the God-Receiver. When the Lord Jesus Christ appeared in the world, Matthias believed in Him as the Messiah and followed Him faithfully, and he was numbered among the Seventy whom the Lord sent out two by two before His face.
Apostle Matthias of the Seventy.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Rhipsime and Gaianḗ of Armenia a.life: The Holy Martyrs Rhipsime and Gaiane and their companions were virgins of a community at Rome, who fled to the East when the emperor Diocletian, having seen the beauty of Rhipsime, sought to take her to wife; and coming to Armenia, they settled in poverty near the city of Vagharshapat, living by the labor of their hands.
Martyrs Rhipsime and Gaianḗ of Armenia a.patron: Invoked for purity; the conversion of Armenia.
Martyrs Rhipsime and Gaianḗ of Armenia a.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Susanna, Queen of Georgia.life: Saint Shushanik, called Susanna, was the wife of Varsken, the ruler of Hereti in eastern Georgia, and had been raised from childhood in a devout Christian family. When her husband journeyed to the Persian king and there renounced Christ to worship fire, promising to convert his wife and children on his return, Shushanik was struck to the heart.
Martyr Susanna, Queen of Georgia.patron: Invoked for steadfast confession; those persecuted by family for the faith.
Martyr Susanna, Queen of Georgia.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Consecration of the Church of the Holy G.life: On this day the Church commemorates the consecration of the church of the Holy Great Martyr George at Lydda in Palestine, and the deposition there of his precious relics. The great martyr, who suffered at Nicomedia in the year 303 under Diocletian, had asked his servant before his contest to carry his body to Lydda, the home of his mother's family in the Holy Land;.
Consecration of the Church of the Holy G.patron: Invoked for the veneration of the Great Martyr George.
Consecration of the Church of the Holy G.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Philotheus, Patriarch of Const.life: Saint Philotheus, Patriarch of Constantinople, called Kokkinos, was a native of Thessalonica and received the monastic tonsure in his youth. After laboring for a time at Mount Sinai he came to the Holy Mountain of Athos, where he became abbot of the Great Lavra; and in 1347 he was made Metropolitan of Heraclea in Thrace, ascending afterward the ecumenical throne of Constantinople, which he occupied first in 1354 and 1355 and again from 1364 to 1376.
Venerable Philotheus, Patriarch of Const.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Savva, Igoumen of Zvenigorod,.life: Saint Savva of Storozhev, the Zvenigorod wonderworker, was among the first disciples of Saint Sergius of Radonezh, formed under the great elder in silence, obedience, and unceasing prayer, and so trusted by the brotherhood that he served as confessor to the whole Trinity community, and for a time, after Nikon withdrew into silence, as abbot of the Lavra itself.
Venerable Savva, Igoumen of Zvenigorod,.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

The Holy Transfiguration of our Lord God.life: The Transfiguration celebrates the day the Lord took Peter, James, and John up a high mountain, held by tradition to be Mount Tabor, and was transfigured before them: His face shone like the sun and His garments became white as the light. Moses and Elijah appeared and spoke with Him of His coming departure at Jerusalem, and a bright cloud overshadowed them, from which the Father's voice declared, This is My beloved Son;.
The Holy Transfiguration of our Lord God.patron: Commemorated in the holy calendar of the Church.
The Holy Transfiguration of our Lord God.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Chariton the Confessor, Abbot.life: Saint Chariton the Confessor was a citizen of Iconium who confessed Christ in the persecution under Aurelian, enduring such tortures that he was accounted a martyr though he survived them, and being set free when the persecution abated, he bore in his body the marks of his confession.
Venerable Chariton the Confessor, Abbot.patron: Invoked for monastics; the monastic rule.
Venerable Chariton the Confessor, Abbot.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Tryphon, Abbot of Vyatka.life: Saint Tryphon of Vyatka was born of a peasant family in the Mezen lands of the far north, and fleeing in his youth from the marriage his family purposed, he wandered as a homeless pilgrim, bearing cold and mockery for the love of God, until he received the monastic tonsure at the Pyskor monastery on the Kama.
Venerable Tryphon, Abbot of Vyatka.patron: Invoked for missionaries; the enlightenment of the northern peoples.
Venerable Tryphon, Abbot of Vyatka.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Commemoration of the Kazan Icon of the M.life: On this day the Church commemorates the Kazan Icon of the Most Holy Theotokos in memory of the deliverance of Moscow and all Russia from the Poles in the year 1612. In the Time of Troubles, when the land was torn by invasion and treachery and Moscow itself was held by foreign arms that mocked the Orthodox faith, the imprisoned Patriarch Hermogenes called the people to rise in defense of Church and country;.
Commemoration of the Kazan Icon of the M.patron: Invoked for the deliverance of nations; protection in time of troubles.
Commemoration of the Kazan Icon of the M.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Prophet Obadiah (Abdia).life: The Holy Prophet Obadiah, whose book, the shortest in the Old Testament, stands among the twelve minor prophets, prophesied the judgment of God upon Edom, the proud brother-nation that rejoiced over the fall of Jerusalem: Though thou exalt thyself as the eagle, and though thou set thy nest among the stars, thence will I bring thee down, saith the Lord;.
Prophet Obadiah (Abdia).patron: Invoked for stewards; the humbling of pride.
Prophet Obadiah (Abdia).src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Sisoes the Great.life: Saint Sisoes the Great was a solitary monk of the Egyptian desert in the fifth century, who took up his dwelling in the very cave once sanctified by the labors of Saint Anthony the Great. Through sixty years of ascetic struggle he attained a rare purity of soul and was granted the gift of wonderworking, once even restoring a dead child to life by his prayer.
Venerable Sisoes the Great.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Cyprian, Virgin Martyr Justi.life: The Hieromartyr Cyprian, the Virgin Martyr Justina, and the Martyr Theoctistus suffered at Nicomedia in the year 304. Cyprian was a philosopher and sorcerer of Antioch, trained from childhood in the pagan mysteries on Olympus and in Argos, Memphis, and Babylon, until he became famous as a servant of the prince of darkness;.
Hieromartyr Cyprian, Virgin Martyr Justi.patron: Invoked for deliverance from sorcery and evil spirits; purity guarded by the Cross.
Hieromartyr Cyprian, Virgin Martyr Justi.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Ephraim, Abbot of Perekop, Won.life: Saint Ephraim of Perekop, wonderworker of Novgorod, was born at Kashin and named Eustathius in the world. Drawn from youth to the monastic life, he left his parents' home and was tonsured with the name Ephraim, laboring first under the guidance of the great elders of the Russian north;.
Venerable Ephraim, Abbot of Perekop, Won.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Right-believing Prince Vladimir Yaroslav.life: The Holy Prince Vladimir Yaroslavich of Novgorod, the wonderworker, was the eldest son of Great Prince Yaroslav the Wise and of the pious Princess Irene, who ended her days as the nun Anna and is honored with her son. Set over Novgorod by his father at fourteen years of age, he was guided by wise counselors and by the holy bishop of the city, and grew into a brave defender of the land and a devout Christian, raising a stone fortress for his people and instructing himself diligently in the law of the Lord.
Right-believing Prince Vladimir Yaroslav.patron: Invoked for builders of churches; church-building.
Right-believing Prince Vladimir Yaroslav.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Liberius, Pope of Rome.life: Saint Liberius became Bishop of Rome in the year 352, after the repose of Pope Julius, and he showed himself a zealous defender of the Orthodox faith against the Arian heresy and a champion of Saint Athanasius of Alexandria. When the emperor Constantius, favoring the Arians, demanded that he condemn Athanasius, Liberius refused and was sent into exile;.
Saint Liberius, Pope of Rome.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Orestes, Physician of Cappadocia.life: The Holy Martyr Orestes the Physician lived at Tyana in Cappadocia in the reign of Diocletian, a learned and skillful healer of bodies and, from childhood, a true Christian. When the officer Maximinus was sent to Tyana to crush the faith, Orestes was among the first brought to trial, and confessed the Crucified and Risen Lord openly, unmoved by the riches and honors offered him;.
Martyr Orestes, Physician of Cappadocia.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Hilarion, Abbot of Gdov and Ps.life: Saint Hilarion of Gdov was a disciple of the great elder Euphrosynus of Pskov, formed in his wilderness school of strict fasting, obedience, and unceasing prayer. Going forth with his elder's blessing, he founded on the river Zhelcha, not far from Gdov by the waters of the Pskov lake country, a monastery in honor of the Protection of the Most Holy Theotokos, in a borderland exposed to the raids of the Livonian knights;.
Venerable Hilarion, Abbot of Gdov and Ps.patron: Invoked for monastics; the borderland monasteries.
Venerable Hilarion, Abbot of Gdov and Ps.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Apostles of the Seventy Archippus and Ph.type: Apostles of the Seventy, Martyrs · 1st c.
Apostles of the Seventy Archippus and Ph.life: The Holy Apostles Archippus and Philemon of the Seventy, and the Martyr Apphia, are the household of the shortest epistle, the family at Colossae to whom Paul wrote the letter that bears Philemon's name.
Apostles of the Seventy Archippus and Ph.patron: Invoked for house churches; husbands and wives who serve together.
Apostles of the Seventy Archippus and Ph.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Nestor, Tribimius, and those wit.life: The Holy Martyrs Nestor, Tribimius, Marcellus, and Anthony of Perge in Pamphylia suffered in the reign of the emperor Decius, about the year 250, in the persecution that demanded of every soul in the empire a certificate of sacrifice and made of every refusal a capital case. The four were Christians of Perge who did not wait to.
Martyrs Nestor, Tribimius, and those wit.patron: Invoked for companions in confession; four crowns by the sword.
Martyrs Nestor, Tribimius, and those wit.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Amphilochius, Bishop of Vladimir,.life: Saint Amphilochius, Bishop of Vladimir in Volhynia, was the third bishop of that see, one of the most ancient of the Russian land, established in the days of Saint Vladimir the Great; his predecessors were Stephen, chosen under Vladimir himself, and Stephen the abbot of the Kyiv Caves who had succeeded Saint Theodosius.
Saint Amphilochius, Bishop of Vladimir,.patron: Invoked for missionaries; the uprooting of paganism.
Saint Amphilochius, Bishop of Vladimir,.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Apostle Nicanor the Deacon of the Sevent.life: The Holy Apostle Nicanor was one of the first seven deacons of the Church of Christ, chosen, as the Acts of the Apostles records, when the Twelve summoned the multitude of the disciples and appointed seven men of honest report, full of the Holy Spirit and wisdom, Stephen, Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas, and Nicholas, to serve tables and care for the widows, that the ministry of mercy might be as ordered as the ministry of the word.
Apostle Nicanor the Deacon of the Sevent.patron: Invoked for deacons; those who serve tables.
Apostle Nicanor the Deacon of the Sevent.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Marcian and Martyrius, the Notar.life: The Holy Martyrs Marcian and Martyrius served as notaries, that is, secretaries and readers, to Saint Paul the Confessor, Patriarch of Constantinople, in the years when the Arian heresy, upheld by the imperial court, raged against the defenders of the Nicene faith.
