When the holy patriarch was banished and secretly strangled in exile, the Arians sought to win his faithful notaries, offering them gold, honors, and even episcopal thrones if they would embrace the heresy that made the Son of God a creature;.
Martyrs Marcian and Martyrius, the Notar.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Forefeast of the Procession of the Honor.life: This day is the forefeast of the Procession of the Precious and Life-giving Cross of the Lord, which the Church celebrates on the first of August. In the imperial city of Constantinople it was the custom, during the month of August when sickness was most prevalent, to bring forth the venerable Wood of the Cross from the treasury.
Forefeast of the Procession of the Honor.patron: Invoked for deliverance from sickness; sanctification.
Forefeast of the Procession of the Honor.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Kyriaina and Juliana in Cilicia.life: The Holy Martyrs Kyriaina and Juliana suffered in Cilicia in the persecution under Maximian, about the year 305. Kyriaina was of Tarsus and Juliana of the city of Rossos, both women who had given their lives to Christ in purity and prayer; and being arrested by Marcian, the governor of Cilicia, they refused every demand to offer sacrifice to the idols.
Martyrs Kyriaina and Juliana in Cilicia.patron: Invoked for dignity under mockery; women faithful unto death.
Martyrs Kyriaina and Juliana in Cilicia.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Aboudimos of the Isle of Tenedos.life: The Holy Martyr Aboudimos was from the island of Tenedos, which lies in the Aegean opposite the ancient city of Troy, and he was among the first to suffer for Christ in the persecution under Diocletian at the beginning of the fourth century. When he was commanded to worship the idols and to eat of the food offered to them, he steadfastly refused, and for this he was bound and cruelly beaten, enduring his sufferings with courage until he received the crown of martyrdom.
Martyr Aboudimos of the Isle of Tenedos.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Virgin Martyr Anysia at Thessalonica.life: The Holy Virgin Martyr Anysia lived at Thessalonica in the reign of Maximian, the orphaned daughter of pious parents who had raised her in the faith; and inheriting their wealth, she sold everything, distributed the price to the poor, and gave herself to a hidden life of fasting, vigil, and prayer, a monastery of one in the great pagan city.
Virgin Martyr Anysia at Thessalonica.patron: Invoked for young women; those accosted on the way to church.
Virgin Martyr Anysia at Thessalonica.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Cornelius the Centurion.life: The Hieromartyr Cornelius the Centurion, the first-fruits of the Gentiles, was a Roman officer of the Italian cohort stationed at Caesarea in Palestine, a devout man who feared God with all his house, gave alms generously, and prayed always, as the Acts of the Apostles bear witness. To him an angel appeared, telling him that his prayers and alms had come up as a memorial before God, and bidding him send for Simon Peter;.
Hieromartyr Cornelius the Centurion.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Glorification of Saint John of Kronstadt.life: Saint John of Kronstadt, one of the great pastors of the Russian Church, was born John Sergiev in 1829 in a poor village of the far north and became a married parish priest at the Saint Andrew Cathedral in Kronstadt, near Saint Petersburg, where he served for over fifty years.
Glorification of Saint John of Kronstadt.patron: Commemorated in the holy calendar of the Church.
Glorification of Saint John of Kronstadt.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Eudoxios, Agapios, Atticus, and.life: The Holy Martyrs Atticus, Agapius, Eudoxius, Carterius, Istucarius called Styrax, Pactobius, and Nictopolion, with their companions, were soldiers of Sebaste in Armenia, and suffered about the year 320 in the persecution under Licinius, who, preparing war against Saint Constantine, purged his armies of Christians and demanded of the garrisons sacrifice to the idols.
Martyrs Eudoxios, Agapios, Atticus, and.patron: Invoked for soldiers; soldiers faithful to Christ.
Martyrs Eudoxios, Agapios, Atticus, and.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

The Discovery of the Relics of Venerable.life: Saint Zosimas of Vorbozomsk was a disciple of the great elder Cornelius of Komel, in whose wilderness school so many founders of the northern monasteries were formed; and going forth with his elder's blessing, he settled on an island of Lake Vorbozomsk, south of Belozersk, where he founded a monastery in honor of the Annunciation of the Most Holy Theotokos.
The Discovery of the Relics of Venerable.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Patermuthius, Coprius, and Alexa.life: The Holy Martyrs Patermuthius, Coprius, and Alexander suffered in Egypt under the emperor Julian the Apostate. Patermuthius had once been a pagan and the leader of a band of robbers, but coming to repentance he was baptized and withdrew into the desert, where he gave himself to ascetic labor and was granted the gifts of healing and prophecy.
Martyrs Patermuthius, Coprius, and Alexa.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Holy Confessor Emilian, Bishop of Kyziko.life: Saint Emilian was Bishop of Cyzicus in the early ninth century, in the time of the second assault upon the holy icons under the iconoclast emperor Leo the Armenian. Summoned with other bishops before the emperor and commanded to forbid his flock the veneration of the sacred images, Saint Emilian answered boldly that a question touching the faith of the Church ought to be examined and decided within the Church by her spiritual shepherds, and not settled at the imperial court.
Holy Confessor Emilian, Bishop of Kyziko.patron: Invoked for the veneration of icons; the freedom of the Church.
Holy Confessor Emilian, Bishop of Kyziko.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Savva, Abbot of Vishera, Novgo.life: Saint Savva of Vishera was the son of a boyar of Kashin, and forsaking betrothal and inheritance in his youth, he received the monastic tonsure and gave himself to strict asceticism, journeying even to the Holy Mountain of Athos to be formed in its traditions. Returning to the Russian land, he settled by the river Vishera not far from Novgorod, where in 1418 he established a monastery in honor of the Ascension of the Lord;.
Venerable Savva, Abbot of Vishera, Novgo.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Trophimus, Sabbatius, and Doryme.life: The Holy Martyrs Trophimus, Sabbatius, and Dorymedon suffered for Christ in the reign of the emperor Probus. Trophimus and Sabbatius, coming to Antioch during a riotous pagan festival, grieved at the spectacle and prayed for the erring, whereupon they were noticed, seized, and brought before the governor; and confessing the faith without wavering, Sabbatius died under his fierce torments, while Trophimus was sent, shod in iron boots set with nails, on the long road to Synnada in Phrygia for crueler tortures still.
Martyrs Trophimus, Sabbatius, and Doryme.patron: Invoked for friendship in Christ; care for prisoners.
Martyrs Trophimus, Sabbatius, and Doryme.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Mary (who was called Marinus),.life: Venerable Mary, who was called Marinus, and her father Eugene, are the Church's astonishing study in the outer limits of patience. When the widower Eugene resolved to end his days in a monastery, his young daughter Mary refused to be left behind in the world, and the two devised the only door that would admit them together: Mary cut her hair, put on men's clothing, and entered the Bithynian monastery beside her father as the young monk Marinus, the family hidden inside a habit.
Venerable Mary (who was called Marinus),.patron: Invoked for the falsely accused; women in disguise for God.
Venerable Mary (who was called Marinus),.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Martyrius of Zelenets, Pskov.life: Venerable Martyrius of Zelenets, in the world Menas, was born at Veliki Luki in the sixteenth century to the pious Cosmas and Stephanida, and orphaned at ten; the boy was raised by his spiritual father, a priest of the city's Annunciation church, and his soul, the life records, cleaved to God from that upbringing in loss, the orphan learning early that one Father does not die.
Venerable Martyrius of Zelenets, Pskov.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Andronicus, and his wife Athan.life: Saints Andronicus and his wife Athanasia lived at Antioch in the fifth century, he a silversmith who divided his earnings into three parts, for the poor, for the Church, and for his household, and both beloved for their charity. When their two children died on a single day, Athanasia was crushed with grief and would not leave their grave, until the holy martyr Julian appeared to her in the guise of a monk and asked why she wept for those who now fed on the bread of angels;.
Venerable Andronicus, and his wife Athan.patron: Invoked for married couples; the bereaved.
Venerable Andronicus, and his wife Athan.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Sophia, Irene, and Castor of Egy.life: The Holy Martyrs Sophia and Irene suffered for Christ in Egypt in the age of the persecutions, and with them is commemorated the Martyr Castor. Of their contest little has been preserved beyond the witness of the ancient calendars, which record that the holy women, having confessed Christ before their persecutors and refused to offer sacrifice to the idols, were beheaded with the sword, and that Castor likewise finished his course in martyrdom.
Martyrs Sophia, Irene, and Castor of Egy.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Euthymius, Bishop of Sardis.life: The Hieromartyr Euthymius, Bishop of Sardis, was raised to that ancient see for his virtuous life in the days of Constantine and Irene, and stood at the Seventh Ecumenical Council in 787 among the denouncers of the iconoclast heresy; and when the heresy returned to the throne, his episcopate became a forty-year chain of exiles, one for each emperor who demanded what he would not give.
Hieromartyr Euthymius, Bishop of Sardis.patron: Invoked for bishops in exile; the veneration of the holy icons.
Hieromartyr Euthymius, Bishop of Sardis.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable John-Barsanuphius, Bishop of D.life: Venerable John, called Barsanuphius, Bishop of Damascus, accomplished the flight that many hierarchs have dreamed and few have dared: he resigned a throne into the hands of God without telling anyone, and finished his life as an anonymous laborer among the monks of Egypt. Bishop of the great see of Damascus in the fifth century, John governed, the tradition holds, with the diligence of a good shepherd;.
Venerable John-Barsanuphius, Bishop of D.patron: Invoked for hierarchs who long for hiddenness; water carriers and woodcutters.
Venerable John-Barsanuphius, Bishop of D.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Finding of the relics of Venerable Cyril.life: On this day the Church commemorates the finding of the relics of Saint Cyril, Abbot of Novoezersk, which took place in the year 1649. Born to a noble family of Galich, he fled from his parents' house at fifteen years of age, drawn by the love of Christ, and came through the forests to the great elder Cornelius of Komel, who, discerning the seal of God upon the boy, tonsured him;.
Finding of the relics of Venerable Cyril.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Hermolaus and Martyrs Hermip.life: The Hieromartyrs Hermolaus, Hermippus, and Hermocrates were among the few who survived after twenty thousand Christians were burned to death in a church at Nicomedia during the persecution under Maximian. Living in hiding, they did not cease to preach the Gospel to the pagans, and it was the priest Hermolaus who, seeing the young pagan Pantoleon pass by his dwelling, called him in and taught him the emptiness of idolatry and the truth of Christ.
Hieromartyr Hermolaus and Martyrs Hermip.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Luke the Steward of the Kyiv C.life: Saint Luke the Steward of the Kyiv Caves bore in the monastery the obedience of economos, the steward to whose care are entrusted the goods, provisions, and practical affairs of the brotherhood; and he showed that this ministry, which so easily entangles a soul in cares and temptations of gain, can be a path of holiness when it is walked in honesty and prayer.
Venerable Luke the Steward of the Kyiv C.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Zeno the Hermit of Antioch, di.life: Venerable Zeno the Hermit of Antioch was born in Pontus to a rich family and served at the court of the emperor Valens among the couriers who carried the imperial edicts across the empire, a man whose profession was speed, roads, and the words of power; and he had been formed in his youth by Saint Basil the Great, whose disciple he was, so that under the courier's cloak a monk was already riding.
Venerable Zeno the Hermit of Antioch, di.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Cyrilla of Cyrene in Libya, a wid.life: The Holy Martyr Cyrilla suffered at Cyrene in Libya during the persecution of Diocletian. A widow devoted to Christ, she was seized and commanded to offer incense to the idols. When burning coals with incense were placed upon her open hand, so that by casting them away she might seem to make an offering to the false gods, she endured the fire without flinching and refused to let the coals fall, choosing to be burned rather than to appear for even a moment to deny her Lord.
Martyr Cyrilla of Cyrene in Libya, a wid.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Onesiphorus and Porphyrius of Ep.life: The Holy Martyrs Onesiphorus and Porphyrius suffered for Christ in the persecution under Diocletian, toward the end of the third century. Confessing themselves Christians, they were brought to trial and subjected to fierce torments, being beaten and burned with fire; and when neither pain nor promises could turn them from Christ, the tormentors tied the martyrs to wild horses, which dragged them over rocks and thorns until they gave up their holy souls to God.
Martyrs Onesiphorus and Porphyrius of Ep.patron: Invoked for endurance to the end.
Martyrs Onesiphorus and Porphyrius of Ep.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Monastic Martyr Joseph of Dionysiou, Mou.life: Saint Joseph was a monk of the monastery of Dionysiou on Mount Athos, where he shone in the virtues of the monastic life and labored as an iconographer, painting the icon of the holy Archangels for the iconostasis of the monastery's principal church. In obedience to his abbot Stephen, he traveled to Constantinople as companion to a certain Eudocimus, who had apostatized to Islam and now, repenting, desired to wash away his denial by martyrdom;.
Monastic Martyr Joseph of Dionysiou, Mou.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Boniface the Merciful, Bishop of F.life: Saint Boniface the Merciful, Bishop of Ferentino in Italy, lived in the sixth century, and his wonders were written down within living memory by Saint Gregory the Great in the Dialogues, where the pope of Rome preserved the stories of the saints of his own Italian soil. Mercy ran ahead of Boniface's reason from childhood: whatever came into the boy's hands went out to the poor, his own shirt included, and once, finding his widowed mother's granary, the whole year's provision of the household, he gave away nearly all the grain to the needy;.
Saint Boniface the Merciful, Bishop of F.patron: Invoked for almsgivers; stewards of small means.
Saint Boniface the Merciful, Bishop of F.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Uncovering of the relics of Saint Andrew.life: On this day the Church commemorates the uncovering of the relics of Saint Andrew, Prince of Smolensk, which took place at Pereslavl-Zalessky in the year 1539 through the labors of Saint Daniel of Pereslavl. The holy prince, grieved by the enmity and strife of his kinsmen, had forsaken his principality in secret, and coming as an unknown poor man to Pereslavl, he served for thirty years as sexton at the church of Saint Nicholas, in fasting, prayer, and perfect hiddenness, no man knowing that the humble server of the church was a prince by birth.
Uncovering of the relics of Saint Andrew.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Hyacinthus of Amastridea.life: The Holy Martyr Hyacinthus was born into a devout Christian family in the city of Amastris in Asia Minor, and it is said that an angel appeared and gave him his name. Even as a small child he was filled with grace, and when he was but three years old his prayer raised a dead infant to life, so that the two children grew up together and gave themselves to an ascetic manner of life.
Martyr Hyacinthus of Amastridea.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Pimen the Great.life: Saint Pimen the Great was born in Egypt about the year 340 and entered a monastery together with his two brothers, Anoub and Paisius, all three receiving the monastic habit and giving themselves to strict ascetic labor.
Venerable Pimen the Great.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Agathon, Wonderworker of the K.life: Venerable Agathon, Wonderworker of the Kyiv Caves, labored in the Far Caves of Saint Theodosius in the thirteenth and fourteenth centuries, and the tradition of the Lavra preserves his portrait in two gifts, healing and foreknowledge, the open hand and the open eye. The sick were brought to Agathon and he healed them by the laying on of hands, the most ancient and most personal of the Church's medicines, the grace of God passing through the monk's palms as through the aprons of the apostles, without herbs, fees, or formulas;.
Venerable Agathon, Wonderworker of the K.patron: Invoked for healers; those who await their hour.
Venerable Agathon, Wonderworker of the K.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Gobron (Michael) and 133 soldiers.life: The Holy Martyr Gobron, in holy baptism Michael, was a Georgian noble and commander, called Gobron, the brave, for his valor; and in the year 914, when the Muslim armies swept through the Georgian lands, he led the defense of the fortress of Kveli. After a long siege the fortress fell, and Michael was taken captive with a hundred and thirty-three of his soldiers;.
Martyr Gobron (Michael) and 133 soldiers.patron: Invoked for soldiers; fidelity in defeat.
Martyr Gobron (Michael) and 133 soldiers.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Dēmḗtrios of Thrace.life: The Holy Martyr Demetrios of Thrace was a Christian of the village of Dabuda, near the town of Amapas in the Thracian country, and suffered in the persecution at the close of the third century, about the year 298. Seized as a Christian and brought before the governor of the province, he confessed the Lord Jesus Christ with plainness and courage, and neither the persuasions nor the threats of the judge could bring him to offer sacrifice to the idols;.
Martyr Dēmḗtrios of Thrace.patron: Invoked for steadfastness of the unknown.
Martyr Dēmḗtrios of Thrace.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saints Martinian, Zoe, and Photina of Ca.life: Saints Martinian, Zoe, and Photina of Caesarea in Palestine share one feast because they share one story, the Church's great chronicle of temptation fought to a triple victory. Martinian went into the wilderness near Caesarea at eighteen, and for twenty-five years devoted himself to ascetic deeds and silence, receiving the gifts of healing and of casting out demons;.
Saints Martinian, Zoe, and Photina of Ca.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Theodora of Alexandria.life: Saint Theodora of Alexandria lived in the fifth century with her husband in love and harmony, until, ensnared by the persistence of a certain rich man and the deceit of a procuress who told her that God does not see what is done in darkness, she fell into sin.
Venerable Theodora of Alexandria.patron: Invoked for repentance; those bearing false accusation.
Venerable Theodora of Alexandria.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Florentius of Thessalonica.life: The Holy Martyr Florentius was a native of Thessalonica, zealous for the glory of God, who fearlessly unmasked the darkness of idolatry among his fellow citizens and led many to the light of the true knowledge of God, teaching them faith in Christ and the doing of His will.
Martyr Florentius of Thessalonica.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Apostle Aristarchus of the Seventy.life: The Holy Apostle Aristarchus of the Seventy was a Macedonian of Thessalonica and one of the most faithful companions of the Holy Apostle Paul, named by him in his epistles as his fellow laborer and fellow prisoner. He shared the Apostle's labors and dangers at Ephesus, where he was seized by the mob in the theater;.
Apostle Aristarchus of the Seventy.patron: Invoked for fellow laborers; faithfulness in companionship.
Apostle Aristarchus of the Seventy.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Perpetua, a woman of Carthage, a.life: The Holy Martyrs Perpetua and Felicitas, with the catechumens Saturus, Revocatus, Saturninus, and Secundulus, suffered at Carthage about the year 203, and their contest is the most intimately known of the ancient Church, for Perpetua kept a diary in prison, and the Church has read her own hand for eighteen centuries, the earliest writing we possess from a Christian woman.
Martyrs Perpetua, a woman of Carthage, a.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Joseph the Wonderworker, Igume.life: On this day the Church commemorates the glorification of Saint Joseph the Wonderworker, Abbot of Volokolamsk, who was numbered among the saints of the whole Russian Church by the council of the year 1591, his local veneration having been established already in 1579. Born in 1440 and formed under Saint Paphnutius of Borovsk, Joseph founded in the forests of his native Volokolamsk the famous monastery of the Dormition, whose strict common life, great library, and boundless almsgiving made it a school of hierarchs and a refuge of the poor, feeding hundreds in time of famine;.
Venerable Joseph the Wonderworker, Igume.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Amphilochius, Abbot of Glushet.life: Saint Amphilochius of Glushitsa came as a hieromonk from Ustyug to the great founder Saint Dionysius of Glushitsa in the Vologda wilderness, having heard of his angelic life, and begged to be received as his disciple. Dionysius, foreseeing in him a worthy co-laborer, accepted him with joy, and for twenty years Amphilochius shared all the labors of his elder, in the building of churches and cells, the painting of icons, the copying of books, and the guidance of the brethren, being to him as a right hand and imitating his humility and severity of life.
Venerable Amphilochius, Abbot of Glushet.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Blessed Andrew the Fool-For-Christ at Co.life: Blessed Andrew the Fool-for-Christ was a Slav by birth, brought as a slave in his youth to Constantinople, where he served a dignitary of the city and was loved for his gentleness and his diligence in the Scriptures. Beholding in a dream the armies of the angels and of the demons contending, and hearing the Lord call him to the contest, he took upon himself with his master's eventual release the hardest of ascetic paths, feigning madness for the sake of Christ;.
Blessed Andrew the Fool-For-Christ at Co.patron: Invoked for the hidden servants of God; visions of heavenly things.
Blessed Andrew the Fool-For-Christ at Co.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Mercurius of Smolensk.life: The Holy Martyr Mercurius of Smolensk, a warrior of noble birth from the western lands who served in the host of Smolensk, was a man of secret prayer and strict life; and in the year 1239, when the hordes of Batu, having drowned Rus in blood, drew near the city and encamped at Dolgomostye, the Mother of God herself raised up its defender.
Martyr Mercurius of Smolensk.patron: Invoked for soldiers; defenders of cities.
Martyr Mercurius of Smolensk.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Anthusa at Rome.life: The Holy Martyr Anthusa was the wife of a Roman official in the days when the Arian heresy, though condemned at Nicaea, still held courts and palaces in its grip; and desiring holy baptism, she would have it from no doubtful hand, but received the saving mystery from Saint Ambrose of Milan himself, the great defender of the Godhead of Christ.
Martyr Anthusa at Rome.patron: Invoked for wives of officials; baptism kept unadulterated.
Martyr Anthusa at Rome.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Seraphim (Samoilovich), Arch.life: The Hieromartyr Seraphim, Archbishop of Uglich, was born Semyon Samoylovich in 1881 at Myrgorod in the Poltava lands, and after seminary he volunteered for the American mission, teaching at the church school of Unalaska and then at Sitka, where he was tonsured and ordained hieromonk, serving the Alaskan missions and the Sitka seminary as a zealous co-laborer of the future Patriarch Tikhon, who valued him highly.
Hieromartyr Seraphim (Samoilovich), Arch.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Athenogenes, Bishop of Herac.life: The Hieromartyr Athenogenes, Bishop of Heracleopolis, suffered together with his ten disciples during the persecution under Diocletian in the city of Sebaste in Cappadocia. When the governor Philomachos held a great festival to the idols and commanded the people to sacrifice, the citizens of Sebaste, most of whom were Christians, refused, and many received the crown of martyrdom under the soldiers' swords.
Hieromartyr Athenogenes, Bishop of Herac.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Holy Righteous David the King.life: The Holy Prophet and King David, sweet singer of Israel, was the youngest son of Jesse of Bethlehem, a shepherd boy fetched from the flock to be anointed by Samuel while his tall brothers were passed over, for the Lord looketh on the heart. His youth is the epic of Israel: the harp that soothed Saul's darkness, the.
Holy Righteous David the King.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Heiromartyr Theokteristus.life: The Holy Confessor-Martyr Theokteristus, called also Theosteriktos, Abbot of the Pelecete monastery near Prusa, stood at the center of one of the iconoclast persecution's darkest atrocities and gave the Church, out of that darkness, one of her most beloved prayers. Born at Triglia in Bithynia, he became a monk in his youth at the monastery of Saint John.
Heiromartyr Theokteristus.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Holy King Askiot of Georgia.life: Saint Ashot the Kuropalates, King of Georgia, reigned in the ninth century, in the generation when the Georgian lands lay wasted by the Arab invasions, and became the ruler under whom the nation began to rise from its ruins. Withdrawing from occupied Kartli to the wooded highlands of Tao-Klarjeti, Ashot, first of the Bagratid line to bear the.
Holy King Askiot of Georgia.patron: Invoked for rulers who rebuild; patrons of monasteries.
Holy King Askiot of Georgia.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Basil and Theodore of the Kyiv C.life: Saints Basil and Theodore struggled as ascetics in the eleventh century in the Near Caves of Kiev. Saint Theodore had distributed his wealth to the poor and entered the monastery, settling in the Varangian Cave, but after many years the enemy tempted him with the thought of a treasure of gold and silver said to be hidden there, seeking to draw him from his monastic vows.
Martyrs Basil and Theodore of the Kyiv C.patron: Invoked for detachment from riches; against greed.
Martyrs Basil and Theodore of the Kyiv C.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Holy, Glorious Apostle Thomas.life: The Holy and Glorious Apostle Thomas, called the Twin, was a Galilean fisherman called by the Lord into the company of the Twelve, and the Gospel shows his ardent heart, for when the Lord went toward Judea to raise Lazarus, it was Thomas who said, Let us also go, that we may die with Him.
Holy, Glorious Apostle Thomas.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Isaac the Ascetic of the Dalma.life: Saint Isaac was a hermit of the eastern wilderness who lived in the fourth century, in the reign of the Arian emperor Valens. When he heard that Valens was persecuting the Orthodox, expelling their bishops and handing over their churches to the heretics, he left his solitude and came to Constantinople to confront the emperor, who was then setting out to war against the Goths.
Venerable Isaac the Ascetic of the Dalma.patron: Invoked for monastics; defense of Orthodoxy against heresy.
Venerable Isaac the Ascetic of the Dalma.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Hierotheus, Bishop of Athens.life: The Hieromartyr Hierotheus, Bishop of Athens, was a member of the court of the Areopagus and was brought to Christ, together with Dionysius the Areopagite, by the preaching of the Holy Apostle Paul, who consecrated him first bishop of Athens; and he in turn instructed Dionysius more perfectly in the mysteries of the faith, so that his disciple calls him teacher and speaks of his hymns and definitions of divine love with reverence.
Hieromartyr Hierotheus, Bishop of Athens.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Hypatius of Gangra.life: The Hieromartyr Hypatius, Bishop of Gangra in Paphlagonia, was one of the fathers of the First Ecumenical Council at Nicaea in 325, where the heresy of Arius was anathematized and the Church confessed the Son of God consubstantial with the Father. A wonderworker famed through all the region for casting out demons and healing the sick, he was.
Saint Hypatius of Gangra.patron: Invoked for deliverance from demons; healing.
Saint Hypatius of Gangra.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Callistratus and 49 companions.life: The Holy Martyr Callistratus was born at Carthage of a Christian family; his ancestor Neochorus, a soldier in Palestine under Pontius Pilate, had beheld the Crucifixion and Resurrection of the Lord and returned home a believer, and the faith was handed down in his house. Callistratus himself became a soldier, excelling all in gentleness of conduct, and rising at night for prayer;.
Martyr Callistratus and 49 companions.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Apostle and Evangelist Luke.life: The Holy Apostle and Evangelist Luke was a native of Antioch, a physician by art and learned also in painting, and coming to the Lord he was numbered among the Seventy and sent before His face; and he was one of the two disciples to whom the risen Christ appeared on the road to Emmaus, when their hearts burned within them as He opened the Scriptures.
Apostle and Evangelist Luke.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Holy Prophet Zachariah and Righteous Eli.life: The Holy Prophet Zachariah and the Righteous Elizabeth were the parents of Saint John, the Forerunner and Baptist of the Lord. Both were of the lineage of Aaron, Zachariah serving as a priest in the Temple at Jerusalem and Elizabeth being kinswoman of the Most Holy Theotokos; and as the Gospel testifies, they walked blamelessly in all the commandments of the Lord, yet had grown old without children.
Holy Prophet Zachariah and Righteous Eli.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable John Cassian the Roman.life: Venerable John Cassian the Roman is the great courier of the desert, the man who packed the wisdom of Egypt into two books and carried it to the West, and the Church gives him the rarest feast in her calendar, the twenty-ninth of February, as though marking that such men come once in a long while.
Venerable John Cassian the Roman.patron: Invoked for monks of the West; writers on prayer.
Venerable John Cassian the Roman.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Alexei, Metropolitan of Moscow, Wo.life: Saint Alexei, Metropolitan of Moscow and All Russia, Wonderworker, was born Eleutherius to the boyar family of the Byakonts about the year 1300, and God addressed him in boyhood through his own pastime: dozing over his fowling nets at twelve, the boy heard a voice say, Alexei, why do you labor in vain? I shall make you a fisher of men;.
Saint Alexei, Metropolitan of Moscow, Wo.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Florus and Laurus of Illyria.life: The Holy Martyrs Florus and Laurus were twin brothers, kindred not only in the flesh but in the spirit, who lived in the second century and settled in Illyria, where they worked as stonemasons; from their Christian masters, Proclus and Maximus, they had learned both their craft and the way of life pleasing to God.
Martyrs Florus and Laurus of Illyria.patron: Invoked for stonemasons; horses and horsemen.
Martyrs Florus and Laurus of Illyria.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Lucian the Presbyter of the.life: The Hieromartyr Lucian, Presbyter of the Kyiv Caves, served God as a priest-monk of the great Lavra in the most terrible years its city ever knew, when the hordes of Batu broke upon Rus, and Kyiv, the mother of her cities, was given to fire and slaughter. In that devastation, about the year 1243, the priest Lucian received the crown of martyrdom, slain by the godless invaders while remaining at his post among the holy caves;.
Hieromartyr Lucian the Presbyter of the.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Nikon, Abbot of Radonezh, disc.life: Saint Nikon of Radonezh, the disciple and successor of Saint Sergius, was born at Yuriev-Polsky and came in his youth to the great elder, who, testing his humility, sent him first to his disciple Athanasius at Serpukhov; and there Nikon was tonsured and ordained, returning at last to Sergius, who so loved him that he kept him in his own cell and, six months before his repose, withdrawing into silence, set Nikon over the brotherhood.
Venerable Nikon, Abbot of Radonezh, disc.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Synaxis of the Archangel Gabriel.life: This feast is a second solemn commemoration of the holy Archangel Gabriel, one of the chief among the bodiless powers, who stands before the throne of God and is sent as the messenger of His saving counsels to mankind. It was Gabriel who was sent to announce to the Most Holy Virgin Mary the good news of the Incarnation of the Son of God, and who through the ages has been the bearer of glad tidings and the defender of the faithful.
Synaxis of the Archangel Gabriel.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs and Passion-Bearers Boris and Gl.life: Saints Boris and Gleb, called Roman and David in holy baptism, were younger sons of Saint Vladimir, the baptizer of Rus, and they were the first saints glorified in the Russian land. Upon the death of their father in the year 1015, their elder brother Svyatopolk seized the throne of Kyiv and resolved to destroy his brothers that he might reign without rival.
Martyrs and Passion-Bearers Boris and Gl.patron: Invoked for non-resistance to evil; brotherly love.
Martyrs and Passion-Bearers Boris and Gl.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Silvanus the Schemamonk of the.life: Saint Silvanus was a schemamonk of the Kyiv Caves who lived at the end of the thirteenth and the beginning of the fourteenth century. Zealously guarding the purity of both soul and body, he subdued his flesh through fasting and vigil and cleansed his mind through unceasing prayer and the remembrance of God, and for this the Lord granted him rich spiritual gifts: boldness in prayer, constant joy in the Lord, clairvoyance, and the working of wonders.
Venerable Silvanus the Schemamonk of the.patron: Invoked for purity of soul and body.
Venerable Silvanus the Schemamonk of the.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Melania the Younger of Rome.life: Venerable Melania the Younger of Rome was born into the highest aristocracy of the empire, heiress of the Valerii, holder of estates in Italy, Sicily, Spain, Africa, and Britain, perhaps the richest private person of her age.
Venerable Melania the Younger of Rome.patron: Invoked for heiresses; founders of monasteries.
Venerable Melania the Younger of Rome.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Afterfeast of the Meeting of our Lord in.life: The Afterfeast of the Meeting of our Lord in the Temple carries the feast of the second of February through the days that follow, to the leavetaking on the ninth, and in them the Church remains standing in the Temple with the Child in her arms; for the Meeting is the hinge on which the whole Nativity cycle closes, the forty-day fulfillment of the Incarnation's law, and a mystery of that weight is not dismissed in a day.
Afterfeast of the Meeting of our Lord in.patron: Commemorated in the holy calendar of the Church.
Afterfeast of the Meeting of our Lord in.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Arsenius, Bishop of Tver.life: Saint Arsenius, Bishop of Tver, was formed as a monk at the Kyiv Caves Lavra, the mother house of Russian monasticism, and carried its tradition north in both of the forms that endure, stone and ink. Taken into the service of the Metropolitan Cyprian, he was consecrated to the see of Tver in 1390, at a moment when that principality was tearing itself in the feuds of its princes and the quarrels that had left the see itself disputed;.
Saint Arsenius, Bishop of Tver.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Forefeast of the Meeting of our Lord in.life: The Forefeast of the Meeting of our Lord in the Temple is kept on the first of February, a single day of preparation before the feast that closes the whole cycle of the Lord's Nativity; and in it the Church turns her eyes to the Temple of Jerusalem, where tomorrow the Lawgiver will be carried in as a forty-day-old child to fulfill His own Law.
Forefeast of the Meeting of our Lord in.patron: Commemorated in the holy calendar of the Church.
Forefeast of the Meeting of our Lord in.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Victor at Damascus.life: The Holy Martyr Victor was a soldier from Italy serving at Damascus in the reign of Marcus Aurelius; and when the persecution required the army to sacrifice, he declared himself a Christian and refused. The commander gave him over to torments of extraordinary cruelty: his fingers were broken and wrenched, he was cast into a burning oven and.
Martyr Victor at Damascus.patron: Invoked for soldiers; endurance beyond nature.
Martyr Victor at Damascus.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Gregory the Iconographer of th.life: Saint Gregory the Iconographer was a monk of the Kiev Caves and a companion of Saint Alypius, the first iconographer of the Russian Land. In the accounts of the holy iconographers it is written that he painted many wonderworking icons throughout Rus, and in the hymns of the monastery he is called a Byzantine, which suggests that he was among the masters who came from Constantinople to adorn the great cathedral of the Dormition in the Caves monastery with holy images.
Venerable Gregory the Iconographer of th.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Translation of the relics of Saint Peter.life: Saint Peter, Metropolitan of Moscow and of all Russia, was the first primate of the Russian Church to make his dwelling in Moscow, and by this he blessed the rise of that city, which under his successors became the heart of the Russian land. A shepherd of great holiness and wisdom, he strengthened the faith among his flock in a hard time of division and Tatar dominion, upheld the unity of the Church, and foretold the future glory of Moscow;.
Translation of the relics of Saint Peter.patron: Invoked for Moscow; the unity of the Church.
Translation of the relics of Saint Peter.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Monastic Martyr Macarius of Dionysiou, M.life: Saint Macarius was a monk of the monastery of Dionysiou on Mount Athos and a disciple of the holy Patriarch Niphon of Constantinople, who in his years of retirement labored in that monastery; and from his elder Macarius learned obedience, prayer, and burning love for Christ. Consumed with longing to bear witness to his Lord among those who denied Him, he received the blessing of Saint Niphon, who foretold his end, and went to Thessalonica, where he began openly to preach Christ to the Turks and to call them from their error.
Monastic Martyr Macarius of Dionysiou, M.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Alexander, Abbot of Svir.life: Saint Alexander of Svir was born in the year 1448 in a village of the Russian North and was named Amos at his baptism, after the prophet on whose feast he came into the world. Drawn from his youth to the monastic life, he departed secretly to Valaam, where he was tonsured, and after some years he withdrew into the deep forests near the river Svir to live in stillness and prayer.
Venerable Alexander, Abbot of Svir.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Romulus and with him many others.life: The Holy Martyr Romulus lived in the reign of the emperor Trajan and held high office at the imperial court. When the emperor, warring in the East, ordered a count of the Christians serving in his armies, eleven thousand were found, and he commanded that they all be stripped of their rank and banished to Armenia.
Martyr Romulus and with him many others.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Herodion, Abbot of Iloezersk.life: Saint Herodion of Iloezersk was a disciple of Saint Cornelius of Komel, in whose monastery he was tonsured and trained in the ascetic traditions of the Vologda wilderness. After the repose of his elder, seeking stillness, he withdrew into the forests of the Belozersk country and settled by the small Lake Ilo, where he built himself a cell and a chapel in honor of the Nativity of the Most Holy Theotokos, and lived alone in fasting, vigil, and unceasing prayer, taking upon himself at the last the great schema.
Venerable Herodion, Abbot of Iloezersk.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Moses the Hungarian of the Kyi.life: Saint Moses, a Hungarian by birth and the brother of Saint Ephraim of Novy Torg, entered together with his brothers the service of the holy Prince Boris the passion-bearer. When Boris was murdered upon the Alta River in the year 1015, and one of the brothers slain with him, Moses fled and found refuge in Kyiv;.
Venerable Moses the Hungarian of the Kyi.patron: Invoked for chastity; those tempted by lust.
Venerable Moses the Hungarian of the Kyi.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Eudoxius, Zeno, and Macarius.life: The Holy Martyrs Eudoxius, Zeno, and Macarius suffered under Maximian Galerius, the successor of Diocletian. Eudoxius was a commander of high rank in the imperial armies and a Christian, as were his friend Zeno and his steward Macarius; and when the decree went out against the faithful, he withdrew with his family, but was sought by soldiers who, not knowing him, received his hospitality.
Martyrs Eudoxius, Zeno, and Macarius.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Repose of Saint Peter, Metropolitan of M.life: Saint Peter, Metropolitan of Kyiv and All Rus, wonderworker of Moscow, was born in Volhynia and given to a monastery at twelve years of age, where alongside obedience and prayer he mastered the art of the icon, painting images of the Savior and the Mother of God, one of which, the Petrovskaya, is venerated to this day;.
Repose of Saint Peter, Metropolitan of M.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Sophronius, Archbishop of Cyprus.life: Saint Sophronius, Archbishop of Cyprus, was born on that island of saints and shone from his youth in the double adornment that his flock would later bless: deep learning in the divine Scriptures, and a heart wholly given to mercy. Raised to the archiepiscopal throne of Cyprus on the repose of his predecessor, being chosen by the love.
Saint Sophronius, Archbishop of Cyprus.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Potitus at Naples.life: The Holy Martyr Potitus suffered in the second century under the emperor Antoninus Pius. Coming to know the Christian faith as a boy, he was baptized at the age of thirteen, and when his pagan father sought first by persuasion and then by threats to turn him from Christ, the father was himself won over by his son's steadfastness and became a Christian.
Martyr Potitus at Naples.patron: Invoked for the sick; deliverance from demons.
Martyr Potitus at Naples.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Clement of Ochrid, Equal of the Ap.life: Saints Clement, Nahum, Sava, Gorazd, and Angelar were Slavs and disciples of the holy Equals of the Apostles Cyril and Methodius, and together with their teachers they are honored as enlighteners of the Slavic peoples. They first labored in Moravia, where they preached and celebrated the divine services in the Slavonic tongue, using the letters devised by Saint Cyril, and Saint Gorazd succeeded Saint Methodius as archbishop.
Saint Clement of Ochrid, Equal of the Ap.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Athanasius the Recluse of the.life: Venerable Athanasius, recluse of the Far Caves, labored in the Kyiv Caves Lavra in the thirteenth century, taking upon himself the hardest of the Caves disciplines, the sealed life of the recluse, in which the monk walls himself into the darkness under the earth with God alone. The tradition of the Lavra, preserved in the old accounts of.
Venerable Athanasius the Recluse of the.patron: Invoked for light in the darkness of the cell; healing of the sick.
Venerable Athanasius the Recluse of the.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Stephanida of Damascus.life: The Holy Martyr Stephanida suffered at Damascus in the second century, in the persecution under Marcus Aurelius. A young Christian woman of Spanish birth and the wife of a soldier, she stood among the onlookers at the torture of the holy Martyr Victor; and beholding the grace of God that upheld him, she saw, as the account relates, two crowns descending from heaven, one for Victor and one for herself, and cried out openly, blessing the martyr and confessing herself a Christian.
Martyr Stephanida of Damascus.patron: Invoked for young wives; witness kindled by witness.
Martyr Stephanida of Damascus.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Daniel the Confessor (in Schem.life: Saint Daniel the Confessor, in the Great Schema Stephen, lived in the tenth century, a dignitary of Spain and prefect of the island of Niverta, a man holding under his hand the honors that most men spend their lives pursuing; and disdaining worldly glory, he laid down his office and his country together, and became a monk at Rome.
Venerable Daniel the Confessor (in Schem.patron: Invoked for officials who renounce office; pilgrims.
Venerable Daniel the Confessor (in Schem.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Uncovering of the relics of Saint Joasap.life: Saint Joasaph, Bishop of Belgorod, was born in 1705 at Priluki in the Poltava lands, on the very feast of the Nativity of the Theotokos, of the noble Ukrainian line of the Gorlenkos, and was named Joachim in baptism. Educated at the Kyiv spiritual academy, he was drawn early to the monastic life, was tonsured with the name Joasaph, and after serving as abbot of the Mgar monastery and vicar of the Trinity-Sergius Lavra, he was consecrated Bishop of Belgorod in 1748.
Uncovering of the relics of Saint Joasap.patron: Invoked for strictness of life; care for the clergy.
Uncovering of the relics of Saint Joasap.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Conception of the Most Holy Theotokos by.life: This feast celebrates the conception of the Virgin Mary by her mother, the righteous Anna, nine months before the feast of Mary's nativity on the eighth of September. According to the tradition of the Church, Joachim and Anna were righteous but childless and advanced in years, and their childlessness was reckoned a reproach.
Conception of the Most Holy Theotokos by.patron: Commemorated in the holy calendar of the Church.
Conception of the Most Holy Theotokos by.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Marinus the Elder at Anazarbus.life: The Holy Martyr Marinus the Elder suffered for Christ at Anazarbus in Cilicia in the reign of Diocletian, being already advanced in years when the persecution overtook him. Brought before the governor Lysias, the old man was urged to spare his grey hairs and offer the sacrifice, but he answered that length of days had only confirmed him in the knowledge of the true God, and that he would not in the evening of his life deny the Master he had served since morning.
Martyr Marinus the Elder at Anazarbus.patron: Invoked for the aged; courage in old age.
Martyr Marinus the Elder at Anazarbus.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Prophet Nahum.life: The Holy Prophet Nahum, whose name means God consoles, was of the village of Elkosh in Galilee, and prophesied in the seventh century before Christ, the seventh in order of the twelve minor prophets. His short book is a single burning oracle against Nineveh, the capital of Assyria, which had crushed Israel and led the ten tribes into.
Prophet Nahum.patron: Invoked for consolation of the afflicted; those suffering mental disorders.
Prophet Nahum.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

The Nativity of our Most Holy Lady the M.life: The Nativity of the Theotokos celebrates the birth of the Virgin Mary to the righteous Joachim and Anna, an aged and childless couple of the royal line of David who had long prayed for a child and borne the reproach of barrenness. In answer to their prayer, an angel announced to each of them that they would have.
The Nativity of our Most Holy Lady the M.patron: Commemorated in the holy calendar of the Church.
The Nativity of our Most Holy Lady the M.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Alexander of Guria.life: The Holy Hierarch Alexander of Guria, in the world Alexi Okropiridze, was born in 1824 in the village of Disevi in the Gori district, the son of the village priest, and after the seminary of Tbilisi he was tonsured a monk and completed his studies with honors at the theological academy of Kazan.
Saint Alexander of Guria.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Titus the Presbyter of the Kyi.life: Venerable Titus the Presbyter of the Kyiv Near Caves is the Caves' own parable of forgiveness, the Russian brother of the ancient Nikephoros, and the Paterikon tells his story as a court record of the judgment of God. Titus, a priest of the monastery, and Evagrius, a deacon, had been friends so close that the brethren held their love for a pattern;.
Venerable Titus the Presbyter of the Kyi.patron: Invoked for the estranged; priests in quarrels.
Venerable Titus the Presbyter of the Kyi.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Peter the Aleut.life: The Holy Martyr Peter the Aleut was a young native of the Kodiak region of Alaska, baptized into the Orthodox faith by the Russian missionaries and employed with his countrymen in the hunting parties of the colony. In the year 1815 he was captured with other Aleuts by Spanish soldiers in California, and there pressure was put upon the prisoners to abandon Orthodoxy for the Latin faith;.
Martyr Peter the Aleut.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Blessed Nicholas (Salos) of Pskov the Fo.life: Blessed Nicholas Salos of Pskov, whom the city called Mikula the Fool, carried the exploit of folly for Christ through more than three decades, sleeping on the porches, enduring frost and mockery in rags, speaking in riddles that came true, and acquiring, long before his repose, the grace of wonderworking and of prophecy, the city's madman quietly becoming its most reliable oracle;.
Blessed Nicholas (Salos) of Pskov the Fo.patron: Invoked for fools for Christ; truth-tellers before power.
Blessed Nicholas (Salos) of Pskov the Fo.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Bassa of Edessa and her sons Theo.life: The Holy Martyr Bassa lived in the city of Edessa in Macedonia and was married to a pagan priest, though she herself had been raised from childhood in the Christian faith, which she also taught to her three sons, Theognis, Agapius, and Pistus. In the persecution under Maximian, her own husband denounced her and the children to the.
Martyr Bassa of Edessa and her sons Theo.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Constantine of Synnada.life: Venerable Constantine of Synnada was born of Jewish parents in that Phrygian city in the ninth century, and grace found him through the smallest of doors. Living among Christians, the youth observed how they sealed themselves with the sign of the Cross, and began, half in imitation, to make the sign upon himself;.
Venerable Constantine of Synnada.patron: Invoked for converts from Judaism; catechumens.
Venerable Constantine of Synnada.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Synaxis of the Hierarchs of Moscow.life: On this day the Church keeps the Synaxis of the Hierarchs of Moscow, the holy first hierarchs of the Russian Church who are also honored each on his own day: Peter, who transferred the metropolitan see to Moscow and foretold its greatness; Alexis, the guardian of the realm in the days of the Horde;.
Synaxis of the Hierarchs of Moscow.patron: Invoked for the Russian Church; right governance of the Church.
Synaxis of the Hierarchs of Moscow.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Lazarus, Wonderworker of Mount.life: Saint Lazarus the Wonderworker of Mount Galesius was born in Lydia in Asia Minor, and in his youth journeyed to the Holy Land, where he labored for ten years in the Lavra of Saint Sabbas and was ordained to the priesthood by the Patriarch of Jerusalem. Returning to his homeland, he settled on the desolate Mount Galesius near Ephesus;.
Venerable Lazarus, Wonderworker of Mount.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Martyrius the Deacon, Recluse.life: Saint Martyrius the Deacon labored in the Kyiv Caves monastery in the fourteenth century, serving at the divine services in the order of the diaconate and adorning his ministry with fasting, purity, and unceasing prayer. Such boldness before God was given him that, as the tradition of the Lavra records, when he prayed for anything standing upon the ambo, the Lord speedily granted it;.
Venerable Martyrius the Deacon, Recluse.patron: Invoked for deacons; prayer heard by God.
Venerable Martyrius the Deacon, Recluse.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Repose of Saint Jonah, Archbishop of Nov.life: Saint Jonah, Archbishop of Novgorod, was in the world John, orphaned in childhood and raised by a pious widow in Novgorod; and once, as the boy stood among his fellows, the blessed Michael of Klops, the fool for Christ, passed by, and bowing to the child said, John, study your book diligently, for you shall be archbishop of Great Novgorod.
Repose of Saint Jonah, Archbishop of Nov.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Uncovering of the relics of Holy Princes.life: Saint Juliana was the daughter of Prince Yuri Dubrovitsky-Olshansky, whose family ruled Olshansk when Kyiv lay under the Lithuanian realm. A benefactor of the Kyiv Caves Lavra, her father buried her near the great church of the monastery when she reposed as a pure virgin at the age of sixteen, in the sixteenth century.
Uncovering of the relics of Holy Princes.patron: Invoked for women; healing of the soul.
Uncovering of the relics of Holy Princes.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Sergius of Malopinega.life: Saint Sergius of Malopinega, in the world Simeon, was born in 1493, the son of Markian Nekliud, of the nobility of Great Novgorod, whose family departed for the far north, toward the icy sea, when the liberty of their city came to its end. Ordained presbyter at the canonical age of thirty, Simeon served for thirty-two years the churches of the Transfiguration of the Lord and of the Great Martyr George in the Malopinega district on the northern rivers;.
Saint Sergius of Malopinega.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Great Martyr Anastasia the Deliverer fro.life: The Holy Great Martyr Anastasia, the Deliverer from Poisons, was a Roman of noble birth, daughter of a pagan father and a secret Christian mother, Fausta, and was formed in the faith by her teacher, the wise confessor Chrysogonos. Married against her heart to the pagan Publius, she preserved her virginity by feigning illness, and putting on a beggar's clothes, she went with a single servant through the prisons of Rome, feeding, treating, and ransoming the captives of Christ, for she was skilled in the medical arts and made her science a ministry;.
Great Martyr Anastasia the Deliverer fro.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Arsenius, Abbot of Komel, Volo.life: Saint Arsenius of Komel was born in Moscow of a noble family and in his youth was tonsured at the Trinity monastery of Saint Sergius, where he labored at the copying of holy books, one of which, a Gospel written in his hand, is preserved to this day.
Venerable Arsenius, Abbot of Komel, Volo.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Holy Wonderworkers and Unmercenaries Cyr.life: The Holy Wonderworkers and Unmercenaries Cyrus and John suffered at Canopus in Egypt in the year 311, and the Church sets them beside Cosmas and Damian among the physicians who would take no fee. Cyrus was a doctor of Alexandria, famous through Egypt for a practice that healed twice, for he treated the body without payment and used the bedside to treat the soul, telling his patients that sickness often follows sin and leading them to the Physician of all;.
Holy Wonderworkers and Unmercenaries Cyr.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Meletius, Archbishop of Antioch.life: Saint Meletius, Archbishop of Antioch, was born at Melitene in Armenia of noble family, and came to the throne of Antioch in 360 with the approval of the Arians, who mistook his mildness for their own doctrine; his first sermon undeceived them, for the new archbishop preached the Son consubstantial with the Father, and within a month the party that had installed him had procured his exile, the gentlest bishop in the East proving unbribable at the first asking.
Saint Meletius, Archbishop of Antioch.patron: Invoked for bishops of divided flocks; peacemakers.
Saint Meletius, Archbishop of Antioch.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Greatmartyr Artemius at Antioch.life: The Holy Great Martyr Artemius of Antioch was a distinguished commander under Saint Constantine the Great and his son Constantius, honored for valor and service and made imperial viceroy of Egypt, where he labored much for the spreading of the faith; and it was Artemius whom the emperor sent to bring the relics of the Apostle Andrew from Patras and of the Apostle Luke from Thebes of Boeotia to Constantinople, where they were laid in the church of the Holy Apostles.
Greatmartyr Artemius at Antioch.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Antherus (Antheros) Pope of.life: Saint Antherus, a Greek by birth, was chosen Bishop of Rome in succession to Saint Pontian, but he held the see for only a short time, for he soon confessed Christ and suffered death for the faith in the year 236. He was laid to rest in the catacomb of Saint Callistus, the first of the bishops of Rome to be buried in that hallowed place, and after him Saint Fabian was chosen to shepherd the Church of Rome.
Hieromartyr Antherus (Antheros) Pope of.patron: Commemorated in the holy calendar of the Church.
Hieromartyr Antherus (Antheros) Pope of.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Translation of the relics of Saint Hilar.life: On this day the Church commemorates the translation of the relics of Saint Hilarion, Bishop of Meglin, which took place in the year 1206, when the Bulgarian tsar Kaloyan, gathering the holy treasures of the land, brought the wonderworking relics of the hierarch to his capital of Tarnovo.
Translation of the relics of Saint Hilar.patron: Invoked for apologists; the defense of Orthodoxy against heresy.
Translation of the relics of Saint Hilar.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Tryphon of Lampsacus Near Apamea.life: The Holy Martyr Tryphon was born in the village of Kampsada near Apamea in Phrygia, a peasant boy who tended geese; and upon this least credentialed of the Church's healers the Lord poured from early years the power to cast out demons and cure every disease. His wonders had the scale of his charity: he saved his native district from starvation by turning back with prayer a plague of locusts that was devouring the grain, the gooseherd commanding the fields' destroyers;.
Martyr Tryphon of Lampsacus Near Apamea.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Stephen the “New Light” of Constan.life: Saint Stephen of Constantinople, called the New Light, Neolampes, served among the clergy of the Great Church of Hagia Sophia in the ninth and tenth centuries, and in the very center of the world's splendor he kindled the older, harder light of the ascetics. Renouncing ease while remaining in the city, he took upon himself an enclosed life of extraordinary severity: confinement in a narrow cell, unbroken fasting, standing prayer, and endurance of illness and deprivation borne without complaint, so that those who knew the outward clergyman discovered with awe the hidden athlete;.
Saint Stephen the “New Light” of Constan.patron: Invoked for clergy of great churches; late-shining holiness.
Saint Stephen the “New Light” of Constan.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Peter, Archbishop of Alexand.life: The Hieromartyr Peter, Archbishop of Alexandria, was raised in that city's great catechetical school, of which he became the head, and in the year 300 he ascended the patriarchal throne, only to shepherd his Church straight into the fires of the last and fiercest persecution. Hunted from place to place, he governed his scattered flock by messengers and epistles, strengthening the confessors, and composing with pastoral wisdom the penitential canons by which those who had lapsed under torture might be restored through repentance, canons the whole Church received into her law.
Hieromartyr Peter, Archbishop of Alexand.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Nilus of Stolbensk Lake.life: Saint Nilus of Stolbensk, one of the sternest ascetics of the Russian north, was born in the Novgorod lands and tonsured at the Krypetsk monastery of Saint Savva near Pskov; and burning for solitude, he lived thirteen years as a hermit in the forest by the river Seremlya, in fasting, prayer, and battle with the demons and with robbers, whom he routed, the accounts tell, by his prayer alone.
Venerable Nilus of Stolbensk Lake.patron: Invoked for hermits; vigilance unto death.
Venerable Nilus of Stolbensk Lake.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Monastic Martyr and Confessor Stephen th.life: The Monastic Martyr and Confessor Stephen the New, the great champion of the holy icons, was born in 715 at Constantinople to pious parents who, having two daughters, prayed the Lord for a son; and his mother, receiving him, carried the infant to the Blachernae church of the Most Holy Theotokos and dedicated him to God before her icon.
Monastic Martyr and Confessor Stephen th.patron: Invoked for monastics; defenders of the icons.
Monastic Martyr and Confessor Stephen th.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Theodotus and Rufina of Caesarea.life: The Holy Martyrs Theodotus and Rufina, the parents of the Great Martyr Mamas, were of patrician families and honored by all for their Christian piety. When the magistrate of Gangra summoned them for refusing to worship the idols as the imperial decree commanded, Theodotus would not comply, and because his noble rank forbade the magistrate to punish him, he was sent to the governor Faustus at Caesarea in Cappadocia, who at once cast him into prison.
Martyrs Theodotus and Rufina of Caesarea.patron: Invoked for married couples; steadfast confession.
Martyrs Theodotus and Rufina of Caesarea.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Repose of Saint Herman, Archbishop of Ka.life: On this day the Church commemorates the repose of Saint Herman, Archbishop of Kazan. Born Gregory, of the boyar family of the Polevs at Starytsa, he was tonsured at the Volokolamsk monastery of Saint Joseph, where learning and asceticism were joined, and became archimandrite of the Dormition monastery in his native Starytsa;.
Repose of Saint Herman, Archbishop of Ka.patron: Invoked for missionaries; the enlightenment of Kazan.
Repose of Saint Herman, Archbishop of Ka.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Macrina, sister of Saint Basil.life: Saint Macrina the Younger was the eldest sister of the great hierarchs Basil the Great and Gregory of Nyssa, born in Cappadocia at the beginning of the fourth century into a family that would give many saints to the Church. Before her birth her mother, Saint Emilia, beheld an angel in a dream who named the child Thekla, after the holy Protomartyr, and so this was her secret name, though she was called Macrina after her grandmother who had suffered in the persecutions.
Venerable Macrina, sister of Saint Basil.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Menodora, Metrodora, and Nymphod.life: The Holy Virgin Martyrs Menodora, Metrodora, and Nymphodora were sisters from Bithynia in Asia Minor, who, desiring to preserve their virginity for Christ and to escape the vanity of the world, withdrew to a solitary place in the hills, where they lived in fasting and prayer; and the report of their holiness spread, for healings began to flow through their prayers.
Martyrs Menodora, Metrodora, and Nymphod.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Clement, Pope of Rome.life: The Hieromartyr Clement, Pope of Rome, was born at Rome of a rich and illustrious family akin to the emperors, and by a strange providence was separated in childhood from his parents and brothers, raised among strangers with every advantage of learning but with an orphan's longing heart.
Hieromartyr Clement, Pope of Rome.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Glorification of the Priestmartyr Alexan.life: On this day the Church commemorates the glorification of the Hieromartyr Alexander Hotovitzky, numbered among the saints by the Russian Orthodox Church on the fourth of December 1994. Born on the eleventh of February 1872 at Kremenets in Volhynia, the son of a beloved archpriest and seminary rector, Alexander graduated with distinction from the Saint Petersburg Theological Academy.
Glorification of the Priestmartyr Alexan.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Solomonia, mother of the Holy Sev.life: Saint Solomonia was the mother of the seven Maccabee brothers who suffered under Antiochus Epiphanes for their faithfulness to the Law of God. Rather than counsel her sons to save their lives by breaking the covenant, this valiant mother encouraged each of them to remain faithful to God even in the face of death, and with a courage beyond her nature she watched all seven die in a single day, exhorting them to endure.
Martyr Solomonia, mother of the Holy Sev.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Mariamne the sister of the Apostle.life: Saint Mariamne, sister of the holy Apostle Philip, gave her virginity and her whole life to the service of her brother's apostolate, and stands in the calendar as the patroness of all who serve the Gospel by accompanying its preachers. When the Twelve went out into the world, Mariamne went with Philip and with the Apostle Bartholomew through.
Saint Mariamne the sister of the Apostle.patron: Invoked for sisters; women who serve the mission.
Saint Mariamne the sister of the Apostle.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Alypios, Iconographer of the K.life: Saint Alypius was one of the first and greatest of the iconographers of the Russian Church. Tonsured in the Kiev Caves monastery by the abbot Nikon and later ordained hieromonk, he learned the sacred art from the Greek masters who had come to adorn the great cathedral of the Caves, and he was himself an eyewitness of a wonder, when an image of the Mother of God imprinted itself upon the wall of the altar and shone more brightly than the sun.
Venerable Alypios, Iconographer of the K.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

7 Holy Youths “Seven Sleepers” of Ephesu.life: The seven holy youths of Ephesus, Maximilian, Iamblicus, Martinian, John, Dionysius, Exacustodianus, and Antoninus, lived in the third century and were sons of illustrious citizens, friends from childhood and soldiers together. When the emperor Decius came to Ephesus and commanded all to sacrifice to the idols, the seven confessed Christ, and though their belts of office were stripped from them, the emperor let them go free for a time, hoping they would relent.
7 Holy Youths “Seven Sleepers” of Ephesu.patron: Invoked for the resurrection of the dead; the sick who cannot sleep.
7 Holy Youths “Seven Sleepers” of Ephesu.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Callinicus of Gangra in Asia Mino.life: The Holy Martyr Callinicus, a native of Cilicia, was raised in the Christian faith from childhood, and grieving that so many should perish in the worship of idols, he went through the cities and villages preaching Christ and turning many to the truth. Arrested at Ancyra in Galatia, he was brought before the fierce governor Sacerdon, and when he fearlessly refused to sacrifice, declaring that he did not dread martyrdom, since every believer receives strength from Christ and through death inherits eternal life, he was cruelly beaten and his body torn with iron hooks.
Martyr Callinicus of Gangra in Asia Mino.patron: Invoked for preaching; compassion for enemies.
Martyr Callinicus of Gangra in Asia Mino.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Moses the Ethiopian of Scete.life: Saint Moses, called the Black, lived in Egypt in the fourth century. An Ethiopian by birth and a slave in his youth, he was driven out by his master after committing a murder, and he joined a band of robbers who, because of his great strength and boldness, made him their leader, so that his name became a terror throughout the region for his robberies and killings.
Venerable Moses the Ethiopian of Scete.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Greatmartyr Eustáthios Placidas, with hi.life: The Holy Great Martyr Eustathius, before his baptism named Placidas, was a renowned Roman general under the emperors Titus and Trajan, generous to the poor though still a pagan; and while hunting one day he was granted a wondrous vision, a stag turning to face him with the radiant Cross of Christ shining between its antlers, and a voice calling him by name, saying, Why do you pursue Me, Placidas, I am the Christ whom you unknowingly honor by your good deeds.
Greatmartyr Eustáthios Placidas, with hi.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Translation of the relics of Hieromartyr.life: This feast commemorates the solemn translation of the relics of Saint Philip, Metropolitan of Moscow, to the capital in the year 1652. Born Feodor Kolychev, Saint Philip was abbot of the Solovki monastery before he was raised to the see of Moscow, where he fearlessly rebuked the cruelties of Tsar Ivan the Terrible and the oppressions of his guard;.
Translation of the relics of Hieromartyr.patron: Invoked for the Church's freedom before the state.
Translation of the relics of Hieromartyr.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Kyriakos the Anchorite.life: Saint Kyriakos the Anchorite was born at Corinth in the year 448, the son of a presbyter, and at eighteen years of age, hearing in church the word of the Lord, Whosoever will come after Me, let him deny himself, he sailed to the Holy Land and was received by Saint Euthymius the Great, who clothed him in the monastic habit and sent him to Saint Gerasimus at the Jordan.
Venerable Kyriakos the Anchorite.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Eusignius of Antioch.life: The Holy Martyr Eusignius was born at Antioch in the middle of the third century, and for sixty years he served as a soldier in the armies of Rome under Diocletian, Maximian, Constantius Chlorus, and Constantine the Great and his sons. He was a companion of the Martyr Basiliscus, whose sufferings he set down in writing, and at the beginning of Constantine's reign he was himself an eyewitness of the appearance of the Cross in the sky that foretold the emperor's victory.
Martyr Eusignius of Antioch.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Virgin Martyr Seraphima (Serapia) of Ant.life: The Holy Virgin Martyr Seraphima was a native of Antioch who lived at Rome in the reign of the emperor Hadrian, dwelling in the house of Sabina, a noble senatorial lady whom she had brought to faith in Christ. When the persecution arose, the governor Virilus summoned her, and desiring the crown of martyrdom she went to him without fear, her faithful Sabina beside her;.
Virgin Martyr Seraphima (Serapia) of Ant.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Eusebius the Hermit of Syria.life: Venerable Eusebius the Hermit of Syria labored on a mountain near the village of Asikha, and his memory is preserved by Theodoret of Cyrrhus, the historian of the Syrian ascetics, who knew that country's athletes at first hand; and among them all, Eusebius practiced the discipline of exposure in perhaps its purest form.
Venerable Eusebius the Hermit of Syria.patron: Invoked for open-air ascetics; the aged in endurance.
Venerable Eusebius the Hermit of Syria.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Icon of the Mother of God of Kholm.life: The Kholm Icon of the Mother of God is one of the most ancient and venerated icons of the western Russian lands, and pious tradition ascribes its painting to the holy Evangelist Luke and holds that it was brought from Byzantium in the days of Saint Vladimir, when the land of Rus received holy baptism.
Icon of the Mother of God of Kholm.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Martha, mother of Venerable Si.life: Saint Martha, the mother of Saint Simeon Stylites the Younger, lived in the sixth century and was a native of Antioch. From her youth she longed for the monastic life, but at her parents' wish she married; her husband John soon died, and she gave all her strength to the raising of her son in holiness, becoming for him an example of Christian virtue.
Venerable Martha, mother of Venerable Si.patron: Invoked for mothers and their children.
Venerable Martha, mother of Venerable Si.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Eudokia of Heliopolis.life: The Holy Monastic Martyr Eudokia of Heliopolis is the Church's great figure of repentance at the head of spring, a Samaritan of the Phoenician Heliopolis, the modern Baalbek, in the days of Trajan, whose beauty had made her one of the wealthiest women of the East and whose wealth was earned in sin, her soul, as her life says plainly, deadened and her heart hardened.
Martyr Eudokia of Heliopolis.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Blessed Laurence the Fool-For-Christ at.life: Blessed Laurence, fool-for-Christ and wonderworker of Kaluga, lived at the beginning of the sixteenth century near the old city of Kaluga, close to a church of the Nativity of Christ set upon a high wooded hill, to which a long underground passage led from his dwelling so that he might attend the services.
Blessed Laurence the Fool-For-Christ at.patron: Invoked for the defense of Kaluga.
Blessed Laurence the Fool-For-Christ at.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Apostle James, the Brother of the Lord.life: The Holy Apostle James, the Brother of the Lord, was the son of the Righteous Joseph the Betrothed by his first marriage, and from childhood he shared the poverty and the journeys of the Holy Family, accompanying them, as tradition relates, in the flight into Egypt. A Nazirite consecrated to God, he drank no wine, ate no flesh, and wore a single garment, and he prayed so unceasingly in the Temple that his knees were hardened like a camel's, for which all Jerusalem, even those outside the Church, called him James the Just.
Apostle James, the Brother of the Lord.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Repose of Venerable Herman of Alaska, Wo.life: Saint Herman of Alaska, Wonderworker of All America, was born about 1756 at Serpukhov near Moscow, and formed as a monk at the Valaam monastery under the elder Nazarius; and in 1794, one of ten missionaries sent across seven thousand miles of empire and ocean, he reached Kodiak Island in Russian America after a journey of nearly a year, to bring the Gospel to the Alutiiq people.
Repose of Venerable Herman of Alaska, Wo.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Pambo the Recluse of the Kyiv.life: Saint Pambo, hieromonk and recluse of the Kyiv Caves, was a confessor of the faith who lived in the age of the Tatar invasions. While he was engaged on a monastic obedience he was captured and carried off by the Tatars, and for many years he endured their cruelty and their demands that he renounce Christ, holding fast to the true faith through every affliction.
Venerable Pambo the Recluse of the Kyiv.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).
