Saint John, Bishop of Suzdal.life: Saint John, Bishop of Suzdal and Nizhny Novgorod, shepherded his diocese in the fourteenth century, in the days of the princes of Suzdal, and was glorified as a wonderworker even in his lifetime. A father to the poor, the widowed, and the orphaned, he gave without measure and healed without payment, so that the people called him merciful;.
Saint John, Bishop of Suzdal.patron: Invoked for unmercenaries; care for the poor.
Saint John, Bishop of Suzdal.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Prophet Hosea.life: The Holy Prophet Hosea, son of Beeri, prophesied in the northern kingdom of Israel in the eighth century before Christ, in the last generations before that kingdom was carried away by Assyria, and his book stands first among the twelve minor prophets. At the command of God he took to wife Gomer, a woman of harlotry, and gave his children names of judgment, that his own household might be a living parable of Israel, the bride who had gone after other gods;.
Prophet Hosea.patron: Invoked for the mercy of God; the return of the unfaithful.
Prophet Hosea.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Thomas of Bithynia.life: Saint Thomas Dephourkinos was born in Bithynia in the tenth century, and giving himself to the monastic life from his youth, he passed through the obediences of the common life and then withdrew into the wilderness, settling at last upon Mount Kyminas, one of the holy mountains of Bithynia whose lavras and hermitages rivaled Olympus and prepared the way for Athos.
Venerable Thomas of Bithynia.patron: Invoked for spiritual fathers; letter writers.
Venerable Thomas of Bithynia.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Serapion of Spaso-Eleazar Mona.life: Saint Serapion of Pskov was born at Yuriev, now Tartu, which then lay under the rule of the Germans, who pressed hard upon the Orthodox; his parents were parishioners of the Russian church of Saint Nicholas there, and the youth, well versed in the holy Scriptures, more than once stood up in defense of the Orthodox faith.
Venerable Serapion of Spaso-Eleazar Mona.patron: Invoked for monastics; steadfastness in Orthodoxy.
Venerable Serapion of Spaso-Eleazar Mona.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

“Ozerianka” Icon of the Mother of God of.life: On this day the Church commemorates the Shuya-Smolensk Icon of the Mother of God, painted in the town of Shuya in the years 1654 and 1655, when a deadly pestilence was devastating the towns of Russia. The people of Shuya, turning to the Mother of God as their last refuge, commissioned an iconographer to paint the Smolensk Hodegetria for their parish church of the Resurrection;.
“Ozerianka” Icon of the Mother of God of.patron: Invoked for deliverance from pestilence; protection in epidemics.
“Ozerianka” Icon of the Mother of God of.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Afterfeast of the Nativity of the Mother.life: These are the days of the Afterfeast of the Nativity of the Most Holy Theotokos, during which the Church continues to celebrate the birth of the Mother of God from the righteous Joachim and Anna. The hymns of the feast are sung together with the daily services, prolonging the joy of the festival, as the faithful contemplate the loosing of Anna's barrenness and the appearing in the world of her who was foreordained from the ages to become the Mother of the Savior.
Afterfeast of the Nativity of the Mother.patron: Commemorated in the holy calendar of the Church.
Afterfeast of the Nativity of the Mother.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Apostle Silvanus of the Seventy.life: The Holy Apostle Silvanus, one of the Seventy, preached the word of God together with the chief apostles Peter and Paul, and the Apostle Peter names him with honor in his First Epistle, calling him a faithful brother through whom he had written. Laboring in the spread of the Gospel and confirming the churches, Saint Silvanus was appointed Bishop of Thessalonica, where he shepherded the flock of Christ.
Apostle Silvanus of the Seventy.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Third Day of the Nativity of our Lord.life: The Third Day of the Nativity of our Lord carries the feast onward in undiminished glory, and the Church, who joined the Mother to the Son on the second day, on the third joins the martyr to the Child. This is the day of the Protomartyr Stephen, and the juxtaposition is the oldest sermon of the season: beside.
Third Day of the Nativity of our Lord.patron: Commemorated in the holy calendar of the Church.
Third Day of the Nativity of our Lord.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Eleutherius of Constantinople.life: The Holy Martyr Eleutherius served as chamberlain at the court of the emperor Maximian, and when he came to faith in Christ he withdrew to a country estate and built a church upon his own land, where he worshipped God. One of his servants betrayed him to the emperor, and being summoned and questioned, Eleutherius fearlessly confessed himself a Christian.
Martyr Eleutherius of Constantinople.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Mercurius the Faster of the Ky.life: Venerable Mercurius the Faster labored in the Kyiv Caves Lavra in the fourteenth century, and his name declares his warfare: he subdued the flesh by extreme abstinence, tasting food with such restraint that fasting became in him not an exercise but a nature, the body wasted and the spirit shining.
Venerable Mercurius the Faster of the Ky.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Adrian and Natalia and 23 compan.life: Saint Adrian was a pagan officer of the imperial court at Nicomedia in the persecution under Maximian, and being present when twenty-three Christians were tortured for their faith, he marveled at their steadfastness and asked what reward they hoped to receive; and when they spoke of the good things God has prepared for those who love Him, he was suddenly moved to declare himself a Christian also, so that his own name was written among the condemned.
Martyrs Adrian and Natalia and 23 compan.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Faustus the Ascetic of the Dal.life: Saint Faustus the Ascetic of the Dalmatian monastery at Constantinople is commemorated together with Saints Isaacius and Dalmatus, and his sanctity grew from a double root, for Dalmatus was his father in the flesh who became his brother in the habit. Dalmatus, an officer of the guard under Theodosius the Great, held rank, wealth, and the emperor's favor;.
Venerable Faustus the Ascetic of the Dal.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Apostle Aristobulus of the Seventy.life: The Holy Apostle Aristobulus of the Seventy, the brother of the Apostle Barnabas, was born in Cyprus and followed the Holy Apostle Paul, who greets his household in the Epistle to the Romans; and being consecrated by Paul, as the ancient accounts relate, he was sent as bishop to Britain, the furthest west of the known world.
Apostle Aristobulus of the Seventy.patron: Invoked for missionaries; the enlightenment of the isles.
Apostle Aristobulus of the Seventy.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

The Adoration of the Magi: Melchior, Cas.life: On the first day of the Nativity the Church commemorates the Adoration of the Magi, the wise men of the East, called by tradition Melchior, Caspar, and Balthasar, to whom the birth of Christ was revealed by a wondrous star. The fathers refused to see in it a common light of the sky: Saint John Chrysostom and Theophylact.
The Adoration of the Magi: Melchior, Cas.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Theodora and her daughter Theo.life: Saint Theodora, who came from the island of Aegina, and her daughter, in monasticism named Theopiste, lived in the city of Thessalonica in the ninth century. While still married, Theodora and her husband gave their only daughter to a convent, where she was tonsured and received her new name;.
Venerable Theodora and her daughter Theo.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Zenobios and his sister Zeno.life: The Holy Hieromartyr Zenobius, Bishop of Aegae, and his sister Zenobia suffered martyrdom in Cilicia in the year 285. Raised by Christian parents in piety and chastity, they gave away their inherited wealth to the poor when they came of age; and the Lord rewarded Zenobius with the gift of healing, so that diseases fled at the touch of his hands, and he restored among others a woman wasting from an incurable affliction of the breast, for which sufferers of that illness invoke him to this day.
Hieromartyr Zenobios and his sister Zeno.patron: Invoked for physicians; those suffering from diseases of the breast.
Hieromartyr Zenobios and his sister Zeno.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Apostle Thaddeus of the Seventy.life: The Holy Apostle Thaddeus, one of the Seventy, was a Hebrew by birth, born in the Syrian city of Edessa; he is to be distinguished from Jude, also called Thaddeus, who was one of the Twelve. Coming to Jerusalem for a feast, he heard the preaching of John the Forerunner and was baptized by him, and beholding the Lord Jesus he followed Him and was numbered among the Seventy disciples.
Apostle Thaddeus of the Seventy.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint John, Patriarch of Constantinople.life: Saint John, surnamed the Faster for his great abstinence and ascetic life, was Patriarch of Constantinople in the latter part of the sixth century. A man of deep humility and prayer, he shepherded the Church of the imperial city in a spirit of strictness toward himself and gentleness toward the penitent, and he is especially remembered as the compiler of a rule of penances for the guidance of priests in hearing confessions, teaching them how to heal the wounds of secret sins and to lead the faithful to true repentance.
Saint John, Patriarch of Constantinople.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Translation of the relics of Saint John.life: On this day the Church commemorates the translation of the relics of Saint John Chrysostom, Archbishop of Constantinople, the reversal in glory of the great injustice of his age. The golden-mouthed had been driven from his throne by the enmity of the empress Eudoxia and the intrigues of his rivals, and had died in exile at Comana in 407, worn out by forced marches, with the words that summarize his whole theology, Glory to God for all things;.
Translation of the relics of Saint John.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Glorification of Venerable Herman of Ala.life: Saint Herman of Alaska, the first of the Orthodox saints of North America, was a humble monk of the Valaam monastery in Russia who in 1794 joined the mission sent to bring the Gospel to the native peoples of Alaska. Settling on Spruce Island, which he called New Valaam, he lived as an ascetic and became a father and protector to the Aleut people, defending them against the injustices of Russian traders, teaching the children, and caring for the sick and orphaned, drawing many to Christ by his gentleness and love.
Glorification of Venerable Herman of Ala.patron: Commemorated in the holy calendar of the Church.
Glorification of Venerable Herman of Ala.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Oleg, Prince of Briansk.life: The Holy Prince Oleg of Briansk was the grandson of the holy Martyr Michael of Chernihiv, and inherited with his blood the piety for which his grandfather had died at the Horde. Ruling the principality of Briansk in the latter part of the thirteenth century, he set his heart not on the enlargement of his power but on the kingdom of God;.
Saint Oleg, Prince of Briansk.patron: Invoked for rulers; renunciation of power.
Saint Oleg, Prince of Briansk.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Hilarion the Schemamonk of the.life: Saint Hilarion the Schemamonk of the Kyiv Caves reposed about the year 1066, and the tradition of the Lavra identifies him with the great Hilarion, Metropolitan of Kyiv, the first of the Rus by birth to occupy the metropolitan throne. A presbyter at the princely village of Berestovo, a man learned and of exceeding piety, he used to withdraw to a wooded hill above the Dnipro, where he dug with his own hands a little cave for prayer and psalmody;.
Venerable Hilarion the Schemamonk of the.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Marinus of Rome.life: The Holy Martyr Marinus was a soldier who suffered at Caesarea in Palestine in the third century, and his contest turned on a promotion. Distinguished in his service and next in line for the centurion's vine-staff, he was denounced by a rival as a Christian who could not lawfully hold the rank, since advancement required the customary oath by the pagan gods and sacrifice to the idols;.
Martyr Marinus of Rome.patron: Invoked for soldiers; officers facing promotion oaths.
Martyr Marinus of Rome.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Niketas of the Kyiv Caves, Far.life: Saint Niketas, Recluse of the Caves and Bishop of Novgorod, is the Church's great case study in deception and recovery, preserved in the Paterikon with clinical honesty because every generation needs it. A young monk of the Kyiv Caves, Niketas begged the igumen, Saint Nikon, for the exploit of reclusion;.
Venerable Niketas of the Kyiv Caves, Far.patron: Invoked for those deceived and restored; students who begin again.
Venerable Niketas of the Kyiv Caves, Far.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Theodosius of the Kyiv Far Cav.life: Saint Theodosius of the Caves, together with Saint Anthony the father of monasticism in the land of Rus, was the founder of the cenobitic life among the Russian monks. He was born at Vasilevo near Kyiv, and from his youth he was drawn to God, shunning games and fine clothing, laboring humbly in the fields, and baking bread for the church, though his mother, who loved him fiercely, often tried by force to turn him from this path.
Venerable Theodosius of the Kyiv Far Cav.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Eudokia of Persia.life: The Holy Martyr Eudokia was a native of Anatolia who lived in the fourth century, and she was carried off into captivity together with nine thousand Christians by the army of the Persian emperor Sapor. Being well versed in the holy Scriptures, she strengthened and instructed her fellow prisoners in their affliction, and she preached the Gospel even to the Persian women, turning many of them to faith in Christ.
Martyr Eudokia of Persia.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyrs Akepsimas, Bishop in Persia.life: The Hieromartyrs Akepsimas the Bishop, Joseph the Presbyter, and Aeithalas the Deacon led the Christian Church in the Persian city of Naesson, where the flock devotedly loved their hierarch for his ascetic life and tireless pastoral labor. In the great persecution under King Shapur the Second, the aged bishop, then some eighty years old, was seized by the king's servants who hunted down the clergy of Christ;.
Hieromartyrs Akepsimas, Bishop in Persia.patron: Invoked for the aged clergy; endurance in long imprisonment.
Hieromartyrs Akepsimas, Bishop in Persia.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Longinus of Yarenga.life: Saint Longinus of Yarenga was a monk of the great Solovki monastery in the White Sea, laboring in the obediences of that severe northern brotherhood in the traditions of Saints Zosima and Sabbatius. About the year 1544, sailing upon the sea in the service of the monastery together with his fellow monk John, he was overtaken by a sudden storm, and the two ascetics perished in the icy waters, sealing with such an end lives spent in obedience and toil.
Venerable Longinus of Yarenga.patron: Invoked for sailors; those who labor on the sea.
Venerable Longinus of Yarenga.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Onuphrius of Saint David Gareji Mo.life: Saint Onuphrius of Gareji, in the world Otar Machutadze, lived in the eighteenth century, a nobleman of Kartli famed for his wealth, his hospitality, and his open hand to the poor. Longing in secret for the ascetic life, he wore a hair shirt beneath his splendid garments and prayed without ceasing that God would count him worthy of the angelic habit;.
Saint Onuphrius of Saint David Gareji Mo.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Holy Prophet and God-seer Moses.life: The Holy Prophet and God-seer Moses, the great lawgiver of Israel, was of the tribe of Levi, and his life is written in the books of Exodus through Deuteronomy. Born in Egypt when Pharaoh had commanded that every male child of the Hebrews be slain, he was hidden by his mother in a basket among the reeds of the Nile, where Pharaoh's daughter found him and raised him as her own son in all the wisdom of the Egyptians.
Holy Prophet and God-seer Moses.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Apostle Mark of the Seventy.life: The Holy Apostle Mark of the Seventy, whom the Church distinguishes from the Evangelist of the same name, is identified in the tradition with John called Mark, in whose mother Mary's house at Jerusalem the faithful gathered for prayer, and to which Peter came when the angel led him out of prison.
Apostle Mark of the Seventy.patron: Invoked for healing; the service of the Gospel.
Apostle Mark of the Seventy.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Michael, Prince of Tver.life: The Holy Martyr Michael, Grand Prince of Tver, ruled his principality in the bitter age of the Tatar yoke, when the princes of Rus contended for the khan's favor and the people paid for every quarrel. Upright, prayerful, and beloved of his city, Michael received the great princedom by right of seniority;.
Martyr Michael, Prince of Tver.patron: Invoked for rulers; rulers who die for their people.
Martyr Michael, Prince of Tver.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Basil the Confessor, companion.life: Venerable Basil the Confessor was a monk who suffered in the reign of the iconoclast emperor Leo the Isaurian, and his feast follows his friend's in the calendar as his life followed it in the flesh, for Basil and Prokopios of Decapolis were companions in asceticism, companions in confession, and companions in chains, the Church commemorating them on adjacent days as a single testimony given by two voices.
Venerable Basil the Confessor, companion.patron: Invoked for confessors; companions in suffering.
Venerable Basil the Confessor, companion.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Conception of the Honorable Glorious Pro.life: On this day the Church celebrates the Conception of the Honorable, Glorious Prophet, Forerunner and Baptist John, the beginning of the Gospel history. When the priest Zachariah, in the course of his division, entered the Temple of the Lord to offer incense, the Archangel Gabriel appeared to him at the right side of the altar of incense and.
Conception of the Honorable Glorious Pro.patron: Invoked for childless couples; answered prayer.
Conception of the Honorable Glorious Pro.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Apostle Andrew, the Holy and All-Praised.life: The Holy and All-Praised Apostle Andrew, the First-Called, was of Bethsaida in Galilee, a fisherman and the brother of Simon Peter; and being a disciple of John the Forerunner, he heard the Baptist say of Jesus, Behold the Lamb of God, and followed the Lord first of all the apostles, for which the Church names him the First-Called.
Apostle Andrew, the Holy and All-Praised.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Repose of Venerable Job the Wonderworker.life: Saint Job of Pochaiv, in the world Ivan Zhelezo, was born about 1551 in Pokutia in Galicia, and came at ten years of age to the Transfiguration monastery at Ugornits, receiving the tonsure at twelve with the name Job. His holiness ripened so early that he was ordained priest while still young and became famous throughout the western lands;.
Repose of Venerable Job the Wonderworker.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Joannicius the Great.life: Saint Joannicius the Great was born in 752 in the Bithynian village of Marikat, of parents so poor that the boy received no schooling but tended the family cattle, filling the pastures with prayer; and grown to strength, he served with distinction for many years as a soldier of the empire, fighting in the Bulgarian wars.
Venerable Joannicius the Great.patron: Invoked for soldiers become monks; repentance from error.
Venerable Joannicius the Great.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Sozon of Cilicia.life: The Holy Martyr Sozon, a native of Lycaonia named Tarasius before his baptism, was a shepherd who lived at the end of the third century, studying the holy Scriptures as he kept his flocks and marveling at the meekness of his sheep, which he strove to imitate and to surpass.
Martyr Sozon of Cilicia.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Severian of Sebaste.life: The Holy Martyr Severian, a nobleman of Sebaste in Armenia, suffered for Christ in the year 320, in the persecution under the emperor Licinius. When the Forty Martyrs of Sebaste lay in prison for their confession of Christ, Severian showed them open and fearless compassion, visiting them in their bonds, encouraging their spirits, and strengthening them for their contest upon the icy lake;.
Martyr Severian of Sebaste.patron: Invoked for care for prisoners; steadfast confession.
Martyr Severian of Sebaste.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Emilian of Silistria in Bulgaria.life: The Holy Martyr Emilian, a Slav by birth, suffered for Christ under Julian the Apostate, who sought to restore the worship of the idols throughout the empire and decreed death for any Christian who would not honor them. Emilian lived in the city of Dorostolum on the Danube, in what is now Bulgaria, as the slave of a cruel and fanatical pagan, while secretly holding to the faith of Christ.
Martyr Emilian of Silistria in Bulgaria.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Theoktίstē of the Isle of Lesb.life: Saint Theoktiste of Lesbos was born at Methymna on that island and, orphaned young, was given to a convent, where she grew in the love of Christ; and when she was about eighteen, visiting her sister in a nearby village, she was carried off in a raid of the Saracen pirates who then scourged the Aegean.
Venerable Theoktίstē of the Isle of Lesb.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Great Martyr Mercurius of Caesarea, in C.life: The Holy Great Martyr Mercurius of Caesarea was a young soldier of Scythian descent serving in the Roman armies, the son of a Christian officer; and when the barbarians poured across the frontier in the days of the emperor Decius, an angel of the Lord appeared to him, placed a sword in his hand, and promised him victory, bidding him remember the Lord his God.
Great Martyr Mercurius of Caesarea, in C.patron: Invoked for soldiers; victory given from heaven.
Great Martyr Mercurius of Caesarea, in C.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Theodota and her three sons in Bi.life: The Holy Martyr Theodota and her three young sons suffered during the persecution under Diocletian. A Christian and a widow of Nicea in Bithynia, she led a devout life and raised her sons in the faith, and she was a close spiritual friend of Saint Anastasia. When the persecution arose and the holy women were arrested, the official Leucadius, captivated by Theodota's beauty, took her into his house meaning to marry her;.
Martyr Theodota and her three sons in Bi.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Germanus, Bishop of Auxerre.life: Saint Germanus was born at Auxerre in Gaul about the year 389, and having studied rhetoric and law at Rome and practiced as an advocate, he was sent back by the emperor Honorius to govern a province of Gaul from his native city. In the year 418 he was chosen, against his own will, to succeed Saint Amator.
Saint Germanus, Bishop of Auxerre.patron: Invoked for defense of the true faith.
Saint Germanus, Bishop of Auxerre.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

The Meeting of our Lord and Savior Jesus.life: The Meeting, or Presentation, celebrates the day, forty days after the Nativity, when the Theotokos and Joseph brought the infant Christ to the Temple in Jerusalem according to the Law of Moses, to present Him to the Lord and to offer the sacrifice of the poor. There the righteous elder Symeon, to whom it had been revealed that.
The Meeting of our Lord and Savior Jesus.patron: Commemorated in the holy calendar of the Church.
The Meeting of our Lord and Savior Jesus.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Paul the Obedient, of the Kyiv.life: Saint Paul the Obedient was an ascetic of the Far Caves of the Kyiv Caves monastery. Having received the monastic schema, he took upon himself without a murmur the most burdensome obediences laid on him by the superior, and he was never found idle: whenever he was not at his appointed task, he ground grain beneath the millstone, wearing down his body with this heavy labor while his soul attained to unceasing inner prayer.
Venerable Paul the Obedient, of the Kyiv.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Onuphrius the Silent and Vener.life: Saints Onuphrius the Silent and Onesimus the Recluse were ascetics of the Kyiv Caves who struggled in the Near Caves of the Lavra in the twelfth and thirteenth centuries. Saint Onuphrius is surnamed the Silent for the strict silence he kept, guarding his lips and his heart that he might commune the more purely with God, while Saint Onesimus shut himself away as a recluse, giving himself wholly to prayer and the remembrance of death in the seclusion of his cell.
Venerable Onuphrius the Silent and Vener.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Quiricus (Kḗrykos) and his mother.life: The Holy Martyrs Quiricus and his mother Julitta lived at Iconium in Asia Minor. Julitta was a Christian of noble birth who, being widowed young, raised her little son Quiricus alone. When the persecution of Diocletian broke out, she fled the city with her three-year-old child and two faithful servants, going first to Seleucia and then to Tarsus, but there she was recognized, arrested, and brought before the governor Alexander.
Saint Quiricus (Kḗrykos) and his mother.patron: Invoked for family happiness; sick children.
Saint Quiricus (Kḗrykos) and his mother.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Nίkander Wonderworker of Pskov.life: Saint Nikander of Pskov, the desert-dweller and wonderworker, was born in 1507 in the village of Videlebye near Pskov, the same village that had given the Church Saint Euphrosynus, and was named Nikon in the world. From childhood he longed for the ascetic life, and having learned his letters and given away his portion, he withdrew to the wilderness on the river Demyanka between Pskov and Porkhov, where after a time he received the monastic tonsure with the name Nikander at the Krypetsk monastery.
Venerable Nίkander Wonderworker of Pskov.patron: Invoked for hermits; the solitary life.
Venerable Nίkander Wonderworker of Pskov.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Simeon of Emessa the Fool-For-.life: Saints Simeon and John were Syrians of the sixth century, bound from childhood by the closest friendship. Both were of wealthy families, Simeon the elder living with his aged mother and John, though married, dwelling with his father and young wife. When Simeon was thirty and John twenty-four, they made a pilgrimage to Jerusalem for the Feast of.
Venerable Simeon of Emessa the Fool-For-.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Modestos, Archbishop of Jerusalem.life: Saint Modestos, Archbishop of Jerusalem, was born at Sebaste in Cappadocia of Christian parents, and embracing the monastic life in the Holy Land, rose to be abbot of the monastery of Saint Theodosius; and God had trained him in the desert for the darkest hour the Holy City had known since Titus.
Saint Modestos, Archbishop of Jerusalem.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Ananias the Iconographer.life: Saint Ananias the Iconographer was a monk of the Monastery of Saint Anthony the Roman at Novgorod, whom God endowed with a gift for the painting of holy icons, which he practiced for the glory of the Lord. He is remembered for the marvelous icons he wrote of many holy wonderworkers, and still more for his profound stability and love of stillness, for it is recounted that during thirty-three years he never once passed beyond the fence of his monastery.
Venerable Ananias the Iconographer.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint John the Wonderworker, Archbishop.life: Saint John, Archbishop of Novgorod, was born in that city of pious parents, and with his brother Gabriel founded a monastery in honor of the Annunciation with their inheritance. Chosen bishop of Novgorod, he was the first of its hierarchs to be raised to the rank of archbishop, and he shepherded his flock with gentleness and power.
Saint John the Wonderworker, Archbishop.patron: Invoked for the deliverance of cities; the slandered.
Saint John the Wonderworker, Archbishop.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Constantine and Cosmas, Abbots.life: Saints Constantine and Cosmas were disciples of Saint Barlaam of Khutyn and of his successor Saint Anthony of Dymsk, in whose monastery they were trained in the monastic life. About the year 1220 they left Khutyn seeking greater solitude, and settled upon a wild peninsula a short way from the town of Staraya Russa, where they founded a monastery.
Venerable Constantine and Cosmas, Abbots.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Translation of the relics of Blessed Jam.life: Blessed James of Borovichi, wonderworker of Novgorod, was revealed to the Church not by the record of his life but by the glory of his relics. In the spring of 1540, at the rapids of the river Msta by the settlement of Borovichi, a great ice floe came up the river against the current, bearing upon it a coffin of charred wood in which lay the body of a youth;.
Translation of the relics of Blessed Jam.patron: Invoked for boatmen; the unknown righteous.
Translation of the relics of Blessed Jam.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Elias, Probus, and Ares in Cilic.life: The Holy Martyrs Elias, Probus, and Ares were Egyptians by birth, and their crime was mercy: in the persecution under Maximian they set out from Egypt to Cilicia, heedless of their own safety, to minister to the confessors of Christ imprisoned there and condemned to the mines, carrying comfort to those the empire had thrown away.
Martyrs Elias, Probus, and Ares in Cilic.patron: Invoked for prison visitors; those who serve the persecuted.
Martyrs Elias, Probus, and Ares in Cilic.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Pelagia the Penitent.life: Saint Pelagia the Penitent was the most famous dancer and courtesan of Antioch, called Margarita, the Pearl, for her beauty and her jewels; and one day, passing in splendor with her train before the doors where a council of bishops sat, she drew the eyes of all, and the holy bishop Nonnus wept, saying to the others, This woman takes more care to adorn herself for men than we do to adorn our souls for God, and he prayed for her through the night.
Venerable Pelagia the Penitent.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Repose of Saint Innocent, first Bishop o.life: On this day the Church commemorates Saint Innocent, first Bishop of Irkutsk, the enlightener of eastern Siberia. Born about 1680 into the noble Kulchitsky family of the Chernigov lands, John was educated at the Kyiv Academy, received the monastic tonsure with the name Innocent, and taught in the schools of Moscow and Saint Petersburg;.
Repose of Saint Innocent, first Bishop o.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Gemellus of Paphlagonia.life: The Holy Martyr Gemellus of Paphlagonia suffered in the year 361 under Julian the Apostate, the emperor who had renounced the Christ in whom he was raised and set himself to restore the worship of the idols. Meeting the emperor at Ancyra in Galatia, Gemellus denounced his apostasy to his face, with the freedom of a man who fears God more than kings;.
Martyr Gemellus of Paphlagonia.patron: Invoked for boldness before apostate rulers.
Martyr Gemellus of Paphlagonia.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Theodotus, Asclepiodotus, and Ma.life: The Holy Martyrs Theodotus, Asclepiodote, and Maximus suffered at the beginning of the fourth century, in the persecution under Maximian Galerius. Maximus and Asclepiodote were eminent citizens of Marcianopolis in Thrace who led a devout Christian life, and together with Theodotus they were denounced for the faith and brought to trial.
Martyrs Theodotus, Asclepiodotus, and Ma.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Dionysius the Recluse of the K.life: Saint Dionysius the Recluse of the Kyiv Caves, called Shchepa, was a hieromonk who served the holy caves in the fifteenth century. In the year 1463, on the day of Holy Pascha, as he passed with the censer through the Far Caves censing the relics of the saints who rest there, he was filled with the joy of.
Venerable Dionysius the Recluse of the K.patron: Invoked for paschal joy; reverence for the saints.
Venerable Dionysius the Recluse of the K.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Holy Unmercenary Physician Diomedes.life: Saint Diomedes was born at Tarsus in Cilicia and was trained in the art of medicine, but his learning did not puff him up, for he kept the piety in which his parents had raised him. In imitation of Christ, the Physician of souls and bodies, he practiced his healing art freely and without charge, and while he tended the sick in body he also cared for their souls, preaching to them the Gospel of salvation and bringing many to faith in the Savior.
Holy Unmercenary Physician Diomedes.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Theophanó the Wonderworker, wife o.life: Saint Theophano the Wonderworker, Empress of the Romans, was born at Constantinople to Constantine Martinakios and his wife Anna, and raised in piety; and chosen by the emperor Basil the Macedonian as bride for his son Leo the Wise, she entered the most gilded and most bitter of cages.
Saint Theophanó the Wonderworker, wife o.patron: Invoked for empresses and first ladies; those in unhappy marriages.
Saint Theophanó the Wonderworker, wife o.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Mardarije (Uskokovic) of Libertyvi.life: Saint Mardarije of Libertyville, first Serbian Bishop of America and Canada, was born Ivan Uskokovic on the second of November 1889 in the village of Kornet in Montenegro; and burning for the monastic life from childhood, he left home at sixteen, was tonsured with the name Mardarije, and was sent to Russia, where he completed his theological formation and served the Serbian church's mission until the revolution drove him westward.
Saint Mardarije (Uskokovic) of Libertyvi.patron: Invoked for immigrant communities; builders of churches.
Saint Mardarije (Uskokovic) of Libertyvi.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Justinian the Emperor.life: Saint Justinian the Emperor, one of the great figures of the Christian empire, was born in 483 at Tauresium in Illyricum, of peasant stock and, as an old tradition holds, of Slavic descent; and being raised to the throne in 527 as nephew and heir of the emperor Justin, he reigned thirty-eight years with a vision of the empire as the earthly servant of the heavenly kingdom.
Saint Justinian the Emperor.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Sadoc (Sadoth), Bishop of Pe.life: The Hieromartyr Sadoc, Bishop of Persia, suffered with one hundred and twenty-eight companions about the year 342, in the great persecution of Shapur the Second, when the Persian empire set itself to extirpate the Church of the East; he had succeeded the hieromartyr Symeon, first of the persecution's bishops to be crowned, and inherited with the throne the near certainty of the same end.
Hieromartyr Sadoc (Sadoth), Bishop of Pe.patron: Invoked for bishops under persecution; companies of confessors.
Hieromartyr Sadoc (Sadoth), Bishop of Pe.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Marinus, his wife Martha, their c.life: This day commemorates the holy martyrs Marinus, his wife Martha, and their sons Audifax and Habakkuk, together with the others who suffered with them at Rome under the emperor Claudius the Second. A devout family from Persia, they journeyed to Rome to venerate the tombs of the apostles Peter and Paul, and there they gave themselves to the service of the persecuted Church, gathering by night the bodies of the slain martyrs and burying them with honor, even recovering from the Tiber the body of the martyr Cyrenus.
Martyr Marinus, his wife Martha, their c.patron: Invoked for Christian families; the burial of the dead.
Martyr Marinus, his wife Martha, their c.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Karion (Cyrion) and his son, V.life: Saints Karion and his son Zachariah labored at Scetis in Egypt in the fourth century, and their story is one of the strangest and tenderest in the desert. Karion left wife and two children for the monastic life; and when famine struck Egypt, his wife brought the children to the monastery gate, and the monk took his son Zachariah to raise in the skete, while the daughter remained with her mother.
Venerable Karion (Cyrion) and his son, V.patron: Invoked for fathers and sons; humiliation embraced.
Venerable Karion (Cyrion) and his son, V.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Archippus of Herapolis.life: Saint Archippus was born at Hierapolis in Phrygia of devout Christian parents, and at ten years of age, coming to pray at the church of the Chief Commander Michael over the wonderworking spring near Colossae, he remained there to serve as its caretaker for the rest of his life.
Saint Archippus of Herapolis.patron: Invoked for church caretakers; faithful service.
Saint Archippus of Herapolis.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Onesiphorus the Confessor of t.life: Saint Onesiphorus the Confessor was a priest-monk of the Kyiv Caves monastery in the twelfth century, adorned with fasting and every virtue, and granted by God the gift of discerning the secrets of hearts; yet the Lord permitted even this seer to be deceived, for the instruction of all.
Venerable Onesiphorus the Confessor of t.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Glorification of Saint Tikhon, Patriarch.life: On this day the Church commemorates the glorification of Saint Tikhon, Patriarch of Moscow and All Russia, numbered among the saints by the Bishops' Council of the Russian Orthodox Church on the ninth of October 1989. Born Basil Bellavin in 1865, the son of a village priest of Toropets, he was so loved for his gentleness that his fellow seminarians called him Patriarch in jest, not knowing they prophesied.
Glorification of Saint Tikhon, Patriarch.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Apostle Crescens of the Seventy.life: The Holy Apostle Crescens, one of the Seventy, was a disciple of the Savior whom the Apostle Paul mentions in his Second Epistle to Timothy, recording that Crescens had gone to preach in Galatia. There he was made bishop, and afterward he carried the Gospel into Gaul, in the West, where at Vienne he established his own disciple Zacharias as bishop.
Apostle Crescens of the Seventy.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saints Zenon and Zoilus.life: The Righteous Zenon and Zoilus are commemorated together on this day, a pair whom the synaxaria carry with the briefest of notices, two names joined by the calendar as they were joined, the Church trusts, in life and in God; and their feast belongs to that quiet company of commemorations by which the Church confesses a truth she never tires of teaching, that the register of the saints is longer than the library of their stories.
Saints Zenon and Zoilus.patron: Invoked for the quietly faithful; righteousness without record.
Saints Zenon and Zoilus.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Apostle Justus of the Seventy.life: The Holy Apostle Justus of the Seventy, called Joseph Barsabas, was, according to the tradition of the Church, a son of the Righteous Joseph the Betrothed, and so was reckoned among the brethren of the Lord, growing up in the shadow of the Incarnate Word. After the Ascension, when the eleven sought to fill the place of Judas, two were set forth from among those who had companied with the Lord from the baptism of John, Joseph called Barsabas, surnamed Justus, and Matthias;.
Apostle Justus of the Seventy.patron: Invoked for contentment without honors; faithfulness unchosen.
Apostle Justus of the Seventy.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Gregory, Archbishop of Alexandria.life: Saint Gregory, Archbishop of Alexandria, lived in the ninth century, in the years when the iconoclast heresy, revived by the emperors, again troubled the Church. Renowned from his youth for purity of life and love of God, he was chosen against his will to the throne of Alexandria, where he shepherded his flock in the apostolic faith;.
Saint Gregory, Archbishop of Alexandria.patron: Invoked for hierarchs; the veneration of the holy icons.
Saint Gregory, Archbishop of Alexandria.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Philoumenus of Ancyra.life: The Holy Martyr Philoumenus suffered for Christ in the year 274, in the persecution under the emperor Aurelian. A native of Lycaonia and a baker by trade, he furnished bread to the towns of Galatia, earning his living honestly and confessing Christ openly; and envious men denounced him to the governor Felix at Ancyra as a Christian.
Martyr Philoumenus of Ancyra.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Holy, Righteous Simeon the God-Receiver.life: Saint Simeon the God-Receiver is the elder of the Meeting, the man appointed by God to stand at the frontier of the two Testaments and receive the second into his arms; the Gospel of Luke describes him completely in three strokes, just and devout, waiting for the consolation of Israel, and the Holy Spirit was upon him, and it records the promise that organized his long life, that it was revealed unto him by the Holy Spirit that he should not see death before he had seen the Lord's Christ.
Holy, Righteous Simeon the God-Receiver.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Prophet Ezekiel.life: The Holy Prophet Ezekiel was of the tribe of Levi, a priest and the son of the priest Buzi, and he was carried away into captivity in Babylon at the age of twenty-five, together with King Jechoniah, when the people of Judah were led into exile. There, among the exiles by the river Chebar, the word of the Lord came to him, and he prophesied for many years, calling the people to repentance and consoling them with the hope of return and restoration.
Prophet Ezekiel.patron: Invoked for repentance; the hope of resurrection.
Prophet Ezekiel.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Paisios Velichkovsky.life: Saint Paisius Velichkovsky, the father of the great renewal of Orthodox monasticism, was born Peter Velichkovsky in 1722 at Poltava in Ukraine, the son of a cathedral priest; and leaving the Kyiv Academy, whose scholastic learning could not quench his thirst for the living tradition, he sought God through the monasteries of Ukraine and Moldavia until, at twenty-four, he reached the Holy Mountain of Athos.
Venerable Paisios Velichkovsky.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Anicetus and Photius of Nicomedi.life: The Holy Martyrs Anicetus and Photius, an uncle and his nephew, were natives of Nicomedia. When the emperor Diocletian set up in the public square an engine of execution to terrify the Christians, Anicetus, an officer of the court, openly denounced him, and the enraged emperor gave him over to torture.
Martyrs Anicetus and Photius of Nicomedi.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Proclus, Archbishop of Constantino.life: Saint Proclus, Archbishop of Constantinople, gave his early years to prayer and the study of the Scriptures, and was granted the great blessing of being the disciple of Saint John Chrysostom, who ordained him deacon and priest; and it was Proclus who beheld the Apostle Paul bending over his teacher and whispering to him as Chrysostom wrote his homilies on the epistles, the disciple thus becoming the witness of his master's inspiration.
Saint Proclus, Archbishop of Constantino.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Monastic Martyrs and Confessors Auxentiu.life: The Holy Martyrs and Confessors Auxentius, Basil, Gregory, another Gregory, John, Andrew, Peter, and many others suffered for the veneration of the holy icons in the persecution of Constantine Copronymus, together with the Monastic Martyr Stephen the New. These were the confessors, most of them monks, whom the iconoclast emperor had gathered out of all the empire into the prisons of Constantinople, men already bearing in their bodies the marks of the persecution, scourged, branded, mutilated in nose and ears and hands and eyes for refusing to blaspheme the image of Christ;.
Monastic Martyrs and Confessors Auxentiu.patron: Invoked for monastics; the holy icons.
Monastic Martyrs and Confessors Auxentiu.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Sebastiana the Martyr, disciple of.life: The Holy Martyr Sebastiana was a disciple of the Holy Apostle Paul, instructed in the faith by the great Apostle of the nations himself, and she labored for the Gospel in the first age of the Church. In the persecution under the emperor Domitian she was seized at Marcianopolis and brought to trial for her confession of Christ.
Saint Sebastiana the Martyr, disciple of.patron: Invoked for women disciples; steadfast confession.
Saint Sebastiana the Martyr, disciple of.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Repose of Saint Nikolai of Zhicha.life: Saint Nikolai of Zhicha, the new Chrysostom of the Serbian Church, was born Nikola Velimirovich in 1880 in the village of Lelich, the eldest of many children of pious peasants, and rose by sheer God-given brilliance through the schools of Serbia and the universities of Europe, taking doctorates in the west while remaining wholly a child of the Serbian village and its faith;.
Repose of Saint Nikolai of Zhicha.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Nikon, Abbot of the Kyiv Far C.life: Venerable Nikon, abbot of the Kyiv Caves, called the Great by the tradition of the Lavra, came to the cave of Saint Anthony already a priest, the first of that dignity in the little brotherhood under the hill, and became the founder's right hand: it was by Nikon's priestly hand, at Anthony's blessing, that the early brethren received the tonsure, and among them the young Theodosius, so that the father of Russian cenobitic monasticism entered the angelic life through Nikon's fingers, the quiet priest standing at the fountainhead of everything the Caves became.
Venerable Nikon, Abbot of the Kyiv Far C.patron: Invoked for those who tonsure and form monks; chroniclers.
Venerable Nikon, Abbot of the Kyiv Far C.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Macarius the Wonderworker, Abb.life: Venerable Macarius the Wonderworker, Abbot of Kalyazin, was born Matthew Kozhin to a boyar family of Kashin, and married in obedience to his parents a maiden named Elena, though his heart had long inclined to the cloister; the young couple agreed between themselves that whichever survived the other would take the monastic habit, and when Elena died in the third year of the marriage, Matthew, still young, fulfilled the compact at once, receiving the tonsure with the name Macarius at the Klobukov monastery in his native town.
Venerable Macarius the Wonderworker, Abb.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Onesimus of Isauria.life: The Holy Martyr Onesimus, called also Onisius, is numbered among the early witnesses of Christ who sealed their confession with their blood by the sword. The accounts that survive of him are of the briefest, and they do not fully agree even on his country, for while he is commemorated in the calendars as Onesimus of Isauria, and set beside the martyr Conon of that region, whose hymn joins their two names, the Lives of the Saints of the Orthodox Church in America record simply that he lived in Palestine;.
Martyr Onesimus of Isauria.patron: Invoked for the steadfast under interrogation; the confession sealed by the sword.
Martyr Onesimus of Isauria.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Sabinus (Abibus) of Egypt.life: The Holy Martyr Sabinus, called also Abibus, was a prominent man of Hermopolis in Egypt, of high standing and known for his charity; and when the persecution fell upon the Egyptian church in the reign of Diocletian, the Christians of the city begged him to preserve himself, and Sabinus withdrew with a few companions to a hut outside the city, where they remained hidden, sustaining themselves in prayer and fasting while the storm passed through Hermopolis.
Martyr Sabinus (Abibus) of Egypt.patron: Invoked for the betrayed; benefactors repaid with evil.
Martyr Sabinus (Abibus) of Egypt.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

The Holy Hieromartyrs of Cherson: Basil,.life: The Holy Hieromartyrs of Cherson, Basil, Ephraim, Eugene, Elpidius, Agathodorus, Aetherius, and Capito, carried the Gospel into the north Black Sea lands, from the Danube to the Dnieper and the Crimea, serving as bishops of Cherson in succession through the early fourth century, sent one after another by Hermon, bishop of Jerusalem, into a mission field that consumed its shepherds;.
The Holy Hieromartyrs of Cherson: Basil,.patron: Invoked for missionary bishops; the Church at hostile frontiers.
The Holy Hieromartyrs of Cherson: Basil,.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Philetus the Senator, his wife an.life: The Holy Martyrs Philetus the Senator, his wife Lydia, their sons Macedon and Theoprepius, Amphilochius the commander, and Cronides the notary suffered in the reign of the emperor Hadrian, at the beginning of the second century, and their contest is one of those the Church remembers for the strange gentleness of its ending.
Martyr Philetus the Senator, his wife an.patron: Invoked for families in confession together; converted officials.
Martyr Philetus the Senator, his wife an.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Drosίs, daughter of Emperor Traja.life: The Holy Virgin Drosis, daughter of the emperor Trajan himself, is the Church's witness that the Gospel climbed in its first century to the very hearth of its persecutor. In the years when her father's rescript governed the treatment of the Christians and the martyrs' bodies were cast out unburied to complete their disgrace, Drosis joined herself secretly.
Martyr Drosίs, daughter of Emperor Traja.patron: Invoked for daughters of hostile houses; those who bury the martyrs.
Martyr Drosίs, daughter of Emperor Traja.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Sophronius, Patriarch of Jerusalem.life: Saint Sophronius, Patriarch of Jerusalem, was born at Damascus about 560, a sophist by training, master of the whole learning of the Greeks; and exchanging the schools for the desert, he became the inseparable companion of the monk John Moschus, with whom he wandered for decades through the monasteries of Palestine, Sinai, and Egypt, gathering the sayings and.
Saint Sophronius, Patriarch of Jerusalem.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Artemon, Bishop of Seleucia.life: Saint Artemon, first bishop of Seleucia in Pisidia, belongs to the generation the apostles appointed with their own hands, and his consecration is his biography's shining center: when the Apostle Paul, in the course of his missionary journeys through the highlands of Asia Minor, came to Seleucia and preached Christ there, he found in Artemon a man already ripe for the harvest, prudent, fervent, and beloved of the people;.
Saint Artemon, Bishop of Seleucia.patron: Invoked for first bishops; those ordained by apostolic hands.
Saint Artemon, Bishop of Seleucia.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

1st Sunday of Great Lent: Sunday of Orth.life: On the first Sunday of the Great Fast the Church keeps the Sunday of Orthodoxy, the feast of the Triumph of the true faith, established in the year 843 when the holy empress Theodora and the holy Patriarch Methodius restored the veneration of the icons and ended the last great heresy of the ancient world;.
1st Sunday of Great Lent: Sunday of Orth.patron: Invoked for the whole Church militant; all who keep the faith of the Fathers.
1st Sunday of Great Lent: Sunday of Orth.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Beginning of Great Lent.life: On this day the Church enters the Great Fast, the holy Forty Days, the oldest and greatest of her seasons of repentance, kept from the earliest generations as the tithe of the year offered to God and the common journey of all the faithful to Pascha. Its roots run to the beginnings: the Lord Himself fasted forty days.
Beginning of Great Lent.patron: Invoked for all the faithful; catechumens preparing for baptism.
Beginning of Great Lent.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Zachariah the Recluse.life: Venerable Zachariah the Recluse is commemorated on this day, and the Byzantine synaxarion itself confesses with honest care that among the many saints who bear the name of Zachariah it cannot be exactly determined which one the Church honors here, holding only the received belief that he lived the enclosed life in a monastery of Constantinople near the gate of Charsia;.
Venerable Zachariah the Recluse.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Finding of the relics of Saint Theodore,.life: On this day the Church commemorates the uncovering of the relics of the right-believing Prince Theodore of Smolensk and Yaroslavl, called the Black, together with his sons David and Constantine, which took place at Yaroslavl on the fifth of March 1463; the prince's own repose is kept in September, but this day belongs to the finding of his incorrupt body.
Finding of the relics of Saint Theodore,.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Benedict of Nursia.life: Venerable Benedict of Nursia, the father of the monks of the West, was born about 480 in the Umbrian hills and sent to Rome for his studies; and seeing the corruption of his fellow students, the youth judged the price of that learning too high, and fled the city, knowingly unlearned and wisely untaught, as Saint Gregory writes of him, choosing to please God alone.
Venerable Benedict of Nursia.patron: Invoked for monks of the common life; abbots.
Venerable Benedict of Nursia.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Nikon and 199 disciples with him.life: The Holy Martyr Nikon and his one hundred ninety-nine disciples suffered in Sicily in the persecution of Decius, about the year 251, and his road to that company began in an army. A soldier by profession, son of a pagan father and a Christian mother, Nikon went to war unbaptized but not untaught, for his mother had planted the faith's seed in him;.
Martyr Nikon and 199 disciples with him.patron: Invoked for bishops with their flocks; teachers and their students.
Martyr Nikon and 199 disciples with him.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Alexis the Man of God.life: Venerable Alexis the Man of God was the only son of the Roman senator Euphemianus, a house famed for wealth and for mercy to the poor, and the longed-for child of his mother Aglais' prayers.
Venerable Alexis the Man of God.patron: Invoked for beggars and the homeless; the unrecognized.
Venerable Alexis the Man of God.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint James the Confessor, Bishop of Cat.life: Saint James the Confessor, Bishop of Catania, was an ascetic from his youth, formed in the monastic life in learning and in strictness, and raised for his virtues to the episcopal throne of Catania in Sicily, where he shepherded his flock in the years when the iconoclast emperors were pressing their war against the holy images upon every province of the empire, the island sees of the west no less than the capital.
Saint James the Confessor, Bishop of Cat.patron: Invoked for bishops in exile; defenders of the icons.
Saint James the Confessor, Bishop of Cat.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Publius, Bishop of Athens.life: The Hieromartyr Publius, Bishop of Athens, enters the Scriptures by an act of hospitality: he is the Publius of the Acts of the Apostles, the chief man of the island of Malta, who, when the Apostle Paul was cast ashore there by the shipwreck on the voyage to Rome, received the Apostle and his companions and lodged them three days courteously;.
Hieromartyr Publius, Bishop of Athens.patron: Invoked for hosts and the hospitable; bishops of ancient sees.
Hieromartyr Publius, Bishop of Athens.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Stephen, Wonderworker, Abbot o.life: Venerable Stephen the Wonderworker, abbot of the Triglia monastery on the Bithynian coast near Prusa, was consecrated to God from his youth, and so excelled in the ascetic life, in purity, fasting, and prayer, that he was set over the brotherhood of Triglia as its hegumen, which he governed in holiness, adorned by God, as his title records, with the grace of wonders, the abbot's prayer bringing healing and help to those who sought the monastery, and his example forming his monks in the full tradition of the Bithynian houses, that nursery of confessors;.
Venerable Stephen, Wonderworker, Abbot o.patron: Invoked for abbots under persecution; the exiled.
Venerable Stephen, Wonderworker, Abbot o.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Basil of Ancyra.life: The Hieromartyr Basil, priest of Ancyra in Galatia, was the guardian of that city's flock through two storms in succession, the Arian and the pagan, and fell in the second. Through the years when the Arians held power and the churches of Galatia were troubled, the presbyter Basil labored tirelessly for the Nicene faith, strengthening the wavering, denouncing the heresy openly, and keeping the people of Ancyra to the true confession though it cost him harassment and suspension at Arian hands, the parish priest holding a line that hierarchs were abandoning;.
Hieromartyr Basil of Ancyra.patron: Invoked for parish priests; defenders of the flock against heresy and apostasy.
Hieromartyr Basil of Ancyra.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Marinus.life: The Holy Martyr Marinus the Soldier suffered at Caesarea in Palestine in the year 262, and his contest, preserved by Eusebius of that city, turns on a single choice staged with unbearable clarity. Marinus was a soldier of distinction and noble birth, and the post of centurion falling vacant, he stood first in line for the promotion;.
Martyr Marinus.patron: Invoked for soldiers at the crossroads of conscience; the Gospel chosen over the sword.
Martyr Marinus.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Pancharius at Nicomedia.life: The Holy Martyr Pancharius was a Roman of high standing, a favorite of the emperor Maximian, and a Christian; and his contest is precious to the Church because it begins with a fall. When the persecution made faith and favor incompatible, Pancharius, unwilling to lose his place at the emperor's side, concealed and in effect denied his Christianity, keeping the court and letting go of Christ, the quiet apostasy of convenience that leaves no scar visible from outside;.
Martyr Pancharius at Nicomedia.patron: Invoked for those who have denied and would return; sons far from home.
Martyr Pancharius at Nicomedia.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Cyril, Bishop of Catania.life: Saint Cyril, Bishop of Catania, was born at Antioch, the city where the disciples were first called Christians, and belonged to the generation formed directly by the apostles, of the circle of the Apostle Peter's disciples; and he was sent to shepherd the church of Catania in Sicily, one of those first mission sees planted at the crossroads of the sea, where the Gospel had to make its way in a Greek and pagan city under the smoking mountain.
Saint Cyril, Bishop of Catania.patron: Invoked for bishops of mission sees; those who thirst.
Saint Cyril, Bishop of Catania.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Urpasianus of Nicomedia.life: The Holy Martyr Urpasianus suffered in the city of Nicomedia under the emperor Maximian Galerius, who cruelly persecuted the Christians serving in his army and at his court; and in that sifting, as the Lives record, some of the timid of soul began to waver and worship the pagan gods, while the strong held out to the very end, and Urpasianus stood at the head of the strong.
Martyr Urpasianus of Nicomedia.patron: Invoked for courtiers; those who resign rank for Christ.
Martyr Urpasianus of Nicomedia.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

42 Martyrs of Ammoria in Phrygia.life: The Holy Forty-Two Martyrs of Amorion were the commanders and nobles of the Byzantine army taken captive when the great city of Amorion in Phrygia fell to the Saracens in the year 838, among them Constantine, Aetius, Theophilus, Theodore, Melissenus, Callistus, and Basoes, the flower of the empire's leadership carried off into Mesopotamia.
42 Martyrs of Ammoria in Phrygia.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Agapius, Publius, Timolaus, Romu.life: The Holy Martyrs Agapius, Publius, Timolaus, Romulus, the two named Dionysius, and the two named Alexander suffered at Caesarea in Palestine at the outbreak of the great persecution, beheaded on the twenty-fourth of March in the year 304 by the reckoning of Eusebius and the Greek synaxarion, or in 303 by the Slavic accounts, and their contest is preserved for the Church by an eyewitness, for Eusebius of Caesarea, who lived through those years in that city, recorded it among the martyrs of Palestine.
Martyrs Agapius, Publius, Timolaus, Romu.patron: Invoked for the young; volunteers of the confession.
Martyrs Agapius, Publius, Timolaus, Romu.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Papas of Lyconia.life: The Holy Martyr Papas of Lycaonia suffered in the persecution at the opening of the fourth century, when the edicts of Diocletian and Maximian reached into the highlands of inner Asia Minor where Paul and Barnabas had first sown the word; and the contest of Papas is remembered for its road and its tree.
Martyr Papas of Lyconia.patron: Invoked for those driven beyond endurance; the march in the nailed sandals.
Martyr Papas of Lyconia.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

40 Holy Martyrs of Sebaste.life: The Holy Forty Martyrs of Sebaste were soldiers of the famed Twelfth Legion, called the Thundering, stationed at Sebaste in Armenia about the year 320, which the Byzantine synaxarion reckons as 322 or 323, when the emperor Licinius, breaking his peace with the Church, commanded his armies to sacrifice;.
40 Holy Martyrs of Sebaste.patron: Invoked for soldiers; companies and brotherhoods.
40 Holy Martyrs of Sebaste.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Mark, Bishop of Arethusa, wh.life: The Hieromartyr Mark, Bishop of Arethusa in Syria, was already an old man full of years and honor when Julian the Apostate loosed the pagans upon the Church, and his contest, preserved for the ages by Saint Gregory the Theologian, is one of the strangest and most glorious of that strange persecution.
Hieromartyr Mark, Bishop of Arethusa, wh.patron: Invoked for the aged in trial; those who surrender themselves for others.
Hieromartyr Mark, Bishop of Arethusa, wh.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Monastic Martyrs Conon and his son, Cono.life: The Holy Monastic Martyrs Conon and his son Conon suffered at Iconium in Asia Minor in the reign of the emperor Aurelian. The elder Conon, left a widower, entered a monastery together with his son, and for the holiness of his life was granted grace from above, casting out demons, healing the sick, giving sight to the blind, and preaching Christ among the pagans, by which he converted many;.
Monastic Martyrs Conon and his son, Cono.patron: Invoked for widowed fathers; fathers and sons.
Monastic Martyrs Conon and his son, Cono.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Thomas, Patriarch of Constantinopl.life: Saint Thomas, Patriarch of Constantinople, served the Great Church first as deacon and sakellarios under the holy Patriarch John the Faster, distinguished by prudence and reverence in the administration of the churches, and was raised to the patriarchal throne in 607, in the reign of Phocas, when the empire, though none yet knew it, stood on the threshold of catastrophe;.
Saint Thomas, Patriarch of Constantinopl.patron: Invoked for those who fear the days ahead; shepherds who pray to be spared.
Saint Thomas, Patriarch of Constantinopl.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Paul the Confessor, Bishop of Plou.life: Saint Paul the Confessor was bishop of the city of Plousias in the province of Bithynia in Asia Minor, and shepherded his flock in the years when the iconoclasts raged for the second time against the Church of Christ, the emperors of the ninth century renewing the war upon the holy images that the Seventh Ecumenical Council had settled.
Saint Paul the Confessor, Bishop of Plou.patron: Invoked for defenders of the icons; exiled hierarchs.
Saint Paul the Confessor, Bishop of Plou.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Innocent of Komél and Vologda disc.life: Venerable Innocent of Komel and Vologda was born at Moscow of the noble line of the Okhlyabinin princes, and left rank and inheritance for the tonsure at the White Lake monastery of Saint Cyril, the great nursery of the northern monks; and there God gave him the treasure of his life, for he became the disciple of Saint Nilus of Sora, the master of the skete life and of inner prayer, and cleaved to him wholly.
Saint Innocent of Komél and Vologda disc.patron: Invoked for disciples who guard a teacher's legacy; founders.
Saint Innocent of Komél and Vologda disc.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

2nd Sunday of Great Lent: St Gregory Pal.life: On the second Sunday of the Great Fast the Church keeps the memory of Saint Gregory Palamas, Archbishop of Thessalonica, and the day is rightly called the second Triumph of Orthodoxy, for it extends the first: as the first Sunday proclaims that God may be depicted because He truly became man, the second proclaims that God may be experienced because He truly gives Himself, the icon and the light being two verdicts of one faith.
2nd Sunday of Great Lent: St Gregory Pal.patron: Invoked for hesychasts and all who pray; theologians of experience.
2nd Sunday of Great Lent: St Gregory Pal.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Theophylactus, Bishop of Nicomedia.life: Saint Theophylact, Bishop of Nicomedia, lived at Constantinople in the age of the Iconoclast heresy, and was among the trusted men of the holy Patriarch Tarasius, who had come to the throne when the Patriarch Paul, lacking strength to guide the flock in the face of iconoclasm, laid it down;.
Saint Theophylactus, Bishop of Nicomedia.patron: Invoked for bishops who serve the poor; nurses of lepers.
Saint Theophylactus, Bishop of Nicomedia.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Chrysanthus and Daria, and those.life: The Holy Martyrs Chrysanthus and Daria suffered at Rome in the year 283 by the Roman and Greek reckonings, though the books that place them under Valerian give about the year 253, and their contest gathered a whole harvest of companions before it closed. Chrysanthus, son of the senator Polemius, came with his father from Alexandria to Rome, and in the course of his studies met the Scriptures, and through the instruction of the presbyter Carpophorus was baptized, and began at once to confess Christ;.
Martyrs Chrysanthus and Daria, and those.patron: Invoked for married couples vowed to purity; converts of converts.
Martyrs Chrysanthus and Daria, and those.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Icon of the Mother of God of Mount Athos.type: Icon of the Mother of God · 9th c.
Icon of the Mother of God of Mount Athos.life: The Icon of the Mother of God called Sweet Kissing, the Glykophilousa, is one of the treasures of the Philotheou monastery on Mount Athos, and shows the Mother and the Child in the fullness of the Tenderness, cheek pressed to cheek, the mutual affection of the Virgin and her God made the whole subject of the image;.
Icon of the Mother of God of Mount Athos.patron: Invoked for those who must give up what they love to save it; pilgrims.
Icon of the Mother of God of Mount Athos.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Cyril the Deacon of Heliopolis, a.life: The Holy Martyr Cyril the Deacon of Heliopolis and those who suffered with him were victims of the pagan reaction under Julian the Apostate, in the year 362, when the emperor's restoration of the idols licensed the old religion's partisans to settle accounts with the Christians who had humbled them under Constantine;.
Martyr Cyril the Deacon of Heliopolis, a.patron: Invoked for deacons; those who suffer for zeal long past.
Martyr Cyril the Deacon of Heliopolis, a.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Virgin Martyrs Alexandria, Claudia, Euph.life: The Holy Virgin Martyrs Alexandria, Claudia, Euphrasia, Matrona, Juliana, Euphemia, and Theodosia suffered together at Amisus on the Black Sea coast of Pontus in the year 310, in the last fury of the persecution under Maximian, when the eastern provinces were sifted household by household for the Christians the earlier edicts had missed.
Virgin Martyrs Alexandria, Claudia, Euph.patron: Invoked for companies of women; the steadfast together.
Virgin Martyrs Alexandria, Claudia, Euph.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Translation of the relics of the Martyr.life: On this day the Church commemorates the translation of the relics of the holy Martyr Epimachus of Pelusium, called also of Alexandria, whose principal feast is kept at the end of October; the March commemoration marks the carrying of his holy relics to Constantinople, where the City received the Egyptian martyr among its treasures and established this yearly memory of his arrival.
Translation of the relics of the Martyr.patron: Invoked for the zealous; those healed by the martyrs.
Translation of the relics of the Martyr.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Prophet Joad.life: The Holy Prophet Joad is the name the tradition gives to the man of God out of Judah whose mission to Bethel the Book of Kings recounts, one of the most solemn and searching of all the prophetic histories. Sent by the word of the Lord to the schismatic altar that Jeroboam had raised, Joad cried against the altar itself, foretelling by name, three centuries in advance, the king Josiah who would burn men's bones upon it;.
Prophet Joad.patron: Invoked for messengers with hard errands; those who must not turn aside.
Prophet Joad.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Repose of Saint Innocent, Metropolitan o.life: Saint Innocent, Metropolitan of Moscow and Enlightener of North America, was born Ivan Popov in 1797 in the village of Anga in the Irkutsk country of Siberia, a poor priest's son who took the surname Veniaminov at seminary; and in 1824, a young married priest of gifts that would have adorned any capital, he volunteered for the assignment no one wanted, the Aleutian islands at the world's edge, and sailed with his family to Unalaska.
Repose of Saint Innocent, Metropolitan o.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Euschemon the Confessor, Bishop of.life: Saint Euschemon the Confessor was bishop of Lampsacus, the ancient city on the Asian shore of the Hellespont, and shepherded his flock in the last generation of the iconoclast persecution, when the emperor Theophilus renewed with fresh severity the war against the holy images that his dynasty had inherited;.
Saint Euschemon the Confessor, Bishop of.patron: Invoked for bishops in prison; friends of the persecuted.
Saint Euschemon the Confessor, Bishop of.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

26 Martyrs in the Crimea.life: The Holy Twenty-Six Martyrs, whose relics sanctified the Crimea, suffered in the land of the Goths beyond the Danube about the year 375, when the pagan Gothic king raised persecution against the Christians of his people, the young Gothic church, planted by captives and missionaries, paying its first great price in blood.
26 Martyrs in the Crimea.patron: Invoked for congregations at worship; peoples newly converted.
26 Martyrs in the Crimea.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Leavetaking of the Annunciation.life: On this day the Church keeps the leavetaking of the Annunciation, the apodosis of the feast of feasts' beginning, singing once more and for the last time this year the hymns of Gabriel's embassy before folding them away and returning to the Fast.
Leavetaking of the Annunciation.patron: Invoked for all who have kept the feast; the mystery sealed into the soul.
Leavetaking of the Annunciation.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Monastic Martyr Euthymius of Prodromou,.life: The Holy New Martyr Euthymius of the Prodromou skete on Mount Athos was born Eleutherios at Demitsana in the Peloponnese, of pious parents, and fell in his youth by the road many of the new martyrs traveled: cast among the Turks in his wanderings, pressured and entangled, the young man in an hour of weakness denied Christ and accepted Islam, gaining the world's safety and losing his own peace, for the denial gave him no rest by day or night, and repentance rose in him like a fever that only one medicine could cool.
Monastic Martyr Euthymius of Prodromou,.patron: Invoked for those who have denied and would return; the young in repentance.
Monastic Martyr Euthymius of Prodromou,.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyred Holy Fathers who were slain at.life: The Holy Fathers slain at the Monastery of Saint Sabbas suffered in the year 796, by some accounts 797, when bands of Arab raiders, in a season of anarchy in Palestine, fell upon the Great Lavra in the Judean desert; and their martyrdom is known to the Church in rare detail, for one of the survivors set down an eyewitness account of everything.
Martyred Holy Fathers who were slain at.patron: Invoked for monks under raid; communities that will not scatter.
Martyred Holy Fathers who were slain at.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Seraphim of Vyritsa.life: Saint Seraphim of Vyritsa, one of the great elders of the Russian Church in her crucified century, was born Vasily Muravyov in 1866 to peasants of the Yaroslavl country, and sent as a boy to Petersburg to earn bread.
Venerable Seraphim of Vyritsa.patron: Invoked for merchants and businessmen turned to God; spiritual children of the elders.
Venerable Seraphim of Vyritsa.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Caesarius, brother of Saint Gregor.life: Saint Caesarius, brother of Saint Gregory the Theologian, was the younger son of Gregory the Elder, bishop of Nazianzus, and the righteous Nonna, born into the one household that gave the Church a family of saints entire; and where his brother took the road of letters and the altar, Caesarius took the road of the sciences, studying at Alexandria medicine, geometry, and astronomy until he became the most distinguished physician of his age, called to Constantinople and raised to the imperial court as its foremost doctor.
Saint Caesarius, brother of Saint Gregor.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Tarasius of Liconium.life: The Righteous Tarasius of Liconium, of the Lycaonian country of inner Asia Minor, is commemorated on this day among that quiet company of the calendar whose names the synaxaria have carried faithfully across the centuries while the stories attached to them have been let fall; and the Church keeps his feast without embarrassment at the silence, because she understands exactly what the title affirms.
Righteous Tarasius of Liconium.patron: Invoked for the quietly faithful; righteousness kept without record.
Righteous Tarasius of Liconium.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Africanus, Publius, and Terence,.life: The Holy Martyrs Africanus, Publius, and Terence suffered at Carthage in the persecution of Decius, about the year 250, three names kept on this day out of a larger company of confessors whose principal commemoration the Church keeps in April; and the services in their honor were celebrated of old at the monastery called Paulopetrion, the capital of the East keeping the feast of Africa's martyrs, as the Church has always pooled her witnesses across the seas.
Martyrs Africanus, Publius, and Terence,.patron: Invoked for companies of confessors; the dungeon of serpents unharmed.
Martyrs Africanus, Publius, and Terence,.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Monastic Martyr Euphrosynus of Blue Jay.life: The Monastic Martyr Euphrosynus of Blue Jay Lake was a Karelian by birth, raised near Ladoga in the orbit of the great Valaam monastery, and served the Church first as a reader before receiving the tonsure at the Tikhvin monastery of the Dormition.
Monastic Martyr Euphrosynus of Blue Jay.patron: Invoked for those who stay when others must flee; hermits of the border country.
Monastic Martyr Euphrosynus of Blue Jay.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).
