Apostle Aristobulus of the Seventy, Bish.life: The Holy Apostle Aristobulus of the Seventy was born on Cyprus, the brother of the Apostle Barnabas, and with his brother accompanied the Apostle Paul on his missionary journeys, one of that second rank of apostles whom the Lord sent out before His face and whom the Twelve deployed across the world after Pentecost;.
Apostle Aristobulus of the Seventy, Bish.patron: Invoked for missionaries to far frontiers; the first preachers of a land.
Apostle Aristobulus of the Seventy, Bish.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint John of Khakhuli the Oqropiri, als.life: Saint John of Khakhuli, called the Oqropiri, that is, the Golden-mouthed or Chrysostom, was one of the luminaries of the monastery of Khakhuli, which King Davit Kuropalates founded in the second half of the tenth century in the historical region of Tao, at the gorge where the Khakhuli river joins the Tortumi;.
Saint John of Khakhuli the Oqropiri, als.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Hilarion the New, Abbot of Pel.life: Venerable Hilarion the New, abbot of the Pelekete monastery near Prusa in Bithynia, was given to God from his youth, and passing through the whole schooling of the monastic life, silence, obedience, fasting, and the psalter by heart, he was ordained priest and in time made hegumen of Pelekete, one of the renowned monastic houses of the Bithynian.
Venerable Hilarion the New, Abbot of Pel.patron: Invoked for abbots in evil days; those who pray for rain and harvest.
Venerable Hilarion the New, Abbot of Pel.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Patrick, Bishop of Armagh, Enlight.life: Saint Patrick, Bishop of Armagh and Enlightener of Ireland, was born about 387 in Roman Britain to a Christian house, son of the deacon Calpurnius and grandson of a priest, and learned the faith's cost at sixteen, when Irish raiders swept the coast and carried him into slavery in the island he would one day carry into the Church.
Saint Patrick, Bishop of Armagh, Enlight.patron: Invoked for missionaries; captives and former slaves.
Saint Patrick, Bishop of Armagh, Enlight.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Paul the Simple, disciple of V.life: Venerable Paul the Simple of Egypt was called the Simple for his simplicity of heart and his gentleness, and he came to the desert by the door of a broken home: a farmer already sixty years old, he discovered his wife's infidelity, and answering the injury with neither violence nor lawsuit, he left her without bitterness and walked out to Saint Anthony the Great, asking to become a monk.
Venerable Paul the Simple, disciple of V.patron: Invoked for the old who begin late; the simple-hearted.
Venerable Paul the Simple, disciple of V.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Right-believing Great Prince Rostislav-M.life: The Right-believing Great Prince Rostislav of Kyiv, named Michael in holy baptism, was the son of Mstislav the Great and grandson of Vladimir Monomakh, and carried the best of that line, its piety and its peacemaking, through one of the most quarrelsome generations of Rus. As prince of Smolensk for more than thirty years he was the true.
Right-believing Great Prince Rostislav-M.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Quadratus and those with him at N.life: The Holy Martyr Quadratus of Nicomedia suffered with Saturninus, Rufinus, and others in the persecutions of the emperor Decius and his successor Valerian. Descended from an illustrious family and possessed of considerable wealth, Quadratus did not spare his means for Christ, but spent them on the imprisoned: when the jails of Nicomedia filled with Christians, he came to them openly, bribing the guards for entry, supplying the prisoners' needs, binding their wounds, and above all strengthening their souls for the contest ahead, the rich man converting his fortune into courage for the poor.
Martyr Quadratus and those with him at N.patron: Invoked for visitors of prisoners; the wealthy who spend themselves.
Martyr Quadratus and those with him at N.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Manuel and Theodosius.life: The Holy Martyrs Manuel and Theodosius suffered in the year 304, at the height of the great persecution, and belong to that company of witnesses whom the deaths of others recruited: beholding the constancy of the martyrs of their region, the tortures endured with joy and the crowns received before the crowds, the two young men were not frightened, as the persecutors intended all beholders to be, but kindled, the spectacle of the arena working exactly backward, as it did throughout that age, and making converts of its audience.
Martyrs Manuel and Theodosius.patron: Invoked for those stirred by the martyrs' example; the confession volunteered.
Martyrs Manuel and Theodosius.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Gerasimus of the Jordan.life: Venerable Gerasimus of the Jordan was one of the great luminaries of the Palestinian desert, born at the beginning of the fifth century in Lycia of a wealthy family, who renounced the world in his youth and was perfected first in the deserts of the Egyptian Thebaid, and then, coming to the Holy Land about the year 450, settled by the river Jordan, where he founded a great lavra and gathered around him a brotherhood of some seventy monks.
Venerable Gerasimus of the Jordan.patron: Invoked for monks of the strict rule; those who tame wild things.
Venerable Gerasimus of the Jordan.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable John the Clairvoyant, Anchorit.life: Venerable John the Clairvoyant, the great anchorite of Lycopolis in the Egyptian Thebaid, was a craftsman in his youth, a builder's laborer, who left the world in early manhood, and after years of formation under the elders sealed himself, about his fortieth year, into a cell he had prepared in the cliff above Lycopolis, three small chambers walled.
Venerable John the Clairvoyant, Anchorit.patron: Invoked for recluses; counselors of rulers.
Venerable John the Clairvoyant, Anchorit.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Sophronius, Bishop of Irkutsk.life: Saint Sophronius, Bishop of Irkutsk, was born Stefan Kristalevsky in 1704 at Berezan in the Poltava region of Ukraine, of a pious family of modest means, and formed in the flowering church culture of his homeland.
Saint Sophronius, Bishop of Irkutsk.patron: Invoked for missionary bishops; the peoples of Siberia.
Saint Sophronius, Bishop of Irkutsk.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Monastic Martyr Adrian of Poshekhonye, Y.life: The Monastic Martyr Adrian of Poshekhonye was formed in the monastic life at the monastery of Saint Cornelius of Komel, where he became a skilled iconographer, one of a company of gifted brethren gathered around that great elder.
Monastic Martyr Adrian of Poshekhonye, Y.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Apostle Hermes of the Seventy.life: The Holy Apostle Hermes of the Seventy is one of the men whom the Scriptures have made immortal in a single word: the Apostle Paul, closing his Epistle to the Romans with the roll-call of the brethren he loved, writes, Salute Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermas, Patrobas, Hermes, and the brethren which are with them, and by that greeting Hermes entered the canon of Scripture, read aloud in every church of the world in every generation since, the shortest imaginable biography and the most widely published.
Apostle Hermes of the Seventy.patron: Invoked for the greeted and unremembered; bishops of quiet sees.
Apostle Hermes of the Seventy.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Eustathius (Eustace) the Confessor.life: Saint Eustathius the Confessor, Bishop of a see of Bithynia, shepherded his flock in the age of the iconoclast persecution, and belongs to the great company of hierarchs whose collective steadfastness carried the holy icons through the empire's long war against them. Formed from his youth in piety and ascetic labor, he was raised to the episcopate for his virtues, and governed his church in meekness and vigilance, adorning his office, the accounts testify, with purity of life, mercy to the poor, and exactness in the faith;.
Saint Eustathius (Eustace) the Confessor.patron: Invoked for bishops driven from their sees; the icons held through deprivation.
Saint Eustathius (Eustace) the Confessor.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Isaac the Confessor, Founder o.life: Venerable Isaac the Confessor, founder of the Dalmatian monastery, was a hermit of the Syrian wilderness whom the crisis of the Church drew out of his solitude and into the road of an emperor. In the days when Valens, an Arian, had given the churches of Constantinople to the heretics and driven out the Orthodox, Isaac came to the capital to strengthen the persecuted;.
Venerable Isaac the Confessor, Founder o.patron: Invoked for monks who confront power; founders.
Venerable Isaac the Confessor, Founder o.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Simeon the New Theologian.life: Venerable Symeon the New Theologian, whom the Church has set as the third bearer of that supreme title beside John the Evangelist and Gregory of Nazianzus, was born George in 949 to a noble family of Galatia in Paphlagonia, and was brought as a boy to Constantinople for the career his uncle's place at court promised;.
Venerable Simeon the New Theologian.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Irenaeus, Bishop of Sirmium.life: The Hieromartyr Irenaeus, Bishop of Sirmium in Pannonia, suffered in the great persecution in the year 304, and his contest is preserved in acts of the first authenticity, among the most precious of the ancient martyr-records. A young man for his office, and a married man with children after the discipline of that age, Irenaeus was seized as bishop and brought before the governor Probus;.
Hieromartyr Irenaeus, Bishop of Sirmium.patron: Invoked for bishops with families; those whose loved ones plead against their confession.
Hieromartyr Irenaeus, Bishop of Sirmium.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Theognostus, Metropolitan of Kyiv.life: Saint Theognostus, Metropolitan of Kyiv and All Russia, was a Greek, born and formed at Constantinople, and was consecrated in 1328 to the vast metropolia of Rus as successor to Saint Peter, whose fresh grave in Moscow fixed the course of Theognostus' whole primacy: the new metropolitan settled where his predecessor lay, confirming Moscow as the seat of.
Saint Theognostus, Metropolitan of Kyiv.patron: Invoked for primates; defenders of the Church's liberty.
Saint Theognostus, Metropolitan of Kyiv.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Gregory Dialogus, Pope of Rome.life: Saint Gregory the Dialogist, Pope of Rome, was born about 540 to a senatorial house that had already given the Church a pope, and rose by pure capacity to be prefect of the city, the highest civil office Rome could bestow; and at the summit he resigned everything, turned the family palace on the Caelian into the monastery of Saint Andrew, sold the estates for the poor, and became a monk, the ruler of Rome exchanging the prefect's chair for the lowest place in his own former house.
Saint Gregory Dialogus, Pope of Rome.patron: Invoked for popes and pastors; chanters.
Saint Gregory Dialogus, Pope of Rome.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Conon of Isauria.life: The Holy Martyr Conon of Isauria was born in the village of Badine near the city of Isauria in Asia Minor, whose people had received the faith from the Apostle Paul; and from his youth he was under the special protection of the Archangel Michael, the leader of the heavenly hosts, who appeared to him and aided him through the whole course of his life.
Martyr Conon of Isauria.patron: Invoked for married couples called to continence; those beset by demons.
Martyr Conon of Isauria.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Emilian of Rome.life: Saint Emilian of Rome, in the world Victorinus, was a Roman by birth who spent nearly the whole of his life in sin, and the Church keeps his memory precisely because the story did not end there: in his old age he came to himself, repented, and, leaving the world that had consumed his years, entered a monastery, where he received the tonsure with the name Emilian and set himself, in the little time remaining, to redeem the decades lost.
Saint Emilian of Rome.patron: Invoked for penitents of old age; those who repent in secret.
Saint Emilian of Rome.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Hypatius the Wonderworker, Bishop.life: The Hieromartyr Hypatius the Wonderworker, Bishop of Gangra in Paphlagonia, stood among the three hundred and eighteen God-bearing fathers of the First Ecumenical Council at Nicaea, a confessor of the consubstantial Son against Arius; and his people knew him not as a theologian of councils but as the man through whom God did wonders, for his prayer healed the sick, turned aside afflictions, and gave the region water and harvest, the bishop's staff serving Gangra as the prophet's rod had served Israel.
Saint Hypatius the Wonderworker, Bishop.patron: Invoked for fathers of Nicaea; those attacked by the embittered.
Saint Hypatius the Wonderworker, Bishop.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Forefeast of the Annunciation.life: On this day the Church keeps the forefeast of the Annunciation, the single day of preparation before the feast that the fathers called the crown of our salvation and the beginning of all the feasts, and the hymns of the day stand on tiptoe: today, they sing, the great mystery draws near, the archangel is being sent, the Virgin is at her prayers, and the joy of the whole creation is one evening away.
Forefeast of the Annunciation.patron: Invoked for all who prepare for great joy; the eve of the great glad tidings.
Forefeast of the Annunciation.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Cyril, Archbishop of Jerusalem.life: Saint Cyril, Archbishop of Jerusalem, was born about 315 in or near the Holy City and given to the Church's service from his youth; ordained priest, he was entrusted with the instruction of the catechumens, and out of that duty came the work that has made him forever the catechist of the whole Church, the Catechetical Lectures, delivered.
Saint Cyril, Archbishop of Jerusalem.patron: Invoked for catechists; teachers of the newly illumined.
Saint Cyril, Archbishop of Jerusalem.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Hilarion of Pskov, Lake Gdov.life: Venerable Hilarion of Pskov, called also of Gdov, was a disciple of the great Euphrosynus of Pskov, the father of the Pskov wilderness tradition, and carried his elder's school of strictness and stillness northward to the very edge of the Russian land.
Venerable Hilarion of Pskov, Lake Gdov.patron: Invoked for founders of the borderlands; disciples of great elders.
Venerable Hilarion of Pskov, Lake Gdov.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Quadratus and those with him at C.life: The Holy Martyr Quadratus of Corinth was born in the wilderness and raised by heaven itself: during a persecution of the third century his mother, a pious woman named Rufina, fled from Corinth into the mountains to escape her pursuers, and there gave birth to a son and died soon after;.
Martyr Quadratus and those with him at C.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Synaxis of the Venerable Fathers of the.life: On this day the Church celebrates the Synaxis of the Venerable Fathers of the Kyiv Caves Lavra, gathering into one feast the whole shining company of the monastery that mothered the monasticism of all Rus; the common commemoration is kept in the season of the Great Fast, and on it the Church names no single saint because she is naming hundreds.
Synaxis of the Venerable Fathers of the.patron: Invoked for all monastics of the Rus tradition; pilgrims to the caves.
Synaxis of the Venerable Fathers of the.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Joasaph of Snetogorsk, Pskov.life: The Hieromartyr Joasaph, abbot of the Snetogorsk monastery near Pskov, suffered with a company of his monks in the German raid that fell upon the Pskov land at the close of the thirteenth century. Snetogorsk, dedicated to the Nativity of the Most Holy Theotokos, was among the most ancient monasteries of the region, and Joasaph governed it as a father, keeping in it a strict common life;.
Venerable Joasaph of Snetogorsk, Pskov.patron: Invoked for abbots; monks of embattled houses.
Venerable Joasaph of Snetogorsk, Pskov.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Icon of the Mother of God of Lubyatov.type: Icon of the Mother of God · 16th c.
Icon of the Mother of God of Lubyatov.life: The Lubyatov Icon of the Mother of God, an image of the Tenderness, was treasured at the monastery of Saint Nicholas at Lubyatov just outside Pskov, and its feast preserves the memory of a single night on which, the tradition of the Pskov land holds, the Mother of God turned aside the destruction of a city.
Icon of the Mother of God of Lubyatov.patron: Invoked for cities under wrath; intercessors for the condemned.
Icon of the Mother of God of Lubyatov.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Athanasius of Murom.life: Venerable Athanasius of Murom was igumen of the monastery that Saint Lazarus had founded on Murom Island in Lake Onega, and labored there in the middle of the fifteenth century, two generations after the founder; and of his godly life, as the Lives of the Saints frankly record, no information has been preserved, the written memory of the man having perished in the fires and losses that the northern monasteries suffered across the centuries.
Venerable Athanasius of Murom.patron: Invoked for hidden ascetics; those whose deeds God alone remembers.
Venerable Athanasius of Murom.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyrs Pionius and Limnus of Smyrn.life: The Hieromartyrs Pionius and Limnus, presbyters, and the martyrs Sabina, Macedonia, and Asclepiades suffered at Smyrna in the persecution of Decius, in the church that the Apostle John the Theologian had founded and the blood of Polycarp had glorified; and the contest of Pionius, preserved in one of the most precious of the ancient martyr-acts, begins with a detail unmatched in the martyrology: he knew.
Hieromartyrs Pionius and Limnus of Smyrn.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Euthymius, Bishop of Novgorod.life: Saint Euthymius, Archbishop of Novgorod, was the son of a Novgorod priest, vowed to God before his birth, and entered the monastic life at fifteen, laboring at the Vyazhishchi monastery near the city; chosen for the archiepiscopal throne in 1429, he governed the greatest see of the Russian north for nearly three decades, and left it transformed.
Saint Euthymius, Bishop of Novgorod.patron: Invoked for builders; restorers of shrines.
Saint Euthymius, Bishop of Novgorod.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Anastasia the Patrician of Alexand.life: Saint Anastasia the Patrician lived at Constantinople, descended from an aristocratic family, an image of virtue who enjoyed the great esteem of the emperor Justinian himself; and precisely that esteem became the danger of her life. Widowed young, and weary of the envy and intrigues her favor at court had bred, Anastasia resolved to leave the world and save her soul far from the capital: she withdrew to Alexandria and founded a monastery outside the city, where the great lady became a nun among her own sisters, and the first flight seemed complete.
Saint Anastasia the Patrician of Alexand.patron: Invoked for widows; women fleeing unwanted honors.
Saint Anastasia the Patrician of Alexand.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Trophimus and Eucarpus of Nicome.life: The Holy Martyrs Trophimus and Eucarpus were soldiers at Nicomedia in the days of the great persecution, about the year 300, and they began on the wrong side of it: proud, violent men, zealous in the hunting of Christians, distinguished among the persecutors for their cruelty in tracking the faithful, dragging them to the tribunals, and enriching themselves on the terror, the two enforcers of the edicts riding out on the very errand that would end them.
Martyrs Trophimus and Eucarpus of Nicome.patron: Invoked for persecutors converted; soldiers turned from cruelty.
Martyrs Trophimus and Eucarpus of Nicome.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Serapion, Archbishop of Novgorod.life: Saint Serapion, Archbishop of Novgorod, was born near Moscow of pious parents and served first as a married parish priest; widowed, he received the monastic tonsure, and his holiness of life raised him against his will through the offices of the Church, abbot of the Dormition house at Stromyn, then abbot of the great Trinity-Sergius monastery itself, where his sanctity and counsel drew the veneration of princes;.
Saint Serapion, Archbishop of Novgorod.patron: Invoked for deposed hierarchs; those wronged in church disputes.
Saint Serapion, Archbishop of Novgorod.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Matrona of Thessalonica.life: The Holy Martyr Matrona of Thessalonica was a slave in the household of Pautila, written Pantila in the Greek accounts, a Jewish woman of rank, wife of a commander of that city, and her martyrdom was accomplished entirely within the walls of a house, without tribunal, governor, or edict, the persecution reduced to its smallest and most intimate scale, a mistress and a serving-girl.
Martyr Matrona of Thessalonica.patron: Invoked for servants and the enslaved; those punished for their prayers.
Martyr Matrona of Thessalonica.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Sabinus of Egypt.life: The Holy Martyr Sabinus of Egypt, whom the Greek calendars commemorate on this day and the Slavic on the thirteenth of March, was a prominent citizen of Hermopolis, esteemed in the city and generous to its poor; and when the persecution of Diocletian's reign broke over Egypt, the Christians of Hermopolis prevailed upon him to preserve himself for the flock's sake, and Sabinus withdrew with a handful of companions to a hut outside the city, where they remained hidden in fasting and continual prayer while the tribunals worked through the city's confessors.
Martyr Sabinus of Egypt.patron: Invoked for the betrayed; benefactors repaid with evil.
Martyr Sabinus of Egypt.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Nicander of Egypt.life: The Holy Martyr Nicander of Egypt was a physician, and in the persecution of Diocletian he turned his calling into a double ministry that the edicts had made a capital crime twice over: he visited the imprisoned Christians, treating their wounds from the tortures, bringing them food and comfort in the jails where the empire intended them to rot between interrogations;.
Martyr Nicander of Egypt.patron: Invoked for physicians; those who bury the dead.
Martyr Nicander of Egypt.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Arcadius of Cyprus.life: Venerable Arcadius of Cyprus devoted himself from his youth to the monastic life, and struggled in asceticism on the island of Cyprus in the days of the emperor Constantine the Great; and though the labors of his own solitude are kept in the reticence the desert prefers, his memory is bound to the Church forever through the two disciples he raised, the holy martyrs Julian the Physician and Eubolos.
Venerable Arcadius of Cyprus.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Alexander of Sίdē, in Pamphy.life: The Hieromartyr Alexander was a priest of the city of Side in Pamphylia, on the southern coast of Asia Minor, and suffered in the reign of the emperor Aurelian, in the third century's last spasm of persecution before the great storm of Diocletian. Brought before the governor Antoninus, the priest was asked his name and calling, and answered with the confession that made the rest inevitable, that he was a Christian and a pastor of Christ's flock;.
Hieromartyr Alexander of Sίdē, in Pamphy.patron: Invoked for priests before tribunals; the bold answer under Aurelian.
Hieromartyr Alexander of Sίdē, in Pamphy.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Theophanes the Confessor of Si.life: Venerable Theophanes the Confessor of Sigriane was born about 760 to a noble house of Constantinople, orphaned young into the emperor's own guardianship, and set on the highest road of the court.
Venerable Theophanes the Confessor of Si.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Gerasimus of Vologda.life: Venerable Gerasimus, first wonderworker of Vologda, received the monastic tonsure on the fourth of March at the Gnilets Dormition monastery near Kyiv, taking, by the custom of that age, the name of the saint commemorated on the day of his tonsure, Gerasimus of the Jordan, whose feast he would afterward share;.
Venerable Gerasimus of Vologda.patron: Invoked for founders; missionaries to the north.
Venerable Gerasimus of Vologda.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

1st Saturday of Great Lent: The Miracle.life: On the first Saturday of the Great Fast the Church commemorates the miracle of the boiled wheat, the kolyva, wrought by the Great Martyr Theodore the Recruit half a century after his own martyrdom, the dead soldier of Christ mounting guard over the Church's first week of fasting.
1st Saturday of Great Lent: The Miracle.patron: Invoked for all who keep the Fast; the tempted and the tricked.
1st Saturday of Great Lent: The Miracle.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Uncovering of the Precious Cross and the.life: On this day the Church commemorates the uncovering of the Precious Cross and the Precious Nails by the holy Empress Helena, the mother of Saint Constantine the Great, in the year 326. Moved by her son the emperor and by her own great love for Christ, the aged Helena journeyed to Jerusalem to seek out the holy places, which the pagans had long defiled and buried, having raised over Golgotha and the Lord's tomb a temple of their idols to blot out the memory of the Christians' shrines;.
Uncovering of the Precious Cross and the.patron: Invoked for all who seek what is buried; pilgrims.
Uncovering of the Precious Cross and the.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Right-believing Prince Basil (Vasilko) o.life: Right-believing Prince Basil, called Vasilko, of Rostov belonged to the Suzdal line of the Monomashichi, grandson of Vsevolod called Big Nest and son of the pious prince Constantine of Rostov; and the chronicles of the north remember him as the flower of his generation, handsome, brave, generous, and devout, beloved by his people and by the clergy whose counsel he kept.
Right-believing Prince Basil (Vasilko) o.patron: Invoked for rulers under conquest; the young.
Right-believing Prince Basil (Vasilko) o.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Phineas the grandson of Aaron.life: The Righteous Phineas, grandson of Aaron and son of Eleazar the high priest, stands in the Scriptures as the pattern of holy zeal, the priest whose single act stayed a plague and purchased a covenant. In the wilderness, at Shittim, when Israel joined itself to Baal-Peor and fell into open defilement with the daughters of Moab, and the plague of the Lord's anger was consuming the camp, a prince of Israel brought his sin publicly before the weeping congregation;.
Righteous Phineas the grandson of Aaron.patron: Invoked for priests; those zealous for God's honor.
Righteous Phineas the grandson of Aaron.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Monastic Martyr Eustratius of the Kyiv N.life: The Monastic Martyr Eustratius of the Kyiv Near Caves, called the Faster, was a Kyivan who gave his estate to the poor and took the tonsure at the Caves, where his fasting was so severe that the brethren gave him the name he bears.
Monastic Martyr Eustratius of the Kyiv N.patron: Invoked for captives; those who fast.
Monastic Martyr Eustratius of the Kyiv N.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Lazarus of Murom.life: Venerable Lazarus of Murom was a Greek, born at Constantinople, who became a monk in his native city at the High-Mount monastery under the Elder Athanasius Diskotes, a builder of many monasteries, and passed after eight years under the guidance of Bishop Basil of Caesarea; and in 1343 that bishop, wishing to encourage the Russian Church, sent Lazarus, already a noted iconographer, with monks and gifts to Saint Basil, Archbishop of Novgorod.
Venerable Lazarus of Murom.patron: Invoked for iconographers; missionaries to the north.
Venerable Lazarus of Murom.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Translation of the relics of Saint Nikep.life: On this day the Church commemorates the translation of the relics of Saint Nikephoros, Patriarch of Constantinople, one of the great confessors of the holy icons, whose principal feast is kept in June; the March commemoration marks the day of his triumphant return to the City, which was also, by God's exact accounting, the day of his expulsion from it.
Translation of the relics of Saint Nikep.patron: Invoked for patriarchs; theologians of the icon.
Translation of the relics of Saint Nikep.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Apostle Sosthenes of the Seventy.life: The Holy Apostle Sosthenes of the Seventy enters the Scriptures twice, once beaten and once blessing, and the distance between the two is the story of his soul. In the Acts of the Apostles he is the ruler of the synagogue at Corinth when the Jews rose against Paul and dragged him to the judgment seat of the proconsul Gallio;.
Apostle Sosthenes of the Seventy.patron: Invoked for converts from among opponents; those beaten unjustly.
Apostle Sosthenes of the Seventy.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable John the Anchorite of Egypt.life: Venerable John the Anchorite of Egypt is commemorated on this day among the fathers of the desert whose names the Church has kept while the deserts kept their stories, one of the great anonymous host of the anchorites, the men who went out beyond even the sketes and the lauras into total solitude, and whose vocation was, by its own definition, to leave no witnesses.
Venerable John the Anchorite of Egypt.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

120 Martyrs of Persia.life: The Holy One Hundred and Twenty Martyrs of Persia suffered in the great persecution of King Sapor the Second, about the year 344, in the years when the Persian kingdom, at war with the newly Christian empire of the Romans, turned upon the Church within its own borders as upon an enemy colony, and the confessors of Christ in Mesopotamia and Persia were seized by the thousands.
120 Martyrs of Persia.patron: Invoked for captives; companies of confessors.
120 Martyrs of Persia.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

3rd Sunday of Great Lent: Veneration of.life: On the third Sunday of the Great Fast the Church brings out the precious and life-giving Cross and sets it in the midst of the faithful, adorned with flowers, for veneration through the week that follows; and the placement is the whole theology of the day, for the Cross is planted at the exact center of the Fast, the midpoint of the forty days, as a tree of rest at the middle of a hard road.
3rd Sunday of Great Lent: Veneration of.patron: Invoked for all who bear crosses; the weary at mid-journey.
3rd Sunday of Great Lent: Veneration of.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

4th Sunday of Great Lent: St John Climac.life: On the fourth Sunday of the Great Fast the Church sets before her children Saint John Climacus, abbot of Sinai and author of the Ladder of Divine Ascent, and the appointment is deliberate pedagogy: past the Fast's midpoint, with the Cross venerated and Pascha not yet in sight, the Church produces her master cartographer of the spiritual life.
4th Sunday of Great Lent: St John Climac.patron: Invoked for all who ascend toward God; strugglers in mid-Fast.
4th Sunday of Great Lent: St John Climac.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

5th Saturday of Great Lent: of the Akath.life: On the fifth Saturday of the Great Fast the Church keeps the feast of the Akathist, singing entire, in one solemn night, the great hymn to the Most Holy Theotokos which through the rest of the year she sings in portions; and the feast is a war memorial as much as a service, for it was established in thanksgiving for the deliverances of Constantinople.
5th Saturday of Great Lent: of the Akath.patron: Invoked for all who flee to the Theotokos; cities under siege.
5th Saturday of Great Lent: of the Akath.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Apostle and Evangelist Luke of the Seven.life: The Holy Apostle and Evangelist Luke, whom the calendars of this day commemorate with the apostles Nathanael and Clement, and whose principal feast the Church keeps in October, was a Greek of Antioch, a physician by profession and, the tradition adds, a painter, the two arts of the body and the eye brought whole into the Gospel's service;.
Apostle and Evangelist Luke of the Seven.patron: Invoked for physicians; iconographers and painters.
Apostle and Evangelist Luke of the Seven.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Apostle Herodion of the Seventy, and tho.life: On this day the Church commemorates six apostles of the Seventy together, Herodion, Agabus, Rufus, Asyncritus, Phlegon, and Hermes, a company gathered chiefly from a single page of Scripture, the sixteenth chapter of the Epistle to the Romans, where the Apostle Paul, greeting the church of the capital name by name, unknowingly dictated a piece of the Church's calendar.
Apostle Herodion of the Seventy, and tho.patron: Invoked for bishops of the first planting; prophets.
Apostle Herodion of the Seventy, and tho.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Apostle James the Brother of Saint John.life: The Holy Apostle James, the son of Zebedee and brother of John the Theologian, was called from the nets of Galilee with his brother in one summons, the two leaving their father in the boat at a word; and the Lord surnamed the pair Boanerges, sons of thunder, for the fire in them that once wished to call down heaven's flame on an inhospitable village and was taught instead the Spirit it was of.
Apostle James the Brother of Saint John.patron: Invoked for apostles and missionaries; the sons of thunder.
Apostle James the Brother of Saint John.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Apostle Nathaniel of the Seventy.life: The Holy Apostle Nathanael, commemorated this day with Luke and Clement, is the man of Cana in Galilee whose calling the Gospel of John preserves as one of its jewels: when Philip found him with the announcement that the One written of by Moses and the prophets had been found, Jesus of Nazareth, Nathanael answered with the honest man's honest prejudice, Can anything good come out of Nazareth, and Philip, wasting no argument, said only, Come and see;.
Apostle Nathaniel of the Seventy.patron: Invoked for the guileless; students of the Scriptures.
Apostle Nathaniel of the Seventy.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Apostle Pudens of the Seventy.life: The Holy Apostle Pudens of the Seventy was a Roman of senatorial rank, and stands in the Scriptures in a single greeting, for the Apostle Paul, writing his last epistle from his Roman prison, sends Timothy the salutations of Eubulus, and Pudens, and Linus, and Claudia, the condemned Apostle's remaining circle in the capital compressed into four names, of which one belonged to this senator;.
Apostle Pudens of the Seventy.patron: Invoked for hosts of the Church; households that become churches.
Apostle Pudens of the Seventy.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Apostle Trophimus of the Seventy.life: The Holy Apostle Trophimus of the Seventy was a Greek of Ephesus, one of the Gentile converts whom the Apostle Paul bound to himself as companions of the road, and the Scriptures show him three times, each glimpse a station of discipleship. He appears first among the delegates accompanying Paul from Greece toward Jerusalem with the collection for the poor saints, the young churches' offering traveling under the guard of their own sons;.
Apostle Trophimus of the Seventy.patron: Invoked for companions of the great; the sick left behind.
Apostle Trophimus of the Seventy.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Apostles Jason and Sosipater of the Seve.type: Apostles of the Seventy, Martyrs · 1st c.
Apostles Jason and Sosipater of the Seve.life: The Holy Apostles Jason and Sosipater of the Seventy, with the Virgin Kerkyra and those with them, gave the Church one of the completest island conversions of the apostolic age; Jason was of Tarsus, the first Christian of the Apostle Paul's own city, and Sosipater of Achaia, and Paul in the Epistle to the Romans calls them his kinsmen, the tradition adding that Jason is the man of Thessalonica who lodged Paul and Silas and answered for it before the rulers, and Sosipater the Sopater of the Acts;.
Apostles Jason and Sosipater of the Seve.patron: Invoked for island churches; prisoners and their converters.
Apostles Jason and Sosipater of the Seve.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Childmartyr Gabriel of Bialystok.life: The Holy Childmartyr Gabriel of Bialystok was born in 1684 in the village of Zverki near Bialystok, the son of pious Orthodox villagers, Peter and Anastasia, and lived the six brief years given him in the ordinary sanctity of a beloved peasant childhood, prayers learned at his mother's knee, the church feasts, the fields;.
Childmartyr Gabriel of Bialystok.patron: Invoked for children; the innocent and defenseless.
Childmartyr Gabriel of Bialystok.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Constantinople Icon of the Mother of God.life: On this day the Church commemorates the Constantinople Icon of the Most Holy Theotokos, an image which the tradition numbers among those painted by the Holy Apostle and Evangelist Luke himself, the physician and iconographer of the Mother of God, whose brush, the Church holds, first gave the faithful her likeness and received her own blessing upon the work, her word that her grace would be with the images;.
Constantinople Icon of the Mother of God.patron: Invoked for iconographers; all who honor the icons of the Theotokos.
Constantinople Icon of the Mother of God.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Antipas, Bishop of Pergamum.life: The Holy Hieromartyr Antipas, Bishop of Pergamum, bears a distinction shared by no other martyr of the Church, that his witness is certified in the Scriptures by the voice of Christ Himself; for in the Apocalypse, in the letter to the church of Pergamum, the Lord says, I know where thou dwellest, even where Satan's seat is, and thou holdest fast My name, and hast not denied My faith, even in those days wherein Antipas was My faithful martyr, who was slain among you, where Satan dwelleth, the bishop's obituary written by his God.
Hieromartyr Antipas, Bishop of Pergamum.patron: Invoked for bishops of the apostolic planting; sufferers from ailments of the teeth.
Hieromartyr Antipas, Bishop of Pergamum.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Artemon of Laodikeia.life: The Hieromartyr Artemon, presbyter of Laodicea in Syria, gave the Church a lifetime before he gave her his blood: born of Christian parents, he served as a reader for sixteen years, as a deacon for twenty-eight, and as a priest for thirty-three, seventy-seven years in the sanctuary's ascending orders, so that when Diocletian's persecution broke, the man it found at Laodicea was an elder whom three generations had heard read, serve, and offer.
Hieromartyr Artemon of Laodikeia.patron: Invoked for readers, deacons, and priests; the long-serving.
Hieromartyr Artemon of Laodikeia.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Basil, Bishop of Amasea.life: The Holy Hieromartyr Basil, Bishop of Amasea in Pontus, won his crown in the persecution's very last hour, under Licinius, when the co-emperor of the East, breaking his pledges of toleration, turned again upon the Christians in his jealousy of Constantine; and Basil's contest arose from an act of shelter.
Hieromartyr Basil, Bishop of Amasea.patron: Invoked for bishops who shelter the hunted; protectors of women in danger.
Hieromartyr Basil, Bishop of Amasea.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Desan, Bishop in Persia, and.life: The Holy Hieromartyr Desan, Bishop in Persia, suffered with two hundred and seventy-two companions in the persecution of King Sapor the Second, about the years 362 to 364, and their contest preserves the memory of one of that persecution's characteristic cruelties, the martyrdom of the deported. When the Persian armies took the Roman frontier fortresses of Mesopotamia, they carried off the Christian populations wholesale into the interior of the kingdom, clergy and people together, congregations uprooted with their shepherds and marched east as living spoil;.
Hieromartyr Desan, Bishop in Persia, and.patron: Invoked for deported congregations; clergy with their people.
Hieromartyr Desan, Bishop in Persia, and.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Januarius, Bishop of Beneven.life: The Holy Hieromartyr Januarius, Bishop of Benevento, suffered with his companions at Pozzuoli in the year 305, at the climax of Diocletian's persecution, and his passion is a portrait of the ancient Church's cords of affection, for he was seized on account of a visit: when his deacon Sossius of Misenum and other clergy were imprisoned in the.
Hieromartyr Januarius, Bishop of Beneven.patron: Invoked for bishops with their deacons; cities and their patrons.
Hieromartyr Januarius, Bishop of Beneven.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Nikḗtas.life: The Holy Hieromartyr Niketas the New, whom the calendars of this day commemorate, was a hieromonk of the Skete of Saint Anne on the Holy Mountain, and belongs to the luminous company of the Athonite new martyrs, the monks whom the Holy Mountain, in the centuries of the Turkish yoke, deliberately ripened and released into martyrdom, elders preparing volunteers by long askesis and unceasing prayer for the one ministry the conquered Church could still exercise in public, the confession of Christ unto blood.
Hieromartyr Nikḗtas.patron: Invoked for hieromonks; preachers under hostile power.
Hieromartyr Nikḗtas.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Paphnutius of Jerusalem.life: The Holy Hieromartyr Paphnutius of Jerusalem suffered in the last great persecution, in the years of Diocletian and his colleagues, and the calendars keep his memory with a title and a company: a bishop, he underwent, the accounts record, the full ascending scale of the tribunal's arguments, tortured by fire, exposed to the wild beasts, and at the last beheaded with the sword, the three classic instruments exhausted upon one immovable confessor;.
Hieromartyr Paphnutius of Jerusalem.patron: Invoked for bishops in the mines and prisons; companies of exiles.
Hieromartyr Paphnutius of Jerusalem.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Patriarch Gregory V of Const.life: The Holy Hieromartyr Gregory the Fifth, Patriarch of Constantinople, was born Georgios Angelopoulos in 1746 at Dimitsana in the Peloponnese, of poor and pious parents, and rose by learning and austerity through the monasteries and the metropolis of Smyrna to the ecumenical throne, which he occupied three times, the intervals filled with exiles on Athos, for his zeal in rebuilding churches, printing books, and disciplining the clergy made him inconvenient to the powers more than once;.
Hieromartyr Patriarch Gregory V of Const.patron: Invoked for patriarchs; the Greek nation.
Hieromartyr Patriarch Gregory V of Const.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Simeon, Bishop in Persia, an.life: The Holy Hieromartyr Simeon, Archbishop of Seleucia-Ctesiphon and Primate of the Church of Persia, stood at the head of that Church when King Sapor the Second, at war with the Christian empire of the Romans, opened upon his own Christian subjects the persecution that would run forty years and reap uncounted thousands;.
Hieromartyr Simeon, Bishop in Persia, an.patron: Invoked for primates under persecution; clergy slain with their bishop.
Hieromartyr Simeon, Bishop in Persia, an.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Simeon, kinsman of the Lord,.life: The Holy Hieromartyr Simeon, kinsman of the Lord and second Bishop of Jerusalem, was the son of Clopas, the brother of Righteous Joseph the Betrothed, and thus, in the manner of the Law's reckoning, a cousin of the Lord according to the flesh, one of that family circle which unbelief had once found a stumbling block and grace made into a nursery of bishops;.
Hieromartyr Simeon, kinsman of the Lord,.patron: Invoked for bishops of long tenure; kinsmen of the Lord.
Hieromartyr Simeon, kinsman of the Lord,.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Theodore of Perge in Pamphyl.life: The Holy Martyr Theodore of Perge in Pamphylia suffered in the second century, in the reign of Antoninus, with his mother Philippa and the martyrs Dioscorus, Socrates, and Dionysius, and his passion gathers into one contest the Church's three favorite conversions, the son, the mother, and the executioners.
Hieromartyr Theodore of Perge in Pamphyl.patron: Invoked for young conscripts; mothers of martyrs.
Hieromartyr Theodore of Perge in Pamphyl.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Hieromartyr Zeno, Bishop of Verona.life: Saint Zeno, Bishop of Verona, came, the tradition holds, from Africa, bringing to the Italian north the fire of the African church that had given the Latin west its first great voices; raised to the see of Verona about the year 362, he shepherded the city through the last convulsions of paganism and the high tide of the Arian troubles, and his weapons were two, the font and the sermon.
Hieromartyr Zeno, Bishop of Verona.patron: Invoked for preachers; fishermen and anglers.
Hieromartyr Zeno, Bishop of Verona.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Holy Virgin Martyr Theodosίa of Tyre.life: The Holy Virgin Martyr Theodosia of Tyre was a maiden not yet eighteen years old, and her martyrdom, recorded by Eusebius who lived through those days at Caesarea, began with an act of reverence. A company of confessors sat in chains before the governor's tribunal at Caesarea, awaiting sentence;.
Holy Virgin Martyr Theodosίa of Tyre.patron: Invoked for the young; those who honor confessors.
Holy Virgin Martyr Theodosίa of Tyre.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Abraham of Bulgaria.life: The Holy Martyr Abraham of Bulgaria, Wonderworker of Vladimir, was a son of the Volga Bulgars, born among the Muslims of the Kama and Volga country and raised in their faith, a wealthy merchant known even before his conversion for a kindliness to the poor and destitute that ran ahead of his creed;.
Martyr Abraham of Bulgaria.patron: Invoked for merchants; converts from Islam.
Martyr Abraham of Bulgaria.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Alexandra the Empress, wife of Di.life: The Holy Martyr Alexandra the Empress, whom the tradition names as the wife of Diocletian himself, won her crown at the epicenter of the persecution, in the hall where it was being conducted; for through the days of the Great Martyr George's contest the empress watched from her place beside the throne, and what the spectacle taught the spearbearers and the servants it taught her also, and more terribly, since she alone of all the witnesses shared the persecutor's table and bed.
Martyr Alexandra the Empress, wife of Di.patron: Invoked for wives of persecutors; empresses and the highly placed.
Martyr Alexandra the Empress, wife of Di.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Ardalion the Actor.life: The Holy Martyr Ardalion the Actor won his crown in the middle of a performance, and the Church has always treasured his contest as one of grace's most audacious ambushes. A gifted mime of the theater in the reign of Maximian Galerius, Ardalion was cast in a spectacle got up to amuse the crowds at the Christians' expense: he was to play a Christian under interrogation, refusing at first to sacrifice, and then, for the comic resolution, renouncing Christ, apostasy staged as entertainment;.
Martyr Ardalion the Actor.patron: Invoked for actors and performers; all whose art becomes truth.
Martyr Ardalion the Actor.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Crescens of Myra in Lycia.life: The Holy Martyr Crescens of Myra in Lycia was a man of noble family and advanced age who could not watch his city worship what its own hands had made: seeing idolatry triumphant and his neighbors enslaved to inanimate things, the old man went of his own accord into their midst and exhorted them to leave the vain error and return to the God whom the Christians adore, the Creator of all and the Master of life, volunteering for a contest no one had yet demanded of him;.
Martyr Crescens of Myra in Lycia.patron: Invoked for the aged in witness; those pressed to pretend.
Martyr Crescens of Myra in Lycia.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Eupsychius of Caesarea, in Cappad.life: The Holy Martyr Eupsychius of Caesarea in Cappadocia was a young man of noble family, newly married, the wedding feast scarcely over, when the reign of Julian the Apostate set before the Christians of his city the choice that made his name; for Caesarea, almost wholly Christian, still housed a temple of Fortune, the last active shrine of the old gods in the city, and Eupsychius, aflame with zeal, gathered a company of the faithful and utterly destroyed it, the bridegroom leading the demolition as other men lead a wedding dance.
Martyr Eupsychius of Caesarea, in Cappad.patron: Invoked for the newly married; the zealous young.
Martyr Eupsychius of Caesarea, in Cappad.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Irene.life: The Holy Martyr Irene is commemorated on this day in the Slavic menaia, which set her name beside the virgin martyr Theodosia of Tyre, the two kept together in the calendars of the Russian and Ukrainian churches as companions of one commemoration; and of her particular contest the books have preserved the essentials only, that she was a woman who confessed Christ in the age of the persecutions and sealed the confession with her death, receiving the martyr's crown.
Martyr Irene.patron: Invoked for companions of the martyrs; the name kept beside Theodosia.
Martyr Irene.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Pausilippus of Heraclea in Thrace.life: The Holy Martyr Pausilippus suffered at Heraclea in Thrace in the reign of the emperor Hadrian, between the years 117 and 138, in the generation when the persecutions ran not by great edicts but by local storms, a governor's zeal or a city's grudge sufficing to fill the prisons;.
Martyr Pausilippus of Heraclea in Thrace.patron: Invoked for those who die of their wounds; confessors outside the arena.
Martyr Pausilippus of Heraclea in Thrace.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Polycarp of Alexandria.life: The Holy Martyr Polycarp of Alexandria suffered at the opening of the fourth century, in the great persecution under Maximian, and his contest belongs to the company of those whom the sight of cruelty itself drove into the arena. Beholding in Alexandria the savagery with which the confessors of Christ were being tormented, the innocent tortured and the.
Martyr Polycarp of Alexandria.patron: Invoked for those who speak against cruelty; the persecutors rebuked to their faces.
Martyr Polycarp of Alexandria.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Savva Stratelates “the General” o.life: The Holy Martyr Savva Stratelates, the General, was a Goth by race who rose in the Roman service to the rank of military commander under the emperor Aurelian, and lived within that career a life the rank was never designed to contain: a Christian from his youth, he kept the commandments with a soldier's exactness, gave to the needy, and made the prisons his second posting, visiting the confessors in their chains, supplying their wants, and strengthening them for their contests, the general reviewing the Church's troops as devotedly as the empire's;.
Martyr Savva Stratelates “the General” o.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Terence and 40 others beheaded at.life: The Holy Martyr Terence and his forty companions suffered at Carthage in the persecution of Decius, about the year 250, and theirs is the principal commemoration of the African company whom the Church remembers also in March; the calendars preserve the names of the leaders, Terence, Africanus, Maximus, Pompeius, and with them Zeno, Alexander, Theodore, and Macarius, and count the whole harvest at above forty crowns.
Martyr Terence and 40 others beheaded at.patron: Invoked for companies of confessors; prisoners.
Martyr Terence and 40 others beheaded at.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Thomais of Alexandria.life: The Holy Martyr Thomais of Alexandria was a young married woman of that city, raised in piety and wedded to a fisherman, and her martyrdom came upon her not from an empire but from inside her own house. One night when her husband was away at the fishing, his father, at the devil's prompting and captive to her beauty, attempted to draw his daughter-in-law into sin;.
Martyr Thomais of Alexandria.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyr Victor, and his companions, of Ni.life: The Holy Martyrs Victor, Zoticus, Zeno, Acindynus, and Severian suffered at Nicomedia in the year 303, and their crowns were kindled at another man's fire: they were among the multitude who beheld the contest of the holy Great Martyr George, then being tortured at the imperial court with the whole inventive cruelty of Diocletian's capital, and what the spectacle was designed to teach them, the futility of the Christian hope, it taught in reverse.
Martyr Victor, and his companions, of Ni.patron: Invoked for soldiers converted by the witness of others; spectators who cross over.
Martyr Victor, and his companions, of Ni.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Agathopodes the Deacon and Theod.life: The Holy Martyrs Agathopodes the Deacon and Theodulus the Reader served one altar at Thessalonica and received one crown, the persecution of Diocletian's years gathering into a single net the two ends of the church's ministry, an aged deacon full of years and reverence and a young reader radiant in purity, the grandfather and the youth of the same sanctuary.
Martyrs Agathopodes the Deacon and Theod.patron: Invoked for deacons and readers; the old and young yoked in one confession.
Martyrs Agathopodes the Deacon and Theod.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Amphianus and Edesius of Lycia.life: The Holy Martyrs Amphianus and Edesius, called in the Greek Apphianus and Aedesius, were brothers of a wealthy pagan house of Lycia, sent to the famous schools of Berytus, where instead of the world they found Christ; and Apphianus, leaving family and inheritance, came to Caesarea in Palestine and joined himself to the holy Pamphilus, in whose school of Scripture and sanctity Eusebius, the historian of his death, was his fellow disciple.
Martyrs Amphianus and Edesius of Lycia.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Anatolius and Protoleon, soldier.life: The Holy Martyrs Anatolius and Protoleon were soldiers at Nicomedia, and their crowns were won in a single moment, the moment the wheel failed. When the Great Martyr George had been broken, as all supposed, upon the wheel of blades, and the court had dispersed satisfied that the Christians' champion was destroyed, the martyr was found standing whole, healed by the angel of the Lord, before the astonished guards;.
Martyrs Anatolius and Protoleon, soldier.patron: Invoked for soldiers; the first to step forward.
Martyrs Anatolius and Protoleon, soldier.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Anthony, John, and Eustathius of.life: The Holy Martyrs Anthony, John, and Eustathius of Vilnius were young courtiers of Algirdas, Grand Duke of pagan Lithuania, the last unbaptized great power of Europe, and bore before baptism the names Kumets, Nezhilo, and Kruglets; instructed and baptized in secret by a priest named Nestor, the brothers Anthony and John betrayed themselves at the prince's own table, for they would not eat meat on the fast days, and the fire-worshipping court read the abstention correctly, the whole conflict of two religions detected in a refused dish.
Martyrs Anthony, John, and Eustathius of.patron: Invoked for courtiers of pagan powers; brothers in confession.
Martyrs Anthony, John, and Eustathius of.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Basilissa and Anastasia of Rome,.life: The Holy Martyrs Basilissa and Anastasia were noblewomen of Rome, converted by the preaching of the chief Apostles and counted among the disciples of Peter and Paul themselves, formed at the fountainhead in the years when the capital's first church met in houses and the faith passed from the Apostles' own lips;.
Martyrs Basilissa and Anastasia of Rome,.patron: Invoked for those who bury the martyrs; disciples of the apostles.
Martyrs Basilissa and Anastasia of Rome,.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Christopher, Theonas, and Anthon.life: The Holy Martyrs Christopher, Theonas, and Anthony were spearbearers of the emperor Diocletian, soldiers of the innermost guard, and their conversion came at the highest price the court could witness: beholding the sufferings of the holy Great Martyr George, the young tribune tortured before the throne with every device and sustained through all of it by a power the whole palace could see, the three guards drew the soldier's conclusion, that the victory was on the prisoner's side;.
Martyrs Christopher, Theonas, and Anthon.patron: Invoked for imperial guards; those closest to power who choose Christ.
Martyrs Christopher, Theonas, and Anthon.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Dada, Maximus, and Quinctilian,.life: The Holy Martyrs Dada, Maximus, and Quinctilian suffered at the village of Ozovia near Dorostolum on the Danube, in the year 286, under the persecution of Diocletian's reign, three more names in the rich martyr-garland of that frontier country whose garrisons and villages fed the Church's calendar for a generation;.
Martyrs Dada, Maximus, and Quinctilian,.patron: Invoked for villagers in confession; those assaulted in the night.
Martyrs Dada, Maximus, and Quinctilian,.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Diodorus and Rhodopianus, Deacon.life: The Holy Martyrs Diodorus and Rhodopianus, deacons, suffered at Aphrodisias in Caria in the persecution of Diocletian, between the years 284 and 305, and their contest bears the mark of its city.
Martyrs Diodorus and Rhodopianus, Deacon.patron: Invoked for deacons; those slain by their neighbors.
Martyrs Diodorus and Rhodopianus, Deacon.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Isaac, Apollos, and Quadratus, o.life: The Holy Martyrs Isaac, Apollos, and Quadratus were servants of the imperial household at Nicomedia, and their crowns complete the astonishing harvest that the contest of the Great Martyr George reaped inside the palace itself.
Martyrs Isaac, Apollos, and Quadratus, o.patron: Invoked for household servants of the great; those who confess after the queen.
Martyrs Isaac, Apollos, and Quadratus, o.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs James (Jacob) the Presbyter, and.life: The Holy Martyrs James the Presbyter and the deacons Azadanes and Abdiesus suffered in Persia under King Sapor the Second, about the year 380, in the last years of that reign's forty-year war upon the Church; they were seized together with their bishop, the holy Akepsimas, whom the Church commemorates in November, the persecutors gathering in one arrest the three orders of the sanctuary, bishop, presbyter, and deacons, a whole clergy taken as a set.
Martyrs James (Jacob) the Presbyter, and.patron: Invoked for priests and deacons in persecution; the starved and frozen.
Martyrs James (Jacob) the Presbyter, and.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Leonidas, Chariessa, Nice, Galin.life: The Holy Martyr Leonidas and the eight holy women who suffered with him, Chariessa, Nike, Galina, Kallista, Nunechia, Basilissa, Theodora, and Irene, were Christians of Corinth, seized in the persecution of the year 258, in the Paschal season, the confessors of the risen Christ arrested in the very weeks the Church sings of His victory over death;.
Martyrs Leonidas, Chariessa, Nice, Galin.patron: Invoked for companies of women confessors; singers.
Martyrs Leonidas, Chariessa, Nice, Galin.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs of the Kvabtakhevi Monastery in.life: The Holy Martyrs of the Kvabtakhevi monastery suffered in the year 1386, when Timur, called Tamerlane, poured his armies into Georgia in the reign of King Bagrat the Fifth, one invasion of the seven with which that scourge visited the land, razing churches, carrying off the treasures of centuries, and cutting down the people of Kartli;.
Martyrs of the Kvabtakhevi Monastery in.patron: Invoked for monastics under invasion; congregations that would not scatter.
Martyrs of the Kvabtakhevi Monastery in.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Processus and Martinian of Rome.life: The Holy Martyrs Processus and Martinian were the wardens of the Mamertine prison at Rome, the keepers set over the chief Apostles Peter and Paul in their last imprisonment; and the Church delights in their story as the perfect miniature of the Gospel's method, for the prison converted backward, from the inside out.
Martyrs Processus and Martinian of Rome.patron: Invoked for prison guards; wardens converted by their prisoners.
Martyrs Processus and Martinian of Rome.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Martyrs Valentine and Pasikrates in Moes.life: The Holy Martyrs Pasikrates and Valentine were soldiers of the garrison of Durostorum on the Danube, the frontier fortress of Moesia in the lands of present Bulgaria, and they suffered under the governor Absolanus, in the year 228 as the books commonly count, young men of twenty-two and thirty whose regiment was their world and whose Christ outranked their regiment.
Martyrs Valentine and Pasikrates in Moes.patron: Invoked for young soldiers; brothers and comrades in arms.
Martyrs Valentine and Pasikrates in Moes.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Monastic Martyr Bademus (Vadim) of Persi.life: The Monastic Martyr Bademus, called Vadim, archimandrite of Persia, was a wealthy man of Bethlapeta who gave his goods to the poor and his life to God, founding a monastery near his city and forming disciples in the desert sciences of fasting, vigil, and unceasing prayer, an abbot of such sweetness and stillness that his fame ran through Persia in the very years King Sapor's persecution was scouring it;.
Monastic Martyr Bademus (Vadim) of Persi.patron: Invoked for abbots; those slain by the lapsed.
Monastic Martyr Bademus (Vadim) of Persi.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Monastic Martyr Christopher of Dionysiou.life: The Holy Monastic Martyr Christopher of Dionysiou walked the road that the Church of the Turkish centuries came to know as the repentance of the deniers, the most demanding penance her pastoral wisdom ever framed; for Christopher, a Christian of the region of Adrianople, had in his youth, in an hour of weakness under pressure, fear, or passion, denied the faith and been received into the religion of the conquerors, the fall that the age made easy and the return from which it made capital.
Monastic Martyr Christopher of Dionysiou.patron: Invoked for penitents seeking to repair a denial; monks of Dionysiou.
Monastic Martyr Christopher of Dionysiou.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Monastic Martyrs Menas, David, and John,.life: The Holy Monastic Martyrs Menas, David, and John were monks of Palestine, ascetics of the desert communities that carried the tradition of Chariton, Euthymius, and Sabbas through the centuries after the Persian and Arab conquests broke the old peace of the Holy Land.
Monastic Martyrs Menas, David, and John,.patron: Invoked for monks slain at their cells; the unrecorded faithful.
Monastic Martyrs Menas, David, and John,.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

New Martyr John the New of Epirus.life: The Holy New Martyr John of Ioannina, called the New, was a young tailor, born in Epirus of pious parents, who came after their death to Constantinople and practiced his craft in the workshops near the palace quarter, a Christian apprentice among Muslim craftsmen in the newly conquered City, in the first generation after the fall;.
New Martyr John the New of Epirus.patron: Invoked for tailors and craftsmen; apprentices among hostile masters.
New Martyr John the New of Epirus.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

New Martyr Lazarus of Bulgaria.life: The Holy New Martyr Lazarus of Bulgaria was a young shepherd, born of Christian parents in the Bulgarian lands, who came south in the way of the poor of those centuries, seeking work, and kept flocks in the countryside of Pergamum in Asia Minor, a Slav laboring among Greeks under the Ottoman power, triply a stranger and armored only in his baptism;.
New Martyr Lazarus of Bulgaria.patron: Invoked for shepherds; the falsely accused.
New Martyr Lazarus of Bulgaria.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Nine Martyrs at Cyzicus: Theognes, Rufus.life: The Holy Nine Martyrs of Cyzicus, Theognes, Rufus, Antipater, Theostichus, Artemas, Magnus, Theodotus, Thaumasius, and Philemon, were gathered by God into one confession out of nine different lives, drawn, the accounts tell, from various cities and conditions, soldiers and citizens, the old and the young, so that their company was a little image of the whole Church, every estate represented at the tribunal;.
Nine Martyrs at Cyzicus: Theognes, Rufus.patron: Invoked for the fevered and ague-stricken; companies of the faithful.
Nine Martyrs at Cyzicus: Theognes, Rufus.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Repose of Saint Tikhon, Patriarch of Mos.life: Saint Tikhon, Patriarch of Moscow and Enlightener of North America, was born Vasily Bellavin in 1865, a village priest's son from Toropets, and rose through seminary and monastic tonsure with a gentleness so marked that his fellow students, half in jest and wholly in prophecy, called the young man Patriarch;.
Repose of Saint Tikhon, Patriarch of Mos.patron: Invoked for patriarchs in captivity; the Church under persecution.
Repose of Saint Tikhon, Patriarch of Mos.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Virgin Martyr Glaphyra.life: The Righteous Virgin Glaphyra served in the household of the empress Constantia, wife of Licinius, and her sanctity began as flight: when the emperor himself conceived a passion for her, the maid, resolved to keep her chastity at the cost of everything else she possessed, took counsel with the empress, who, protecting her servant against her own husband, helped her escape the court in disguise, and Glaphyra fled across Asia Minor as a nameless woman, carrying nothing intact but her virginity and her faith, the palace exchanged in a night for the road.
Righteous Virgin Martyr Glaphyra.patron: Invoked for women fleeing powerful men; fugitives and the sheltered.
Righteous Virgin Martyr Glaphyra.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Akakios, Bishop of Melitēnḗ.life: Saint Akakios, Bishop of Melitene in Armenia, confessed Christ in the persecution of the emperor Decius, about the year 250, and his contest belongs to the order the Church names the confessors, those who endured the martyrs' torments without receiving the martyrs' death. Shepherd of Melitene in an age when the episcopate was the persecution's first target, Akakios.
Saint Akakios, Bishop of Melitēnḗ.patron: Invoked for bishops under interrogation; confessors released alive.
Saint Akakios, Bishop of Melitēnḗ.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Barsanuphius, Bishop of Tver.life: Saint Barsanuphius, Bishop of Tver and enlightener of Kazan, was born Vasily, a priest's son of Serpukhov, and received his life's strangest equipment by catastrophe: seized as a youth in a Crimean Tatar raid, he spent years in captivity, serving Muslim masters, and there, instead of despairing, he did what only grace explains, keeping his prayers, his fasts within slavery's limits, and his hope, and meanwhile learning perfectly the Tatar language and the faith, customs, and heart of his captors, the slave conducting, without knowing it, the field study for a mission not yet conceived.
Saint Barsanuphius, Bishop of Tver.patron: Invoked for former captives; missionaries who speak the peoples' tongues.
Saint Barsanuphius, Bishop of Tver.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Basil of Poiana Marului.life: Saint Basil of Poiana Marului was the hidden spring of the great hesychast renewal, the elder whose cell in the Buzau mountains of Wallachia fed the river that would water Athos, Moldavia, and all Russia; a monk formed in the Carpathian sketes in the hard years of the Turkish centuries, he became igumen of the skete of Poiana Marului, the Apple Glade, and in time the spiritual guide of all the sketes of the Buzau mountains, a dozen small brotherhoods looking to one elder, the wilderness organized invisibly around a single discerning heart.
Saint Basil of Poiana Marului.patron: Invoked for elders and spiritual guides; teachers of the Jesus Prayer.
Saint Basil of Poiana Marului.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Basil the Confessor, Bishop of Par.life: Saint Basil the Confessor, Bishop of Parium on the Hellespont, shepherded his see in the age of the first iconoclasm, and the Byzantine synaxarion sums his whole episcopate in a single grave sentence, that following the example of the Apostle Paul he spent his life in persecutions, griefs, and tribulations, unceasingly fleeing from place to place so as not to fall into the iconoclasts' hands and be made to subscribe against the holy icons;.
Saint Basil the Confessor, Bishop of Par.patron: Invoked for bishops who will not sign; the hunted and displaced.
Saint Basil the Confessor, Bishop of Par.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Basil, Bishop of Zakholmsk in Mont.life: Saint Basil, Bishop of Zakholm, is commemorated on this day in the Slavic calendars, which mark him a hierarch of the sixteenth century; his see, Zahumlje, called in the older books Zakholm, lay in the mountain country where Herzegovina and Montenegro meet, a diocese of the Serbian Church whose bishops kept their throne at the Tvrdos monastery through the hardest centuries of the Turkish yoke, shepherding a flock the conquest had made poor in everything but faith.
Saint Basil, Bishop of Zakholmsk in Mont.patron: Invoked for the hierarchs of the Zahumlje see; the see of Zahumlje kept holy under the yoke.
Saint Basil, Bishop of Zakholmsk in Mont.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Cosmas, Bishop of Chalcedon, and h.life: Saint Cosmas, Bishop of Chalcedon, and his fellow ascetic Auxentius confessed the holy icons together in the second iconoclasm, and the Church commemorates them together, the hierarch and his companion of the cell joined in the calendar as they were joined in the stand. Cosmas had embraced the monastic life from his youth, and his ascetic measure carried him, in the Church's usual way with the unwilling, to the episcopal throne of Chalcedon, the see of the Fourth Ecumenical Council, whose bishop bore in his very title the memory of the Church's defined faith;.
Saint Cosmas, Bishop of Chalcedon, and h.patron: Invoked for bishops and their companions; friends in confession.
Saint Cosmas, Bishop of Chalcedon, and h.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Cyril, Bishop of Turov.life: Saint Cyril, Bishop of Turov, is the golden mouth of the Russian lands, the writer whom his own age called a second Chrysostom, shining, as the old encomium says, more than all others in Rus'.
Saint Cyril, Bishop of Turov.patron: Invoked for preachers and homilists; hymnographers.
Saint Cyril, Bishop of Turov.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Donatus, Bishop of Euroea in Epiru.life: Saint Donatus, Bishop of Euroea in Epirus, shepherded his see in the days of the emperor Theodosius the Great, and his memory comes down wreathed in the wonders by which God confirmed the Gospel in the countryside where the old fears died hardest.
Saint Donatus, Bishop of Euroea in Epiru.patron: Invoked for bishops against the dragon; keepers of wells and springs.
Saint Donatus, Bishop of Euroea in Epiru.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Eleni (also called Susanna), New M.life: The Holy New Martyr Eleni, called also Susanna, of the island of Lesbos, is commemorated on this day in the company of the island's new martyrs, and her memory belongs to one of the most wondrous chapters of the Church's modern history, the revelation of the hidden martyrs of Lesbos;.
Saint Eleni (also called Susanna), New M.patron: Invoked for the young; those whose stories God kept.
Saint Eleni (also called Susanna), New M.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Eulogius the Hospitable of Constan.life: Righteous Eulogius the Hospitable, whose story the desert preserved in the cycle of Abba Daniel of Sketis, was an Egyptian quarryman, a cutter of stone who lived by his day's wage and had made of that wage a liturgy: each evening he returned from the quarry, and gathered in whatever poor, strangers, and cripples the day had washed.
Saint Eulogius the Hospitable of Constan.patron: Invoked for laborers and quarrymen; hosts of the poor.
Saint Eulogius the Hospitable of Constan.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Eutychius, Patriarch of Constantin.life: Saint Eutychius, Patriarch of Constantinople, was a native of Phrygia who rose through the Church's orders at Amasia, reader, subdeacon, and priest, and then monk and archimandrite, and was in the capital on his monastery's business when the Patriarch Menas died; and the emperor Justinian, warned, tradition tells, in a vision, and the clergy concurring in the choice, raised the Amasian archimandrite to the first throne of the East in 552.
Saint Eutychius, Patriarch of Constantin.patron: Invoked for patriarchs; presidents of councils.
Saint Eutychius, Patriarch of Constantin.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint George Matskevereli of Georgia.life: Saint George Matskvereli, whom the Georgian Church commemorates on this day, bore the title of the bishops of Atskuri, called Matskveri in the old usage, the ancient cathedral see of Samtskhe in southern Georgia, whose church guarded one of the most venerable treasures of the Georgian land, the wonderworking Atskuri icon of the Most Holy Theotokos, held by tradition to have come to Georgia in apostolic times;.
Saint George Matskevereli of Georgia.patron: Invoked for bishops of ancient sees; guardians of wonderworking icons.
Saint George Matskevereli of Georgia.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint George the Confessor and Bishop of.life: Saint George the Confessor, Bishop of Antioch in Pisidia, gave his name to the roll of the hierarchs who would not sign, the confessors of the iconoclast age whose sees were the price of their subscription refused. A monk from his youth, renowned for holiness of life, George was raised against his desire to the throne of Pisidian Antioch, the ancient city of the Apostle Paul's first great sermon, and shepherded it in the decades when the empire made war on the holy images;.
Saint George the Confessor and Bishop of.patron: Invoked for bishops against councils of error; the exiled.
Saint George the Confessor and Bishop of.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint George the Confessor, Bishop of My.life: Saint George the Confessor, Archbishop of Mytilene, called in the Greek tradition the Standard-Bearer, was born about 776 on the Anatolian coast facing Lesbos, and given to God from his youth in the monastic life, where his ascetic labors and his mercy to the poor made his name known across the strait;.
Saint George the Confessor, Bishop of My.patron: Invoked for bishops deposed for the faith; the exiled.
Saint George the Confessor, Bishop of My.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Illyricus of Mount Myrsinon in the.life: Venerable Illyricus of Mount Myrsinon is kept in the calendars with a name and a mountain, and scarcely anything more: the synaxaria of the Greek and Slavic churches alike commemorate on this day the ascetic who sanctified Myrsinon in the Peloponnese, the mountain of the myrtles, and are silent about his century, his origins, and his end, the books preserving the address of his sanctity and entrusting its contents to God.
Saint Illyricus of Mount Myrsinon in the.patron: Invoked for hermits of the mountains; the mountain sanctified.
Saint Illyricus of Mount Myrsinon in the.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Isaac the Syrian, Abbot of Spoleto.life: Venerable Isaac the Syrian of Spoleto carried the desert of the East into the hills of Italy, and his memory the Church receives from Saint Gregory the Dialogist, who gathered the elders' testimonies of him with delight. A monk of Syria fleeing, in the age of the Monophysite troubles, to the West, Isaac arrived at Spoleto a nameless stranger, entered the church, and asked leave to pray;.
Saint Isaac the Syrian, Abbot of Spoleto.patron: Invoked for strangers and immigrants; monks who refuse possessions.
Saint Isaac the Syrian, Abbot of Spoleto.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).
