Saint Joannicius of Devich, Serbia.life: Venerable Joannicius of Devich was one of the great hesychasts of the Serbian lands, a man of the Zeta country who fled from human glory as other men flee ruin.
Saint Joannicius of Devich, Serbia.patron: Invoked for hermits; the sick brought to the saints.
Saint Joannicius of Devich, Serbia.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Martin the Confessor, Pope of Rome.life: Saint Martin the Confessor, Pope of Rome, was born in Tuscany toward the end of the sixth century, served as the Roman Church's apocrisiarius at Constantinople, where he learned the imperial heresy at its source, and was elected to the throne of Rome in 649.
Saint Martin the Confessor, Pope of Rome.patron: Invoked for popes and patriarchs; prisoners of state.
Saint Martin the Confessor, Pope of Rome.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Methodius, Equal of the Apostles,.life: Saint Methodius, Equal of the Apostles and Archbishop of Moravia, was the elder of the two brothers of Thessalonica through whom the Slavic nations received the Scriptures and the Liturgy in their own tongue.
Saint Methodius, Equal of the Apostles,.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Niphon, Bishop of Novgorod.life: Saint Niphon, Bishop of Novgorod, was tonsured at the Kyiv Caves Lavra and carried its formation to the north when he was consecrated to the great see of Novgorod in 1130; there he shepherded with the energy of the Caves tradition, building and adorning churches, roofing Saint Sophia and beautifying her, reconciling the ever-quarreling princes and once turning back, by sheer moral weight, a fratricidal campaign between Novgorod and Kyiv, and governing his turbulent city as a father who could neither be bought nor frightened.
Saint Niphon, Bishop of Novgorod.patron: Invoked for defenders of canonical order; bishops between princes.
Saint Niphon, Bishop of Novgorod.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Platonis of Nisibis, Syria.life: Saint Platonis of Nisibis served the Church in the order of deaconess, the ancient ministry by which consecrated women assisted at the baptism of women, instructed the newly illumined of their own sex, carried the Church's care into the women's quarters where no clergyman could go, and stood in the assembly as the ordered face of female service;.
Saint Platonis of Nisibis, Syria.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Simeon of Egypt.life: Venerable Simeon of Egypt is commemorated on this day in a company, for the calendars keep together on the fifth of April a small brotherhood of Egyptian ascetics, Simeon, Theonas, Publius, and Phorbinus, venerable monks of the fourth century whose names came down the tradition yoked in a single memorial, as they had presumably lived, contemporaries and perhaps companions in the golden age of the Egyptian desert;.
Saint Simeon of Egypt.patron: Invoked for desert monks; the unrecorded faithful.
Saint Simeon of Egypt.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Stephen, Bishop of Perm.life: Saint Stephen, Bishop of Perm, enlightener of the Zyrians, carried the Gospel to a people no one had ever written down, and began, like a new Cyril, by giving them letters.
Saint Stephen, Bishop of Perm.patron: Invoked for missionaries and translators; makers of alphabets.
Saint Stephen, Bishop of Perm.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Theodore the Sykeote, Bishop of An.life: Saint Theodore the Sykeote, Bishop of Anastasiopolis, was born in the village of Sykeon in Galatia, the son of an innkeeper's daughter named Mary, and his Life, written by his own disciple George, is one of the great treasuries of Byzantine sanctity, a whole world of village, road, demon, and wonder preserved around one ascetic;.
Saint Theodore the Sykeote, Bishop of An.patron: Invoked for ascetics of iron and enclosure; exorcists.
Saint Theodore the Sykeote, Bishop of An.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Theonas of Egypt.life: Venerable Theonas of Egypt stands in the calendar of this day beside Simeon, Publius, and Phorbinus, the little company of fourth-century Egyptian venerables whom the tradition commemorates together; and his entry, like theirs, is of the kind the Church calls a bare memorial, the name, the land, the century, and the rank, everything else entrusted to the God for whom it was all performed in the first place.
Saint Theonas of Egypt.patron: Invoked for desert monks; companions in asceticism.
Saint Theonas of Egypt.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

St Anthony of the Kyiv Caves.life: Saint Anthony, the founder of monasticism in the land of Rus, was born in the year 983 at Liubech near Chernigov and named Antipas in baptism. Drawn from his youth to the monastic life, he journeyed to Mount Athos, where he was tonsured and trained in the ascetic struggle, until the abbot, moved by God, sent him back to his homeland to plant there the monastic way.
St Anthony of the Kyiv Caves.patron: Invoked for monastics; monastic life in Rus.
St Anthony of the Kyiv Caves.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

St Basil of Ostrog.life: Saint Basil of Ostrog, Metropolitan of Zahumlje, the most beloved wonderworker of the Serbian lands, was born Stojan Jovanovic in 1610 in the village of Mrkonjici in the Popovo plain of Herzegovina, to pious peasants Peter and Anastasia, and kept his father's flocks as a boy with a prayer rope in his hand;.
St Basil of Ostrog.patron: Invoked for the sick and suffering of every faith; pilgrims.
St Basil of Ostrog.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

St Calinic of Cernica.life: Saint Calinic of Cernica, one of the great lamps of the Romanian Church, was born in Bucharest in 1787 to devout parents and entered the Cernica monastery at twenty, where the Paisian tradition of the Jesus Prayer, strict fasting, and obedience formed him so thoroughly that at thirty-one, against his tears, he was made abbot;.
St Calinic of Cernica.patron: Invoked for abbots and bishops; ascetics in active office.
St Calinic of Cernica.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

St Dimitrie the New of Bucharest.life: Saint Dimitrie the New, the protector of Bucharest, was born in the thirteenth century in the village of Basarbov on the river Lom in the Bulgarian lands, of poor and pious parents, and in his youth he herded the cattle of the village. So tender was his conscience that, having once unknowingly crushed a nest of fledglings beneath his foot, he punished that foot for three years, leaving it unshod in frost and heat;.
St Dimitrie the New of Bucharest.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

St Dionysios of Zakynthos.life: Saint Dionysios of Zakynthos was born in 1547 on that island, of the noble house of Sigouros, and fleeing the world in his youth, he entered the monastery of the Strophades, where he was clothed in the angelic schema and, surpassing his elders in virtue while young in years, was found worthy of the priesthood;.
St Dionysios of Zakynthos.patron: Invoked for those who must forgive the unforgivable; forgiveness of enemies.
St Dionysios of Zakynthos.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

St Joseph of Damascus & the New Martyrs.life: The Hieromartyr Joseph of Damascus was a learned and zealous priest of the Church of Antioch, renowned as a preacher, teacher, and translator, who labored tirelessly for the instruction of his flock. In July of 1860, when a savage persecution broke out against the Christians of Damascus and the Christian quarter was given over to slaughter and flames, Saint Joseph did not flee but ran through the burning streets bearing the Holy Gifts, hearing confessions and giving communion to the dying and encouraging the faithful to hold fast to Christ.
St Joseph of Damascus & the New Martyrs.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

St Kosmas Aitolos, Equal-to-the-Apostles.life: Saint Cosmas of Aetolia, called Equal-to-the-Apostles, was born about the year 1714 in Aetolia and in the world was named Konstas. After his early studies he went to the Holy Mountain, where he was educated at the school of Vatopedi and was tonsured a monk at the monastery of Philotheou, receiving the name Cosmas and being ordained hieromonk.
St Kosmas Aitolos, Equal-to-the-Apostles.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

St Olga, Equal-to-the-Apostles.life: Saint Olga, Equal-to-the-Apostles, was the wife of the Kievan Great Prince Igor, and after his death she ruled the land of Rus with strength and wisdom as regent for her young son Sviatoslav. Though raised in paganism, she came to desire the true faith, and journeying to Constantinople she was baptized by the Patriarch, taking the name Helen, with the emperor himself standing as her godfather.
St Olga, Equal-to-the-Apostles.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

St Parascheva of Iași.life: Saint Parascheva of Iași, called the New, was born in the eleventh century at Epivato in Thrace, on the shore of the sea of Marmara, of pious and wealthy parents. As a girl, hearing in church the word of the Lord, Whosoever will come after Me, let him deny himself, she began giving her rich clothing to the poor, enduring the reproaches of her family;.
St Parascheva of Iași.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

St Sava, First Archbishop of Serbia.life: Saint Sava, first Archbishop of Serbia and the father of his nation's Church, was born Rastko, youngest son of the great prince Stefan Nemanja; and at seventeen, evading the marriage his rank required, the prince fled to Mount Athos and was tonsured Sava, the runaway heir hiding in the Russian monastery of Panteleimon and then at Vatopedi while his father's envoys searched the Mountain for him.
St Sava, First Archbishop of Serbia.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

St Seraphim of Sarov.life: Saint Seraphim of Sarov, one of the most beloved ascetics of the Russian Church, was born Prochor Moshnin at Kursk in 1754 and entered the Sarov monastery as a young man. After years of monastic obedience he withdrew to a forest hermitage, where he pursued severe ascetic labors, on one occasion praying a thousand nights upon a rock, and endured a beating by robbers that left him bent for the rest of his life.
St Seraphim of Sarov.patron: Commemorated in the holy calendar of the Church.
St Seraphim of Sarov.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

St Sergius of Radonezh.life: Saint Sergius of Radonezh, the great abbot and reviver of Russian monasticism, was born Bartholomew around 1314 to the pious nobles Cyril and Maria near Rostov, and as a boy received by a wondrous encounter the gift of learning that had eluded him. After his parents' death he withdrew with his brother into the forest wilderness of Radonezh, where he built a small church of the Holy Trinity and lived in solitude and severe labor until disciples gathered to him and a great monastery arose, the Trinity Lavra that still bears his name.
St Sergius of Radonezh.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

St Simeon the Myrrh-gusher.life: Saint Simeon the Myrrh-gusher was born Stephen Nemanja, Great Zhupan of Serbia, the founder at once of a state, a dynasty, and a river of holiness. Ruling in the twelfth century, he toiled greatly for his fatherland, uniting the greater part of the Serbian lands and winning for his country its independence;.
St Simeon the Myrrh-gusher.patron: Invoked for rulers who renounce; fathers of saints.
St Simeon the Myrrh-gusher.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

St Stephen the Great.life: Saint Stephen the Great, Prince of Moldavia, succeeded his murdered father Bogdan the Second upon the throne in 1457 and ruled for nearly half a century as a fearless defender of the Christian faith and of his people against the advancing Turks. He was a spiritual son of Saint Daniel the Hesychast, who counseled him to raise a church in thanksgiving after every victory;.
St Stephen the Great.patron: Invoked for soldiers; defense of the faith and homeland.
St Stephen the Great.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

St Vladimir, Equal-to-the-Apostles.life: Saint Vladimir, Equal-to-the-Apostles and Enlightener of the land of Rus, was the son of Prince Svyatoslav and the grandson of Saint Olga, and was born in the year 963. Reared in paganism and hardened by war, he ruled at first as a fierce and idolatrous prince, yet the seed of faith planted by his grandmother was not lost.
St Vladimir, Equal-to-the-Apostles.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

St Volodymyr, Equal-to-the-Apostles.life: Saint Vladimir, Equal-to-the-Apostles and Enlightener of the land of Rus, was the son of Prince Svyatoslav and the grandson of Saint Olga, and was born in the year 963. Reared in paganism and hardened by war, he ruled at first as a fierce and idolatrous prince, yet the seed of faith planted by his grandmother was not lost.
St Volodymyr, Equal-to-the-Apostles.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

St Xenia of St Petersburg.life: Blessed Xenia of Saint Petersburg, fool for Christ's sake, was a young wife of the capital in the reign of the empress Elizabeth, married to the colonel Andrei Feodorovich Petrov, a singer of the court chapel; and when her husband died suddenly in the night, at twenty-six she stood at a graveside that had opened without confession or Communion, and answered it with the strangest and most complete act of love in the Russian calendar.
St Xenia of St Petersburg.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

The Burning of Saint Sava's relics.life: On this day the Serbian Church keeps the solemn memory of the burning of the relics of Saint Sava, her first archbishop, enlightener, and father, an act of calculated desecration that God, in the deep irony the Church has read in it ever since, converted into the saint's widest enthronement.
The Burning of Saint Sava's relics.patron: Invoked for the Serbian people; all whose shrines are destroyed.
The Burning of Saint Sava's relics.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Translation of the relics of Blessed Vse.life: On this day the Church commemorates the translation of the relics of Blessed Vsevolod, in holy baptism Gabriel, Prince of Pskov, the wonderworker whose principal memory she keeps in February; grandson of Vladimir Monomakh, prince first of great Novgorod, where he ruled with justice and open-handed mercy until that changeable city cast him out, he was received with love by Pskov, which he served the remainder of his short life and where he raised the first stone church of the Holy Trinity, the cathedral that became the heart and symbol of the Pskov land;.
Translation of the relics of Blessed Vse.patron: Invoked for all who honor the relics of the saints; the prince returned to his cathedral in glory.
Translation of the relics of Blessed Vse.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Uncovering of the relics of Saint Basil,.life: On this day the Church commemorates the uncovering of the relics of the Holy Hieromartyr Basil, Bishop of Amasea, whose contest she keeps earlier in this same week; beheaded at Nicomedia in the persecution of Licinius, about the year 322, for sheltering the virgin Glaphyra from the emperor's designs, Basil suffered after death the persecutor's final spite, his body cast into the sea, the tyrant intending that the Church should lack even a grave to gather at, the martyr erased, as the enemies of the martyrs always hope, by water and silence.
Uncovering of the relics of Saint Basil,.patron: Invoked for all who seek the relics of the martyrs; the sea compelled to restore its trust.
Uncovering of the relics of Saint Basil,.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Uncovering of the relics of Saint Nikḗta.life: On this day the Church commemorates the uncovering of the relics of Saint Niketas, Bishop of Novgorod, the recluse of the Kyiv Caves who fell in his youth to the enemy's deception, was restored by the prayers of the fathers, and rose through humility to the episcopate he had once nearly forfeited to pride, shepherding Novgorod in holiness and wonders, praying down rain and quenching a fire of the city by his intercession, until his repose in 1108;.
Uncovering of the relics of Saint Nikḗta.patron: Invoked for all who honor the relics of the saints; those with ailments of the eyes.
Uncovering of the relics of Saint Nikḗta.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Uncovering of the relics of Venerable Al.life: On this day the Church commemorates the uncovering of the relics of Venerable Alexander of Svir, the great ascetic of the northern forests between the Ladoga and Onega lakes, whose principal feast she keeps at the end of August.
Uncovering of the relics of Venerable Al.patron: Invoked for all who honor the relics of the saints; the incorrupt founder revealed.
Uncovering of the relics of Venerable Al.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Alexander, Abbot of Oshevensk.life: Venerable Alexander of Oshevensk was born in 1427, the son of a prosperous peasant named Nikephoros Oshaven, and given in baptism the name Alexis; drawn to God from boyhood, he left his family for the great monastery of Saint Cyril at White Lake, the mother-house of the northern desert, and there received the tonsure with the name Alexander and the formation of the Kirillov school, the long services, the labor, the strict fast, and the letters, growing into a monk whom the abbot trusted and the brethren loved.
Venerable Alexander, Abbot of Oshevensk.patron: Invoked for founders on family land; sons who exceed their fathers' plans.
Venerable Alexander, Abbot of Oshevensk.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Alexius the Recluse of the Kyi.life: Venerable Alexius the Recluse of the Kyiv Caves took upon himself the severest of the monastery's recognized paths, the enclosure, and the Church commemorates him on this day together with Venerable Savva, his fellow recluse, the two shut doors of one commemoration. The recluse's calling, which the Caves tradition received from the East and proved on its own.
Venerable Alexius the Recluse of the Kyi.patron: Invoked for recluses; those enclosed with God.
Venerable Alexius the Recluse of the Kyi.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Daniel, Abbot of Pereslavl-Zal.life: Venerable Daniel of Pereslavl found his sanctity in a work of mercy most men cross the road to avoid: the burial of the abandoned dead. Born at Pereslavl-Zalessky and tonsured in the strict school of Saint Paphnutius' monastery at Borovsk, he returned to his native town as a monk of the Goritsky monastery, and there took upon himself.
Venerable Daniel, Abbot of Pereslavl-Zal.patron: Invoked for those who bury the forgotten dead; undertakers and mourners of strangers.
Venerable Daniel, Abbot of Pereslavl-Zal.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Euthymius of Suzdal.life: Venerable Euthymius of Suzdal was born in 1316 at Nizhny Novgorod, taught his letters from early childhood and raised in piety, and received the monastic tonsure at the Caves monastery of Nizhny Novgorod under its founder, Saint Dionysius, the future archbishop of Suzdal, in whose school of strictness the young monk was formed in obedience, fasting, and the unbroken round of prayer, sleeping little and serving all, until his measure was evident to his elder;.
Venerable Euthymius of Suzdal.patron: Invoked for abbots of the common life; founders.
Venerable Euthymius of Suzdal.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable George of Mount Maleon in the.life: Venerable George of Maleon lived his ascetic life on the mountain of Malea in Laconia, the wild cape at the southern extremity of the Peloponnese, whose storms were proverbial among sailors and whose heights, precisely for their harshness, drew the hermits of the Byzantine centuries.
Venerable George of Mount Maleon in the.patron: Invoked for hermits; fathers of scattered disciples.
Venerable George of Mount Maleon in the.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Gerontius the Canonarch of the.life: Venerable Gerontius, Canonarch of the Kyiv Caves, lived in the fourteenth century and spent his whole earthly life within the Lavra in a single obedience, that of canonarch, the leader of the church singing, who stands before the choirs and intones the verses and announces the tones, the living hinge on which the whole audible order of the services turns;.
Venerable Gerontius the Canonarch of the.patron: Invoked for church singers and readers; canonarchs.
Venerable Gerontius the Canonarch of the.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable James, Abbot of Zheleznoborov.life: Venerable James of Zheleznoborov was born in the second half of the fourteenth century to the noble Amosov line, whose lands lay near Galich in the Kostroma country, and as a young man he made the choice that placed him inside the greatest spiritual lineage of his age, going to the Trinity monastery and becoming the disciple of.
Venerable James, Abbot of Zheleznoborov.patron: Invoked for disciples of Sergius; founders in hard country.
Venerable James, Abbot of Zheleznoborov.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable John of the Ancient Caves in P.life: Venerable John of the Ancient Caves, called in the Greek books the Paleolavrite, was a monk and priest of the Old Lavra in the Judean desert, the monastery of the caves of Souka founded by Venerable Chariton the Confessor in the fourth century, the most ancient of all the desert's houses, which the monks of later ages called simply the Old Lavra, its very name a genealogy;.
Venerable John of the Ancient Caves in P.patron: Invoked for priests of the desert; pilgrims who stay.
Venerable John of the Ancient Caves in P.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable John, disciple of Venerable Gr.life: Venerable John, the disciple of Saint Gregory of Decapolis, belongs to one of the luminous circles of the ninth century, the little company that gathered in Constantinople around the great Decapolite in the years of the second iconoclasm; for Gregory, the wonderworking ascetic who had crossed the empire defending the icons, drew to himself disciples worthy of the school, among them Joseph, the future hymnographer of the whole Church, and this John, who gave to the elder the disciple's entire offering, obedience, service, and the imitation that is the desert's truest praise.
Venerable John, disciple of Venerable Gr.patron: Invoked for disciples of great elders; monks of the second rank.
Venerable John, disciple of Venerable Gr.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Joseph the Hymnographer.life: Venerable Joseph the Hymnographer, the most abundant poet the Church has ever possessed, was born in Sicily about 816 to pious parents, Plotinus and Agatha, and when the Arab invasion broke over the island his family fled to the Peloponnese; the youth went on to Thessalonica, received the tonsure and in time the priesthood, and shone in fasting, vigil, and psalmody until the great Gregory of Decapolis, meeting him, recognized his measure and took him to his own monastery at Constantinople.
Venerable Joseph the Hymnographer.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Joseph the Much-Ailing, of the.life: Venerable Joseph the Much-Ailing, of the Kyiv Far Caves, earned his surname in the world before he sanctified it in the monastery: he was a man worn by long and grievous illness, year upon year of a sickness that medicine could not lift, and in the depth of it he turned to God with the bargain of the desperate and the devout, vowing that if the Lord would raise him from his bed, he would go to the Caves monastery and serve the brotherhood there all the days that were given back to him.
Venerable Joseph the Much-Ailing, of the.patron: Invoked for the chronically ill; those who bargain with God in sickness.
Venerable Joseph the Much-Ailing, of the.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Memnon the Wonderworker.life: Venerable Memnon the Wonderworker was an abbot in Egypt, formed from his youth in the desert's whole curriculum, fasting, vigil, and the guarding of the thoughts, until, having first governed himself, he was set to govern others, and guided his brotherhood with the blend of severity toward himself and gentleness toward the weak that marks the authentic abbas;.
Venerable Memnon the Wonderworker.patron: Invoked for abbots; sailors in storm.
Venerable Memnon the Wonderworker.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Niketas the Confessor, Abbot o.life: Venerable Niketas the Confessor, abbot of the Medikion monastery, was born at Caesarea in Bithynia and, his mother dying in his infancy, was raised by his grandmother in piety.
Venerable Niketas the Confessor, Abbot o.patron: Invoked for abbots under persecution; those who have lapsed and returned.
Venerable Niketas the Confessor, Abbot o.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Publius of Egypt.life: Venerable Publius of Egypt completes the company of this day's Egyptian venerables, commemorated with Simeon, Theonas, and Phorbinus in the joint memorial the calendars have carried since the early centuries.
Venerable Publius of Egypt.patron: Invoked for desert monks; watchers in prayer.
Venerable Publius of Egypt.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Rufus the Obedient of the Kyiv.life: Venerable Rufus the Obedient, of the Kyiv Far Caves, lived in the fourteenth century and bears in his very title the whole of his biography and the summit of monastic science, for the fathers of the Caves, who had among them fasters, recluses, wonderworkers, and healers, judged that this monk's distinction was obedience, and fixed the word to his name forever, the community's collective verdict that in the surrender of the will Rufus had no equal among them.
Venerable Rufus the Obedient of the Kyiv.patron: Invoked for novices; all under obedience.
Venerable Rufus the Obedient of the Kyiv.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Savva the Recluse of the Kyiv.life: Venerable Savva the Recluse of the Kyiv Caves shares this day's commemoration with Venerable Alexius, the two recluses joined in the calendar as neighbors in the same hidden warfare.
Venerable Savva the Recluse of the Kyiv.patron: Invoked for recluses; the hidden intercessors.
Venerable Savva the Recluse of the Kyiv.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Stephen, Abbot of the Kyiv Far.life: Saint Stephen, Abbot of the Kyiv Caves and Bishop of Vladimir in Volhynia, carried the heaviest of monastic inheritances, the succession of a saint; a disciple formed under Venerable Theodosius himself, he served the great founder as domestikos, the master of the church singing, and stood so high in his father's trust that Theodosius, dying in 1074, named Stephen to the brethren as his successor, and the community that had just buried the greatest abbot in Rus' set Theodosius' cantor in Theodosius' stall.
Venerable Stephen, Abbot of the Kyiv Far.patron: Invoked for successors of great founders; the unjustly deposed.
Venerable Stephen, Abbot of the Kyiv Far.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Sylvester, Abbot of Obnora.life: Venerable Sylvester of Obnora was a disciple of Saint Sergius of Radonezh and a contemporary of Saint Alexis, Metropolitan of Moscow, and his full Life, the Church admits plainly, has not survived the centuries, the fire and forgetfulness of the northern land leaving her his name, his river, his monastery, and the outline of a sanctity she trusts more than documents;.
Venerable Sylvester, Abbot of Obnora.patron: Invoked for hermits discovered against their will; founders of forest houses.
Venerable Sylvester, Abbot of Obnora.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Theodore Trichinas “the Hair-S.life: Venerable Theodore, whom the Church surnames Trichinas, the Hair-Shirt Wearer, was born in Constantinople of wealthy parents, and made of his renunciation a geography lesson, for he did not flee to Egypt or Sinai but withdrew to a monastery in the wild country near the capital itself, renouncing the City within sight of it, the rich man's son keeping his poverty where his inheritance could always have been reclaimed, so that every day of his asceticism was a fresh refusal rather than a settled distance.
Venerable Theodore Trichinas “the Hair-S.patron: Invoked for hermits; all who wear hard garments for God.
Venerable Theodore Trichinas “the Hair-S.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Titus the Wonderworker.life: Venerable Titus the Wonderworker was inflamed with the love of Christ from his childhood, and entering a coenobium in his youth, he gave himself to the common life with a completeness the synaxaria record as his distinguishing mark: in humility and obedience, the Byzantine synaxarion testifies, he surpassed all the monks of his community, the young man competing for the last place as others compete for the first, and keeping himself from his youth as chaste in body and in spirit as an angel of God.
Venerable Titus the Wonderworker.patron: Invoked for monks of the common life; the obedient.
Venerable Titus the Wonderworker.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Zosimas, Abbot of Solovki.life: Venerable Zosimas, Abbot of Solovki, completed the planting that Sabbatius and Herman had begun on the islands of the White Sea, and stands with them as founder of the great monastery at the edge of the habitable world. A Novgorodian who had given away his inheritance for the wilderness, Zosimas met the elder Herman, companion of the reposed.
Venerable Zosimas, Abbot of Solovki.patron: Invoked for island monastics; founders in the uttermost places.
Venerable Zosimas, Abbot of Solovki.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Venerable Zosimas, Abbot of Vorbozomsk.life: Venerable Zosimas of Vorbozomsk belongs to the great dispersal of the northern Thebaid, the generations in which the disciples of the White Lake and Komel elders carried the monastic life outward lake by lake into the wildernesses beyond Belozersk.
Venerable Zosimas, Abbot of Vorbozomsk.patron: Invoked for island monastics; disciples of great elders.
Venerable Zosimas, Abbot of Vorbozomsk.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Virgin Martyrs Agape, Irene and Chionia,.life: The Holy Virgin Martyrs Agape, Irene, and Chionia were three sisters whose contest at Thessalonica in 304 is known to the Church from the very acts of their trial, among the most precious authentic documents of the age of the martyrs.
Virgin Martyrs Agape, Irene and Chionia,.patron: Invoked for sisters; keepers of the Scriptures.
Virgin Martyrs Agape, Irene and Chionia,.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

“Svena” Icon of the Mother of God.life: On this day the Church commemorates the Svena Icon of the Most Holy Theotokos, one of the treasures of the Caves tradition, ascribed by the tradition to the hand of Venerable Alipy of the Kyiv Caves.
“Svena” Icon of the Mother of God.patron: The icon of Alipy carried north.
“Svena” Icon of the Mother of God.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Apostle Alphaeus of the Seventy.life: The Holy Apostle Alphaeus was one of the Seventy whom the Lord chose and sent out before Him, two by two, into every city and place where He Himself would come, and is honored by the Church among that second band of apostles who, after the Twelve, carried the Gospel through the world.
Apostle Alphaeus of the Seventy.patron: The Gospel preached among the first disciples.
Apostle Alphaeus of the Seventy.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Apostle Andronicus of the Seventy and hi.life: The Holy Apostle Andronicus, one of the Seventy, and his fellow-laborer Junia, have their names preserved for the Church by Saint Paul himself, in the greeting of his epistle to the Romans where he writes, Greet Andronicus and Junia my kinsmen and my fellow-prisoners.
Apostle Andronicus of the Seventy and hi.patron: The kinsmen and fellow-prisoners of Paul.
Apostle Andronicus of the Seventy and hi.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Apostle Carpus of the Seventy.life: The Holy Apostle Carpus was one of the Seventy and a companion and helper of the Apostle Paul, and his name is preserved for the Church in the Scriptures by Paul's own hand, in the second epistle to Timothy.
Apostle Carpus of the Seventy.patron: The cloak kept for the Apostle at Troas.
Apostle Carpus of the Seventy.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Apostle Hermas of the Seventy.life: The Holy Apostle Hermas was one of the Seventy, and his name too is kept for the Church in the Scriptures by the hand of Saint Paul, who in the closing greetings of his epistle to the Romans salutes Hermas among the faithful of the Roman church.
Apostle Hermas of the Seventy.patron: The name saluted in the epistle to the Romans.
Apostle Hermas of the Seventy.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Apostle Simon the Zealot.life: The Holy Apostle Simon the Zealot was one of the Twelve chosen by the Lord, called by Saint Matthew the Cananean and by Saint Luke the Zealot, the two names meaning the same thing, for Cananean renders the Aramaic word that the Greek Zealotes translates.
Apostle Simon the Zealot.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Appearance of the Icon of the Mother of.life: On this day the Church commemorates the appearance of the Most Holy Theotokos upon the mountain of Pochaiv, the wonder that founded the great Volhynian Lavra and left in the living rock the print of her foot that the faithful call simply the Footprint.
Appearance of the Icon of the Mother of.patron: The footprint left in the rock.
Appearance of the Icon of the Mother of.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Blessed Dovmont (Timothy), Prince of Psk.life: The Holy Right-believing Prince Dovmont of Pskov, called Timothy from his baptism, was a Lithuanian prince and a pagan who became one of the most beloved rulers and the heavenly protector of a Russian city, his life a parable of the convert's zeal poured out in the defense of his adopted people.
Blessed Dovmont (Timothy), Prince of Psk.patron: The pagan prince made a Christian champion.
Blessed Dovmont (Timothy), Prince of Psk.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Commemoration of the Apparition of the S.life: On this day the Church commemorates the apparition of the sign of the precious Cross in the sky over Jerusalem, in the year 351, under the emperor Constantius, son of Constantine the Great; on the seventh of May, the Tuesday before the feast of the Ascension.
Commemoration of the Apparition of the S.patron: The Cross written across the sky.
Commemoration of the Apparition of the S.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Commemoration of the Founding of Constan.life: On this day the Church commemorates the foundation and dedication of Constantinople, which took place on Monday, the eleventh of May, in the year 330, in the third Indiction; for the great and Christian emperor Constantine.
Commemoration of the Founding of Constan.patron: The New Rome founded under the Cross.
Commemoration of the Founding of Constan.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Commemoration of the Holy Fathers of the.life: On this day the Church commemorates the Holy Fathers of the Second Ecumenical Council, the one hundred and fifty who gathered at Constantinople in the year 381, under the emperor Theodosius the Great.
Commemoration of the Holy Fathers of the.patron: The Creed completed with the article of the Spirit.
Commemoration of the Holy Fathers of the.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Equals of the Apostles and Teachers of t.life: The Holy Equals-to-the-Apostles Cyril and Methodius, Teachers of the Slavs, were brothers of a senatorial family of Thessalonica, the city on the edge of the Slavic world whose streets had taught them the Slavonic tongue from childhood, a providence for the work that awaited them.
Equals of the Apostles and Teachers of t.patron: The alphabet given to the Slavs.
Equals of the Apostles and Teachers of t.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Great Martyr Irene.life: The Holy Great Martyr Irene, one of the most beloved of the women martyrs of the East, was born, the Greek accounts tell, in the city of Magedon, the daughter of a pagan ruler named Licinius, and named Penelope; her father, proud of her beauty.
Great Martyr Irene.patron: The name of Peace earned through wars.
Great Martyr Irene.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Greatmartyr George the New at Sofia, Bul.life: The Holy Great Martyr George the New, who suffered at Sofia, was a young South Slavic Christian of the age of the Turkish yoke, and this day keeps the memory of the taking up and enshrining of his holy relics, which followed soon upon his martyrdom.
Greatmartyr George the New at Sofia, Bul.patron: The eighteen-year-old firm as a diamond.
Greatmartyr George the New at Sofia, Bul.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Hieromartyr Hermogenes, Patriarch of Mos.life: The Holy Hieromartyr Hermogenes, Patriarch of Moscow and All Russia, whose glorification the Church commemorates on this day, was the pastor whose steadfastness in prison saved his country, and whose feast the Russian Church keeps on the date of his glorification as she keeps his repose in February.
Hieromartyr Hermogenes, Patriarch of Mos.patron: The letters that raised the militias.
Hieromartyr Hermogenes, Patriarch of Mos.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Hieromartyr Mocius the Presbyter of Amph.life: The Holy Hieromartyr Mocius was a priest of the church of Amphipolis in Macedonia, or as some accounts place him in Thrace, and suffered at Byzantium in the persecution of Diocletian, about the beginning of the fourth century.
Hieromartyr Mocius the Presbyter of Amph.patron: The temple of the idols cast down.
Hieromartyr Mocius the Presbyter of Amph.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Hieromartyr Patrick, Bishop of Prusa, an.life: The Holy Hieromartyr Patrick, Bishop of Prusa in Bithynia, suffered with his companions the presbyters Acacius, Menander, and Polyenus in the age of the persecutions, and his contest turned upon a bold and beautiful confession made at the famous hot springs of his city.
Hieromartyr Patrick, Bishop of Prusa, an.patron: The Maker of the warm springs and the fire of judgment confessed.
Hieromartyr Patrick, Bishop of Prusa, an.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Hieromartyr Philosophos of St. Petersbur.life: The Holy Hieromartyr Philosophos Ornatsky, archpriest of Saint Petersburg, was one of the first and most eminent of the new martyrs of the Russian Church under the Bolshevik persecution, a renowned pastor of the imperial capital who was martyred together with his two sons at the very dawn of the godless terror.
Hieromartyr Philosophos of St. Petersbur.patron: The faith preached boldly in the capital.
Hieromartyr Philosophos of St. Petersbur.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Hieromartyr Therapon, Bishop of Cyprus.life: The Holy Hieromartyr Therapon, Bishop of Cyprus, was a shepherd of the Church on that island who sealed his ministry with a martyr's death, and whose relics became famous for the healing myrrh that flowed from them.
Hieromartyr Therapon, Bishop of Cyprus.patron: The confession sealed in blood on Cyprus.
Hieromartyr Therapon, Bishop of Cyprus.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Hieromartyr Therapon, Bishop of Sardis.life: The Holy Hieromartyr Therapon, Bishop of Sardis in Lydia, suffered for Christ in the persecutions of the third century, and his passion is adorned by a wonder that turned the very instrument of his torment into a sign of life.
Hieromartyr Therapon, Bishop of Sardis.patron: The dry stake made green by a martyr's blood.
Hieromartyr Therapon, Bishop of Sardis.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Hieromartyr Urban, Pope of Rome.life: The Holy Hieromartyr Urban, Pope of Rome, governed the Church of Rome in the first decades of the third century, in the reign of the emperor Alexander Severus, a shepherd who held the chair of the Apostle Peter through years when to be a Christian.
Hieromartyr Urban, Pope of Rome.patron: The flock of Rome shepherded in the age of blood.
Hieromartyr Urban, Pope of Rome.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Holy Confessor Erasmus, Bishop of Formia.life: The Holy Confessor Erasmus, Bishop of Formia in Campania, began in the East and finished in the West, and between the two ends of his road lay the whole geography of the last persecution.
Holy Confessor Erasmus, Bishop of Formia.patron: The torments outlived and the confession kept.
Holy Confessor Erasmus, Bishop of Formia.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Icon of the Mother of God “the Surety of.life: On this day the Church commemorates the wonderworking Icon of the Most Holy Theotokos called the Surety of Sinners, whose very name is a theology and a comfort, for the image bears the inscription by which the Mother of God declares herself the surety, the pledge and guarantor.
Icon of the Mother of God “the Surety of.patron: The Mother of God pledged as surety for sinners.
Icon of the Mother of God “the Surety of.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Icon of the Mother of God of Mt. Athos,.life: On this day the Church commemorates the wonderworking icon of the Most Holy Theotokos called Glykophilousa, the Sweet Kissing, one of the treasures of the Philotheou monastery on Mount Athos and one of the most tender of all her images.
Icon of the Mother of God of Mt. Athos,.patron: The icon saved from the iconoclasts by the sea.
Icon of the Mother of God of Mt. Athos,.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Inexhastible Chalice Icon of the Mother.life: On this day the Church commemorates the Inexhaustible Chalice Icon of the Most Holy Theotokos, glorified at Serpukhov in 1878 and given by God, with a directness the age required.
Inexhastible Chalice Icon of the Mother.patron: The cup that does not run dry.
Inexhastible Chalice Icon of the Mother.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Martyr Acacius the Centurion at Byzantiu.life: The Holy Martyr Acacius the Centurion suffered at Byzantium in the year 303, in the first fury of Diocletian's persecution, and his memory belonged afterward to the very fabric of the city that would become Constantinople.
Martyr Acacius the Centurion at Byzantiu.patron: The thanksgiving offered at the block.
Martyr Acacius the Centurion at Byzantiu.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Martyr Asclas of Egypt.life: The Holy Martyr Asclas suffered for Christ in the city of Antinoe in the Thebaid of Egypt, in the persecutions at the turn of the fourth century, and his contest is remembered for the wonder by which he forced his own judge to confess the truth.
Martyr Asclas of Egypt.patron: The governor's boat halted on the Nile.
Martyr Asclas of Egypt.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Martyr Barbarus the Soldier, and those w.life: The Holy Martyr Barbarus the Soldier suffered with his companions Bacchus, Callimachus, and Dionysius in the days of Julian the Apostate, about the year 362, and his contest turned on the oldest trap laid for the Christian soldier, the sacrifice of victory.
Martyr Barbarus the Soldier, and those w.patron: The single combat won and the greater combat chosen.
Martyr Barbarus the Soldier, and those w.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Martyr Basiliscus, Bishop of Comana.life: The Holy Martyr Basiliscus suffered near Comana in Pontus in the persecution of the emperor Maximian, about the year 308, and was a kinsman, the tradition holds a nephew, of the Great Martyr Theodore the Recruit.
Martyr Basiliscus, Bishop of Comana.patron: The confession kept after his companions' crowns.
Martyr Basiliscus, Bishop of Comana.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Martyr Christopher of Lycia, and, with h.life: The Holy Great Martyr Christopher suffered in Lycia under the emperor Decius, about the year 250, and the Church has loved him for seventeen centuries as the patron of travelers and the standing rebuke to every judgment by appearances.
Martyr Christopher of Lycia, and, with h.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Martyr Heliconis of Thessalonica.life: The Holy Virgin Martyr Heliconis was a native of Thessalonica who suffered for Christ at Corinth in the third century, in the reign of the emperor Gordian and, the accounts continue, of Aurelian after him.
Martyr Heliconis of Thessalonica.patron: The temple of Athena cast down at her prayer.
Martyr Heliconis of Thessalonica.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Martyr Hermias at Comana.life: The Holy Martyr Hermias was an aged soldier who suffered for Christ at Comana in Cappadocia in the reign of the emperor Antoninus, in the second century, and his passion is a chronicle of torments miraculously survived until God willed to receive him.
Martyr Hermias at Comana.patron: The old soldier steadfast under every cruelty.
Martyr Hermias at Comana.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Martyr Laodicius the Keeper of the Priso.life: The Holy Martyr Laodicius was the keeper of the prison in which the virgin martyr Glyceria was confined at Heraclea in Thrace, and his conversion and crown were the fruit of the angel's visit to her cell.
Martyr Laodicius the Keeper of the Priso.patron: The angel's healing believed and confessed.
Martyr Laodicius the Keeper of the Priso.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Martyr Meletius Stratelates who suffered.life: The Holy Martyr Meletius the General, called Stratelates, suffered with a great host of companions in Galatia of Asia Minor in the reign of the emperor Antoninus Pius, in the second century, and his passion is one of the calendar's great mass martyrdoms, a whole command crowned together.
Martyr Meletius Stratelates who suffered.patron: The demons driven from the temples.
Martyr Meletius Stratelates who suffered.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Martyr Philosophus at Alexandria.life: The Holy Martyr Philosophus suffered for Christ at Alexandria in the persecution of the emperor Decius, about the year 250, and his contest was of a rare and terrible kind, a battle not against the sword but against the flesh, in which he conquered by turning his own pain against his tempters.
Martyr Philosophus at Alexandria.patron: The temptation of the flesh conquered by a wound.
Martyr Philosophus at Alexandria.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Martyr Theodotus of Ancyra, and with him.life: The Holy Martyr Theodotus and the seven holy Virgins Alexandra, Tecusa, Claudia, Phaine, Euphrasia, Matrona, and Julia suffered at Ancyra in Galatia in the great persecution at the turn of the fourth century, and their linked story is one of the most moving in the calendar.
Martyr Theodotus of Ancyra, and with him.patron: The relics of the martyrs rescued and buried.
Martyr Theodotus of Ancyra, and with him.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Martyr Timothy the Reader and his wife,.life: The Holy Martyrs Timothy and Maura, husband and wife, suffered in the Thebaid of Egypt in the great persecution, in the year 304 as the Melkite synaxarion counts, or about 286 as some books reckon, and their contest is the Church's most tender portrait of marriage perfected in blood.
Martyr Timothy the Reader and his wife,.patron: The books refused to the fire.
Martyr Timothy the Reader and his wife,.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Martyrs Heraclius, Paulinus, and Benedim.life: The Holy Martyrs Heraclius, Paulinus, and Benedimus suffered for Christ at Noviodunum in Scythia Minor, the fortress town on the lower Danube in the land that is now Romania, and are joined in the calendar of this day to the martyrs Peter, Dionysius.
Martyrs Heraclius, Paulinus, and Benedim.patron: The faith confessed at the empire's northern edge.
Martyrs Heraclius, Paulinus, and Benedim.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Martyrs Isidore and Myrope of Chios.life: The Holy Martyr Isidore of Chios, a native of Alexandria in Egypt, suffered on the island of Chios under the emperor Decius, about the year 251, and his passion joined a soldier's confession to a woman's fidelity.
Martyrs Isidore and Myrope of Chios.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Martyrs Peter, Dionysius, Andrew, Paul,.life: The Holy Martyrs Peter, Dionysius, Andrew, Paul, and Christina suffered for Christ in the persecution of the emperor Decius, about the middle of the third century, and are commemorated together on this day, though the tradition places their sufferings in more than one city of the East, Peter.
Martyrs Peter, Dionysius, Andrew, Paul,.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Martyrs Philadelphus, Cyprian, Alphius,.life: The Holy Martyrs Alphius, Philadelphus, and Cyprian, three brothers, suffered with their teacher Onesimus, with Erasmus, and with fourteen others in the persecution of Decius, about the year 251, and their contest joined the two ends of the Christian Mediterranean, beginning in southern Italy and ending in Sicily.
Martyrs Philadelphus, Cyprian, Alphius,.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Martyrs Simeon, Isaac and Bachtisius, of.life: The Holy Martyrs Simeon, Isaac, and Bachtisius suffered for Christ in Persia, among the great host of martyrs whom the Church of the Persian empire gave to God in the fourth century, when the Zoroastrian power.
Martyrs Simeon, Isaac and Bachtisius, of.patron: Christ confessed against the worship of fire.
Martyrs Simeon, Isaac and Bachtisius, of.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Martyrs Solochon, Pamphamer, and Pamphal.life: The Holy Martyrs Solochon, Pamphamer, and Pamphalon were soldiers, Egyptians by birth, serving in the Roman army at Chalcedon in Bithynia in the reign of the emperor Maximian, at the turn of the fourth century, and they suffered together for refusing the sacrifice that the persecution made the test of a soldier's loyalty.
Martyrs Solochon, Pamphamer, and Pamphal.patron: The sacrifice refused before the tribune.
Martyrs Solochon, Pamphamer, and Pamphal.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Meeting of the Vladimir Icon of the Moth.life: On this day the Church commemorates one of the three great feasts of the Vladimir Icon of the Most Holy Theotokos, the protectress of the Russian land, established in thanksgiving for the deliverance of Moscow from the Tatar invasion of the year 1521.
Meeting of the Vladimir Icon of the Moth.patron: Moscow delivered from the Tatar without a battle.
Meeting of the Vladimir Icon of the Moth.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Monastic Martyr Paul of the Lavra, Mount.life: The Monastic Martyr Paul of the Lavra on Mount Athos is commemorated by the Church on this day as one of her saints, though of the particulars of his life and contest the record has not come down, and the common books confess plainly that no account of him survives.
Monastic Martyr Paul of the Lavra, Mount.patron: The crown won and the account unwritten.
Monastic Martyr Paul of the Lavra, Mount.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

New Martyr Archpriest Vasily Martysz.life: The Holy New Martyr Archpriest Vasily Martysz spanned in one life the Orthodox worlds of Alaska and Poland, and sealed both with a Holy Friday death.
New Martyr Archpriest Vasily Martysz.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

New Martyr Ephraim.life: The Holy Hieromartyr Ephraim of Nea Makri, the Newly Revealed, was hidden by God for five hundred years and given to the Church in her modern need, and his life is therefore told from both its ends.
New Martyr Ephraim.patron: The eight months of torments endured.
New Martyr Ephraim.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

New Martyr Euthymius of Mount Athos.life: The Holy New Martyr Euthymius of Mount Athos, commemorated this day in the common synaxis of the three new martyrs of the Skete of the Forerunner, was born at Demetsana in the Peloponnese, the mountain town that gave the Greek nation so many of its priests and martyrs.
New Martyr Euthymius of Mount Athos.patron: The apostasy of youth washed in blood.
New Martyr Euthymius of Mount Athos.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

New Martyr Ignatius the Martyr of Mount.life: The Holy New Martyr Ignatius of Mount Athos, commemorated this day with Euthymius and Acacius in the synaxis of the three new martyrs of the Forerunner Skete, was born John at Stara Zagora in Bulgaria.
New Martyr Ignatius the Martyr of Mount.patron: The promise extorted by fear unsaid in blood.
New Martyr Ignatius the Martyr of Mount.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Prophet Isaiah.life: The Holy Prophet Isaiah, first in rank of the great prophets and called by the fathers the fifth evangelist, was the son of Amoz, of the royal stock of Judah as the tradition holds, and received his commission in the year that king Uzziah died.
Prophet Isaiah.patron: The Lord beheld high and lifted up.
Prophet Isaiah.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Prophet Jeremiah.life: The Holy Prophet Jeremiah, second in rank of the great prophets, was the son of Hilkiah, of the priestly line, from the city of Anathoth in the land of Benjamin, and was called by God as hardly more than a child, protesting that he could not speak.
Prophet Jeremiah.patron: The word like fire shut up in the bones.
Prophet Jeremiah.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Repose of Saint Alexis Toth, Confessor a.life: Saint Alexis Toth, Confessor and Defender of Orthodoxy in America, accomplished by one closed door what committees never accomplish by a hundred open ones.
Repose of Saint Alexis Toth, Confessor a.patron: The door shut at Minneapolis and the greater door opened.
Repose of Saint Alexis Toth, Confessor a.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Repose of the Blessed John of Ustiug the.life: Blessed John of Ustyug, fool for Christ, was an ascetic of the northern city of Veliky Ustyug who took up the hardest and most hidden of the ways of holiness, the folly for Christ's sake, and practiced it from his very childhood.
Repose of the Blessed John of Ustiug the.patron: The folly feigned to hide the fasting and the vigils.
Repose of the Blessed John of Ustiug the.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Repose of Venerable Nilus, Abbot of Sora.life: Venerable Nilus of Sora, the great teacher of the skete life and of the prayer of the heart in Russia, was born Nicholas Maikov about 1433, of Moscow, and tonsured at the Kirillo-Belozersk monastery, the strictest school of the north; and his formation was completed abroad.
Repose of Venerable Nilus, Abbot of Sora.patron: The skete way planted in Russia.
Repose of Venerable Nilus, Abbot of Sora.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Repose of Venerable Shio the Anchorite o.life: Venerable Shio of Mgvime, the Anchorite, one of the Thirteen Syrian Fathers who planted monasticism in Georgia, came from Antioch in the sixth century as a disciple of Saint John of Zedazeni, in the company that the Georgian Church reveres as her desert's founding constellation.
Repose of Venerable Shio the Anchorite o.patron: The dove that brought his bread.
Repose of Venerable Shio the Anchorite o.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Right-believing John, Prince of Uglich,.life: The Holy Right-believing Prince John of Uglich, tonsured before his death as Ignatius, was a devout and God-fearing Christian from his youth who was given by the world a lot of pure injustice and turned it, by grace, into a hidden sanctity.
Right-believing John, Prince of Uglich,.patron: The thirty-two years of prison borne without bitterness.
Right-believing John, Prince of Uglich,.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Righteous Job the Long-Suffering.life: The Holy and Righteous Job the Long-Suffering, whose memory the Church keeps on this day, dwelt in the land of Uz, which the tradition locates in the Hauran east of Jordan, and the ancient reckoning preserved in the Greek Scriptures counts him of the lineage of Esau.
Righteous Job the Long-Suffering.patron: The patience that argued and still blessed.
Righteous Job the Long-Suffering.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Righteous Virgin Glykerίa of Novgorod.life: The Righteous Virgin Glykeria of Novgorod was so hidden a saint that the very scarcity of what is known about her is her portrait, the sign that she kept her ascetic struggles concealed from all around her, hiding her holiness in the crowd of a great city as others hid theirs in the desert.
Righteous Virgin Glykerίa of Novgorod.patron: The life so hidden that only heaven kept the account.
Righteous Virgin Glykerίa of Novgorod.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Saint Athanasius of Lubensk, Patriarch o.life: Saint Athanasius Patellarios, Patriarch of Constantinople, called of Lubensk from the place of his repose, and known among the faithful as Athanasius the Seated for the unique enthronement of his relics, was born Alexios at Rethymnon in Crete about 1597, of a distinguished family.
Saint Athanasius of Lubensk, Patriarch o.patron: The ecumenical throne held in poverty.
Saint Athanasius of Lubensk, Patriarch o.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Saint Athanasius the Great, Patriarch of.life: On this day the Church keeps the memory of the repose and the translation of the relics of Saint Athanasius the Great, Patriarch of Alexandria, the pillar of Orthodoxy, whose principal feast she celebrates in January with Saint Cyril; and the May commemoration.
Saint Athanasius the Great, Patriarch of.patron: The Homoousios held against the world.
Saint Athanasius the Great, Patriarch of.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Saint Emmeleίa.life: Saint Emmeleia was the mother of Saint Basil the Great, and of a whole household of saints, and is honored by the Church as the very type of the Christian mother, she who raised for God not one saint but many.
Saint Emmeleίa.patron: The household that gave the Church a multitude of saints.
Saint Emmeleίa.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Saint Epiphanius, Bishop of Cyprus.life: Saint Epiphanius of Cyprus, one of the great fathers and teachers of the fourth century, was born about the year 315 at Besanduc, a small town of Palestine near Eleutheropolis, and embraced the monastic life under the direction of Saint Hilarion the Great, the founder of Palestinian monasticism.
Saint Epiphanius, Bishop of Cyprus.patron: The eighty heresies refuted in the Panarion.
Saint Epiphanius, Bishop of Cyprus.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Saint Euphrosynē, Great Princess of Mosc.life: Saint Euphrosyne of Moscow, in the world Eudokia, whose name meant good will and whose monastic name means joy, was a grand princess who wore a crown over a hair shirt and hid a desert's asceticism beneath the robes of a sovereign.
Saint Euphrosynē, Great Princess of Mosc.patron: The crown worn over the hidden chains.
Saint Euphrosynē, Great Princess of Mosc.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Saint Eutychius, Bishop of Melitene.life: Saint Eutychius, Bishop of Melitene in Armenia Minor, was one of the early shepherds of the Church in Asia Minor, honored among those pastors of the first Christian generations who received the faith close to its apostolic source and handed it on.
Saint Eutychius, Bishop of Melitene.patron: The faith received from the apostles' disciples.
Saint Eutychius, Bishop of Melitene.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Saint Germanus, Patriarch of Constantino.life: Saint Germanus, Patriarch of Constantinople, was a confessor of the holy icons who preferred to lay down his throne rather than lend it to heresy, and the Church honors him both as a hierarch and as one of her hymnographers.
Saint Germanus, Patriarch of Constantino.patron: The omophorion laid on the altar in protest.
Saint Germanus, Patriarch of Constantino.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Saint Ignatius the Wonderworker, Bishop.life: Saint Ignatius, Bishop of Rostov, the Wonderworker, shepherded the Church of Rostov through the hard middle decades of the thirteenth century, in the depths of the Tatar yoke, and is remembered for the singular honor God gave him.
Saint Ignatius the Wonderworker, Bishop.patron: The see of Rostov shepherded through the Tatar yoke.
Saint Ignatius the Wonderworker, Bishop.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Saint Isaiah the Wonderworker, Bishop of.life: Saint Isaiah, Bishop of Rostov, the Wonderworker, was one of the company of the Kyiv Caves who carried the light of that monastery out to the raw frontiers of the newly-baptized land, and he labored in a see where Christianity was still contending with paganism.
Saint Isaiah the Wonderworker, Bishop of.patron: The pagan remnants of the Rostov land brought to Christ.
Saint Isaiah the Wonderworker, Bishop of.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Saint John the Russian and Confessor, wh.life: The Holy Confessor John the Russian was born about the year 1690 in Little Russia, in the lands of modern Ukraine, of pious Orthodox parents.
Saint John the Russian and Confessor, wh.patron: Christ confessed through years of slavery.
Saint John the Russian and Confessor, wh.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Saint John-Vladimir, Prince of Bulgaria,.life: The Holy Prince John Vladimir of Dioclea, great-martyr and wonderworker, was one of the first saints of the Serbian lands and a rare example of a ruler sainted for the holiness of his reign and the innocence of his death.
Saint John-Vladimir, Prince of Bulgaria,.patron: The prince who ruled in righteousness and peace.
Saint John-Vladimir, Prince of Bulgaria,.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Saint Matrona of Moscow.life: Blessed Matrona of Moscow, the sightless eldress who became the seeing eye of Orthodox Russia through the darkest half century of her history, was born Matrona Nikonova in 1881 in the village of Sebino in the Tula country, the fourth child of poor and pious peasants.
Saint Matrona of Moscow.patron: The sight given to the sightless.
Saint Matrona of Moscow.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Saint Michael the Confessor, Bishop of S.life: Saint Michael the Confessor, Bishop of Synnada in Phrygia, was a hierarch, an ambassador, and a confessor of the holy icons, spending his gifts in the service of the Church and the empire and his sufferings in defense of the images of Christ.
Saint Michael the Confessor, Bishop of S.patron: The icons defended against the emperor.
Saint Michael the Confessor, Bishop of S.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Saint Niketas, Bishop of Chalcedon.life: Saint Niketas the Confessor, Bishop of Chalcedon, was a hierarch of the early ninth century, renowned both for his mercy to the poor and for his steadfast confession of the holy icons in the second outbreak of the iconoclast heresy.
Saint Niketas, Bishop of Chalcedon.patron: The icons defended against the emperor.
Saint Niketas, Bishop of Chalcedon.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Saint Nikḗtas, Bishop of Novgorod, Reclu.life: Saint Nikita, Bishop of Novgorod, recluse of the Kyiv Caves, is the Church's great cautionary and consoling example of the soul deceived and restored, and his memory is kept on this day at Novgorod, where his relics rest, as it is kept in January at his repose and in April at their uncovering.
Saint Nikḗtas, Bishop of Novgorod, Reclu.patron: The recluse deceived by the angel of light and saved.
Saint Nikḗtas, Bishop of Novgorod, Reclu.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Saint Peter the Wonderworker, Bishop of.life: Saint Peter the Wonderworker, Bishop of Argos, came of a Constantinopolitan family that gave itself to God almost entire, his parents and brothers embracing the monastic life and Peter with them, a household dissolving into the angelic estate; and his gifts made him hunted for the episcopate.
Saint Peter the Wonderworker, Bishop of.patron: The grain multiplied in the hunger.
Saint Peter the Wonderworker, Bishop of.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Saint Simon, Bishop of Vladimir and Suzd.life: Saint Simon, Bishop of Vladimir and Suzdal, was a monk of the Kyiv Caves before he was a hierarch, and he loved the monastery of his tonsure so entirely that he made it, in a single letter, the subject of one of the foundational texts of Russian spiritual literature.
Saint Simon, Bishop of Vladimir and Suzd.patron: The Paterik of the Caves begun by his pen.
Saint Simon, Bishop of Vladimir and Suzd.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Saint Stephen, Archbishop of Constantino.life: Saint Stephen, Archbishop of Constantinople, was a son of the imperial house given to the service of the altar, and governed the first see of the East in a brief and peaceful patriarchate at the end of the ninth century.
Saint Stephen, Archbishop of Constantino.patron: The imperial son given to the sanctuary.
Saint Stephen, Archbishop of Constantino.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Saint Vincent of Lerins.life: Saint Vincent of Lérins was a monk and teacher of the fifth century, of the famous island monastery of Lérins off the coast of Gaul, and one of the great fathers of the undivided Church of the West.
Saint Vincent of Lerins.patron: The rule of catholicity, what is believed everywhere, always, and by all.
Saint Vincent of Lerins.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

St Theodosius of the Kyiv Caves.life: Venerable Theodosius of the Kyiv Caves, father of the common monastic life in the land of Rus', was born at Vasyliv near Kyiv and raised at Kursk, and fought his first ascetic war against his own mother.
St Theodosius of the Kyiv Caves.patron: The common life planted in the Rus' earth.
St Theodosius of the Kyiv Caves.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Synaxis of the Saints of Rostov.life: On this day the Church keeps the Synaxis of the Saints of Rostov and Yaroslavl, gathering into one joyful commemoration the whole choir of the saints who enlightened and adorned that ancient region of the Russian land.
Synaxis of the Saints of Rostov.patron: The whole choir of a region's saints gathered in one feast.
Synaxis of the Saints of Rostov.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

The Holy Right-believing Tsarevich Demet.life: The Holy Right-believing Tsarevich Demetrius of Uglich, passion-bearer, was the youngest son of Tsar Ivan the Terrible, born at Moscow in 1582 of the tsar's last wife Maria Nagaya, and after his father's death and the accession of his feeble half-brother Fyodor.
The Holy Right-believing Tsarevich Demet.patron: The innocent blood shed at Uglich.
The Holy Right-believing Tsarevich Demet.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Third Finding of the Honorable Head of t.life: On this day the Church commemorates the Third Finding of the honorable head of the holy and glorious Prophet, Forerunner, and Baptist John, the last of the three recoveries by which the Lord preserved and gave back to His Church the sacred relic of the greatest born of women.
Third Finding of the Honorable Head of t.patron: The head of the Baptist found a third time.
Third Finding of the Honorable Head of t.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Translation of the relics of Saint Nicho.life: On this day the Church commemorates the translation of the relics of Saint Nicholas the Wonderworker, Archbishop of Myra in Lycia, from Myra to the city of Bari in Italy, in the year 1087, the feast the Russian people came to call the spring Nicholas and to love scarcely less than his December memory.
Translation of the relics of Saint Nicho.patron: The wonderworker carried west before the storm.
Translation of the relics of Saint Nicho.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Translation of the Relics of the Holy Pa.life: On this day the Church commemorates the translation of the relics of the Holy Passion-bearers Borys and Hlib, in holy baptism Romanus and David, the first saints glorified by the land of Rus', whose principal memory she keeps in July; sons of Equal-to-the-Apostles Vladimir.
Translation of the Relics of the Holy Pa.patron: The brothers enthroned by their people.
Translation of the Relics of the Holy Pa.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Translation of the relics of Venerable E.life: On this day the Church commemorates the translation of the relics of Venerable Ephraim, Abbot of Perekop and Wonderworker of Novgorod, a translation that took place in the year 1545 and was confirmed as a feast by the Moscow Council of 1549.
Translation of the relics of Venerable E.patron: The canal dug through to the lake.
Translation of the relics of Venerable E.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Translation of the relics of Venerable N.life: On this day the Church commemorates the uncovering and translation of the relics of Venerable Nilus of Stolobensk, the great hermit of Lake Seliger, which took place in the year 1667, more than a century after his repose.
Translation of the relics of Venerable N.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Uncovering of the relics of Saint Alexis.life: On this day the Church commemorates the uncovering of the relics of Saint Alexis, Metropolitan of Moscow and Wonderworker of All Russia, the great hierarch and statesman who guided the Russian Church and the Muscovite state through the middle of the fourteenth century.
Uncovering of the relics of Saint Alexis.patron: The incorrupt relics revealed by a falling roof.
Uncovering of the relics of Saint Alexis.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Uncovering of the relics of Venerable Ja.life: On this day the Church keeps the second memory of Venerable James of Zheleznoborov, the commemoration of the uncovering of his relics, joined in the calendar to his principal feast of April; the disciple whom Saint Sergius of Radonezh himself tonsured.
Uncovering of the relics of Venerable Ja.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Uncovering of the relics of Venerable Ma.life: On this day the Church commemorates the uncovering of the relics of Venerable Macarius, Abbot of Kalyazin, one of the founders of the monastic life on the upper Volga, whose incorrupt body was revealed in the year 1521, some four decades after his repose.
Uncovering of the relics of Venerable Ma.patron: The Trinity monastery of Kalyazin founded.
Uncovering of the relics of Venerable Ma.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Unmercenary Physician Thallelaios at Aeg.life: The Holy Martyr Thallelaios, an unmercenary physician, suffered at Aegae in Cilicia with his companions Alexander and Asterius under the emperor Numerian, about the year 284, and his passion is adorned with wonders that spared his body until God willed to take it.
Unmercenary Physician Thallelaios at Aeg.patron: The healing art offered to Christ.
Unmercenary Physician Thallelaios at Aeg.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Venerable Alphan, with his brothers, of.life: The Righteous Alphanov brothers of Novgorod, Nikita, Kirill, Nikifor, Kliment, and Isaac, are commemorated on this day as the founders of the Sokolnitsky monastery, and their sanctity is of the kind the Church delights to point out precisely because it required no singularity, five brothers of one Novgorod family who agreed together upon God.
Venerable Alphan, with his brothers, of.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Venerable Arsenius the Great.life: Venerable Arsenius the Great, the most august fugitive in the history of the desert, was born of a patrician family at Rome, raised in all learning sacred and profane, and elevated by the emperor Theodosius to the imperial court at Constantinople.
Venerable Arsenius the Great.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Venerable Arsenius the Lover-of-Labor of.life: Venerable Arsenius the Lover-of-Labor, of the Kyiv Far Caves, lived in the fourteenth century and carried in his title the whole of his ascetic doctrine, for the fathers of the Caves, surveying his life, judged that its distinguishing grace was labor, and fixed the word to his name.
Venerable Arsenius the Lover-of-Labor of.patron: The hands that never rested from work or prayer.
Venerable Arsenius the Lover-of-Labor of.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Venerable Cassian the Greek of Uglich.life: Venerable Cassian the Greek of Uglich was a nobleman of the Byzantine world who exchanged the rank of a prince for the habit of a monk and became a wonderworker of the Russian north, and his memory is fittingly kept on the feast of Saint Constantine the Great.
Venerable Cassian the Greek of Uglich.patron: The Greek prince become a Russian monk.
Venerable Cassian the Greek of Uglich.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Venerable Cassian, Abbot of Komel (Volog.life: Saint Cassian of Komel and Vologda was a disciple of Saint Cornelius of Komel, the great founder whose monastery in the Vologda forests became one of the schools of northern Russian monasticism, and Cassian's sanctity is of the kind that consists in perfect fidelity to a master.
Venerable Cassian, Abbot of Komel (Volog.patron: The rule of Cornelius kept without change.
Venerable Cassian, Abbot of Komel (Volog.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Venerable Constantine, (in baptism Yaros.life: The Holy Right-believing Prince Constantine of Murom, called Yaroslav in baptism, with his sons Michael and Theodore, was the enlightener of the city of Murom, and his family's labor to convert a stubborn pagan people cost the blood of a child before it bore its fruit.
Venerable Constantine, (in baptism Yaros.patron: The pagan city of Murom asked for and won for Christ.
Venerable Constantine, (in baptism Yaros.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Venerable Cornelius, Abbot of Komel, Vol.life: Venerable Cornelius of Komel was one of the great founders and lawgivers of the northern Russian monasticism that filled the Vologda forests with houses of prayer in the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries, the region the historians came to call the northern Thebaid.
Venerable Cornelius, Abbot of Komel, Vol.patron: The desert of Komel made a city of monks.
Venerable Cornelius, Abbot of Komel, Vol.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
