Venerable Cornelius, Abbot of Paleostrov.life: Venerable Cornelius of Paleostrov and Olonets was a founder of monastic life in the far northern lakelands of Russia, carrying the desert into the cold islands of Lake Onega at the end of the fourteenth century.
Venerable Cornelius, Abbot of Paleostrov.patron: The desolate island made a house of prayer.
Venerable Cornelius, Abbot of Paleostrov.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Venerable Dionysius, Archimandrite of Sa.life: Venerable Dionysius of Radonezh, archimandrite of the Trinity-Sergius Lavra, was, with the Patriarch Hermogenes, one of the two great churchmen whose patriotic labors delivered Russia from the Time of Troubles, and his memory is fittingly kept on the day of Hermogenes' glorification, the two fellow-strugglers joined in the calendar as they were joined in the work.
Venerable Dionysius, Archimandrite of Sa.patron: The Lavra's letters that raised the nation.
Venerable Dionysius, Archimandrite of Sa.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Venerable Euphrosyne, Abbess of Polotsk.life: Saint Euphrosyne of Polotsk, named Predslava in the world, was a princess of the house of Polotsk, the daughter of Prince George Vseslavich and a descendant of the line of Saint Vladimir, and she became the great enlightener of the Belarusian land and one of the most luminous women of the whole Russian Church.
Venerable Euphrosyne, Abbess of Polotsk.patron: The royal maiden who chose the veil over the crown.
Venerable Euphrosyne, Abbess of Polotsk.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Venerable Isaac, Founder of Dalmátos Mon.life: Venerable Isaac, founder of the Dalmatos monastery at Constantinople, was a confessor who feared the face of no emperor, and is remembered above all for his fearless rebuke of the Arian emperor Valens and his prophecy of that emperor's terrible end.
Venerable Isaac, Founder of Dalmátos Mon.patron: The Arian emperor rebuked to his face.
Venerable Isaac, Founder of Dalmátos Mon.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Venerable Isaiah, Wonderworker of the Ky.life: Venerable Isaiah the Wonderworker, of the Kyiv Near Caves, labored in the great monastery in the late eleventh and early twelfth centuries and reposed, the tradition records, about the year 1115, and his memory is kept on this day, which he shares with his namesake Isaiah of Rostov.
Venerable Isaiah, Wonderworker of the Ky.patron: The labors of the Caves offered to God.
Venerable Isaiah, Wonderworker of the Ky.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Venerable Isidore the Fool-For-Christ an.life: Blessed Isidore Tverdislov, Fool-for-Christ and Wonderworker of Rostov, came to Russia and to sanctity from the Latin West, one of the calendar's reminders that the folly for Christ knew no single nation.
Venerable Isidore the Fool-For-Christ an.patron: The wealth of a foreign house left for a hut of brushwood.
Venerable Isidore the Fool-For-Christ an.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Venerable Laurence, Abbot of Komel.life: Saint Laurence of Komel was, like Saint Cassian with whom the Church commemorates him this day, a disciple of Saint Cornelius of Komel, and he carried on the work of governing the Vologda monastery in the spirit and the rule of their common teacher.
Venerable Laurence, Abbot of Komel.patron: The lineage of Cornelius carried on.
Venerable Laurence, Abbot of Komel.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Venerable Macarius, Archimandrite of Ovr.life: On this day the Church commemorates the translation of the relics of the Hieromartyr Macarius, Archimandrite of Ovruch and Pinsk, whose principal feast falls in September and whose martyrdom crowned a life spent holding his people in the Orthodox faith through the storms of the seventeenth century.
Venerable Macarius, Archimandrite of Ovr.patron: The flock of Ovruch and Pinsk kept in the faith.
Venerable Macarius, Archimandrite of Ovr.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Venerable Micah, disciple of Venerable S.life: Venerable Micah of Radonezh was the cell-attendant of Saint Sergius, and his whole biography is a single night, prepared for by a lifetime of littleness.
Venerable Micah, disciple of Venerable S.patron: The visitation of the Theotokos beheld.
Venerable Micah, disciple of Venerable S.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Venerable Niketas the Stylite, Wonderwor.life: Venerable Nikita the Stylite of Pereyaslavl-Zalessky was a great sinner made a great saint, one of the Church's most vivid examples of the power of a single word of Scripture to break and remake a hardened heart.
Venerable Niketas the Stylite, Wonderwor.patron: The extortioner's heart broken by the prophet's word.
Venerable Niketas the Stylite, Wonderwor.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Venerable Pachomius the Great, Founder o.life: Venerable Pachomius the Great, the father of cenobitic monasticism, was born of pagan parents about the year 292 in the Upper Thebaid of Egypt, and came to Christ by the road of a soldier.
Venerable Pachomius the Great, Founder o.patron: The common life given its first written rule.
Venerable Pachomius the Great, Founder o.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Venerable Paisius, Abbot of Galich.life: Venerable Paisius of Galich was an abbot of the Dormition monastery in the town of Galich, in the Kostroma land, in the fifteenth century, and his memory is bound up with the wonderworking Ovinov Icon of the Mother of God that was the treasure of his house.
Venerable Paisius, Abbot of Galich.patron: The Dormition monastery of Galich shepherded.
Venerable Paisius, Abbot of Galich.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Venerable Paphnutius, Abbot of Borov.life: Venerable Paphnutius, Abbot of Borovsk, carried in his blood the Church's answer to the Tatar yoke, for his grandfather had been a Tatar baskak, a tax officer of the conquerors over the Russian land, who came to faith and was baptized Martin.
Venerable Paphnutius, Abbot of Borov.patron: The Tatar line grafted into sanctity.
Venerable Paphnutius, Abbot of Borov.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Venerable Pimen the Ascetic of the Kyiv.life: Venerable Pimen the Ascetic, of the Kyiv Caves, called in the tradition the Faster, lived in the twelfth century, in the Lavra's heroic age, and won his place in the calendar by the oldest and most unglamorous of the ascetic arts, the mastery of the appetite.
Venerable Pimen the Ascetic of the Kyiv.patron: The fast kept as a lifelong feast.
Venerable Pimen the Ascetic of the Kyiv.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Venerable Simeon Stylites the Younger of.life: Venerable Simeon the Stylite the Younger, of the Wonderful Mountain, renewed in his own generation the astonishing ascesis of the first great stylite, and spent almost his whole life upon a pillar, from his boyhood to his death in extreme old age.
Venerable Simeon Stylites the Younger of.patron: The pillar kept from boyhood to old age.
Venerable Simeon Stylites the Younger of.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Venerable Sophronius the Recluse of the.life: Venerable Sophronius the Recluse, of the Kyiv Far Caves, lived in the thirteenth century, in the age when the Caves monastery, already the mother of Russian monasticism, was passing through the fire of the Mongol devastation of Kyiv.
Venerable Sophronius the Recluse of the.patron: The enclosure kept for God alone.
Venerable Sophronius the Recluse of the.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Venerable Theodore the Sanctified, disci.life: Saint Theodore the Sanctified was the disciple and emulator of Saint Pachomius the Great in the way of monastic perfection, and reposed in the fourth century, in the first flowering of the cenobitic life along the Nile; and his surname carries the whole account of his holiness.
Venerable Theodore the Sanctified, disci.patron: The perfection learned at Pachomius' side.
Venerable Theodore the Sanctified, disci.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Venerable Theodosius, Abbot of the Kyiv.life: Venerable Theodosius, Abbot of the Kyiv Far Caves Monastery, commemorated under this title on this day, is one and the same father as Venerable Theodosius of the Kyiv Caves.
Venerable Theodosius, Abbot of the Kyiv.patron: The one father of the Caves honored under every style.
Venerable Theodosius, Abbot of the Kyiv.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Venerable Therapon, Abbot of White Lake.life: Venerable Ferapont of White Lake and Mozhaisk was a founder of monasteries in the northern forests of Russia and the friend and fellow-laborer of Saint Cyril of White Lake, and his life is a testimony to the fruitfulness of holy friendship in the monastic work.
Venerable Therapon, Abbot of White Lake.patron: The Ferapontov monastery founded by the White Lake.
Venerable Therapon, Abbot of White Lake.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Virgin Martyr Glyceria at Heraclea.life: The Holy Virgin Martyr Glyceria, whose name means sweetness, suffered at Heraclea in Thrace under the emperor Antoninus, in the middle of the second century, and now, as the Church sings, rejoices in the unending sweetness of the Kingdom.
Virgin Martyr Glyceria at Heraclea.patron: The cross traced on the brow before the idol.
Virgin Martyr Glyceria at Heraclea.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Virgin Martyr Pelagia of Tarsus, in Asia.life: The Holy Virgin Martyr Pelagia of Tarsus was sought by grace before she sought it: a maiden of noble family in Cilicia at the turn of the fourth century, she had heard of the Christian faith and sincerely desired to know its teaching.
Virgin Martyr Pelagia of Tarsus, in Asia.patron: The baptism sought through a dream.
Virgin Martyr Pelagia of Tarsus, in Asia.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

Virgin Martyr Theodosia the Nun of Const.life: The Holy Virgin Martyr Theodosia of Constantinople was a nun of the imperial city who gave her life in defense of the holy icons at the very outbreak of the iconoclast heresy, one of the first martyrs of that long persecution.
Virgin Martyr Theodosia the Nun of Const.patron: The icon of Christ over the Chalke gate defended.
Virgin Martyr Theodosia the Nun of Const.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources

“Bogolyubov” Icon of the Mother of God.life: On this day the Church commemorates the wonderworking Bogolyubov Icon of the Most Holy Theotokos, an image unique among the icons of the Mother of God, for it depicts her not with her Child but as she herself appeared in a vision, standing alone in prayer.
“Bogolyubov” Icon of the Mother of God.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
“Bogolyubov” Icon of the Mother of God.patron: Those who behold the Mother of God in prayer; the founders of churches by her command

“Seven Arrows” Icon of the Mother of God.life: On this day the Church commemorates the wonderworking Seven Arrows Icon of the Most Holy Theotokos, an image that depicts the sorrow of the Mother of God and is invoked for the softening of hardened hearts.
“Seven Arrows” Icon of the Mother of God.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
“Seven Arrows” Icon of the Mother of God.patron: Those who seek the softening of hard hearts; the reconcilers of enemies

“Surety of Sinners” Icon of the Mother o.life: On this day the Church commemorates the wonderworking Icon of the Most Holy Theotokos called Surety of Sinners, in the version venerated at Korets, an image whose very name proclaims the mercy of the Mother of God toward the penitent.
“Surety of Sinners” Icon of the Mother o.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
“Surety of Sinners” Icon of the Mother o.patron: Sinners who seek the intercession of the Mother of God; those who repent

Apostle Barnabas of the Seventy.life: The Holy Apostle Barnabas, one of the Seventy, was among the earliest and most beloved leaders of the apostolic Church, the companion of Saint Paul and the founder of the Church of his native Cyprus.
Apostle Barnabas of the Seventy.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Apostle Barnabas of the Seventy.patron: The island of Cyprus; those who encourage and console

Apostle Bartholomew of the Twelve.life: The Holy and All-praised Apostle Bartholomew, one of the Twelve, is generally held by the tradition of the Church to be the same as Nathanael of Cana in Galilee, the guileless Israelite whom the Lord, seeing him under the fig tree before Philip called him.
Apostle Bartholomew of the Twelve.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Apostle Bartholomew of the Twelve.patron: The land of Armenia; missionaries to the East

Apostle Jude the Brother of the Lord.life: The Holy Apostle Jude, called the Brother of the Lord, was one of the Twelve Apostles, known also by the names Thaddaeus and Lebbaeus, and honored as a kinsman of Christ according to the flesh.
Apostle Jude the Brother of the Lord.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Apostle Jude the Brother of the Lord.patron: The kinsmen of the Lord; those who ask how Christ is made known

Blessed Constantine, Metropolitan of Kyi.life: Blessed Constantine, Metropolitan of Kyiv, governed the Russian Church in the middle of the twelfth century, in a time of grievous strife over the metropolitan see, and is remembered chiefly for the astonishing humility with which he sought, even in death, the lowest place.
Blessed Constantine, Metropolitan of Kyi.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Blessed Constantine, Metropolitan of Kyi.patron: Hierarchs who seek the last place; the humble in high office

Blessed Prince Gleb Andreevich, son of S.life: Saint Gleb Andreevich was a young prince of Vladimir, the son of the holy Prince Andrew Bogoliubsky, who lived a brief life of rare piety and was glorified by God with incorruption.
Blessed Prince Gleb Andreevich, son of S.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Blessed Prince Gleb Andreevich, son of S.patron: Young princes of piety; those who love the Scriptures and the Church

Commemoration of the Holy Fathers of the.life: On this day the Church commemorates the Holy Fathers of the First Ecumenical Council.
Commemoration of the Holy Fathers of the.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Commemoration of the Holy Fathers of the.patron: The defenders of the divinity of the Son; the fathers of the councils

Yaroslavl-Pechersk (Caves) Icon of the M.life: On this day the Church commemorates the wonderworking Yaroslavl-Pechersk Icon of the Most Holy Theotokos, an image of the Kyiv-Caves type that was glorified in the city of Yaroslavl in the nineteenth century through a remarkable healing.
Yaroslavl-Pechersk (Caves) Icon of the M.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Yaroslavl-Pechersk (Caves) Icon of the M.patron: The sick in body and soul; those who suffer long illness

Finding of the relics of Saint Basil, Bi.life: On this day the Church commemorates the finding of the relics of Saint Basil, Bishop of Ryazan, a hierarch of the thirteenth century whose innocence was vindicated by a famous wonder and whose relics were revealed in the troubled years of the seventeenth.
Finding of the relics of Saint Basil, Bi.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Finding of the relics of Saint Basil, Bi.patron: The falsely accused; bishops driven out by slander

Finding of the Relics of Saints Basil an.life: On this day the Church commemorates the finding of the relics of the Holy Right-believing Princes Basil and Constantine of Yaroslavl, brothers who ruled and suffered for their city in the bitter years of the Tatar yoke and whose incorrupt bodies were revealed long after in a fire.
Finding of the Relics of Saints Basil an.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Finding of the Relics of Saints Basil an.patron: The princes of Yaroslavl; those whose relics are found after fire

Hieromartyr Dorotheus, Bishop of Tyre.life: The Holy Hieromartyr Dorotheus, Bishop of Tyre, was a confessor and martyr of extraordinary length of life, who endured through three persecutions and gave to the Church, besides his witness, a valued account of the apostles.
Hieromartyr Dorotheus, Bishop of Tyre.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Hieromartyr Dorotheus, Bishop of Tyre.patron: Bishops of long life and many trials; confessors under successive persecutions

Hieromartyr Eusebius, Bishop of Samosata.life: The Holy Hieromartyr Eusebius, Bishop of Samosata, was one of the great champions of the Orthodox faith against the Arian heresy in the fourth century, a friend and fellow-laborer of the greatest fathers of his age and a confessor who died a martyr's death.
Hieromartyr Eusebius, Bishop of Samosata.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Hieromartyr Eusebius, Bishop of Samosata.patron: Defenders of Orthodoxy against heresy; bishops exiled for the faith

Hieromartyr Lucian, Bishop of Beauvais,.life: The Holy Hieromartyr Lucian, Bishop of Beauvais, was one of the missionary enlighteners of ancient Gaul, sent, the tradition holds, from Rome to preach the Gospel among the still-pagan tribes of the north, and he sealed his apostolate there with martyrdom in the third century.
Hieromartyr Lucian, Bishop of Beauvais,.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Hieromartyr Lucian, Bishop of Beauvais,.patron: Missionary bishops; the enlighteners of Gaul

Hieromartyr Marcellinus, Pope of Rome, a.life: The Holy Hieromartyr Marcellinus, Pope of Rome, governed the Church of Rome at the height of the Diocletian persecution, when, the accounts say, thousands were martyred in a single month.
Hieromartyr Marcellinus, Pope of Rome, a.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Hieromartyr Marcellinus, Pope of Rome, a.patron: The penitent after a fall; those restored by repentance

Hieromartyr Methodius, Bishop of Patara.life: The Holy Hieromartyr Methodius, Bishop of Patara, was one of the learned fathers and theologians of the early Church, a defender of the true faith against error and a martyr in the last great persecution. He was bishop of Olympus and of Patara in Lycia, and afterward, the tradition says, of Tyre, a man of wide learning and eloquence, and he used his gifts in the service of the faith, above all in two great works.
Hieromartyr Methodius, Bishop of Patara.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Hieromartyr Methodius, Bishop of Patara.patron: Bishops and theologians; the defenders of the resurrection of the body

Hieromartyr Sisinius the Deacon of Rome.life: The Holy Hieromartyr Sisinius the Deacon suffered for Christ at Rome, with a great company of fellow-martyrs, in the fierce persecution of the emperors at the turn of the fourth century.
Hieromartyr Sisinius the Deacon of Rome.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Hieromartyr Sisinius the Deacon of Rome.patron: Deacons and servants of the Church; whole companies martyred together

Hieromartyr Terence, Bishop of Iconium.life: The Holy Hieromartyr Terence, Bishop of Iconium, was one of the first shepherds of the apostolic age, set over the Church of Iconium in Lycaonia, the city where the Apostle Paul had preached and suffered, and he sealed his episcopate with martyrdom.
Hieromartyr Terence, Bishop of Iconium.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Hieromartyr Terence, Bishop of Iconium.patron: The first bishops of the apostolic Churches; those ordained by the apostles

Hieromartyr Theodotus, Bishop of Ancyra.life: On this day the Church keeps the particular commemoration of the Holy Martyr Theodotus of Ancyra, whose passion is told more fully in the calendar together with the seven virgins of Ancyra, and whom this feast honors especially at his own martyrdom.
Hieromartyr Theodotus, Bishop of Ancyra.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Hieromartyr Theodotus, Bishop of Ancyra.patron: Innkeepers and hosts; those who bury the martyrs

Hieromartyr Timothy, Bishop of Prusa.life: The Holy Hieromartyr Timothy, Bishop of Prusa in Bithynia, was a shepherd, wonderworker, and martyr who suffered for Christ under Julian the Apostate in the fourth century.
Hieromartyr Timothy, Bishop of Prusa.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Hieromartyr Timothy, Bishop of Prusa.patron: Bishops and wonderworkers; those who slay the dragon by prayer

Holy Great-martyr Tsar Lazar (Vidovdan).life: The Holy Great-martyr Prince Lazar of Serbia led his people at the Battle of Kosovo on the day the Serbs call Vidovdan, and by his death and choice became the heart of the faith and identity of the Serbian nation.
Holy Great-martyr Tsar Lazar (Vidovdan).src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Holy Great-martyr Tsar Lazar (Vidovdan).patron: The Serbian people and nation; those who choose the heavenly kingdom

Icon of the Mother of God “of the Passio.life: On this day the Church commemorates the wonderworking Icon of the Most Holy Theotokos called of the Passion, an image whose very composition is a meditation on the sufferings of Christ foreknown.
Icon of the Mother of God “of the Passio.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Icon of the Mother of God “of the Passio.patron: Those who take refuge from suffering in the Mother of God; the frightened and the grieving

Icon of the Mother of God “The Unbreakab.life: On this day the Church commemorates the ancient and venerable Icon of the Most Holy Theotokos called the Unbreakable Wall, the great mosaic image of the Mother of God that stands in the apse of the Cathedral of Holy Wisdom in Kyiv.
Icon of the Mother of God “The Unbreakab.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Icon of the Mother of God “The Unbreakab.patron: Those who take refuge in the Mother of God; the defenders of cities and churches

Icon of the Mother of God of Kasperov.life: On this day the Church commemorates the wonderworking Kasperov Icon of the Most Holy Theotokos, an image glorified in the southern Russian lands by its renewal and by the deliverance of a great city.
Icon of the Mother of God of Kasperov.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Icon of the Mother of God of Kasperov.patron: Those who pray before neglected icons; the defenders of cities

Icon of the Mother of God of Kyiv-Bratsk.life: On this day the Church commemorates the wonderworking Icon of the Most Holy Theotokos called of Kyiv-Bratsk, the icon of the Kyiv Brotherhood, or Bratsky, Monastery on the Podil, the quarter of Kyiv by the Dnieper.
Icon of the Mother of God of Kyiv-Bratsk.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Icon of the Mother of God of Kyiv-Bratsk.patron: The Kyiv Brotherhood and its school; those who take refuge in the Mother of God

Martyr Agrippina of Rome.life: The Holy Virgin-martyr Agrippina suffered for Christ at Rome in the persecution of the emperors, and her holy relics became in a later age the treasure and protection of a city of Sicily.
Martyr Agrippina of Rome.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Martyr Agrippina of Rome.patron: Virgins consecrated to Christ; those whose relics are borne to safety

Martyr Aquilina of Byblos in Syria.life: The Holy Martyr Aquilina, a native of the Phoenician city of Byblos, suffered for Christ while still a child in the persecution of Diocletian, and shows that the confession of the faith knows no age.
Martyr Aquilina of Byblos in Syria.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Martyr Aquilina of Byblos in Syria.patron: Children and young girls; those who convert their friends

Martyr Archil II, King of Georgia.life: Saint Archil was a king of Kartli, the heartland of Georgia, in the eighth century, who defended his Christian people against the invader and was crowned with martyrdom for refusing to deny Christ.
Martyr Archil II, King of Georgia.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Martyr Archil II, King of Georgia.patron: Kings who die for the faith; the defenders of Georgia against the invader

Martyr Julian of Tarsus, in Cilicia.life: The Holy Martyr Julian of Tarsus in Cilicia suffered for Christ in the persecution of Diocletian, and his long endurance and strange death were praised by Saint John Chrysostom himself. Julian was a young man of noble birth in the city of Tarsus, a Christian from his youth; and when the persecution came, he was seized and brought before the governor and commanded to sacrifice to the idols, and, refusing, confessed Christ boldly.
Martyr Julian of Tarsus, in Cilicia.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Martyr Julian of Tarsus, in Cilicia.patron: The young who confess Christ; those who endure long torture

Martyr Justin the Philosopher and those.life: The Holy Martyr Justin the Philosopher was one of the first and greatest of the Christian apologists, a seeker of truth through all the schools of pagan philosophy who found it at last in Christ, and sealed his witness with his blood at Rome about the year 165.
Martyr Justin the Philosopher and those.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Martyr Justin the Philosopher and those.patron: Philosophers and seekers of truth; apologists and defenders of the faith

Martyr Lucillian and those who suffered.life: The Holy Martyr Lucillian and those who suffered with him at Byzantium bore witness to Christ in the reign of the emperor Aurelian, in the third century, and their company joined an old man converted late in life to four young men and a holy virgin.
Martyr Lucillian and those who suffered.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Martyr Lucillian and those who suffered.patron: The converted in old age; the young who confess together

Martyr Nectan of Hartland.life: Saint Nectan of Hartland was a Celtic hermit and martyr of the sixth century, honored in the West Country of Britain, whose life belongs to that great family of the saints of the Celtic Church who left their homelands to seek God in solitude.
Martyr Nectan of Hartland.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Martyr Nectan of Hartland.patron: Hermits and solitaries; those who carry their own heads

Martyr Zosimus the Soldier at Antioch, i.life: The Holy Martyr Zosimus the Soldier suffered for Christ in the age of the persecutions, and is honored for the steadfast confession by which a man of arms laid down his life for his Lord.
Martyr Zosimus the Soldier at Antioch, i.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Martyr Zosimus the Soldier at Antioch, i.patron: Soldiers who confess Christ; those tortured for the faith

Martyrs Eustochius, Gaius, Probus, Lolli.life: The Holy Martyrs Eustochius, Gaius, Probus, Lollius, and Urban suffered for Christ at Ancyra in Galatia in the age of the persecutions, and their company was gathered to Christ by the very constancy of the martyrs they had once opposed.
Martyrs Eustochius, Gaius, Probus, Lolli.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Martyrs Eustochius, Gaius, Probus, Lolli.patron: Converts from paganism; kinsmen who confess together

Martyrs Frontasius, Severinus, Severian,.life: The Holy Martyrs Frontasius, Severinus, Severian, and Silanus are honored as among the first preachers of the Gospel and the first martyrs of Gaul, held by the tradition of their region to belong to the earliest generation of the Church's mission into the western lands.
Martyrs Frontasius, Severinus, Severian,.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Martyrs Frontasius, Severinus, Severian,.patron: The first enlighteners of Gaul; the disciples of the apostolic missionaries

Martyrs Galacteon, Juliana, and Saturnin.life: The Holy Martyrs Galacteon, Juliana, and Saturninus suffered for Christ at Byzantium in the age of the persecutions, and though the particulars of their passion have not been preserved in fullness.
Martyrs Galacteon, Juliana, and Saturnin.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Martyrs Galacteon, Juliana, and Saturnin.patron: Those martyred together; the steadfast in confession

Martyrs Inna, Pinna, and Rimma, disciple.life: The Holy Martyrs Inna, Pinna, and Rimma were among the first fruits of the Gospel in the northern lands by the Black Sea and the Danube, disciples of the Holy Apostle Andrew the First-called.
Martyrs Inna, Pinna, and Rimma, disciple.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Martyrs Inna, Pinna, and Rimma, disciple.patron: Disciples of the apostles; the enlighteners of the northern lands

Martyrs Kyriake, Kaleria, and Mary of Ca.life: The Holy Women Martyrs Kyriake, Kaleria, also called Valeria, and Mary suffered for Christ at Caesarea in Palestine in the persecution of Diocletian, and their brief and beautiful story is one of conversion, prayer, and steadfast confession.
Martyrs Kyriake, Kaleria, and Mary of Ca.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Martyrs Kyriake, Kaleria, and Mary of Ca.patron: Women who forsake paganism for Christ; those who pray for the end of persecution

Martyrs Leontius, Hypatius, and Theodulu.life: The Holy Martyrs Leontius, Hypatius, and Theodulus suffered for Christ at Tripoli in Phoenicia in the first age of the Church, and their martyrdom is a story of a persecutor turned into a fellow-confessor.
Martyrs Leontius, Hypatius, and Theodulu.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Martyrs Leontius, Hypatius, and Theodulu.patron: Soldiers and commanders; those converted while persecuting

Martyrs Manuel, Sabel, and Ismael, of Pe.life: The Holy Martyrs Manuel, Sabel, and Ismael were three brothers of noble Persian birth who suffered for Christ at the court of Julian the Apostate in the fourth century, and their martyrdom turned an embassy of peace into a testimony of faith.
Martyrs Manuel, Sabel, and Ismael, of Pe.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Martyrs Manuel, Sabel, and Ismael, of Pe.patron: Envoys and ambassadors; brothers in the faith

Martyrs Modestus, Crescentia, and Vitus,.life: The Holy Martyrs Vitus, Modestus, and Crescentia suffered for Christ in the persecution of Diocletian, and their company joined a young boy to the tutor and nurse who had raised him in the faith and died with him.
Martyrs Modestus, Crescentia, and Vitus,.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Martyrs Modestus, Crescentia, and Vitus,.patron: Children and their guardians; tutors and nurses

Martyrs Zeno and his servant, Zenas, of.life: The Holy Martyrs Zeno and Zenas his servant suffered for Christ at Philadelphia in Arabia in the persecution of the emperors, and their story is a testimony to the brotherhood that the faith makes between master and servant.
Martyrs Zeno and his servant, Zenas, of.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Martyrs Zeno and his servant, Zenas, of.patron: Masters and their servants; those who free their slaves

New Martyr John the New of Sochi, who su.life: The Holy Great Martyr John the New of Suceava was a young merchant of Trebizond on the Black Sea, who suffered for Christ at Belgorod on the Black Sea coast in the fourteenth century, and became the great-martyr and heavenly patron of the land of Moldavia.
New Martyr John the New of Sochi, who su.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
New Martyr John the New of Sochi, who su.patron: Merchants and travelers; the martyrs under paganism and Islam

New Martyrs and Confessors of Butovo.life: On this day the Church commemorates the New Martyrs and Confessors of Butovo, the great company of the faithful who were shot for Christ at the Butovo firing range near Moscow in the terror of the Soviet years.
New Martyrs and Confessors of Butovo.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
New Martyrs and Confessors of Butovo.patron: The martyrs of the godless persecution; clergy and faithful slain for the faith

Prophet Amos.life: The Holy Prophet Amos was one of the twelve Minor Prophets of the Old Covenant, a herdsman called from his flock to cry the word of the Lord against a prosperous and corrupt kingdom.
Prophet Amos.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Prophet Amos.patron: Herdsmen and laborers called to prophesy; those who preach against injustice

Prophet Elisha.life: The Holy Prophet Elisha was the disciple, companion, and successor of the great Prophet Elijah, and one of the mightiest of the prophets of the Old Covenant, whose life was filled with wonders of mercy and power.
Prophet Elisha.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Prophet Elisha.patron: The disciples and heirs of the prophets; those who receive a double portion of grace

Recovery of the Relics (1650) and the Se.life: On this day the Church commemorates the recovery of the relics in 1650 and the second glorification in 1909 of the Holy Right-believing Great Princess Anna of Kashin, a woman whose life was a long martyrdom of grief and whose veneration itself passed through suppression and restoration.
Recovery of the Relics (1650) and the Se.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Recovery of the Relics (1650) and the Se.patron: Widows and grieving mothers; those who lose all and keep the faith

Repose of Saint Theodore Yaroslavich, ol.life: Saint Theodore Yaroslavich was the elder brother of the great Saint Alexander Nevsky.
Repose of Saint Theodore Yaroslavich, ol.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Repose of Saint Theodore Yaroslavich, ol.patron: The young who die in purity; princes cut off before their time

Righteous Artemius of Verkola.life: The Righteous Artemius of Verkola was a peasant boy of the Russian North, a child of remarkable piety, whom God glorified after a sudden death and the long neglect of his body.
Righteous Artemius of Verkola.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Righteous Artemius of Verkola.patron: Pious children; the sick and those with fevers

Righteous Martha and Mary, the sisters o.life: The Righteous Martha and Mary, the sisters of Lazarus, were among the closest friends of the Lord upon earth, of that household at Bethany which He loved and often visited.
Righteous Martha and Mary, the sisters o.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Righteous Martha and Mary, the sisters o.patron: Sisters and hostesses; those who serve and those who sit at the Lord's feet

Righteous Youths John and Jacob (James).life: The Righteous Youths John and Jacob of Menyusha were two little brothers of the Novgorod country who were taken by death in their earliest childhood and glorified by God as righteous wonderworkers.
Righteous Youths John and Jacob (James).src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Righteous Youths John and Jacob (James).patron: Young children; the innocent taken early

Saint Alban, Protomartyr of Britain.life: Saint Alban is honored as the Protomartyr of Britain, the first of that land to shed his blood for Christ, and his conversion and death are a parable of the Gospel's power. He was a citizen of the Roman town of Verulamium in Britain, a pagan, when in a time of persecution a Christian priest, fleeing from his pursuers, came to his door; and Alban, moved by pity, took the priest in and hid him.
Saint Alban, Protomartyr of Britain.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Saint Alban, Protomartyr of Britain.patron: The first martyrs of a land; those who shelter the persecuted

Saint David of Thessaloniki.life: Saint David of Thessaloniki was a hermit and wonderworker of the sixth century, one of that remarkable company of ascetics who, in imitation of the stylites, sought God by strange and severe austerities.
Saint David of Thessaloniki.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Saint David of Thessaloniki.patron: Hermits and ascetics; those who dwell in trees like the stylites

Saint Dionysios, the builder of Prodromo.life: Saint Dionysios the builder was the founder of the great monastery of the Forerunner on Mount Athos, the house that took his own name and is called Dionysiou.
Saint Dionysios, the builder of Prodromo.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Saint Dionysios, the builder of Prodromo.patron: Founders of monasteries; those who build at the vision of a light

Saint Dionysius, Archbishop of Suzdal.life: Saint Dionysius, Archbishop of Suzdal, in the world David, was a founder of monasteries, a teacher of saints, and a hierarch who served the Russian Church in the hard years of the Tatar yoke and the striving for its freedom.
Saint Dionysius, Archbishop of Suzdal.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Saint Dionysius, Archbishop of Suzdal.patron: Founders of monasteries made bishops; the teachers of holy disciples

Saint Ephraim, Patriarch of Antioch.life: Saint Ephraim, Patriarch of Antioch, was a defender of the Orthodox faith of the Council of Chalcedon in the sixth century, and came to the shepherd's throne by way of the world's highest service.
Saint Ephraim, Patriarch of Antioch.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Saint Ephraim, Patriarch of Antioch.patron: Patriarchs and defenders of Orthodoxy; those who rise from the world's service to the Church's

Saint Joanna the Myrrhbearer.life: The Righteous Joanna the Myrrhbearer was one of the holy women who followed the Lord and ministered to Him, and is numbered among the myrrh-bearing women who came to the tomb on the morning of the Resurrection.
Saint Joanna the Myrrhbearer.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Saint Joanna the Myrrhbearer.patron: The myrrh-bearing women; those who minister to the Lord of their substance

Saint John Maximovitch, Metropolitan of.life: Saint John, Metropolitan of Tobolsk and all Siberia, in the world John Maximovitch, was a great missionary hierarch, ascetic, and spiritual writer, and the last saint glorified by the Church of the Russian Empire before the Revolution.
Saint John Maximovitch, Metropolitan of.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Saint John Maximovitch, Metropolitan of.patron: Missionary hierarchs; the enlighteners of Siberia

Saint John, Bishop of the Goths in the C.life: Saint John, Bishop of the Goths in the Crimea, was a shepherd and confessor of the eighth century, who defended the holy icons and shared the sufferings of his flock under a foreign yoke.
Saint John, Bishop of the Goths in the C.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Saint John, Bishop of the Goths in the C.patron: Confessors of the icons; bishops of a persecuted flock

Saint Jonah, Bishop of Perm.life: Saint Jonah, Bishop of Perm, was one of the successors of Saint Stephen of Perm in the great work of bringing the peoples of the far Russian north to Christ, and completed much of what the first enlightener had begun.
Saint Jonah, Bishop of Perm.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Saint Jonah, Bishop of Perm.patron: Missionary bishops; the enlighteners of the northern peoples

Saint Jonah, Metropolitan of Moscow.life: Saint Jonah, Metropolitan of Moscow and all Russia, was the primate under whom the Russian Church, guarding the Orthodox faith, became in fact independent, and a holy and wonderworking hierarch.
Saint Jonah, Metropolitan of Moscow.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Saint Jonah, Metropolitan of Moscow.patron: The primates of the Russian Church; those who guard the faith against false union

Saint Julius, Presbyter of Novara, and h.life: Saints Julius the Presbyter and Julian the Deacon were two brothers, a priest and a deacon, who labored as missionaries in northern Italy in the age of the Christian emperors, casting down the temples of the idols and raising up churches of Christ in their place.
Saint Julius, Presbyter of Novara, and h.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Saint Julius, Presbyter of Novara, and h.patron: Missionary brothers; the builders of churches

Saint Kevin of Glendalough.life: Saint Kevin of Glendalough was one of the great monastic founders of Ireland, a hermit whose flight into a mountain solitude gave rise to one of the most famous monastic cities of the Celtic Church.
Saint Kevin of Glendalough.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Saint Kevin of Glendalough.patron: Founders of monasteries; hermits and lovers of solitude

Saint Luke (Voino-Yasenetsky), Archbisho.life: Saint Luke of Simferopol, in the world Valentin Feliksovich Voino-Yasenetsky, was one of the great confessors of the Russian Church under the Soviet persecution, a renowned surgeon who became a bishop and bore witness to Christ through prison, exile, and unceasing labor for the sick.
Saint Luke (Voino-Yasenetsky), Archbisho.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Saint Luke (Voino-Yasenetsky), Archbisho.patron: Physicians and surgeons; confessors under the godless power

Saint Methodius, Patriarch of Constantin.life: Saint Methodius, Patriarch of Constantinople, was a confessor of the holy icons who suffered greatly for the faith and lived to proclaim its final victory in the Triumph of Orthodoxy.
Saint Methodius, Patriarch of Constantin.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Saint Methodius, Patriarch of Constantin.patron: Confessors of the holy icons; those imprisoned for the faith

Saint Metrophanes, first Patriarch of Co.life: Saint Metrophanes, honored as the first Patriarch of Constantinople, was the bishop of Byzantium at the very hour when that city became the Christian capital of the world, a contemporary of Saint Constantine the Great who lived to a great old age in holiness and humility.
Saint Metrophanes, first Patriarch of Co.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Saint Metrophanes, first Patriarch of Co.patron: The first hierarchs of the imperial city; patriarchs of great age and humility

Saint Mstislav (George), Prince of Novgo.life: Saint Mstislav, in baptism George, called the Brave, was a prince of Novgorod in the twelfth century, honored for his valor, his justice, and his selfless care for the people and the land committed to him.
Saint Mstislav (George), Prince of Novgo.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Saint Mstislav (George), Prince of Novgo.patron: Just and valiant princes; the defenders of the people

Saint Nikephoros the Confessor, Patriarc.life: Saint Nikephoros the Confessor, Patriarch of Constantinople, was a defender of the holy icons who lost his throne and died in exile rather than surrender the faith, and was also one of the learned historians of his age.
Saint Nikephoros the Confessor, Patriarc.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Saint Nikephoros the Confessor, Patriarc.patron: Confessors of the holy icons; patriarchs deposed for the truth

Saint Paul, Physician of Corinth.life: Saint Paul, called the Physician of Corinth, was a holy man of the seventh century, honored for the wonder by which God cleared him of a grievous slander and for the gift of healing granted him thereafter.
Saint Paul, Physician of Corinth.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Saint Paul, Physician of Corinth.patron: Those falsely accused; physicians of soul and body

Saint Peter, Prince of Ordinsk, Rostov.life: Saint Peter, Prince of the Horde, called of Ordinsk, was a prince of the Tatar Golden Horde who was converted to Christ at Rostov and ended his royal life as a monk.
Saint Peter, Prince of Ordinsk, Rostov.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Saint Peter, Prince of Ordinsk, Rostov.patron: Converts from among the conquerors; princes who become monks

Saint Sampson the Hospitable of Constant.life: Saint Sampson the Hospitable was a physician of Constantinople who gave his wealth, his skill, and his life to the service of the poor and the sick, and founded a great hospital that bore his name for centuries.
Saint Sampson the Hospitable of Constant.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Saint Sampson the Hospitable of Constant.patron: Physicians and the hospitable; the founders of hospitals

Saint Shalva of Akhaltsikhe.life: Saint Shalva of Akhaltsikhe was a Georgian prince and military commander of the thirteenth century, who defended his homeland and his faith against the invaders and was crowned with martyrdom.
Saint Shalva of Akhaltsikhe.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Saint Shalva of Akhaltsikhe.patron: Soldiers and commanders; the defenders of Georgia

Saint Theodore, first Bishop of Rostov a.life: Saint Theodore, the first Bishop of Rostov and Suzdal, was a Greek by birth who was sent into the Russian land in the first generation after its baptism, and bore the hard beginning of the Church in a region long resistant to the Gospel.
Saint Theodore, first Bishop of Rostov a.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Saint Theodore, first Bishop of Rostov a.patron: Missionary bishops; the first enlighteners of a land

Saint Tikhon, Bishop of Amathus in Cypru.life: Saint Tikhon, Bishop of Amathus in Cyprus, was a wonderworking shepherd of the fifth century whose gift of miracles and boundless charity were shown from his very childhood.
Saint Tikhon, Bishop of Amathus in Cypru.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Saint Tikhon, Bishop of Amathus in Cypru.patron: Bishops and wonderworkers; the charitable to the poor

Saint Triphyllius, Bishop of Leucosia (N.life: Saint Triphyllius, Bishop of Leucosia, which is Nicosia in Cyprus, was a learned and eloquent hierarch of the fourth century who was formed in humility by the simple holiness of Saint Spyridon of Tremithus.
Saint Triphyllius, Bishop of Leucosia (N.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Saint Triphyllius, Bishop of Leucosia (N.patron: Bishops formed by humble teachers; the learned who choose humility

Saints Peter and Fevronia (tonsured Davi.life: Saints Peter and Fevronia of Murom, tonsured in the end David and Euphrosyne, were a prince and his princess whose married love became for the Russian people the very image of Christian marriage.
Saints Peter and Fevronia (tonsured Davi.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Saints Peter and Fevronia (tonsured Davi.patron: Married couples and families; spouses in fidelity and love

Second Translation of the relics of Sain.life: On this day the Church commemorates a translation of the relics of Saint Herman, the second Archbishop of Kazan and an enlightener of that newly-converted land.
Second Translation of the relics of Sain.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Second Translation of the relics of Sain.patron: The enlighteners of Kazan; those whose relics are translated in glory

Seven Martyred Brothers: Orentius, Pharn.life: The Holy Seven Martyred Brothers, Orentius, Pharnacius, Eros, Firmus, Firminus, Cyriacus, and Longinus, were soldiers in the Roman army in the age of the persecutions, seven brothers who confessed Christ together and were scattered into exile about the Black Sea and the Caucasus.
Seven Martyred Brothers: Orentius, Pharn.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Seven Martyred Brothers: Orentius, Pharn.patron: Soldiers who confess Christ; brothers martyred together

Synaxis of the Holy, Glorious and All-Pr.life: On the day after the feast of the chief apostles Peter and Paul, the Church keeps the Synaxis, the assembly, of the Holy, Glorious, and All-praised Twelve Apostles.
Synaxis of the Holy, Glorious and All-Pr.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Synaxis of the Holy, Glorious and All-Pr.patron: The whole company of the apostles; preachers and missionaries

The Holy Glorious and All-Praised Leader.life: The Holy and All-praised Apostle Paul, together with Saint Peter the chief of the apostles, is honored as a leader of the apostolic choir and the great apostle to the Gentiles, though he came to the faith by way of persecution.
The Holy Glorious and All-Praised Leader.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
The Holy Glorious and All-Praised Leader.patron: The apostles to the Gentiles; preachers and missionaries

The Holy Glorious and All-Praised Leader.life: The Holy and All-praised Apostle Peter, the chief of the Twelve, is honored with Saint Paul as a leader of the apostolic choir and a pillar of the Church. He was Simon, a fisherman of Bethsaida in Galilee, the brother of the Apostle Andrew, who brought him to Christ; and the Lord, looking upon him, named him Cephas, which is Peter, the rock, and called him from his nets to be a fisher of men.
The Holy Glorious and All-Praised Leader.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
The Holy Glorious and All-Praised Leader.patron: The leaders and shepherds of the Church; fishermen

The Holy Glorious and All-Praised Leader.life: On this day the Church keeps the great feast of the Holy, Glorious, and All-praised Leaders of the Apostles, Peter and Paul, honoring together the two chief apostles who labored above all others for the Gospel and were crowned together with martyrdom at Rome.
The Holy Glorious and All-Praised Leader.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
The Holy Glorious and All-Praised Leader.patron: The pillars and leaders of the Church; the apostolic preaching to Jew and Gentile

Translation of the relics of Saint Guria.life: On this day the Church commemorates the translation of the relics of Saint Gurias, first Archbishop of Kazan, the enlightener of that newly-conquered land.
Translation of the relics of Saint Guria.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Translation of the relics of Saint Guria.patron: The first hierarchs of a converted land; those whose relics are translated in glory

Translation of the relics of Saint Tikho.life: On this day the Church commemorates the translation of the relics of Saint Tikhon of Lukhov, the former soldier who became a poor monk in the Kostroma country and was glorified by God with incorruption.
Translation of the relics of Saint Tikho.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Translation of the relics of Saint Tikho.patron: Those whose relics are found incorrupt; the poor monks glorified by God

Translation of the relics of slain Crown.life: On this day the Church commemorates the translation of the relics of the Holy Right-believing Tsarevich Demetrius of Uglich, the boy prince and passion-bearer murdered at Uglich in 1591.
Translation of the relics of slain Crown.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Translation of the relics of slain Crown.patron: The murdered and vindicated; those whose relics confound the impostor

Translation of the relics of the Greatma.life: On this day the Church commemorates the translation of the relics of the Holy Greatmartyr Theodore Stratelates, the general, whose martyrdom is kept in February and whose sacred body was borne home to his own city to be a fountain of grace.
Translation of the relics of the Greatma.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Translation of the relics of the Greatma.patron: Soldiers and commanders; those who honor the great martyrs

Translation of the Relics of the holy an.life: On this day the Church commemorates the translation of the relics of the holy and wonderworking Unmercenaries Cyrus and John, martyrs of Egypt, whose sacred bodies were borne to a place of healing to cast down the power of the demons.
Translation of the Relics of the holy an.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Translation of the Relics of the holy an.patron: Physicians and the unmercenary; those who displace the demons by the saints

Translation of the relics of the Right-b.life: On this day the Church commemorates the translation of the relics of the Holy Passion-bearer Igor, in baptism George, of the princely house of Chernihiv, who briefly held the throne of Kyiv, became a monk, and was murdered by the mob at his prayers.
Translation of the relics of the Right-b.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Translation of the relics of the Right-b.patron: Princes who become monks; the victims of the mob

Uncovering of the relics of Venerable Ep.life: On this day the Church commemorates the uncovering of the relics of Venerable Ephraim, Abbot of Novy Torg, a founder of monastic life whose story is bound to the first martyrs of the Russian land.
Uncovering of the relics of Venerable Ep.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Uncovering of the relics of Venerable Ep.patron: Founders of monasteries; the faithful servants of the passion-bearers

Uncovering of the relics of Venerable Ju.life: On this day the Church commemorates the uncovering of the relics of the Holy Right-believing Princess Juliana of Vyazma, a martyr who defended her marriage vow and her chastity unto a cruel death.
Uncovering of the relics of Venerable Ju.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Uncovering of the relics of Venerable Ju.patron: Wives who defend their honor; the victims of violence

Venerable Agapitus the Unmercenary Physi.life: Venerable Agapitus of the Caves, the Unmercenary Physician, was a disciple of Saint Anthony of the Kyiv Caves and one of the first and most beloved of the healing saints of the Russian land, who tended the sick for the love of Christ and took no payment.
Venerable Agapitus the Unmercenary Physi.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Venerable Agapitus the Unmercenary Physi.patron: Physicians and the healers of the sick; the unmercenary

Venerable Alexander, Abbot of Kushta, Vo.life: Venerable Alexander of Kushta was one of the founders of the Northern Thebaid, the multitude of monasteries that filled the Vologda wilderness in the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries, and he planted his house in the silent country by the great Lake Kubenskoye.
Venerable Alexander, Abbot of Kushta, Vo.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Venerable Alexander, Abbot of Kushta, Vo.patron: Founders of the northern monasteries; hermits who exchange their solitudes

Venerable Andronikos, Disciple of Saint.life: Venerable Andronikos of Moscow was a disciple of Saint Sergius of Radonezh and the first abbot of the Savior-Andronikov monastery in Moscow, one of the houses through which the grace of Radonezh was planted in the capital of Russia.
Venerable Andronikos, Disciple of Saint.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Venerable Andronikos, Disciple of Saint.patron: Disciples of Saint Sergius; founders of monasteries

Venerable Anthony, Abbot of Dymsk, Novgo.life: Venerable Anthony of Dymsk was a disciple of Saint Varlaam of Khutyn and a founder of monastic life in the Novgorod country, who joined to the labors of a founder the hidden ascesis of a hermit.
Venerable Anthony, Abbot of Dymsk, Novgo.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Venerable Anthony, Abbot of Dymsk, Novgo.patron: Hermits and founders; the disciples of holy elders

Venerable Arsenius, Abbot of Konevits.life: Venerable Arsenius of Konevits was a founder of monastic life in the far north of Russia, who brought the grace of the Holy Mountain to an island of Lake Ladoga.
Venerable Arsenius, Abbot of Konevits.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Venerable Arsenius, Abbot of Konevits.patron: Founders of island monasteries; those who bring back grace from the Holy Mountain

Venerable Barlaam of Shenkursk.life: Venerable Barlaam of Shenkursk, in the world Vasily, was a great man of Novgorod who forsook rank and wealth in his last years to found a monastery and become a monk in the northern wilderness.
Venerable Barlaam of Shenkursk.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Venerable Barlaam of Shenkursk.patron: Those who leave rank and wealth for God; founders of monasteries

Venerable Barnabas, Abbot of Vetluga.life: Venerable Barnabas of Vetluga was a hermit of the northern Russian forests in the fifteenth century, who hallowed by his long solitude the wild country of the river Vetluga.
Venerable Barnabas, Abbot of Vetluga.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Venerable Barnabas, Abbot of Vetluga.patron: Hermits and solitaries; the settlers of the northern forests

Venerable Bessarion, Wonderworker of Egy.life: Venerable Bessarion the Wonderworker was one of the great fathers of the Egyptian desert in the fourth and early fifth centuries, an ascetic of such radical poverty and detachment that he seemed to possess nothing at all upon the earth.
Venerable Bessarion, Wonderworker of Egy.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Venerable Bessarion, Wonderworker of Egy.patron: Hermits and wanderers; the utterly poor

Venerable Cassian and Gregory, Abbots of.life: Venerable Cassian and Gregory of Avnezh were founders of monastic life in the Vologda wilderness and disciples of the tradition of Saint Sergius of Radonezh, who were crowned with martyrdom in the monastery they had raised.
Venerable Cassian and Gregory, Abbots of.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Venerable Cassian and Gregory, Abbots of.patron: Disciples of Saint Sergius; founders slain in their monastery

Venerable Cyril, Igoumen of White Lake.life: Venerable Cyril of White Lake, the founder of the great Kirillo-Belozersky monastery, was one of the chief fathers of the Northern Thebaid and a spiritual son of the tradition of Saint Sergius of Radonezh, called to his life's work by the very voice of the Mother of God.
Venerable Cyril, Igoumen of White Lake.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Venerable Cyril, Igoumen of White Lake.patron: Founders of monasteries; the fathers of the Northern Thebaid

Venerable Dionysius, Abbot of Glushitsa,.life: Venerable Dionysius of Glushitsa was one of the greatest ascetics and founders of the Northern Thebaid, that wilderness of the Vologda and Beloozero forests which the monks of the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries filled with houses of prayer.
Venerable Dionysius, Abbot of Glushitsa,.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Venerable Dionysius, Abbot of Glushitsa,.patron: Founders of the northern monasteries; iconographers

Venerable Dometius of Dionysiou.life: Saint Dometius of Dionysiou was a disciple and fellow-labourer of Saint Dionysios, the founder of the Dionysiou monastery on Mount Athos, and shared in the ascetic life and the holiness of that house in its first days.
Venerable Dometius of Dionysiou.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Venerable Dometius of Dionysiou.patron: Disciples of holy founders; hermits and ascetics

Venerable Hilarion the New, Abbot of the.life: Saint Hilarion the New was abbot of the ancient Dalmatos monastery at Constantinople, the first monastery of the imperial city, and a confessor of the holy icons who suffered greatly for the faith through the reigns of the iconoclast emperors.
Venerable Hilarion the New, Abbot of the.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Venerable Hilarion the New, Abbot of the.patron: Abbots and confessors of the icons; those imprisoned and scourged for the faith

Venerable Leontius of the Kyiv Far Caves.life: Venerable Leontius the Canonarch labored in asceticism in the Far Caves of the Kyiv Lavra, and served the brethren in the ordering and the chanting of the divine services.
Venerable Leontius of the Kyiv Far Caves.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Venerable Leontius of the Kyiv Far Caves.patron: Chanters and directors of the choir; those reared from childhood in the monastery

Venerable Leontius the Hagiorite.life: Saint Leontius the Hagiorite was a monk of Mount Athos, the Holy Mountain, who is honored above all for the strictness of his monastic stability, for he kept himself within the walls of his monastery for sixty years and never once passed beyond them.
Venerable Leontius the Hagiorite.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Venerable Leontius the Hagiorite.patron: Monks of strict enclosure; those who never leave their monastery

Venerable Methodius, Abbot of Peshnosha,.life: Saint Methodius, Abbot of Peshnosha, was a disciple of the great Saint Sergius of Radonezh and one of the many founders of monasteries who went out from under Sergius' guidance to plant the monastic life across the Russian land.
Venerable Methodius, Abbot of Peshnosha,.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Venerable Methodius, Abbot of Peshnosha,.patron: Disciples of holy founders; the builders of monasteries

Venerable Onuphrius the Great.life: Venerable Onuphrius the Great was one of the most famous of the hermits of the Egyptian desert, an anchorite who spent sixty years in utter solitude in the deep wilderness, alone with God.
Venerable Onuphrius the Great.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Venerable Onuphrius the Great.patron: Hermits and anchorites; those who dwell alone with God

Venerable Paisius the Great.life: Venerable Paisius the Great was one of the most exalted of the fathers of the Egyptian desert, an ascetic of extraordinary abstinence and prayer who was granted visions of Christ Himself.
Venerable Paisius the Great.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Venerable Paisius the Great.patron: Ascetics and men of prayer; those who fast for weeks together

Venerable Paisius, Abbot of Uglich.life: Venerable Paisius of Uglich was a founder of monastic life on the upper Volga and a kinsman and disciple of Saint Macarius of Kalyazin, in whose tradition he was formed and which he carried into his own foundation.
Venerable Paisius, Abbot of Uglich.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Venerable Paisius, Abbot of Uglich.patron: Founders of monasteries; the kinsmen and disciples of holy men

Venerable Peter of Mount Athos.life: Saint Peter of Mount Athos was the first known hermit of the Holy Mountain, who dwelt there in solitude for three and fifty years and is honored as a father of Athonite monasticism.
Venerable Peter of Mount Athos.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Venerable Peter of Mount Athos.patron: Hermits and the first of the solitaries; Mount Athos and its monks

Venerable Savva, Abbot of Moscow.life: Venerable Savva, Abbot of Moscow, was a successor of Saint Andronikos as abbot of the Savior-Andronikov monastery in Moscow, and continued in that house the tradition of the common life that had come down from Saint Sergius of Radonezh.
Venerable Savva, Abbot of Moscow.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Venerable Savva, Abbot of Moscow.patron: Successors of holy founders; abbots of the common life

Venerable Serapion of Kozhe Lake.life: Venerable Serapion of Kozhe Lake was a convert from among the Tatars who became a monk and a founder of monastic life in the far north of Russia.
Venerable Serapion of Kozhe Lake.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Venerable Serapion of Kozhe Lake.patron: Converts from the peoples of the East; founders of northern monasteries

Venerable Sergius and Herman, Wonderwork.life: Venerable Sergius and Herman, the Wonderworkers of Valaam, were the founders of the great monastery of Valaam on an island in Lake Ladoga and enlighteners of the Karelian people of the Russian north.
Venerable Sergius and Herman, Wonderwork.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Venerable Sergius and Herman, Wonderwork.patron: Founders of island monasteries; the enlighteners of Karelia

Venerable Silvanus the Schemamonk, of th.life: The Holy Schemamonk Silvanus of the Kyiv Caves labored in asceticism in the Far Caves of the Lavra in the thirteenth and fourteenth centuries, and is remembered for a wonder that reveals the power God gives to the prayer of the righteous.
Venerable Silvanus the Schemamonk, of th.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Venerable Silvanus the Schemamonk, of th.patron: The guardians of holy places; those who labor in the garden

Venerable Tikhon of Kaluga Or Medin.life: Saint Tikhon of Kaluga, called also of Medin, was a hermit and founder of the fifteenth century who hallowed by his solitude the deep forests of the Kaluga country.
Venerable Tikhon of Kaluga Or Medin.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Venerable Tikhon of Kaluga Or Medin.patron: Hermits and lovers of solitude; founders of forest monasteries

Venerable Tikhon of Luchov, Kostroma.life: Saint Tikhon of Lukhov, in the world Timothy, was a monk of the Kostroma country who exchanged the service of an earthly prince for the service of God and lived and died in the poverty he loved.
Venerable Tikhon of Luchov, Kostroma.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Venerable Tikhon of Luchov, Kostroma.patron: Those who leave the world and its service; the poor and the laborers

Venerable Xenophon, Abbot of Robeika, No.life: Venerable Xenophon of Robeika was a disciple of Saint Varlaam of Khutyn and a founder of monastic life near Novgorod, who from his youth chose the way of purity and prayer.
Venerable Xenophon, Abbot of Robeika, No.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Venerable Xenophon, Abbot of Robeika, No.patron: Disciples of holy elders; founders of monasteries

Virgin Martyr Febronia of Nisibis.life: The Holy Virgin-martyr Febronia of Nisibis was a young nun of Mesopotamia who suffered a martyrdom of fearful torments for Christ in the persecution of Diocletian, and whose life became a beloved pattern of virginity and courage.
Virgin Martyr Febronia of Nisibis.src: Great Synaxarion; Lives of the Saints (OCA); Melkite Synaxarion; jurisdictional sources
Virgin Martyr Febronia of Nisibis.patron: Nuns and virgins; those who endure fearful torments

Righteous Forefather Noah.life: The Holy Righteous Forefather Noah, tenth from Adam, found grace in the eyes of the Lord when the wickedness of men had grown great upon the earth, and at God's command built the ark in which his household and every living kind were preserved through the flood; the Fathers see in it a figure of the Church.
Righteous Forefather Noah.patron: Invoked for perseverance amid mockery; deliverance from the flood.
Righteous Forefather Noah.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Forefather Adam.life: Adam was the first man, formed by God from the dust of the earth and given the breath of life, and set in Paradise to till and keep it. He was made in the image of God and given dominion over every living thing, and he gave names to the beasts of the field and the birds of the air.
Righteous Forefather Adam.patron: Invoked for repentance; the mourning of sin.
Righteous Forefather Adam.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Forefather Seth.life: Seth was the third son of Adam and Eve, given to them after the murder of Abel, and Eve said at his birth that God had appointed her another seed in place of the son whom Cain slew. Through him the righteous line was continued to Noah and so to Christ.
Righteous Forefather Seth.patron: Invoked for the beginning of true worship.
Righteous Forefather Seth.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Forefather Enos.life: Enos was the son of Seth and the grandson of Adam. Of his generation Scripture records that men began to call upon the name of the Lord, and the Fathers understand this as the beginning of public worship offered openly to God.
Righteous Forefather Enos.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Forefather Cainan.life: Cainan was the son of Enos and the fourth generation from Adam. Scripture records of him only his place in the genealogy and that he lived nine hundred and ten years.
Righteous Forefather Cainan.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Forefather Mahalalel.life: Mahalalel was the son of Cainan and the fifth generation from Adam. His name is understood to mean the praise of God. Scripture records that he lived eight hundred and ninety five years.
Righteous Forefather Mahalalel.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Forefather Jared.life: Jared was the son of Mahalalel and the father of Enoch, the sixth generation from Adam. Scripture records that he lived nine hundred and sixty two years, and gives no further account of him.
Righteous Forefather Jared.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Forefather Enoch.life: Enoch was the son of Jared and the seventh generation from Adam. Scripture says of him what it says of no other man of that age, that Enoch walked with God, and he was not, for God took him.
Righteous Forefather Enoch.patron: Invoked for a blameless life; hope of the resurrection.
Righteous Forefather Enoch.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Forefather Methuselah.life: Methuselah was the son of Enoch and the grandfather of Noah. He lived nine hundred and sixty nine years, longer than any other man recorded in Scripture, and he died in the year of the flood.
Righteous Forefather Methuselah.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Forefather Lamech.life: Lamech was the son of Methuselah and the father of Noah. At the birth of his son he said that this one would comfort them concerning their work and the toil of their hands, because of the ground which the Lord had cursed, and the Fathers see in these words a prophecy of the rest that would come through the ark and afterward through Christ.
Righteous Forefather Lamech.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Shem, son of Noah.life: Shem was the eldest son of Noah and passed through the flood with him in the ark. When his father lay uncovered in his tent, Shem and Japheth took a garment and walked backward and covered him, not looking upon his shame, and for this Noah blessed Shem and said that the Lord God of Shem be blessed.
Righteous Shem, son of Noah.patron: Invoked for the blessing of the fathers.
Righteous Shem, son of Noah.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Japheth, son of Noah.life: Japheth was a son of Noah and passed through the flood with him in the ark. With his brother Shem he covered their father without looking upon him, and Noah blessed him saying that God shall enlarge Japheth and he shall dwell in the tents of Shem.
Righteous Japheth, son of Noah.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Forefather Arphaxad.life: Arphaxad was the son of Shem, born two years after the flood, and stands at the head of the line that runs from Noah to Abraham. Scripture records his place in the genealogy and that he lived four hundred and thirty eight years.
Righteous Forefather Arphaxad.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Forefather Salah.life: Salah was the son of Arphaxad and the father of Eber. Scripture records of him only his place in the line from Noah to Abraham and that he lived four hundred and thirty three years.
Righteous Forefather Salah.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Forefather Eber.life: Eber was the son of Salah and the father of Peleg, and from his name the Hebrew people are traditionally said to be called. Scripture records that he lived four hundred and sixty four years.
Righteous Forefather Eber.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Forefather Peleg.life: Peleg was the son of Eber. Scripture says that in his days the earth was divided, which is understood of the scattering of the nations after the tower of Babel, and his name carries that meaning. He lived two hundred and thirty nine years.
Righteous Forefather Peleg.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Forefather Reu.life: Reu was the son of Peleg and the father of Serug, born in the generations after the scattering of the nations. Scripture records his place in the genealogy and that he lived two hundred and thirty nine years, and gives no further account of him.
Righteous Forefather Reu.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Forefather Serug.life: Serug was the son of Reu, the father of Nahor, and the great grandfather of Abraham. Scripture records his place in the line that runs from Noah to Abraham and that he lived two hundred and thirty years.
Righteous Forefather Serug.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Forefather Nahor.life: Nahor was the son of Serug and the father of Terah, and so the grandfather of Abraham. Scripture records that he lived a hundred and forty eight years, the lives of the patriarchs growing shorter as the generations approached Abraham.
Righteous Forefather Nahor.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Forefather Terah.life: Terah was the father of Abraham, Nahor, and Haran, and the grandfather of Lot. He took his household out of Ur of the Chaldees to go into the land of Canaan, but came to Haran and dwelt there, and died in Haran at two hundred and five years.
Righteous Forefather Terah.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Melchizedek, King of Salem.life: Melchizedek was king of Salem and priest of the Most High God. When Abraham returned from the slaughter of the kings, Melchizedek came out to meet him and brought forth bread and wine, and blessed him saying, blessed be Abram of the Most High God, possessor of heaven and earth. Abraham gave him a tenth of all the spoil.
Righteous Melchizedek, King of Salem.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Foremother Sarah.life: Sarah was the wife of Abraham and went out with him from Ur of the Chaldees. She was barren into old age, and when the three angels came to the oak of Mamre and said that she would bear a son, she laughed within herself, for she was ninety years old. The Lord asked whether anything is too hard for God, and in due time she bore Isaac, whose name means laughter.
Righteous Foremother Sarah.patron: Invoked for barrenness; hope against expectation.
