Righteous Foremother Sarah.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Foremother Rebecca.life: Rebecca was the wife of Isaac. When the servant of Abraham came into Mesopotamia seeking a wife for his master's son, he prayed that the maiden who gave him drink and watered his camels would be the one appointed, and Rebecca came out with her pitcher and did so before he had finished speaking.
Righteous Foremother Rebecca.patron: Invoked for hospitality; guidance in marriage.
Righteous Foremother Rebecca.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Foremother Rachel.life: Rachel was the daughter of Laban and the beloved wife of Jacob, who served seven years for her and they seemed to him but a few days for the love he had for her. She was long barren while her sister Leah bore sons, and she bore at last Joseph and then Benjamin, and died in giving birth to him on the road to Bethlehem.
Righteous Foremother Rachel.patron: Invoked for barrenness; mothers in sorrow.
Righteous Foremother Rachel.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Foremother Leah.life: Leah was the elder daughter of Laban and the first wife of Jacob, given to him in place of Rachel whom he had served for. Scripture says that she was not loved as her sister was, and that the Lord therefore opened her womb.
Righteous Foremother Leah.patron: Invoked for the unloved; patience in marriage.
Righteous Foremother Leah.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Miriam, sister of Moses.life: Miriam was the sister of Moses and Aaron. As a child she watched the ark of bulrushes among the reeds of the river and spoke to the daughter of Pharaoh, so that her own mother was called to nurse the child.
Righteous Miriam, sister of Moses.patron: Invoked for deliverance; thanksgiving after deliverance.
Righteous Miriam, sister of Moses.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Foremother Judith.life: Judith was a widow of Bethulia who fasted and prayed in a chamber upon her roof. When the city was besieged by the army of Holofernes and the elders had resolved to surrender if no help came in five days, she rebuked them for putting God to the test and went out with her maid into the camp of the enemy.
Righteous Foremother Judith.patron: Invoked for courage; widows; deliverance of a city.
Righteous Foremother Judith.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Foremother Esther.life: Esther was a Jewish maiden of the tribe of Benjamin, brought up by her kinsman Mordecai, who was chosen queen by the king of Persia. When Haman obtained a decree for the destruction of all the Jews in the empire, Mordecai sent word to her that she should plead for her people, saying that she had perhaps come to the kingdom for such a time as this.
Righteous Foremother Esther.patron: Invoked for intercession; courage before rulers.
Righteous Foremother Esther.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Foremother Huldah the Prophete.life: Huldah was a prophetess in Jerusalem in the days of King Josiah. When the book of the law was found in the temple during its repair and read before the king, he rent his clothes and sent the high priest and his servants to inquire of the Lord, and they went to Huldah.
Righteous Foremother Huldah the Prophete.patron: Invoked for repentance; the reading of Scripture.
Righteous Foremother Huldah the Prophete.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Jael.life: Jael was the wife of Heber the Kenite. When Sisera, the captain of the army that had oppressed Israel twenty years, fled from the battle and came to her tent, she received him and gave him milk to drink, and when he slept she slew him with a tent peg and delivered Israel from his hand.
Righteous Jael.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Foremother Tamar.life: Tamar was the daughter in law of Judah, twice widowed and left without the child that was owed her by the custom of the law. When Judah withheld his remaining son from her, she obtained by stratagem what was her right, and Judah acknowledged when the matter came to light that she was more righteous than he.
Righteous Foremother Tamar.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Foremother Bathsheba.life: Bathsheba was the wife of Uriah the Hittite and afterward of King David, who took her in the great sin for which the Prophet Nathan rebuked him and for which David composed the Fiftieth Psalm. The child of that union died, and the Church reads the whole account as the chief scriptural instance of repentance in a righteous man.
Righteous Foremother Bathsheba.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Foremother Eve.life: Eve was the first woman, formed by God from the side of Adam while he slept, and given to him as a helper meet for him. Adam called her Eve, that is, life, because she was the mother of all living.
Righteous Foremother Eve.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Abel the Shepherd.life: Abel was the second son of Adam and Eve and kept sheep, while his brother Cain tilled the ground. Both brought offerings to God, and God had respect to the offering of Abel and to his sacrifice of the firstlings of his flock, but not to the offering of Cain. Cain was wroth, and rising up against his brother in the field he slew him, and the voice of his blood cried from the ground.
Righteous Abel the Shepherd.patron: Invoked for the innocent slain; shepherds.
Righteous Abel the Shepherd.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Lot.life: Lot was the nephew of Abraham and went out with him from Ur of the Chaldees. When their herdsmen strove together they parted, and Lot chose the well watered plain of Jordan and dwelt toward Sodom.
Righteous Lot.patron: Invoked for deliverance from a doomed city.
Righteous Lot.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Forefather Isaac.life: Isaac was the son of Abraham and Sarah, born to them in their old age according to the promise, and his name means laughter, for Sarah laughed when she heard that she would bear a son.
Righteous Forefather Isaac.patron: Invoked for obedience; children long awaited.
Righteous Forefather Isaac.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Forefather Jacob.life: Jacob was the younger son of Isaac and Rebecca and received the blessing of the firstborn. Fleeing from the anger of his brother Esau he lay down at a certain place and dreamed of a ladder set up on the earth whose top reached to heaven, with the angels of God ascending and descending upon it, and the Lord standing above it and renewing to him the promise given to Abraham. Waking he said that.
Righteous Forefather Jacob.patron: Invoked for struggle in prayer; exiles.
Righteous Forefather Jacob.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Joseph the All-Comely.life: Joseph was the eleventh son of Jacob and the firstborn of Rachel, and his father loved him more than all his children and made him a coat of many colors. His brothers hated him for his dreams and sold him to merchants going down into Egypt, and dipped his coat in blood and brought it to their father.
Righteous Joseph the All-Comely.patron: Invoked for chastity; the falsely accused; prisoners.
Righteous Joseph the All-Comely.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Foremother Ruth.life: Ruth was a Moabitess, the widow of a son of Naomi. When Naomi returned to Bethlehem and urged her daughters in law to go back to their own people, Ruth would not leave her, and said, whither thou goest I will go, and where thou lodgest I will lodge, thy people shall be my people and thy God my God.
Righteous Foremother Ruth.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Joshua the Son of Nun.life: Joshua was the son of Nun and the servant and successor of Moses. He was one of the twelve sent to spy out the land, and with Caleb alone brought back a good report and urged the people to go up. For this the Lord appointed that he and Caleb of all that generation should enter the land.
Righteous Joshua the Son of Nun.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Solomon the King.life: Solomon was the son of David and Bathsheba and reigned after his father over Israel. At Gibeon the Lord appeared to him in a dream and told him to ask what he would, and he asked neither long life nor riches nor the lives of his enemies, but an understanding heart to judge the people and to discern between good and bad. This pleased the Lord, who gave him wisdom and also what he had not asked.
Righteous Solomon the King.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Patriarch Reuben.life: Reuben was the eldest son of Jacob by Leah. He alone among his brothers sought to save Joseph when the rest would have killed him, saying that they should shed no blood but cast him into a pit, intending to deliver him afterward to his father.
Righteous Patriarch Reuben.patron: Invoked for repentance after grave fault.
Righteous Patriarch Reuben.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Patriarch Levi.life: Levi was the third son of Jacob by Leah. He shared with Simeon in the vengeance taken at Shechem, and their father foretold that they would be scattered in Israel.
Righteous Patriarch Levi.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Patriarch Judah.life: Judah was the fourth son of Jacob by Leah. It was he who persuaded his brothers to sell Joseph rather than kill him, and afterward, when the household went down into Egypt, he offered himself as surety for Benjamin and pleaded before the governor of the land in words that moved Joseph to make himself known.
Righteous Patriarch Judah.patron: Invoked for kings; the royal line.
Righteous Patriarch Judah.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Patriarch Zebulun.life: Zebulun was a son of Jacob by Leah. His father said in blessing him that he would dwell at the haven of the sea and be for a haven of ships, and the portion of his tribe lay in the north toward the Sea of Galilee.
Righteous Patriarch Zebulun.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Patriarch Issachar.life: Issachar was a son of Jacob by Leah. In the blessing of his father he was likened to a strong beast of burden couching down between two burdens, who saw that rest was good and the land pleasant and bowed his shoulder to bear.
Righteous Patriarch Issachar.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Patriarch Dan.life: Dan was a son of Jacob by Bilhah the handmaid of Rachel. His name means judgment, and his father said in blessing him that Dan would judge his people as one of the tribes of Israel.
Righteous Patriarch Dan.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Patriarch Naphtali.life: Naphtali was a son of Jacob by Bilhah. His father likened him in blessing to a hind let loose, that gives goodly words.
Righteous Patriarch Naphtali.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Patriarch Gad.life: Gad was a son of Jacob by Zilpah the handmaid of Leah. His father said in blessing him that a troop would overcome him, but that he would overcome at the last.
Righteous Patriarch Gad.patron: Invoked for soldiers; those overcome who rise again.
Righteous Patriarch Gad.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Patriarch Asher.life: Asher was a son of Jacob by Zilpah. His father said in blessing him that his bread would be fat and that he would yield royal dainties, and the portion of his tribe lay along the fertile coast toward Tyre and Sidon.
Righteous Patriarch Asher.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Righteous Patriarch Simeon.life: Simeon was the second son of Jacob by Leah. With his brother Levi he avenged the dishonor of their sister Dinah upon the men of Shechem, and for the fierceness of that deed their father did not bless them as he blessed the others, but said that he would divide them in Jacob and scatter them in Israel.
Righteous Patriarch Simeon.src: Adapted from the Synaxarion (Lives of the Saints).

Saint Theophilus, Bishop of Antioch.life: The sixth bishop of Antioch in succession from the apostles, who came to the faith by reading the Scriptures he had taken up to refute. His three books to Autolycus survive, answering a learned pagan friend who had asked to be shown the Christians' God. He governed Antioch thirteen years and reposed about the year 181.
Saint Theophilus, Bishop of Antioch.patron: Invoked by apologists and catechists, and by those brought to faith through reading.
Saint Theophilus, Bishop of Antioch.src: The Prologue of Ohrid; Eusebius, Church History IV.20 and IV.24.

Saint Papias, Bishop of Hierapolis.life: Bishop of Hierapolis in Phrygia, called by Saint Irenaeus a hearer of John and a companion of Polycarp. His five books, the Exposition of the Oracles of the Lord, are lost but for the fragments others quoted, which preserve the earliest account the Church has of how the Gospels of Mark and Matthew came to be written.
Saint Papias, Bishop of Hierapolis.patron: Invoked by those who gather and hand on testimony.
Saint Papias, Bishop of Hierapolis.src: The Prologue of Ohrid; Eusebius, Church History III.36 and III.39.
